S01.title: Read the product and what it sells
S01.purpose: Build one dated fact sheet of what the product does, what it costs, and what is still unknown, so every later sentence of sales copy can be checked against something real.

steps.do: Open the product's own pages: home page, sales page, pricing page, and any help or delivery documents. Write down each URL and the date and time you read it.
steps.evidence: A list of URLs or file names, each with the time it was read.

steps.do: Look at the live product or a demo and list what a user can actually get done with it today. Ask the owner about anything you cannot see for yourself.
steps.evidence: Each listed function points to a screen, a document page, or the owner's confirmation.

steps.do: For each item on that list, mark whether the software does it, a person does it as a service, or it is not delivered yet.
steps.evidence: Every item is labeled software, human service, or not yet available, with who delivers it and any limit.

steps.do: Write down what is for sale: plan names, price, currency, billing period, current discounts, and when each discount ends. If a price is not shown on the product's pages, write 'unknown' and ask the owner.
steps.evidence: Every price and term has the URL or owner message it came from.

steps.do: Open the existing trial, sign-up, and buy links and check that each one loads and lands on the right product. Do not fill in forms and do not pay.
steps.evidence: Each link is listed with the page it actually reached and whether it worked.

steps.do: Collect proof that may be quoted: real customer cases, screenshots, numbers, and statements the owner has approved for public use.
steps.evidence: Each piece of proof has a source and a note on where it may be used.

steps.do: List what must never be promised without the owner's say: features that do not exist, new prices, extra deliverables, and business limits.
steps.evidence: A 'do not promise' list that later posts and replies can be checked against.

steps.do: Put everything into one product fact sheet: what is sold, proof, links, limits, and unknowns. Date it so later steps know which version they used.
steps.evidence: One dated fact sheet that the following steps can use without reopening the site.

steps.do: Note when the sources should be checked again, and update the fact sheet whenever the owner says something changed.
steps.evidence: A next-check date written on the fact sheet.

blockers.do: If the product pages will not load, ask the owner for a working URL or the page text, and do not describe the product from memory.
If no price is visible, record the price as unknown and ask the owner; never guess one.
If the product can only be seen after signing in, ask the owner for screenshots or a short walk-through; never ask for a password.
If two pages state different prices or features, list both versions with their URLs and ask the owner which one is current.
If a sign-up or buy link fails or lands on the wrong page, report it to the owner before any post sends people there.

deliver_help.product_facts: What the product does today, one fact per line, each with its source URL. Example: 'Turns a YouTube link into a piano score PDF (source: home page)'.
deliver_help.offer_and_price: Plans, price, currency, billing period, discounts, and the buy link, each with its source. Write 'unknown' where the page does not say.
deliver_help.limits_and_unknowns: What the product does not do, what must not be promised, and every question still open for the owner.

A-VOC.title: Collect real buyer quotes
A-VOC.purpose: Gather the exact words real people use for this problem and the result they want, because copy written in buyers' own words gets read and copy written in the seller's words gets skipped.

steps.do: List where real buyers talk about this problem: interviews, reviews, public help threads, customer emails, and refund reasons. Mark which of these the owner allows you to use.
steps.evidence: A source list with the URL or origin of each source and whether its use is allowed.

steps.do: Collect at least five posts or comments where real people describe this problem in their own words. For each one keep the shortest exact quote, its URL, its date, and an anonymous label such as 'person 1' instead of a name.
steps.evidence: At least five quotes, each with URL, date, and anonymous label.

steps.do: Sort each quote under one of five headings: the situation they were in, what they do today, what it costs them, the result they want, and what makes them hesitate before buying.
steps.evidence: Every quote sits under one heading.

steps.do: Remove sellers promoting themselves, AI-written answers, and guesses with no source. If you cannot read the original text, mark it as missing and do not paraphrase it from memory.
steps.evidence: A list of what was removed and why.

steps.do: Note which kind of people the sample came from (people who have not bought, buyers, people who refunded) and state its limits. Do not present it as the whole market.
steps.evidence: A short note on who is in the sample and who is missing.

blockers.do: If you find fewer than five real quotes, ask the owner for customer emails or reviews, say which public places you searched, and label everything else as a guess.
If a page is blocked or needs sign-in, skip it or ask the owner for a copy; do not rebuild the quote from search snippets.
If the only material is private customer messages, ask the owner whether they may be used and remove names before using them.
If a quote exposes health, money, or relationship details about an identifiable person, drop the identifying details and keep only the need that relates to the product.

deliver_help.buyer_quotes: Exact quotes with an anonymous label and date. Example: 'person 3, 2026-10-02: I spent a whole weekend writing this out by hand'.
deliver_help.sources: The URL or origin of every quote, and the time you read it.
deliver_help.patterns_found: What repeats across quotes, grouped as situation, current workaround, cost, wanted result, and hesitation.
deliver_help.limits_and_unknowns: Who the sample leaves out, what you could not read, and anything that is still a guess.

A-SEGMENTS.title: Group buyers by situation and trigger
A-SEGMENTS.purpose: Split buyers into groups by the moment the problem shows up, then choose one group to speak to, because copy aimed at one clear situation gets more response than copy aimed at everyone.

steps.do: Read the collected quotes and the product fact sheet. Do not work out why people buy from their age or gender.
steps.evidence: Each observation points to a quote or a product fact.

steps.do: Group buyers by five things: when the problem shows up, what they use instead today, what that costs them, the result they want, and the time, money, or skill they have.
steps.evidence: Two to four named groups, each described on those five points.

steps.do: Attach at least one real quote to each group, or label the group as a guess. For each group, say who is not a fit.
steps.evidence: Each group shows its quote or the word 'guess', plus who it leaves out.

steps.do: Leave ability to pay, who decides, budget, and timing as 'unknown' unless a source says otherwise. Do not answer these from a job title.
steps.evidence: A list of unknowns for each group.

steps.do: Choose the one group you can reach on this goal's channel now and that the product can serve today. Record why you chose it and what would show the choice is wrong.
steps.evidence: The chosen group, the reason, and at least one case that argues against it.

blockers.do: If there are no buyer quotes, go back and collect them; if the owner wants to continue anyway, label every group as a guess.
If all you have is age, gender, or job title, do not build groups from it; ask the owner about three recent buyers and what happened just before they bought.
If the best-supported group needs something the product does not do, choose the next group and report the gap to the owner.
If two groups differ only in name, keep the one with more quotes and drop the other.

deliver_help.buyer_groups: Two to four groups, each with its trigger moment and a supporting quote or the word 'guess'. Example: 'Parents whose child has a recital in two weeks'.
deliver_help.chosen_group: The one group this round of posts will speak to.
deliver_help.why_chosen: Why this group is reachable and can be served now, and what result would prove the choice wrong.
deliver_help.unknowns: Budget, who decides, and timing questions that no source has answered yet.

A-MOTIVES.title: Map each problem to a buying motive
A-MOTIVES.purpose: Connect each stated problem to the deeper result the buyer wants, because people pay for a change in their life or work, not for a feature.

steps.do: For each group, reread the real quotes and separate the problem they have right now from the change they want in their life or work.
steps.evidence: Each group has a 'problem now' line and a 'change wanted' line, both tied to quotes.

steps.do: Give each motive a working label such as earning money or career, love or company, health, looks, being liked, saving time, independence, or belonging. Treat every label as a guess to be tested.
steps.evidence: A list of motives, each with its label and marked 'to be tested'.

steps.do: For each motive write the quote behind it, the situation, how confident you are, and any quote that points the other way. Do not infer sensitive weaknesses from personal data.
steps.evidence: Each motive has a quote, a confidence note (strong, some, or guess), and any opposing quote.

steps.do: Split each motive into three parts: the practical job they want done, how they want to feel, and how they want others to see them.
steps.evidence: Each motive lists its practical, emotional, and social part, with 'unknown' where there is no evidence.

steps.do: Keep only the parts the product can really help with. Do not inflate fear, and do not promise income, health, or relationship outcomes.
steps.evidence: A final list of motives the product can serve, plus the ones you dropped and why.

blockers.do: If a motive has no quote behind it, mark it as a guess and go back to collect buyer quotes before relying on it.
If a motive does not fit the common labels, describe it in the buyer's own words and do not force it into one.
If the product does not really help with a motive, drop it from the selling plan and tell the owner what buyers wanted.
If a motive depends on guessing someone's health, finances, or relationship status, remove it and use only needs people stated themselves.

deliver_help.motives: Each motive in one line, with its group. Example: 'Wants to play the song at the recital without paying a teacher to transcribe it'.
deliver_help.supporting_quotes: The quote and source behind each motive, plus any quote that contradicts it.
deliver_help.guesses_to_test: Motives with no quote behind them yet, clearly marked as guesses.
deliver_help.limits: Outcomes the product cannot deliver and so must not be promised.

A-PRIORITY.title: Pick the strongest motive and objection
A-PRIORITY.purpose: Choose the single motive and the single objection that matter most to the chosen group right now, so the post makes one strong point and not five weak ones.

steps.do: For the chosen group, read the list of motives, what they use today, and the event that makes them look for a solution. Count repeated quotes from the same person once.
steps.evidence: The group name and the quotes used, with repeats from one person merged.

steps.do: Compare the motives on four points: how strong the quotes are, how urgent the timing is, what the buyer already pays or loses, and how much of it the product can help with. Judge by this evidence, not by scoring a fixed list of desires.
steps.evidence: A short comparison showing each motive against the four points.

steps.do: Name the main motive, the second motive, and the cases that contradict them. If the evidence is thin, keep two candidates and say so.
steps.evidence: Main and second motive, opposing cases, and a plain statement of how sure you are.

steps.do: Separate people who have the budget and the authority to buy from people who only want it. List unknown buying obstacles as questions to ask.
steps.evidence: Known objections, plus a list of open questions for the owner or for buyers.

steps.do: Pass the main motive on to the benefits step and the angle test. Write down beforehand which real replies or payments would prove it wrong.
steps.evidence: The main motive in one sentence and what result would disprove it.

blockers.do: If the ranking rests on no buyer quotes, say it is a guess and go back to collect quotes before treating it as settled.
If the quotes cannot separate two motives, keep both and let the angle test compare them.
If nothing shows who has the budget or the say, leave it unknown and ask the owner who has actually paid before.
If the owner believes a different motive is strongest, record both views with their evidence and test both.

deliver_help.main_motive: One sentence, with the quote that best supports it.
deliver_help.main_objection: The strongest reason this group hesitates to buy, or 'unknown' if no source says. Example: 'Not sure the score will be accurate enough to play from'.
deliver_help.second_motive: The runner-up, or a second candidate if the evidence could not separate them.
deliver_help.what_would_disprove_it: The reply, click, or payment result that would show the main motive is wrong.
deliver_help.open_questions: Budget, authority, and timing questions still unanswered.

A-LADDER.title: Turn features into benefits you can prove
A-LADDER.purpose: Translate each real feature into the benefit and result a buyer cares about, and mark exactly where proof stops, so the post is persuasive and still true.

steps.do: Read the product facts, the limits, and the buyer quotes one at a time. Do not add anything the product cannot do.
steps.evidence: The facts and quotes you used, each traceable to the fact sheet or a source URL.

steps.do: For each feature write a chain of four items: the feature, the benefit a buyer can observe, the result they want, and the point past which nothing may be promised.
steps.evidence: One chain per feature with all four items filled in.

steps.do: Mark each link in every chain as verified, guess, or unsupported, and give the reason.
steps.evidence: Every link carries one of the three marks and its basis.

steps.do: Check every number and every cause-and-effect claim separately. For example, 'meet people from five industries' and 'raise your chance of a new job' are two claims, and each needs its own proof.
steps.evidence: A list of claims, each with its proof or the note 'no proof, do not state as fact'.

steps.do: Choose the value statement that is both true and matches the main motive, and write it as one to three short message options ready to test.
steps.evidence: The chosen statement and its message options, each tied to verified facts.

blockers.do: If the product fact sheet is missing or out of date, go back and read the product before writing any benefit.
If a benefit has no proof, word it as an invitation to try or as something being tested, never as a result.
If a number has no source, remove it or ask the owner where it comes from.
If the benefit buyers want depends on a feature that does not exist, drop it from the copy and tell the owner about the gap.

deliver_help.chosen_message: The one true statement that best matches the main motive. Example: 'Photograph a receipt and the expense is filed for you'.
deliver_help.message_options: One to three short ways of saying it, for testing.
deliver_help.facts_used: The product facts and sources each option relies on.
deliver_help.must_not_promise: Results and numbers that have no proof and must stay out of the copy.

A-ANGLES.title: Design the sales angle test
A-ANGLES.purpose: Write two or three ways to present the same true benefit, choose the one this round publishes, and write the win rule before posting, so the goal's own number, compared with the baseline, decides whether it works. The other angles are kept for later rounds.

steps.do: Name one buyer group in one situation, the quote that represents them, the motive, and the benefit the product can deliver.
steps.evidence: Group, quote, motive, and benefit written in four short lines.

steps.do: Write two or three angles: the progress they hope for, getting past the real obstacle, and a believable demonstration. Do not use fear to exaggerate outcomes.
steps.evidence: Two or three angles, each in one or two sentences.

steps.do: For each angle list the facts that support it, the promises that are still unknown, and the wording that must not be used.
steps.evidence: Each angle has supporting facts, unknowns, and banned wording next to it.

steps.do: Choose the one angle this round publishes. The round compares it with the baseline, not with the other angles; keep those unchanged for later rounds. Keep the same channel, audience, and destination link as the baseline. If a channel step later offers a second version (?v=B), it differs in one labeled thing only and is extra information; the verdict still comes from the round's total. Before posting, write the guess being tested, how long the round runs, the number that counts as a win, and the cost in time or money.
steps.evidence: A test plan written before posting, showing the chosen angle, the guess, the duration, the win number, the cost, and the angles kept for later rounds.

steps.do: Choose the main number: the goal's metric, shown with this step (for example link clicks divided by views, followers gained, or purchases). Likes are supporting information only. State when the number is read.
steps.evidence: The main number, when it is read, and the chosen angle ready to be written as the post.

blockers.do: If no main motive has been chosen, go back and choose one before writing angles.
If an angle only works with a claim that has no proof, rewrite it as an invitation to try or drop the angle.
If the post is unlikely to get enough views to compare with the baseline, say so and report the result as an early signal, not as proof.
If the goal's main number cannot be read anywhere, ask the owner how it can be checked, and do not declare a winner from likes.

deliver_help.test_guess: One sentence. Example: 'Leading with the recital deadline raises the link click rate above the baseline'.
deliver_help.angles: The two or three angles, with the one this round publishes marked; the others are kept for later rounds.
deliver_help.facts_used: The product facts and buyer quotes each angle relies on.
deliver_help.win_rule: The main number, how long the round runs, and the result that counts as a win against the baseline. Example: 'Link clicks divided by views, read 48 hours after posting; the round wins if the post beats the baseline by 20% with at least 300 views'.

C-INSTAGRAM-ACCESS.title: Confirm the Instagram account and who publishes
C-INSTAGRAM-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which Instagram account posts, whether its insights can be read, and who presses Share, so every post and every number in this goal comes from the right brand account.

steps.do: Ask the owner for the URL of the brand's Instagram profile. Open it as a public page and check that the handle, name, and bio website match this product, not a personal account or a brand from an earlier goal.
steps.evidence: The profile URL and handle, with a note that the name and bio website match the product.

steps.do: Ask the owner whether the account is a professional account (business or creator). Insights such as reach, saves, and profile visits only exist on professional accounts. Do not switch the account type yourself; if it is personal, ask the owner whether they want to switch it in the app.
steps.evidence: The account type, and the owner's answer if a switch was discussed.

steps.do: Note which Instagram accounts are signed in right now in the agent's browser or tools. If another account is active, switch to the brand account in the account switcher without signing out of the others; if the brand account is not there, the owner signs in on the official Instagram screen. Never ask for a password and never copy cookies or tokens.
steps.evidence: The handles that are signed in, and the brand handle now active, or a note that nobody is signed in.

steps.do: Decide who presses Share: the owner in the Instagram app, or the agent if its browser or Instagram tool is signed in to this exact handle. If the agent uses a tool rather than a browser, check that the tool shows this handle and can both create a post and read insights; if it can only read, the owner publishes.
steps.evidence: Who will publish, the handle shown as signed in, and what the agent's tool can and cannot do on this account.

steps.do: Decide who reads the numbers: the agent if it can open the account's insights, or the owner by sending screenshots. Ask the owner who can read direct messages, and write down the time zone the insights use.
steps.evidence: Who reads insights and messages, and the time zone.

steps.do: Write down the current bio and bio link exactly as they appear. Instagram captions do not make links clickable, so a later step may ask to point the bio link at this round's tracked link; that change needs the owner's yes.
steps.evidence: The current bio text and bio link, copied from the profile.

steps.do: Create a new account only if the owner asked for one in this conversation and no brand account exists. Use one real account with the owner's approved name, bio, and website. Sign up with the owner's email, or with inbox_address if the owner agrees, and read the code with inbox_latest. Never invent a birthday or other details.
steps.evidence: The owner's request and the approved profile details, or a note that the existing account is used.

steps.do: If Instagram asks for a phone code, a login check, a CAPTCHA, an identity check, or acceptance of terms, stop and tell the owner which screen needs them. Note where you stopped and continue from there once they are done.
steps.evidence: What the owner must do, on which screen, and where to resume, or a note that nothing was needed.

steps.do: Open the public profile once more and confirm that whoever publishes can start a new post on this handle. Write down the time you checked.
steps.evidence: Profile URL, handle, account type, who publishes, and the time of the check.

blockers.do: If the active account is a personal account or another brand, stop before any posting and ask the owner to switch to the brand account or to post it themselves.
If the account is personal, tell the owner the goal's numbers cannot be read there and ask whether they want to switch it to a professional account in the app themselves.
If a phone code, login check, CAPTCHA, identity check, or terms screen appears, stop and tell the owner which screen and which button; never do these for them.
If neither the agent's browser nor its tool is signed in to the brand handle, set who_publishes to 'owner' and plan to hand them the final files and caption.
If Instagram says the account is restricted or an action is blocked, stop all posting and ask the owner to check the account's status in the app; never try a second account.

deliver_help.account_handle: The Instagram handle that will post. Example: '@yourbrand'.
deliver_help.profile_url: The public URL of that profile, opened and confirmed to belong to the product.
deliver_help.account_type: 'business', 'creator', or 'personal', as the owner confirmed it.
deliver_help.who_publishes: 'owner' or 'agent', plus one line on who reads insights and direct messages.

C-IG-RESEARCH.title: Study Instagram posts and comments for hooks that work
C-IG-RESEARCH.purpose: Find, from real recent posts and comments in the product's niche, the buyer situations and opening hooks worth testing, so the next post starts from what this audience already responds to.

steps.do: Write a short search list from the chosen angle and buyer quotes: 3 to 5 keywords or hashtags, and 5 accounts in the niche of different sizes, not only the biggest ones. Include accounts the buyers follow, not only competitors.
steps.evidence: The keywords, hashtags, and account handles you will search.

steps.do: Open at least 10 carousels or Reels from the last 90 days, one by one, with read_page or the agent's browser. Record each post's URL, author, date (or 'unknown'), format, and only the likes, comments, or views that are visible. Never guess reach.
steps.evidence: A list of at least 10 posts with URL, author, date, format, and visible numbers.

steps.do: Read the comments under those posts. Copy at least 5 comments, word for word, where a person describes a problem, asks how to do something, or asks where to buy. Keep the creator's own promotion apart from what the audience says.
steps.evidence: At least 5 exact comment quotes, each with the post URL it came from.

steps.do: For the 3 posts with the most visible engagement for their account size, break down the first slide or first 2 seconds, the first caption line, the order of the content, and the call to action.
steps.evidence: A breakdown of 3 posts: hook, first caption line, structure, and call to action.

steps.do: Check each hook against the product fact sheet. Drop any hook that would need a claim the product cannot back up, such as a result, a number, or a before-and-after you do not have.
steps.evidence: The hooks kept and the hooks dropped, each with a one-line reason.

steps.do: Write one test idea that changes only one thing: the hook, or the layout inside the format this goal publishes (for example a checklist carousel versus a step-by-step carousel). Describe version A and version B in one line each, in the product's own words; never copy another creator's images, text, or video.
steps.evidence: One hypothesis and two versions that differ in one labeled thing.

steps.do: Write down how you picked the posts, the date range, and what this research cannot show. Visible likes and comments do not show reach, followers gained, or sales.
steps.evidence: A short note on sample choice, date range, and limits.

blockers.do: If Instagram shows a sign-in wall and no posts, search the web for public post URLs in the niche, or ask the owner to send 10 post links or screenshots from their app.
If fewer than 10 posts from the last 90 days can be found, widen to 180 days, say so in limitations, and keep going.
If the comments hold fewer than 5 real questions or problems, use the buyer quotes already collected for this goal and say so; never write quotes yourself.
If every strong hook depends on a result the product cannot prove, ask the owner for the proof or pick a hook built on the buyer's situation instead.
If a post is private or removed, leave it out and pick another; never describe a post you could not open.

C-IG-RESEARCH.title_zh: 研究IG買家情境與內容鉤子

deliver_help.examples: Each post studied, with URL, author, date or 'unknown', format, visible numbers, and its hook.
deliver_help.buyer_quotes: Exact comment quotes that show a need or a buying question, each with its post URL; empty if none were found.
deliver_help.hypothesis: The one thing to test, and version A and version B in one line each.
deliver_help.limitations: How posts were chosen, the date range, and what the research cannot prove.

S10.title: Plan this round's post and the files it needs
S10.purpose: Turn the chosen angle, the research, and last round's result into one post with one clear idea and a production brief, so the round tests that idea against the goal's main number.

steps.do: Read the goal, its main number, and last round's result with where_are_we. Write in one sentence what this round should improve and the one thing it tests. If there is an earlier round, keep its post as it was and note what changes and why. If there is none, start from the chosen angle; never claim an earlier winner that does not exist.
steps.evidence: One sentence naming the goal's number, the thing being tested, and last round's result with the reason for the change, or 'first round'.

steps.do: List the posts, photos, videos, and product screenshots the owner already has. Mark each one 'owner made', 'licensed', or 'unknown'. Leave out anything marked unknown until the owner confirms the rights.
steps.evidence: A list of usable files, each with its rights status.

steps.do: Give the post one buyer group and one stage: first hears of the problem, compares options, or is ready to buy. If the idea speaks to two groups, keep one and save the other for a later round.
steps.evidence: The post's one buyer group and stage.

steps.do: Pick the angle and the proof: the problem, the promise, and a real demo, screenshot, or fact from the product fact sheet. Leave out any result you cannot prove.
steps.evidence: The angle and the facts or demos the post relies on.

steps.do: Use the format this goal's plan publishes: a carousel of 4:5 images at 1080 x 1350, or, for the Reels goal, a vertical 9:16 Reel at 1080 x 1920.
steps.evidence: The format and size of the post.

steps.do: Choose the one action the post asks for, matched to the goal's main number: save, follow, send a message, or tap the link in bio. If it sends people to the product, get this round's tracked link from tracking and open it to check it loads; if tracking says it is not available, use the product URL and note that clicks will be read from Instagram.
steps.evidence: The call to action, and the link opened and checked, or a note that the post has no link.

steps.do: Write version A, the one this round publishes. If the research suggests a second idea, write version B that differs in one thing only (the hook, the proof, or the layout), label the difference, and keep it as the candidate change for the next round. Do not publish both in one round: Instagram has one bio link and the round is judged on one post.
steps.evidence: Version A, and version B if any, labeled with the single difference and marked 'next round'.

steps.do: Write a production brief for version A: slide count or video length, the text for each slide or on-screen line, the files to use, and the size. Keep slide text under 20 words and put the hook on the first slide or in the first 2 seconds.
steps.evidence: One brief with files, size, length, and the text for each part.

steps.do: Pick the publish day and hour, at a time the owner can approve and, if the account's insights show when followers are most active, inside that time. Note that the numbers are read when the goal's observation window ends (48 hours for these goals), and that no other post for this goal goes out during the window.
steps.evidence: The planned publish date and hour with time zone, and when the numbers will be read.

blockers.do: If no angle has been chosen, go back to the angle test step before planning the post.
If there are no files with known rights, plan a post made from product screenshots or plain text slides, and ask the owner for one real photo or demo.
If the link does not open the product, stop and ask the owner which product URL to use before planning a link call to action.
If version B differs from version A in more than one thing, cut it back to one difference so the next round can show what worked.
If the post needs a fact you do not have, drop that claim or ask the owner; never fill the gap with a guess.

S10.title_zh: 安排下一批內容與素材

deliver_help.batch_plan: What the round tests and why, the buyer group, the stage, the call to action, and the facts the post relies on.
deliver_help.versions: Version A to publish now, version B for the next round if any, the one thing that differs, and the link the post uses.
deliver_help.production_brief: For version A: format, size, slide count or length, text per slide or line, and files to use.
deliver_help.schedule: The publish date and hour with time zone, and when the numbers will be read.

A-COPY.title: Write the post from proven facts
A-COPY.purpose: Write the post or message that opens with the buyer's own situation and offers one true step forward, because specific, believable copy is what makes a reader act.

steps.do: Read the chosen angle, the buyer quotes, and the product fact sheet. Open the post with the situation the reader is in right now, in words close to how buyers describe it.
steps.evidence: The opening line, with the quote and facts it draws on.

steps.do: Then state one specific step forward the product helps with, and point to the existing link where the reader can act on it.
steps.evidence: One or more draft versions, each with one benefit and one link you have opened and checked.

steps.do: Keep what the product delivers separate from what the buyer hopes will follow. Without data, do not write 'improves X%' and do not guarantee an outcome such as getting a job.
steps.evidence: A list of the claims in the post, each marked 'delivered by the product' or 'hoped-for result'.

steps.do: If you write more than one version, change only one thing between them and label what changed, so the versions can be compared fairly.
steps.evidence: Each version is labeled with the single thing that differs.

steps.do: Check every sentence against the fact sheet and against the way the owner writes. Remove any number without support, or reword it as a clearly labeled guess.
steps.evidence: The final text, a sentence-by-sentence fact check, and a note that it is ready to show the owner.

blockers.do: If no angle has been chosen, go back to the angle test step before writing.
If a sentence needs a fact you do not have, remove the sentence or ask the owner; never fill the gap with a guess.
If you do not have a product link that you have opened and seen load, ask the owner which URL to use.
If you do not know how the owner writes, ask for two of their past posts and match that tone.
If the text is over the channel's length limit, cut it to one situation, one benefit, and one link.

deliver_help.post_text: The exact final text of the post, including the link, as it will be shown to the owner for approval.
deliver_help.facts_used: Each product fact or buyer quote the post relies on, with its source.
deliver_help.claims_avoided: Numbers, guarantees, and outcomes you left out because there was no proof. Example: 'Did not say it is 99% accurate'.

S12.title: Make the marketing images from real product visuals
S12.purpose: Produce finished image files in the exact size the channel needs, built from real product visuals and approved copy, because a clear image that matches the product is what stops the scroll and moves the goal's main number.

steps.do: Write down what images this round needs: the channel and placement, the image type (single image, carousel, cover or ad), the pixel size, and how many. If the size is unknown, check the channel's current help page; for example 1080x1350 for a portrait feed image and 1080x1920 for a full-screen vertical one.
steps.evidence: A list of images with channel, placement, size and purpose for each.

steps.do: Collect the real visuals: product screenshots, product photos, logo and brand colours. Use only material the owner made or has the right to use; never copy other brands' images or stock photos without a licence.
steps.evidence: Each visual with where it came from and who owns it.

steps.do: Take the words only from the approved copy. For feed and ad images keep the text to at most two short lines, around 10 words, placed where it stays readable and clear of the channel's own buttons and captions; follow the channel's own text rules for covers and store screenshots. Do not let an image tool add numbers, prices, ratings or badges.
steps.evidence: The exact text for each image, matching the approved copy.

steps.do: Lay out each image with one headline, the product shown working, and one call to action. If there is more to say, split it into carousel slides instead of crowding one image.
steps.evidence: A short layout note or sketch for each image.

steps.do: Make the actual image files with the image or design tool available. Place the text as a real text layer, not generated lettering. A prompt or description is not a finished image. If the only available tool charges money, ask the owner before using it.
steps.evidence: Image files that open.

steps.do: Open each file at full size and check spelling, cropping, faces, and that any product screen shown is the real product. Fix any garbled or wrong text by rebuilding it, never by handing over a flawed image.
steps.evidence: A checked list of each image with any fixes made.

steps.do: Check each file's type (JPG or PNG), pixel size and file size against the channel's limits, and view it at phone width to confirm the text is readable.
steps.evidence: Type, pixel size and file size for each image, all within the channel's limits.

steps.do: If the round tests versions, make only the versions the test needs and change one thing between them, labelled A, B and so on. Do not make extra variations for channels not in this round.
steps.evidence: Each version labelled with the single thing that differs.

steps.do: Save the final files with clear names and a note of version, purpose and sources, in a place the publishing step can open and upload from.
steps.evidence: File paths or links that open, with the note for each file.

blockers.do: If there are no screenshots or photos of the real product, ask the owner for two or three, and meanwhile make a text-and-brand-colour design without fake product screens.
If the channel's required size is unclear, check its current help page; if still unclear, ask the owner where the image will run.
If the image tool produces wrong or garbled text, rebuild the text as a real text layer before handing over the file.
If you cannot tell who owns a visual, leave it out and use one the owner confirms they own.
If the image tool fails, try another available tool with the same brief; do not start the whole brief over or create duplicate charges.

deliver_help.image_files: Paths or links to the final image files, each with its pixel size and file type.
deliver_help.image_text: The exact words on each image, matching the approved copy, so the owner can approve them before publishing.
deliver_help.versions: What each version is for and the single thing that differs between versions, or 'one version'.
deliver_help.sources: Where every screenshot, photo and logo in the images came from and who owns it.

C-IG-METRICS.title: Read this goal's numbers on Instagram
C-IG-METRICS.purpose: Record the numbers this goal is judged on, for the account before and after the new post, so each round is compared on real numbers. record_numbers lists exactly which numbers it needs.

steps.do: Confirm the handle, whether this is the baseline or the current reading, and the time zone. The baseline is read just before this round's post goes live; the current reading is read after the goal's observation window ends, which the engine tells you (48 hours for these goals). Read only the components the step lists, and leave out any the engine says it counted itself.
steps.evidence: Handle, baseline or current, the components needed, and the time zone.

steps.do: For numbers read per post, such as reach, saves, and profile visits: for the baseline, add up the account's last 3 to 5 posts of the same format from the past 30 days, each at least 48 hours old; for the current reading, use this round's post. Take both parts of a rate from the same posts, and keep per-post numbers apart from account totals.
steps.evidence: The posts measured with their URLs, and each number as shown, per post and added up.

steps.do: For a Reel, read the views figure the Reel's insights show and use it for video_starts, saying so in source. Use a figure for views that reached the end only if the insights display one as a number, either a count or a percentage you can multiply by views; never read it off a graph by eye.
steps.evidence: Views and the end-of-video figure exactly as displayed, with the screen they came from, or a note that no end-of-video figure is shown.

steps.do: For followers, read the follower count on the profile at the moment of reading; it is a running total and the engine subtracts the earlier reading. Note follows and unfollows too if the account's insights show them. Never report the total alone as this round's growth.
steps.evidence: The follower count with the time read, plus follows and unfollows if shown.

steps.do: For link clicks and profile visits on the account: in the current reading, link_clicks are usually counted by the engine from the tracked link, so leave them out when the step says so. For the baseline, read external link taps and profile visits from the account's insights for the shortest date range offered that ends just before publishing, both from the same range.
steps.evidence: Link clicks and profile visits with their source and date range.

steps.do: For qualified_inquiries, keep a running total: the number of different people who asked in comments or direct messages about price, availability, how to buy, or whether the product fits their case, counted from this goal's first baseline reading (0 at that reading). Leave out the owner, the agent, spam, and bots. The owner reads direct messages or sends screenshots.
steps.evidence: The running total of different people who asked, with the date and a short summary of each question, without names.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with only this goal's metric components, by their exact names from the step's list. Put the screen or tool, the post URLs, the date range, and the time read in source. If there is no history for a component, record 0 and say in source that there is no history. Never estimate a number Instagram does not show.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call with each component name, its value, and its source.

steps.do: Report site visits or sales separately and only from a source the owner already has, such as site analytics or payment records. Say plainly when a visit or sale cannot be tied to the post.
steps.evidence: Any visit or sales figure with its source, or a note that none was available.

blockers.do: If you cannot open the insights, ask the owner for a screenshot of the post's insights or the account's insights for each number this goal needs.

If Instagram does not display a number this goal needs, ask the owner for another source they already have; if none exists, submit status 'blocked' naming the missing number, and never estimate it or read it off a graph.
If the account has no history for these numbers, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline.
If a screenshot or screen shows a different handle from the agreed one, do not use those numbers and ask again.
If the observation window has not ended, report the numbers as early and read them again once the engine says the window is over.
If the account is personal and shows no insights, record only what the public profile shows, say so in source, and send the owner back to the account step.

C-IG-METRICS.title_zh: IG追蹤成長與內容到網站漏斗核對

deliver_help.numbers: Each metric component of this goal by its exact name, with the value passed to record_numbers.
deliver_help.where_read: The screen or tool each number came from, the post URLs, and the time it was read.
deliver_help.date_range: The start and end of the measured range, with the time zone.

C-IG-CAROUSEL.title: Publish one Instagram carousel and confirm it
C-IG-CAROUSEL.purpose: Publish the approved carousel once, under the right account, and hand back its public URL, because the post has to be live and exactly as approved before its numbers can be measured.

steps.do: Confirm the handle about to post is the agreed brand account. Look through its last 12 posts so you do not publish the same images or caption twice.
steps.evidence: The handle, and a note on the recent posts you checked.

steps.do: Open every slide file and check it shows correctly, is in the planned order, uses one size (4:5 at 1080 x 1350 works well), keeps text away from the edges, and is owner made or licensed. Check the slide count is within Instagram's current limit.
steps.evidence: The ordered list of slide files, the slide count, and the rights status of each.

steps.do: Check the caption against the product fact sheet: under 2,200 characters, no more than 5 hashtags, and no price, promise, or number the facts do not support. Links in captions are not clickable, so a link call to action points to the link in bio.
steps.evidence: The final caption, its character count, and the facts each claim relies on.

steps.do: If the call to action uses the bio link, get this round's tracked link from tracking and open it to check it loads the product. Changing the bio link changes the owner's profile, so it is part of the approval.
steps.evidence: The tracked link, opened and checked, and the bio link it would replace, or a note that the bio link stays.

steps.do: Show the owner the slides in order, the exact caption, and any bio link change. Get a clear yes to this exact version before anything goes live.
steps.evidence: The owner's approval message for these slides, this caption, and this bio link.

steps.do: The agreed person updates the bio link if approved, creates the post, adds the slides in order, and checks the preview of every slide for bad crops. Press Share once. If an upload is still running, wait; do not press Share again.
steps.evidence: Confirmation that the preview matched the approved slides, who pressed Share, and when.

steps.do: Open the post's public URL and check every slide, the slide order, the caption, and the handle. Open the profile and check the bio link. If the post shows as under review or not yet public, report that status and do not post again; if publishing seemed to fail, check the profile for the post before any retry.
steps.evidence: The public post URL, the caption as it appears there, and the live bio link.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to these exact slides, caption, and bio link, do not publish; show them and stop until they answer.
If the signed-in account is not the agreed handle, stop and ask the owner to switch accounts or to post it themselves.
If the agent cannot post, give the owner the slide files in order, the caption, and the bio link, and ask them to send back the post URL.
If the preview cuts off text or images, pick the original size in the crop option, or resize every slide to the same 4:5 size, then check the preview again.
If the post does not show up after Share, check the profile again after a few minutes before any retry, and never post the same carousel twice.
If the tracked link does not open the product, stop before publishing and fix the link with the owner.

deliver_help.post_url: The public link to the live carousel, opened and confirmed. Example: 'https://www.instagram.com/p/...'.
deliver_help.published_text: The full caption exactly as it appears on the live post, copied from the public page.
deliver_help.bio_link: The link in the profile bio after publishing, or 'unchanged' if the post does not use it.

S13.title: Make a faceless demo video from real product footage
S13.purpose: Produce a finished, playable video that shows the real product working, with subtitles and the right format for the channel, because a clear demo people watch to the end is what moves the goal's main number.

steps.do: Write down who the video must convince, the channel and placement, the length, and the shape; for example under 60 seconds and 1080x1920 vertical for short-form, or 16:9 for a longer video.
steps.evidence: One line on the viewer and the goal of the video, plus length and size.

steps.do: Collect real footage: screen recordings, screenshots, existing videos, music and voice the owner has the right to use. Every feature the video shows needs real footage of the product.
steps.evidence: A list of footage with where each piece came from, and any feature still missing footage.

steps.do: Turn the approved script into a shot list: a hook in the first 2 seconds, the product being used, the result, and one call to action. Replace any claim you cannot show on screen with one you can.
steps.evidence: A shot list where each line names the footage it uses.

steps.do: Record missing demo footage only in a demo account or test setup the owner approved, or cut it from existing material. Hide customer names, emails and private data. If a shot needs a real person's face or voice or a change to the live product, list it for the owner and make the rest.
steps.evidence: The new footage, checked for private data, and a list of any shots left for the owner.

steps.do: Add subtitles that match the script word for word, and a voice-over only with a voice the owner has the right to use. Check every number, product name and spelling in the subtitles.
steps.evidence: The subtitle file or burned-in subtitles, checked against the script.

steps.do: Edit the full video with footage, subtitles, pacing and an end card that shows the call to action. A script alone is not a finished video. If the only available editing or voice tool charges money, ask the owner before using it.
steps.evidence: A video file that plays.

steps.do: Play the whole video and check the start, middle and end: sound, subtitles, that each product screen is real, and that no private data or misleading scene appears.
steps.evidence: A note that the full video was played, with any fixes made.

steps.do: Export the versions each channel needs, checking length, size, shape and file size against the channel's limits. If a file fails, fix and export it again; never hand over the same broken file twice.
steps.evidence: Each exported file with its length, pixel size and file size.

steps.do: Prepare what publishing needs: a cover image, a title and a caption from the approved copy. If several versions are tested, label them A, B and so on, with one difference between them.
steps.evidence: The cover, title and caption for each version, labelled.

steps.do: Save the final files with clear names and a note of version, purpose, sources and subtitles, in a place the publishing step can open and upload from.
steps.evidence: File paths or links that open and play, with the note for each file.

blockers.do: If there is no real footage of a feature, ask the owner for a screen recording of it and drop that claim from the video until it arrives.
If any frame shows customer names, emails or other private data, blur or recut it before going further.
If recording would change the live product or real customer data, stop that recording and ask the owner for a safe demo account or existing footage.
If you cannot confirm the right to use a voice or music track, use subtitles only or a track the owner confirms they may use.
If an export is over the channel's length or file size limit, shorten or compress it and check again before handing it over.

S13.title_zh: 製作不露臉影片與產品示範

deliver_help.video_files: Paths or links to the final video files, each with length, pixel size and file size.
deliver_help.versions: What each version is for and the single thing that differs, or 'one version'.
deliver_help.sources: Where every clip, screenshot, music track and voice came from and who owns it.
deliver_help.publish_kit: The cover image, title and caption for each video, taken from the approved copy.

C-IG-REEL.title: Publish one Instagram Reel and confirm it
C-IG-REEL.purpose: Publish the approved Reel once, under the right account, and hand back its public URL, because the video has to be live and exactly as approved before its watch-through can be measured.

steps.do: Confirm the handle about to post is the agreed brand account. Look through its recent Reels so you do not publish the same video or caption twice.
steps.evidence: The handle, and a note on the recent Reels you checked.

steps.do: Play the video file from start to end. Check it is vertical 9:16 (1080 x 1920 works well), within Instagram's current length limit, and that the hook lands in the first 2 seconds. If it runs much longer than 30 seconds, tell the owner that shorter Reels are usually easier to watch to the end.
steps.evidence: The video file, its length in seconds, its size, and a note on the first 2 seconds.

steps.do: Check the rights for every image, clip, and sound. Use only owner-made audio or sound from Instagram's own library that this account may use. If the video is a slideshow or mock-up, do not call it a real product recording.
steps.evidence: The rights status of each image, clip, and sound, and whether the video shows the real product.

steps.do: Check that on-screen text sits away from the bottom and right edge, where Instagram places buttons and the caption. Pick a cover frame that shows the hook. Check the caption: under 2,200 characters, no more than 5 hashtags, only claims the facts support, and a link call to action points to the link in bio.
steps.evidence: The cover frame, the final caption with its character count, and the facts each claim relies on.

steps.do: If the call to action uses the bio link, get this round's tracked link from tracking and open it to check it loads. Show the owner the video, cover, exact caption, any bio link change, and the time it will go live, and get a clear yes.
steps.evidence: The link checked or a note that none is used, and the owner's approval message for this exact video, cover, caption, and time.

steps.do: The agreed person uploads the video, sets the cover, pastes the caption, updates the bio link if approved, and checks the preview. Press Share once, or schedule it for the approved time if the app offers that. If Instagram is still processing, wait up to 30 minutes and check the profile; do not upload the video again.
steps.evidence: Who pressed Share or set the schedule, when, and whether processing finished.

steps.do: Once the Reel is public, open its URL and check that the video plays and that the cover, caption, and handle are right. Open the profile and check the bio link. Hand in the step only after it is public; if publishing seemed to fail, check the profile and drafts before any retry.
steps.evidence: The public Reel URL, the caption as it appears there, and the live bio link.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to this exact video, cover, and caption, do not publish; show them and stop until they answer.
If the signed-in account is not the agreed handle, stop and ask the owner to switch accounts or to post it themselves.
If the agent cannot upload video, give the owner the video file, cover frame, caption, and bio link, and ask them to send back the Reel URL.
If the sound is not owner made or Instagram marks it as unavailable for this account, replace it with owner-made audio or an allowed sound and show the owner again.
If the Reel is still processing after 30 minutes, check the profile and drafts, tell the owner, and never upload the same video again while the first may still go live.
If the file does not play to the end on the agent's side, ask the owner for a fresh export from the video step before uploading.

deliver_help.reel_url: The public link to the live Reel, opened and confirmed to play. Example: 'https://www.instagram.com/reel/...'.
deliver_help.published_text: The full caption exactly as it appears on the live Reel, copied from the public page.
deliver_help.video_length_seconds: The length of the published video in seconds.

C-THREADS-ACCESS.title: Confirm the Threads account and who publishes
C-THREADS-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which Threads account will post and who presses publish (the owner, or the agent's own browser), so the post goes out under the right brand without the owner being stopped halfway.

steps.do: Ask the owner for the URL of the Threads profile that will post. Note separately which Threads account and which Instagram account are signed in right now; being signed in to Instagram does not mean the Threads profile exists.
steps.evidence: Both handles written down, with whether each profile exists.

steps.do: Open the Threads profile URL as a public page and confirm that it exists and belongs to the owner. If it exists, use it and do not create a second profile.
steps.evidence: The profile URL and the owner's confirmation that it is theirs.

steps.do: Decide who presses publish: the owner on their own device, or the agent's own browser if it is already signed in to that account. If nobody is signed in, the owner signs in themselves on the official Threads screen and, if it offers 'Continue with Instagram', checks the Instagram handle shown first. Never ask for a password.
steps.evidence: Who will publish, how the owner signed in, and the handle that was selected.

steps.do: Create a new Threads profile only if the owner asked for one in this conversation. Check the name, bio, and website link with the owner, and never enter a made-up birthday or made-up verification details.
steps.evidence: The owner's request and the profile details they approved, or a note that no new profile was needed.

steps.do: If Threads asks for a verification code, acceptance of terms, or an identity check, stop and tell the owner exactly which screen needs them. Note where you stopped and return to the same profile once they have finished.
steps.evidence: A note of what the owner needs to do, on which screen, and where to resume.

steps.do: After sign-in or profile creation, open the public profile again and the account's own profile screen. Confirm the handle matches the brand and that whoever publishes can open the new post box.
steps.evidence: Profile URL, handle, confirmation that a new post can be started, and the time this was checked.

blockers.do: If the Instagram account offered at sign-in is not the one tied to the intended Threads profile, have the owner go back to the account chooser and pick the right handle.
If the Threads URL shows no profile, tell the owner; a successful Instagram sign-in is not a Threads profile, and a new one is created only if the owner asks.
If a verification code, terms screen, or identity check appears, stop and tell the owner which screen and which button; never enter codes or accept terms for them.
If the agent's browser is not signed in to the right account, set who_publishes to 'owner' and plan to hand them the final text to post.
If the signed-in account is a personal account or a different brand, stop before any posting and ask the owner which account to use.

deliver_help.account_handle: The Threads handle that will post. Example: '@yourbrand'.
deliver_help.profile_url: The public URL of that profile, opened and confirmed to exist.
deliver_help.who_publishes: 'owner' or 'agent browser', plus one line on why.

C-TH-METRICS.title: Read this goal's numbers on Threads
C-TH-METRICS.purpose: Record the numbers this goal is judged on, for the account's posts before and after the new post, so rounds are compared on real numbers. record_numbers lists exactly which numbers it needs.

steps.do: Confirm which Threads profile and which posts you are measuring, the date range, and the time zone. Check whether you can open the Threads insights screen; if you cannot, ask the owner for a screenshot or the numbers.
steps.evidence: Profile handle, post URLs, date range with time zone, and how the numbers will be obtained.

steps.do: Read the follower count at the start and end of the range, plus views, replies, and link clicks where Threads shows them. Write 'not shown' for any number Threads does not display, and do not estimate it.
steps.evidence: The numbers exactly as displayed, with the screen they came from and the time they were read.

steps.do: Count conversations once per person who shows a real need for the product. Do not count the owner's or the agent's own replies as new prospects.
steps.evidence: The number of different people who asked about the product, with the URL of each reply.

steps.do: Add website visits and sales only if the owner already has a source for them, such as site analytics or payment records. Where you cannot tell which post led to a visit or a sale, say so plainly.
steps.evidence: Each visit or sales figure names its source, and unknown links between post and sale are stated.

blockers.do: If you cannot open the Threads insights screen, ask the owner for a screenshot of it or for the numbers this goal needs.

If Threads shows no link clicks for the post, ask the owner for clicks from the site analytics or link tool they already use and name that source. If there is no source at all, say so; do not estimate.
If the account has no history for these numbers, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline.
If the screenshot or screen shows a different handle from the agreed one, do not use those numbers and ask again.
If the post is less than 24 hours old, report the numbers as early and read them again later.

C-TH-METRICS.title_zh: 讀取瀏覽與連結點擊數

C-TH-POST.title: Publish one Threads post and confirm it
C-TH-POST.purpose: Publish the approved post once, under the right account, and hand back its public URL, because the post has to be live and exactly as approved before any click can be measured.

steps.do: Confirm the handle about to post is the agreed one, and look through its recent posts so you do not repeat the same content.
steps.evidence: The handle, and a note on the most recent posts you checked.

steps.do: Read the final text and any image for this post and check they fit the current Threads limits. Show the owner the exact text and get a clear yes before publishing.
steps.evidence: The final text, its character count, any image file, and the owner's approval message.

steps.do: If the message needs a follow-up post, plan it as a reply under the first post so everything stays in one thread. Do not publish it as several unrelated posts.
steps.evidence: A plan showing which post comes first and which one replies to it, or a note that one post is enough.

steps.do: Put the approved text, link, and image in the Threads post box, or hand them to the owner to paste, and check the preview matches the approved text. The agreed person presses Post once; if an upload is still in progress, let it finish and do not press Post again.
steps.evidence: Confirmation that the preview matched the approved text, who pressed Post, and when.

steps.do: After publishing, open the post's public URL and read back the full text, the author handle, and, for a follow-up, the post it sits under. If publishing seemed to fail, check the profile for the post before trying again so nothing is posted twice.
steps.evidence: The public URL, the text as it appears there, and the author handle.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to this exact text, do not publish; show them the text and stop until they answer.
If the signed-in account is not the agreed handle, stop and ask the owner to switch accounts or to post it themselves.
If the agent's browser cannot post, give the owner the final text and link to paste, and ask them to send back the post URL.
If the post does not show up after publishing, check the profile again after a few minutes before any retry, and never post the same text twice.
If the link in the post does not open the product site, stop before publishing and fix the link with the owner.

deliver_help.post_url: The public link to the live post, opened and confirmed to load. Example: 'https://www.threads.net/@handle/post/...'.
deliver_help.published_text: The full text exactly as it appears on the live post, copied from the public page.

C-TH-INTENT.title: Find recent Threads posts where people ask for help
C-TH-INTENT.purpose: Produce a checked list of recent public Threads posts where real people ask for a recommendation or describe the problem the product solves, because these posts are the round's eligible requests and the only places a reply can help.

steps.do: Write 5 to 10 search phrases from the buyer quotes, in the words buyers use: '<task> recommend', 'any alternative to <tool>', 'how do I <problem>'. Use the buyers' language, not product terms.
steps.evidence: The list of phrases, each with the date it was run.

steps.do: Search with Threads search in the agent's browser, or with a web search limited to threads.com or threads.net. Prefer posts from the last 7 days and drop anything older than 30 days.
steps.evidence: For each phrase, the candidate post URLs found and how they were found.

steps.do: Open each candidate post itself. Read the author's handle, the date, the full text and the replies below it. A search snippet is not a read post.
steps.evidence: For each post: URL, author handle, date, and whether you read the full post and its replies.

steps.do: Keep only posts where the author asks for a recommendation or describes the problem in their own words. Exclude sellers promoting themselves, trend or joke posts, posts already solved in the replies, and posts that limit who can reply.
steps.evidence: For each kept post, the exact quote that shows the need; for each excluded post, the reason.

steps.do: Check each kept post against the product fact sheet: does the product truly solve what this person asked? Write the fit as your inference, separate from what they said. Also check whether the brand account already replied in that thread.
steps.evidence: Each kept post marked fits, partly fits, or does not fit, plus whether the brand already replied.

steps.do: Hand back the qualified posts, the excluded ones and the unknown ones, each with a reason. The count of qualified posts is this round's number of eligible requests for the goal. If fewer than three qualify, report the true number; never invent a need.
steps.evidence: The qualified list with its count, and the excluded and unknown lists with reasons.

blockers.do: If Threads search does not work in your browser, use a web search limited to threads.com or threads.net; if a post cannot be opened, leave it out rather than guessing its content.
If Threads asks you to sign in to search, ask the owner to sign in in your browser or to run the phrases and send you the post URLs.
If no post qualifies, rewrite the phrases once using different buyer words, then report the true zero.
If the brand already replied in a thread, exclude it; never reply to the same person twice in one round.
If the author limits who can reply, exclude the post and do not reach out by DM instead.

deliver_help.demand_posts: Each qualified post: URL, author handle, date, the exact quote showing the need, and why the product fits.
deliver_help.exclusions: Posts left out and why. Example: 'seller promoting own app' or 'solved in replies'.
deliver_help.search_phrases: The phrases you searched, where you searched them, and the date.

C-TH-REPLY.title: Reply helpfully to Threads posts that ask for help
C-TH-REPLY.purpose: Post one honest, useful reply under each qualified request, with the owner's approval, because a reply that solves the person's problem first is what turns a public request into a real conversation.

steps.do: Reopen each post on the qualified list just before writing. Confirm the author, that the post is still up and still open to replies, that it was not solved, that the brand has not replied, and that the author has not asked people to stop.
steps.evidence: Each post marked still eligible or skipped, with the reason and the time checked.

steps.do: Write one reply per post, under 500 characters. Answer the question first with something useful even if they never buy. Mention the product only if it truly fits, and say plainly that you make it, for example 'I'm the founder of ...'.
steps.evidence: One draft per post, its character count, and the line that states the relationship to the product.

steps.do: If the reply includes a link, use the round's tracked link. If you are testing two reply angles, add ?v=A to one and ?v=B to the other, and change only the angle.
steps.evidence: Each draft's link and version label, or a note that it has no link.

steps.do: Check each claim against the product fact sheet; remove any number, result or promise you cannot support. Do not move the person to DM or email unless they ask for it.
steps.evidence: Each draft with its claims and the fact each one rests on.

steps.do: Show the owner every reply word for word, with the post it answers. Post at most 10 replies in a round, never the same text twice. Nothing goes out without the owner's yes.
steps.evidence: The approved replies and the owner's approval message.

steps.do: Confirm the signed-in account is the agreed brand handle. Post each approved reply once, directly under the original post. The owner posts it, or the agent's own browser does if it is signed in and the owner said yes. Leave at least 10 minutes between replies.
steps.evidence: For each reply: who posted it and the time.

steps.do: Open each reply's public URL. Check the text, the author handle and that it sits under the right post. If posting seemed to fail, look for the reply before trying again so nothing is posted twice.
steps.evidence: The public URL of each reply and its text as it appears there.

steps.do: Over the next 48 hours, check each thread for answers. Draft short responses to real questions for the owner to approve, and stop at once if someone says no thanks.
steps.evidence: For each reply: no answer, answered with interest, or declined, with the URL of any answer.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to a reply's exact text, do not post it; show it to them and wait.
If the signed-in account is not the agreed brand handle, stop and ask the owner to switch accounts or post the replies themselves.
If the post was deleted, solved, or closed to replies, skip it and do not contact the author another way.
If the author or anyone in the thread asks the brand to stop, do not reply again and record it.
If a reply does not appear after posting, check again after a few minutes before any retry, and never post the same text twice.

deliver_help.reply_urls: The public URL of each reply that went live, with the post it answers and its version label if any.
deliver_help.published_text: The full text of each reply as it appears on the live page.
deliver_help.author_responses: What each author did after the reply: no answer, a question, interest, or no thanks, with the URL.

C-X-ACCESS.title: Confirm the X account and who posts
C-X-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which X account will post, who presses post, and what limits that account has, so threads and replies go out under the right brand without stopping the owner halfway.

steps.do: Ask the owner for the URL of the X profile that will post. Open it and confirm the handle, display name, bio and website link match the brand.
steps.evidence: The profile URL and handle, with the owner's confirmation that it is theirs.

steps.do: Decide who presses post: the owner on their own device, or the agent only through a posting tool the owner connected that uses X's official API. X's automation rules forbid scripting the x.com website and can suspend the account, so the agent never posts by driving x.com in a browser. Write down which tools actually exist.
steps.evidence: Who will post, and the tool or device they will use.

steps.do: If the owner needs to sign in, they do it themselves on x.com or in the X app. Never ask for a password, and never sign in for them.
steps.evidence: The owner's confirmation that they are signed in, and the handle shown after sign-in.

steps.do: If X asks for an email or phone code, a CAPTCHA, terms or an identity check, stop and tell the owner exactly which screen needs it. Return to the same account once they finish.
steps.evidence: A note of what the owner had to do and where work resumed.

steps.do: Note the account's limits that affect this round: whether it can post more than 280 characters, whether it can add images or video, and whether the owner can open post analytics. Do not buy an X plan or API access; if a step needs one, tell the owner the price shown and let them decide.
steps.evidence: A short list of what the account can and cannot do this round.

steps.do: Use only this one real account. Never create extra accounts or switch accounts to get around limits; if X shows a limit, write down when it resets.
steps.evidence: Confirmation that one account is used, and any limit seen with its reset time.

steps.do: If the account cannot post right now, finish what does not need posting, such as search phrases and drafts, and list the one thing the owner must do to unblock posting.
steps.evidence: The work already done and the single owner action still needed, or 'none'.

blockers.do: If the signed-in account is a personal account or a different brand, stop before any posting and ask the owner which account to use.
If a verification code, CAPTCHA, terms screen or identity check appears, stop and tell the owner which screen and which button; never enter codes or accept terms for them.
If the agent has no posting tool that uses X's official API, set who_publishes to 'owner' and plan to hand them the final text to post.
If X shows the account is locked or limited, stop posting, tell the owner what X shows, and continue drafting until it is cleared.
If the round needs something only a paid X plan or paid API access offers, tell the owner what it is and the price shown, and let them decide; never buy it.

deliver_help.account_handle: The X handle that will post. Example: '@yourbrand'.
deliver_help.profile_url: The public URL of that profile, opened and confirmed to be the owner's.
deliver_help.who_publishes: 'owner' or 'agent via official X API tool', plus one line on why.
deliver_help.account_limits: Post length, media, search and analytics limits that matter this round, and any limit reset time seen.

C-X-INTENT.title: Find recent public posts on X where buyers ask for help
C-X-INTENT.purpose: Collect recent public X posts where real people describe the problem the product solves, in their own words, because these show who to speak to and what to say, which is what moves the goal's main number.

steps.do: Write 3 to 5 search phrases from the buyer quotes and segments, such as "looking for" plus the task, "any recommendations" plus the category, or "alternative to" plus a tool buyers name. Add -filter:retweets and since: with a date 14 days back.
steps.evidence: The exact search phrases.

steps.do: Run each phrase on X search's Latest tab. If the owner connected a search tool that uses X's official API, the agent may use it; otherwise give the owner the phrases to run and ask them to paste back the post links, or use the agent's own web search for public x.com posts. Never script x.com or collect results in bulk, and stop if X shows a limit message.
steps.evidence: For each phrase, who ran it, the date run, and the number of posts looked at.

steps.do: Open each promising post itself, not a repost or quote, with read_page or through the owner if it does not load, and read the whole thread. Write down the post URL, author handle, date, and the person's exact words about their need.
steps.evidence: A list of posts with URL, handle, date and exact quote.

steps.do: Sort each post: keep it only if the person wants to switch tools, is looking for a product or service, or is stuck with their current way. Exclude promotions, job posts, vendors, bots, and needs already solved, with a reason.
steps.evidence: Kept and excluded posts, each with a one-line reason.

steps.do: For each kept post, check the product can actually solve this need using the fact sheet. Write what the person said and what you infer as two separate lines.
steps.evidence: For each kept post, the stated need and the inferred fit written separately.

steps.do: Check each kept post can be answered: replies are open to the owner's account, it is less than 7 days old, and the owner has not already replied to that person about it. Keep one entry per person.
steps.evidence: Each kept post marked 'can reply' or 'cannot reply', with one entry per person.

steps.do: Stop at 10 qualified posts or after 50 posts reviewed, whichever comes first. Hand back the list. Do not look up emails, phone numbers or other personal details beyond the public post.
steps.evidence: The final list with counts of posts reviewed, kept and excluded.

blockers.do: If no official X search tool is connected and web search finds nothing usable, give the owner the exact phrases to run and ask them to paste back the post links.
If X shows a limit message, stop, note the time, and continue from the same phrase after the limit resets.
If no phrase finds a real need in the last 14 days, try two new phrases from different buyer quotes, then report zero with the phrases tried.
If the author limits replies, mark the post 'cannot reply'; never plan a mention or DM instead.
If a later step asks for emails or phone numbers of these people, refuse and keep only the public post details.

deliver_help.demand_posts: Each qualified post with URL, handle, date, the person's exact words, the inferred fit, and whether a reply is possible.
deliver_help.excluded_posts: Posts you looked at and left out, each with a one-line reason.
deliver_help.search_phrases: The exact search phrases used, the date each was run, and how many posts each returned.

C-X-METRICS.title: Read this goal's numbers on X
C-X-METRICS.purpose: Record the numbers this goal is judged on for the account and its threads, for a fixed range before and after the new post, so rounds are compared on real numbers. record_numbers lists exactly which numbers it needs.

steps.do: Confirm the X handle, the post or thread URLs being measured, whether this is the baseline or the current reading, the date range, and the time zone. Check whether you can open the post's analytics; if not, ask the owner for a screenshot or the numbers.
steps.evidence: Handle, post URLs, baseline or current, date range with time zone, and how the numbers will be obtained.

steps.do: If the goal needs followers, read the follower count on the profile at the start and the end of the range, at about the same time of day. Record the end count as followers and put the start count in source.
steps.evidence: Both follower counts with the time each was read.

steps.do: If the goal needs impressions, profile_visits or url_clicks, read them from each post's analytics. For a thread, decide once whether you use the first post only or the sum of all posts, and use the same choice for baseline and current. Impressions are views, not unique people.
steps.evidence: Each number as shown, the post it came from, and whether it is the first post or the thread total.

steps.do: For url_clicks, prefer the click count of the round's tracked link from tracking when the post used it, and note X's link click number next to it. Say which one you recorded, and use the same one for baseline and current.
steps.evidence: The click number recorded, its source, and the other number for comparison.

steps.do: If the goal needs qualified_conversations or qualified_replies, count each different person once who showed a real need for the product, with the URL of their reply or the date of their message. Do not count the owner's or the agent's own replies, bots or vendors. If it needs eligible_requests, count the public requests on the round's list that were still open to a reply in the range.
steps.evidence: Each count, with one URL or date per person or request and a one-line reason each qualifies.
