steps.do: Add website visits or purchases only if the owner already has a source for them, such as the tracked link, site analytics or payment records. Where you cannot tell which post led to a sale, say so plainly; never infer a purchase.
steps.evidence: Each visit or sales figure names its source, and unknown links are stated.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with the goal's exact metric component names as listed for this goal, each with its source. If there is no history, record 0 and say so in source. Never estimate; if a number is not shown, say which one and why.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call with each component, its value and its source.

blockers.do: If you cannot open the post's analytics, ask the owner for a screenshot of it or for the numbers this goal needs.
If the account has no history for these numbers, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline.
If the screenshot or screen shows a different handle from the agreed one, do not use those numbers and ask again.
If the baseline used a different thread counting choice, read the baseline again the same way before comparing.
If the post is less than 24 hours old, report the numbers as early and read them again when the 48-hour range ends.

deliver_help.numbers: Each of the goal's metric components by exact name with its value, 0 with a note where there is no history.
deliver_help.where_read: For each number, where it was read: the profile, the post's analytics, the tracked link, or the owner's screenshot.
deliver_help.date_range: The start and end of the range with time zone, and whether it is the baseline or the current reading.

C-X-POST.title: Publish an approved X thread in order and confirm it
C-X-POST.purpose: Publish the approved thread once, post by post in the right order under the right account, and hand back its public URL, because the thread must be live and complete before anything it does to the goal's main number can be measured.

steps.do: Confirm with the owner which X handle will post and who presses Post: the owner, or the agent's own browser if it is signed in to that account. Look at the profile's recent posts to make sure this round's first post is not already live.
steps.evidence: The handle, who will publish, and a note on the recent posts checked.

steps.do: Lay out the thread as a numbered list. Keep each post under 280 characters unless the account clearly allows longer posts, and keep the thread to 2 to 8 posts. The first post must make sense on its own. Attach images in the planned order with short alt text.
steps.evidence: The numbered thread with each post's character count and its images in order.

steps.do: If the thread links to the product, put the link only in the last post, using the round's tracked link. If there are two versions of the thread, add ?v=A to one and ?v=B to the other, and open the link once to confirm it loads.
steps.evidence: The exact link with its version label and confirmation it opens the product, or a note that the thread has no link.

steps.do: Check every post against the product fact sheet; remove any number, result, quote or promise you cannot support.
steps.evidence: The list of claims in the thread, each with its fact source.

steps.do: Show the owner the full thread word for word, with images, and get a clear yes before anything is posted.
steps.evidence: The approved thread and the owner's approval message.

steps.do: Publish the first post once. Then publish each next post as a reply to the one before it, in order, using X's own thread composer or reply button. Use only normal X features; never use scripts to get around X's rules.
steps.evidence: The URL of each post as it went live, in order.

steps.do: If publishing stops halfway, open the profile and find which posts are live. Continue from the first missing post as a reply to the last live one. Never post the first post again.
steps.evidence: A note of where it stopped and where it resumed, or a note that it ran without a break.

steps.do: Open the first post's public URL and read the whole thread: author handle, order, full text of each post, and that the link opens the product page.
steps.evidence: The thread's public URL, its text as it appears, and confirmation the link works.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to this exact thread, do not post; show it to them and wait.
If the signed-in account is not the agreed handle, stop and ask the owner to switch accounts or post it themselves.
If only part of the thread went live, continue from the first missing post as a reply to the last live one; never repost the first post.
If X says you have hit a limit, wait until it lifts and then continue the same thread; never switch to another account.
If the agent's browser cannot post, give the owner the numbered thread to post and ask them to send back the first post's URL.
If the tracked link does not open the product page, stop before posting and fix the link with the owner.

C-X-POST.title_zh: X串文逐篇發布與部分成功恢復

deliver_help.thread_url: The public URL of the first post of the live thread, opened and confirmed to load.
deliver_help.post_urls: The URL of every post in the thread, in order.
deliver_help.published_text: The full text of each post as it appears on the live thread.

C-TIKTOK-ACCESS.title: Confirm the TikTok account, who posts, and the link option
C-TIKTOK-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which TikTok account will post, who presses post, whether the profile can show a clickable website link, and which numbers can be read, so videos go out under the right brand and the goal's number can be measured.

steps.do: Ask the owner for the URL of the TikTok profile that will post and the brand's website. Open the profile as a public page and confirm it exists and belongs to the brand. If it exists, use it and do not create a second account.
steps.evidence: The profile URL, the handle, and the owner's confirmation that it is theirs.

steps.do: Decide who presses post: the owner in the TikTok app, or the agent's own browser if it is already signed in to that account and the owner agrees. Some TikTok features work only in the app, so the owner may need to do those parts. Never ask for a password, and do not reuse another brand's signed-in session.
steps.evidence: Who will post, and which parts the owner must do in the app.

steps.do: If the owner asked for a new account, the owner signs up on the official TikTok screen with their real details. If an email code is needed, the agent may give an address from inbox_address and read the code with inbox_latest. Phone checks, QR confirmations, and puzzles are for the owner. Create one real account only.
steps.evidence: How sign-in or sign-up was done, which steps the owner handled, and the resulting handle.

steps.do: Check the account type, the country or region it is set to, and whether the profile can show a clickable website link right now. Do not assume every account has this, because it differs by account type and region. Do not switch the account type or fill in business details to get a link unless the owner asks and the details are true.
steps.evidence: The account type, the region, and a yes or no on whether a clickable website link can be added.

steps.do: If a website link is available, plan to put the round's tracked link in the profile, with the owner's approval of the change. If it is not available, tell the owner that clicks and sales from TikTok cannot be tracked through the profile this round, and focus on video numbers.
steps.evidence: The planned profile link, or a note that no clickable link is available and what that means for measurement.

steps.do: Check the sound and footage rights for the planned videos. Business accounts can use only sounds cleared for commercial use, so prefer original audio. Read the current length and size limits on the upload screen instead of assuming them.
steps.evidence: The sound and footage source for each planned video, marked original or cleared, and the limits shown on the upload screen.

steps.do: Check which numbers the account's analytics shows, such as video views, average watch time, full-watch share, profile views, and followers, and the time zone it uses. If analytics is off or empty, note that it may only fill in after the first post and a day or two of delay.
steps.evidence: A list of numbers that can be read, the time zone, and how they will be obtained.

blockers.do: If the profile cannot show a clickable website link, do not treat plain text in the bio as a trackable link; tell the owner and measure video numbers only.
If TikTok asks for a phone check, QR confirmation, puzzle, or terms, stop and tell the owner exactly which screen needs them, then resume where you stopped.
If a planned sound is not cleared for commercial use, switch to original audio or a cleared sound before the video is made.
If a feature exists only in the app, write down the exact step for the owner to do on their phone; never describe a web button you have not seen.
If analytics shows nothing yet, note it and plan to read numbers after the first video has been live for at least 48 hours.
If the signed-in account is a personal account or another brand, stop before any posting and ask the owner which account to use.

deliver_help.account_handle: The TikTok handle that will post. Example: '@yourbrand'.
deliver_help.profile_url: The public URL of that profile, opened and confirmed to exist.
deliver_help.who_publishes: 'owner' or 'agent browser', plus which parts can only be done in the app.
deliver_help.profile_link: Whether a clickable website link can be shown, and the tracked link planned for it, or 'not available'.
deliver_help.numbers_visible: The numbers the account's analytics shows, the time zone, and whether analytics is ready yet.

C-TT-RESEARCH.title: Study TikTok openings and calls to action that fit the buyer
C-TT-RESEARCH.purpose: Find how real TikTok videos about the buyer's problem open and end, and turn that into one opening or call-to-action test, because the first seconds and the ending decide whether viewers keep watching, follow, or click.

steps.do: Turn the chosen angle and buyer quotes into three to five TikTok search phrases, such as '<situation> tutorial', '<problem> review', or '<category> alternative'. Search with web search, read_page, or the agent's browser.
steps.evidence: The search phrases and the date they were searched.

steps.do: Collect at least ten videos from the last 90 days that speak to the buyer's problem. Choose them for the problem they address, not for a trending sound. Write down the URL, the author, and the posting date, or 'unknown'.
steps.evidence: A list of at least ten video URLs with author and date or 'unknown'.

steps.do: For each video, write a short note on the first three seconds: the first image, the on-screen text, and the first spoken line. Also note the length, the pace, whether captions are on screen, and how it ends. Paraphrase; quote no more than a few words.
steps.evidence: A note per video covering the opening, length, pace, captions, and ending.

steps.do: Read the comments and copy up to three real viewer questions or objections per video word for word. Skip comments from the creator and obvious spam.
steps.evidence: Viewer questions and objections, each with the video URL it came from.

steps.do: Record only the numbers shown publicly, such as views, likes, and comments. Profile visits, link clicks, and site visits are not public, so leave them empty and never guess them. Do not treat views as sales.
steps.evidence: The public numbers per video, with private numbers left empty.

steps.do: Pick one thing for the next video to test, either the opening or the call to action, and write versions A and B that differ only in that thing. Choose the opening when the goal's main number depends on watching or following, and the call to action when it depends on profile visits, clicks, or sales.
steps.evidence: The single thing tested, versions A and B, and the videos or viewer quotes each draws on.

steps.do: Take from the account step whether the profile can show a clickable website link. If it cannot, the call to action must not say 'link in bio', the test should aim at video numbers or profile visits only, and the plan must not claim website sales can be measured.
steps.evidence: A note on whether a link is available and how the call to action was adjusted.

blockers.do: If fewer than ten relevant videos turn up, widen the search phrases to the buyer's wider situation or extend the date range to 180 days, and say so.
If TikTok pages will not open for the agent, ask the owner to share five to ten video links they find relevant, and study those.
If the profile cannot show a clickable link, drop 'link in bio' from every call to action and test openings or profile visits instead.
If a pattern depends on a sound the brand cannot use commercially, note it and plan the test with original audio.
If the videos found do not match the buyer's problem, go back to the buyer quotes and rewrite the search phrases before collecting more.

deliver_help.videos_studied: Each video's URL, author, posting date or 'unknown', and its public numbers only.
deliver_help.openings_found: The patterns seen in the first three seconds and the endings, each with the video URLs that show it.
deliver_help.viewer_questions: Real viewer questions or objections copied word for word, each with its video URL.
deliver_help.test_plan: The one thing to test, versions A and B, and why it fits the goal's main number.

C-TT-METRICS.title: Read this goal's numbers on TikTok
C-TT-METRICS.purpose: Record the numbers this goal is judged on, for the account's videos before and after the new video, so rounds are compared on real numbers from video to profile to website to sale. record_numbers lists exactly which numbers it needs.

steps.do: Confirm the TikTok handle, which videos you are measuring, the date range, and the time zone. For a baseline, use the account's recent videos over a range of the same length as this round; for current, use this round's video URL over this round's range. Note whether the profile has a clickable website link.
steps.evidence: The handle, the video URLs, the date range with time zone, and whether a profile link exists.

steps.do: Pass only this goal's metric components, by these exact names: followers for net followers; completed_views and video_starts for completion rate; profile_visits and video_views for profile visit rate; website_clicks and profile_visits for profile link rate; external_purchases and attributed_sessions for site purchase rate. Decide where each is read before reading anything, and never borrow a number from another goal.
steps.evidence: A list of each component name and the source it will be read from.

steps.do: Open the video's analytics and the account's analytics, or ask the owner for screenshots if you cannot, and read the numbers exactly as displayed. video_views and video_starts are the views TikTok shows for the video. If full watches are shown only as a percentage, multiply it by the views on the same screen, round down, and say so in source. For followers, record the net change in the range, the end count minus the start count, and say so in source.
steps.evidence: The numbers as displayed, the screen they came from, and the time they were read.

steps.do: Keep each stage separate: video views are not profile visits, profile visits are not website clicks, and website clicks are not site visits. Read website_clicks from the round's tracked link, split by ?v= label if there are versions. If the baseline period had no tracked link, read website clicks for both baseline and current from TikTok's analytics and give the tracked-link count in source as a cross-check.
steps.evidence: Each stage's number with its own source, and no stage filled in from another.

steps.do: Read attributed_sessions from the owner's site analytics with TikTok as the source; if there is none, use clicks on the round's tracked link and say in source that these are clicks, not sessions. Read external_purchases from the sale counter or payment records, count each paid order once, and leave out refunds and the owner's own test payments. Do not add new tracking code.
steps.evidence: Site visit and purchase counts with their sources, and any orders excluded and why.

steps.do: If the account has no history for a number, record 0 and say in source that there is no history. If TikTok does not show a number, write 'not shown' and never estimate it. If the video is less than 48 hours old, label the numbers early and read again later.
steps.evidence: Each zero or missing number with its reason.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with each component by its exact name and a source naming the screen, screenshot, link, or record and the time read. If a rate's bottom number is 0, still record both numbers and do not claim any improvement.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call with every component, its value, and its source.

blockers.do: If you cannot open TikTok's analytics, ask the owner for screenshots of the video's and the account's analytics for the exact date range.
If analytics is empty or the video is less than 48 hours old, label any numbers early and read them again after the delay.
If the account has no history for these numbers, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline.
If a screenshot shows a different handle or other videos, do not use those numbers and ask again.
If the profile has no clickable link, record website clicks and site visits from TikTok as 'not available' in source and do not estimate them.
If there is no sale counter, site analytics, or payment record, say so in source and do not count any purchases.

deliver_help.numbers: Each goal component by its exact name with its value, with 0 marked as 'no history' and missing numbers marked 'not shown'.
deliver_help.where_read: For each number, the analytics screen, screenshot, tracked link, or payment record it came from, and the time it was read.
deliver_help.date_range: The start and end of the range measured, with the time zone. Example: '2026-11-20 09:00 to 2026-11-22 09:00, Asia/Taipei'.

C-TT-VIDEO.title: Publish one TikTok video and confirm it
C-TT-VIDEO.purpose: Publish the approved vertical video once, under the right account and with the right cover, caption, and profile link, and hand back its public URL, because the video must be live exactly as approved before its numbers can be read.

steps.do: Open the final video file and check it: vertical 9:16, the opening hook shows in the first two seconds, on-screen captions are readable, a cover frame is chosen, and the sound is original or cleared for commercial use. Check its length against the limit shown on TikTok's upload screen.
steps.evidence: The file name, length, cover frame, and sound source, with each check passed.

steps.do: Confirm the handle about to post is the agreed one, and look through its last ten videos so you do not repeat the same opening or caption.
steps.evidence: The handle and a note on the recent videos you checked.

steps.do: Write the caption: one line on the viewer's situation, one true benefit, and a call to action, aiming for under 300 characters with no more than five relevant hashtags. Links in captions are not clickable, so point to the profile link only if the profile has one. Use only claims the product facts support.
steps.evidence: The caption text, its character count, and the facts it relies on.

steps.do: If the profile can show a website link, prepare the round's tracked link for it, with ?v=A or ?v=B if this round runs one version at a time. Open the link and check it lands on the product page. One profile link carries one label, so when two versions run at the same time, compare them on each video's own numbers instead. Do not change the profile yet.
steps.evidence: The profile link as it will appear, opened and confirmed to load, or a note that no link is available.

steps.do: Show the owner the video, the cover, the caption word for word, and any profile link change, and get a clear yes before anything goes public.
steps.evidence: The exact material shown to the owner and their approval quoted word for word.

steps.do: Make the approved profile link change, then upload the video once. The agent does this only if its own browser is signed in to the agreed account and the owner said yes; otherwise the owner does it from the app using the approved files and caption. If the upload is still processing, wait and do not upload again.
steps.evidence: Who changed the link and posted, the date and time, and any processing or review status shown.

steps.do: Once the video is public, open its URL and read back the caption, the handle, the cover, and that captions show on screen. A video still under review is not live. If posting seemed to fail, check the profile before trying again so nothing is posted twice.
steps.evidence: The public video URL, the caption as it appears there, and the handle.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to this exact video, cover, and caption, do not post; show them the material and stop until they answer.
If the signed-in account is not the agreed handle, stop and ask the owner to switch accounts or to post it themselves.
If the sound is not original or cleared for commercial use, replace it before posting and show the owner the new version.
If the video is still processing or in review, wait and check its status again later; never upload the same video twice.
If posting or setting the cover works only in the app, give the owner the files, caption, and exact steps, and ask them to send back the video URL.
If the profile cannot show a clickable link, remove 'link in bio' from the caption and post with a call to follow or visit the profile instead.

C-TT-VIDEO.title_zh: TikTok直式影片發布與封面讀回

deliver_help.video_url: The public link to the live video, opened and confirmed to load. Example: 'https://www.tiktok.com/@handle/video/...'.
deliver_help.published_caption: The caption exactly as it appears on the live video, copied from the public page.
deliver_help.profile_link: The tracked link shown on the profile with its ?v= label, or 'none' if the profile cannot show a link.
deliver_help.posted_at: The date, time, and time zone the video went public, and who posted it.

C-YOUTUBE-ACCESS.title: Confirm the YouTube channel and who publishes
C-YOUTUBE-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which YouTube channel this round uses, who signs in and who presses publish or reply, and which features the channel can use, so the round's videos or replies go out under the right brand without stopping halfway.

steps.do: Ask the owner for the URL of the YouTube channel this round will use. Open it as a public page and write down the handle and the channel ID (the part starting with 'UC' in a /channel/ URL, or the ID shown in the channel's About details). Go by the channel ID, not the display name, because several channels can share a name.
steps.evidence: The channel URL, handle and channel ID, opened as a public page.

steps.do: Ask the owner which Google account manages that channel. If the channel belongs to a brand account, the owner must switch to that channel in the account menu; being signed in to Gmail does not mean you are acting as the channel. The owner signs in on the official Google page and does any two-step verification. Never ask for a password.
steps.evidence: The Google account that manages the channel, and the owner's confirmation that the right channel is selected.

steps.do: Decide who publishes or replies: the owner on their own device, or the agent's own browser if it is already signed in as that channel. Have whoever publishes open YouTube Studio for this channel and check the channel name and picture at the top match the brand.
steps.evidence: Who will publish, and a note or screenshot showing YouTube Studio open on the right channel.

steps.do: List what this round needs (upload a video, reply to comments, read analytics, a clickable link in a description) and check each one for this channel. Videos longer than 15 minutes and custom thumbnails need YouTube's extra features, which are usually unlocked by verifying the channel with a phone number; check the channel's feature eligibility in YouTube Studio settings. Links in Shorts descriptions and comments are not clickable, so a link-click goal needs a long video.
steps.evidence: A short list of the actions this round needs, each marked 'works', 'needs the owner' or 'not available', with the reason.

steps.do: Create a new channel only if the owner asked for one in this conversation, with a name and handle the owner approved. The owner creates it from their own Google account, or the agent does it in a browser already signed in to that account after the owner says yes. Use one real account only, never extra or fake channels. If a new Google account is truly needed and the owner agrees, you may use inbox_address and read the verification code with inbox_latest; phone verification, identity checks and terms are left to the owner.
steps.evidence: The owner's request and the approved channel name, or a note that the existing channel is used.

steps.do: If YouTube asks for a verification code the agent cannot read, a phone check, acceptance of terms or an identity check, stop and tell the owner exactly which screen needs it. Note where you stopped and return to the same channel once they are done.
steps.evidence: What the owner needs to do, on which screen, and where to resume, or a note that nothing was needed.

steps.do: Check the channel's comment settings in YouTube Studio: whether comments are on, and whether comments are held for review. Note the time zone the channel's reports use, so later numbers are read for the right days.
steps.evidence: The comment setting, the review setting and the report time zone.

steps.do: Finish by opening the public channel page again, and confirm whoever publishes can open the upload screen or the reply box on one of the channel's videos.
steps.evidence: Channel URL, handle, confirmation that upload or reply can be started, and the time this was checked.

blockers.do: If the signed-in account is acting as a different channel or a personal channel, stop and ask the owner to switch to the channel with the agreed channel ID.
If the URL shows no channel, tell the owner; a Google sign-in is not a channel, and a new one is created only if the owner asks.
If a phone check, terms screen or identity check appears, stop and tell the owner which screen and which button; never accept terms or verify on their behalf.
If the agent's browser is not signed in as the right channel, set who_publishes to 'owner' and plan to hand them the final text and files.

If a needed feature such as clickable links or long uploads is not available, or YouTube limits how much the channel can upload or reply today, say so, change the round to use what works (for example a long video instead of a Short) or wait for the limit to reset, never switch to another channel, and never claim the link drives visits.
If comments are off on the channel or a video, do not change the setting yourself; tell the owner and leave that video out of any reply work.

deliver_help.channel_url: The public URL of the channel this round uses, opened and confirmed to load with the brand's name and picture, and the time it was checked.
deliver_help.channel_id: The channel ID that starts with 'UC', so later steps never act on a channel with a similar name.
deliver_help.who_publishes: 'owner' or 'agent browser', plus one line on why.
deliver_help.available_actions: Each action this round needs (upload, reply, analytics, description link) marked 'works', 'needs the owner' or 'not available'.

C-YT-METRICS.title: Read this goal's numbers on YouTube
C-YT-METRICS.purpose: Record the numbers this goal is judged on, for the same channel and the same length of time before and after the round, so rounds are compared on real YouTube and link numbers. record_numbers lists exactly which numbers it needs.

steps.do: Confirm the channel ID, the videos or comment threads you are measuring, the date range and the time zone. For the baseline use the same number of days just before the round; for the current reading use the round's own days. If you cannot open YouTube Studio analytics, ask the owner for screenshots or the numbers.
steps.evidence: Channel ID, video or comment URLs, date range with time zone, and how the numbers will be obtained.

steps.do: Read the numbers exactly as YouTube Studio shows them for those videos and days: views, watch time, average view duration, subscribers gained and subscribers lost. Read Shorts and long videos separately and never add them into one figure without saying so.
steps.evidence: The numbers as displayed, split by Shorts and long videos, with the screen they came from and the time they were read.

steps.do: Fill the goal's components by their exact names. For a subscriber goal, 'subscribers' is subscribers gained minus subscribers lost in the range. For a completion goal, 'video_starts' is the views of the measured videos; for 'completed_views', use a count of viewers who reached the end only if YouTube shows one. If it shows only the video's audience retention chart, multiply the views by the percentage still watching at the last moment of the video, round down, use the same method for the baseline and the current reading, and say in source that it was calculated from the retention chart. If the chart cannot be read at the end, leave 'completed_views' out and name it as missing.
steps.evidence: Each component name with its number and a one-line note on how it was read.

steps.do: For a link-click goal, take 'link_clicks' from the round's tracked link (from tracking), not from YouTube, and 'views' from YouTube Studio for the same videos and days. Comments and likes never stand in for clicks.
steps.evidence: The tracked link's click count and the matching views, each with its source.

steps.do: For a comment-request goal, 'eligible_requests' is the number of different request comments the round replied to, and 'qualified_replies' is the number of those commenters who answered back with a real next step (asked for the link, a price or a demo, or said they will try it). Count each person once, and never count likes or the owner's or the agent's own replies.
steps.evidence: Both counts, with the URL of each reply that was counted as qualified.

steps.do: Add website visits or sales only if the owner already has a source for them, such as the tracked link, site analytics or payment records. Where you cannot tell which video or reply led to a visit or a sale, say so plainly.
steps.evidence: Each visit or sales figure names its source, and unknown links between video and sale are stated.

steps.do: Pass the goal's exact component names to record_numbers with the source of each. If there is no history, record 0 and say in source that there is no history. Never estimate a missing number; leave it out and name it as missing.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers entry with every component, its source, and any missing number named.

blockers.do: If you cannot open YouTube Studio analytics for this channel, ask the owner for screenshots of the screens that show the numbers this goal needs.
If a screen or screenshot shows a different channel from the agreed channel ID, do not use those numbers and ask again.
If the channel has no history for these numbers, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline.
If the description had no tracked link, say that link clicks cannot be read for this round, record nothing for clicks, and make sure the next round uses the tracked link.
If the videos or replies are less than 48 hours old, YouTube figures may still be filling in; report the numbers as early and read them again later.

C-YT-METRICS.title_zh: YouTube訂閱與既有網站引流核對

deliver_help.numbers: Each of the goal's component names with its value exactly as read or calculated, for example 'video_starts: 412'.
deliver_help.where_read: For each number, the screen, report, screenshot or tracked link it came from, and the time it was read.
deliver_help.date_range: The first and last day measured, with the time zone, for example '2026-11-15 to 2026-11-21, Asia/Taipei'.

C-YT-VIDEO.title: Upload the approved video to the right YouTube channel
C-YT-VIDEO.purpose: Upload and publish the approved video or Short once, on the brand's own channel, with honest settings and the tracked link, and hand back its public URL, because only a live, correctly set video can move the goal's main number.

steps.do: Ask the owner for the URL of the brand's YouTube channel. The owner signs in to Google themselves. In YouTube Studio, confirm the channel selected is that brand channel and not a personal one.
steps.evidence: The channel URL, the channel name shown in YouTube Studio, and who will upload.

steps.do: Check the video file. A Short is vertical and up to 3 minutes; a regular video is usually horizontal. Confirm with the owner that they own or have licensed all footage, music and images in it.
steps.evidence: The file name, its length and shape, and the owner's confirmation of rights.

steps.do: Write the title (under 100 characters) and description (under 5,000 characters). Put the round's tracked link in the first two lines of the description; if there are two versions of the video, use ?v=A and ?v=B. Prepare a thumbnail for a regular video and a captions file if one exists.
steps.evidence: The title and description with character counts, the link with its version label, and the thumbnail and captions files if any.

steps.do: Check every claim in the title, description and video against the product fact sheet; remove anything you cannot support.
steps.evidence: A list of the claims in the video and text, each with its fact source.

steps.do: Ask the owner the required answers: whether the video is made for kids, whether it contains realistic altered or synthetic content if YouTube Studio asks, and whether it includes paid promotion. Never guess these answers.
steps.evidence: The owner's answer to each required setting.

steps.do: Show the owner the title, description, thumbnail, settings and the planned visibility (public now or scheduled) and get a clear yes.
steps.evidence: Everything that will go live, and the owner's approval message.

steps.do: Upload once as private or unlisted, by the owner or by the agent's own browser if it is signed in and the owner said yes. Wait until processing and YouTube's checks finish, then set it to public or schedule it as approved. If the upload seems to fail, check the channel's content list before uploading again.
steps.evidence: The video's status after checks, any copyright or restriction notice, and the time it went public or the scheduled time.

steps.do: Once the video is public, open its watch URL in a signed-out or private browser window. Check the channel name, title, description and that the link opens the product. If it is scheduled, record the scheduled time and do this check after it goes public. If the link is not clickable, as can happen with Shorts, tell the owner and do not claim the video sends visitors to the site.
steps.evidence: The public video URL, the title and description as they appear, and whether the link is clickable, or the scheduled time if it is not public yet.

blockers.do: If YouTube Studio shows a different channel from the brand's, stop and ask the owner to switch to the right channel before uploading.
If the owner has not said yes to the title, description and settings, do not make the video public; show them and wait.
If YouTube flags a copyright claim during checks, keep the video private and show the owner the notice; do not publish around it.
If YouTube asks for phone verification or another identity check, tell the owner which screen needs them and wait.
If the description link is not clickable for this video, tell the owner and do not count the video as a source of site visits.

deliver_help.video_url: The public watch or Shorts URL, opened in a signed-out or private window and confirmed to play.
deliver_help.published_text: The title and description exactly as they appear on the public page.
deliver_help.visibility: 'public' or 'scheduled', with the time it went public or will go public.

C-YT-INTENT.title: Find YouTube comments asking for what the product does
C-YT-INTENT.purpose: Build a short list of recent YouTube comments where a real person asks, in their own words, for the tool, service or help the product gives, because only answering those people can turn replies into conversations.

steps.do: From the chosen buyer situation, write three to five YouTube searches, such as '{task} how to', '{category} comparison', '{problem} solution' and 'best {tool} for {situation}', using the product's words and the buyer's words. Look at results sorted by relevance as well as recent uploads, because older popular videos often still get new comments.
steps.evidence: The list of searches used and the filter applied.

steps.do: Open the top results and pick at least ten videos whose topic matches the product and whose viewers are the buyer. Read each title and description, and skip videos with comments turned off.
steps.evidence: The chosen video URLs, each with one line on why its viewers match.

steps.do: Read each video's comments sorted by newest, including the replies under them. Keep only comments that ask for a tool, service, template or help the product actually gives. General praise, jokes and questions about the video itself are not requests.
steps.evidence: Every request comment found, with the commenter's channel name and channel link, and the shortest exact quote that shows the need.

steps.do: For each request, get its own link by clicking the comment's date (the URL then contains '&lc=' and the comment ID). Note when it was posted as YouTube shows it, for example '2 weeks ago', and drop it if it is older than 30 days.
steps.evidence: Each request's comment link and posting date.

steps.do: Read the replies under each request. Drop it if the person says it is solved, if the brand already replied, or if the person asked not to be contacted. If the same person asked more than once, keep only their newest comment. Write the reason for every comment you drop.
steps.evidence: An excluded list, each item with its link and the reason.

steps.do: For each request you keep, write one line on why the product fits, citing the product fact it relies on. Keep this separate from the quote, and mark the fit 'unsure' when the comment does not say enough.
steps.evidence: Each kept request with its quote and a separate fit line marked 'fits' or 'unsure'.

steps.do: Hand over the kept requests, the excluded list and the counts. Never pad the list to reach a number; if nothing qualifies, report a real zero and suggest which searches to change next.
steps.evidence: The final list with counts of comments read, kept and excluded.

blockers.do: If no comment qualifies, report a real zero, change the searches toward the buyer's own words, and never count general viewers as buyers.
If comments are off on a video, skip it and note it; never move to private messages instead.
If a comment link does not show the comment, mark it unknown and leave it out of the list.
If the requests found ask for something the product does not do, drop them and go back to the buyer situation before searching again.
If YouTube limits or blocks your searching, stop for the day and report what you have; do not switch accounts or tools to get around the limit.

deliver_help.requests: Each kept comment: its link, the commenter's channel name and channel link, the exact quote, the posting date, and the fit line.
deliver_help.excluded: Each dropped comment with its link and the reason, for example 'already solved in replies'.
deliver_help.searches_used: The YouTube searches and filters you used, and how many videos and comments you read.

C-YT-REPLY.title: Reply to YouTube request comments with a useful answer
C-YT-REPLY.purpose: Answer each listed request in its own comment thread with real help and an honest product mention, approved by the owner, because a useful reply in the right place is what makes the commenter answer back.

steps.do: Take the request list and reopen each comment link. Confirm the comment is still visible, comments are still on, the brand has not already replied, and the person has not said it is solved or asked not to be contacted; if the owner already uses a CRM, also check it shows no earlier contact or opt-out for that person. Plan no more than ten replies in one round.
steps.evidence: The requests still open for a reply, each with its comment link, and the ones dropped with a reason.

steps.do: Draft one reply per comment. Answer the person's actual question first in one to three sentences that help even without the product. Then mention the product as one option, say plainly that you make it or work on it, and use only claims the product facts support. Keep each reply under 500 characters, and do not paste the same text under different comments.
steps.evidence: One draft per request, each with the facts it relies on.

steps.do: Add the round's tracked link only when the person asked for a tool or a link; otherwise name the product and offer to share the link. Replies with links may be held for review more often. If you test two versions, change one thing and give them ?v=A and ?v=B.
steps.evidence: Each draft marked 'with link' or 'no link', and the tracked link with its version tag where used.

steps.do: Show the owner every reply word for word, next to the comment it answers. Nothing is posted until the owner says yes to that exact text.
steps.evidence: The approved texts and the owner's approval message.

steps.do: Post each approved reply under its comment, from the agreed channel, never as a new top-level comment or on another video. The agent posts only if its browser is signed in as that channel and the owner said yes; otherwise the owner posts. Leave at least 10 minutes between replies. Press reply once; if it seems to fail, check the thread before trying again.
steps.evidence: Who posted each reply and when.

steps.do: Open each comment link in a signed-out or private window and confirm the reply shows under the right comment, as the right channel, with the approved text. Copy the reply's own link. If it does not show, mark it 'held or missing' and never post it again.
steps.evidence: The public URL of each reply, or its 'held or missing' status.

steps.do: Check each thread again after 24 and 48 hours. Draft answers to any follow-up questions and show them to the owner before posting. Do not move anyone to email or private messages unless they ask, and send no follow-up to people who did not answer.
steps.evidence: A list of who answered back, what they asked, and the approved follow-up replies.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to the exact text, do not post; show them the text and stop until they answer.
If the reply box shows a channel other than the agreed one, stop and ask the owner to switch channels or post it themselves.
If comments have been turned off, drop that request and never contact the person another way instead.
If a posted reply does not show publicly, mark it held or missing, check again after a few hours, and never post it twice.
If the person says no thanks or asks not to be contacted, stop replying to them and remove them from the round.
If YouTube blocks or limits replies from the channel, stop for the day, tell the owner, and never switch channels or accounts to get around it.

deliver_help.reply_urls: The public link of each reply that went live, opened and confirmed to show.
deliver_help.replied_text: The exact text of each reply as it appears on the public page, with the comment it answers.
deliver_help.held_or_missing: Replies that were posted but do not show publicly, or 'none'.
deliver_help.follow_ups: Who answered back after 24 and 48 hours, what they asked, and what was replied, or 'none yet'.

C-REDDIT-ACCESS.title: Confirm the Reddit account and each subreddit's rules
C-REDDIT-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which Reddit account posts, who presses publish, and what each target subreddit allows, so every reply or post stays within the rules and is not removed or banned.

steps.do: Ask the owner for the Reddit username that will post. Open its public profile and note the account age, karma and recent activity, and whether its history is only about the product.
steps.evidence: The username, profile URL, account age, karma, and a one-line note on its history.

steps.do: From the buyer situation, pick three to five subreddits where these buyers ask for help. For each, read the rules in the sidebar and the wiki, and copy the parts on self-promotion, links, private messages, minimum account age or karma, flair, required disclosure and promotion days.
steps.evidence: Each subreddit with its rules URL, the copied rule text, and the time you read it.

steps.do: Mark each subreddit 'reply with a product mention allowed', 'story post allowed', 'answers only, no product' or 'no promotion'. If the rules are unclear, draft a short message to the moderators asking what is allowed and show it to the owner; it is sent, by the owner or by the agent's signed-in browser, only after the owner says yes.
steps.evidence: Each subreddit marked with what is allowed, and any moderator question with its approval.

steps.do: Decide who publishes: the owner, or the agent's own browser if it is already signed in to that username. If nobody is signed in, the owner signs in on the official Reddit page. Never ask for a password; CAPTCHAs and checks are left to the owner.
steps.evidence: Who will publish, and confirmation that the right username is signed in.

steps.do: Create a new account only if the owner asked for one in this conversation; you may use inbox_address and inbox_latest for the verification email. Use one real account only. Never create extra accounts to get around limits, never buy or trade upvotes or karma, and never ask others to vote.
steps.evidence: The owner's request and the new username, or a note that the existing account is used.

steps.do: Check the account's past comments in the target subreddits, and, if whoever is signed in can open it, the account's inbox, for removals, moderator warnings, bans, or people asking the brand to stop. Note any thread where the brand already replied, so it is not answered twice.
steps.evidence: A list of past brand activity, removals and stop requests, or 'none found'.

steps.do: Read Reddit pages one at a time with read_page or a browser. Do not scrape in bulk or pull data through Reddit's API for business use unless the owner already has permission for that. If read_page returns little text or a login page (for example only 'Welcome to Reddit'), the page was not read: ask the owner to paste the thread text into the conversation. Never use Reddit's API and never sign in to read a page.
steps.evidence: A note of how Reddit pages will be read this round, including any thread the owner pasted because read_page met a login page.

steps.do: Agree a one-line disclosure with the owner, for example 'Disclosure: I built this.' Then confirm whoever publishes can open the comment box in each allowed subreddit.
steps.evidence: The approved disclosure line, and the subreddits where the comment box opens.

blockers.do: If a subreddit forbids promotion, leave it out of product replies and posts; never get around it with altered spelling or private messages.
If the account is too new or has too little karma for a subreddit, skip that subreddit this round and tell the owner; never farm karma or use another account.
If a CAPTCHA, verification or terms screen appears, stop and tell the owner which screen to finish, then resume on the same account.
If the account was banned or warned in a subreddit, leave that subreddit out and tell the owner.
If the round needs Reddit data beyond reading pages one at a time, wait for the owner's existing permission; never buy access or claim free business use.
If the signed-in account is not the agreed username, stop and ask the owner to switch or to post themselves.

deliver_help.username: The Reddit username that will post, with its profile URL, age and karma.
deliver_help.subreddit_rules: Each target subreddit with its rules URL and what is allowed: product mention in replies, story post, answers only, or no promotion.
deliver_help.who_publishes: 'owner' or 'agent browser', plus one line on why.
deliver_help.disclosure_line: The exact line the owner approved for saying the account is connected to the product.

C-RD-METRICS.title: Read this goal's numbers from Reddit and sales records
C-RD-METRICS.purpose: Record the numbers this goal is judged on, for the same length of time before and after the round, from the round's Reddit threads and the owner's own sales records, so rounds are compared on real people and real purchases. record_numbers lists exactly which numbers it needs.

steps.do: Confirm the username, the list of this round's post and reply URLs, the date range and the time zone. For the baseline use the same number of days just before the round; for the current reading use the round's own days.
steps.evidence: Username, the URLs measured, and the date range with time zone.

steps.do: Open each URL in a signed-out or private window and mark it 'visible', 'removed' or 'locked'. A removed reply can get no answers, so list it separately rather than hiding it.
steps.evidence: Each URL with its visibility and the time it was checked.

steps.do: Count real responses only: a qualified reply or inquiry is a different person who asks for the link, a price or a demo, asks how to use the product, or says they will try it. Upvotes, thanks without a question, and the owner's or the agent's own comments never count. Count each person once and keep the URL of each one counted.
steps.evidence: The list of counted responses, each with its URL and the person's username.

steps.do: Fill the goal's components by their exact names. 'read_requests' and 'qualified_requests' come from the search step's counts of posts read and kept; when the baseline comes before this round's search, take them from the last search log of an earlier round, or record 0 with 'no history' in source. 'eligible_requests' is the number of different request threads the round replied to. 'qualified_replies' and 'qualified_inquiries' are the people counted in the step before; inquiries may also include private messages or emails the owner reports, if they mention Reddit.
steps.evidence: Each component name with its number and a one-line note on how it was counted.

steps.do: For a purchase goal, count 'external_purchases' only from the round's sale counter in tracking or the owner's payment records, within the date range. Leave out the owner's or team's own test payments and refunded orders, and say plainly when a sale cannot be tied to Reddit.
steps.evidence: Each purchase counted with its source and date, and the ones left out with the reason.

steps.do: Add website visits only if the owner already has a source for them, such as the tracked link or site analytics. If the owner already uses a CRM, check it for the same people; never turn a silent reader into a counted lead.
steps.evidence: Each extra figure names its source, and unknown links between Reddit and the result are stated.

steps.do: Pass the goal's exact component names to record_numbers with the source of each. If there is no history, record 0 and say in source that there is no history. Never estimate a missing number; leave it out and name it as missing.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers entry with every component, its source, and any missing number named.

blockers.do: If a reply or post was removed, keep its URL and the removal reason, count it as removed, and never post it again; if the subreddit offers a normal way to appeal, draft a short appeal and show it to the owner before anything is sent.

If there is no sale counter and no payment record to read, record no purchases for this round, say there is no source, and ask the owner to add the tracking sale counter to the page shown after payment.
If there is no history for these numbers, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline.
If you cannot tell whether a response comes from a real prospect or from the owner's side, leave it out and say so.
If the replies or posts are less than 24 hours old, report the numbers as early and read them again later.

deliver_help.numbers: Each of the goal's component names with its value exactly as counted, for example 'qualified_replies: 3'.
deliver_help.where_read: For each number, the thread URLs, sales record or tracked link it came from, and the time it was read.
deliver_help.date_range: The first and last day measured, with the time zone, for example '2026-11-20 to 2026-11-22, Asia/Taipei'.

C-RD-INTENT.title: Find recent Reddit posts from people who need the product
C-RD-INTENT.purpose: Read recent posts in the allowed subreddits and keep only those where a real person asks for what the product does, because the share of matching requests and the replies that follow depend on picking the right posts.

steps.do: For each subreddit marked as allowed, write three to five searches from the buyer's own words, such as the problem in plain words, 'alternative to {category}', 'recommend {tool}' and 'looking for {solution}'. Search inside the subreddit, sorted by new, limited to the past month.
steps.evidence: Each subreddit with the searches and the time filter used.

steps.do: Open each result and read the full post and its comments; if read_page returns a login page or little text, ask the owner to paste the thread text, as agreed in the account step. Note what the person uses now, their role, and whether the question is already solved (a 'Solved' flair, an edit by the poster, or an accepted answer). Count every post you open as read, including the ones you drop later, so the share of matching posts is honest.
steps.evidence: A log of every post read, with its URL, the poster's username and a one-line summary, and the total number of posts read.

steps.do: Drop job posts, self-promotion, posts from people who are not the buyer, deleted or removed posts, locked or archived posts, solved questions, and posts older than 30 days. Write the reason for each one.
steps.evidence: An excluded list, each with its URL and reason.

steps.do: For each post you keep, copy the shortest exact quote that shows the need. Separately, write one line on why the product fits, citing the product fact it relies on, and mark it 'unsure' when the post does not say enough.
steps.evidence: Each kept post with its quote and a separate fit line marked 'fits' or 'unsure'.

steps.do: Check each kept post for an earlier reply from the brand's account and drop it if one exists. Count each person once even if they posted twice.
steps.evidence: The kept list after removing duplicates and threads the brand already answered.

steps.do: Hand over the kept posts, the excluded list and the counts, and note the last post read in each search so the next round continues from there. Never pad the list to reach a number; if nothing qualifies, report a real zero and say which searches or subreddits to change next.
steps.evidence: The final list with counts of posts read, kept and excluded, and where each search stopped.

blockers.do: If a subreddit forbids promotion, do not collect posts there for product replies; never move the conversation to private messages to get around it.
If a post is solved, locked, archived or older than 30 days, drop it and write the reason; never follow up on it to sell.
If nothing qualifies, report a real zero, change the searches toward the buyer's own words or try another allowed subreddit, and never invent requests.
If the posts found ask for something the product does not do, drop them and go back to the buyer situation before searching again.
If you would need bulk data or Reddit's API to continue, stop at what you have read page by page and wait for the owner's existing permission.

C-RD-INTENT.title_zh: Reddit子版需求與替代方案搜尋

deliver_help.qualified_posts: Each kept post: its URL, subreddit, poster's username, the exact quote, the posting date, and the fit line.
deliver_help.excluded: Each dropped post with its URL and the reason, for example 'solved by another commenter'.
deliver_help.posts_read: The total number of posts opened and read this round, kept or not.
deliver_help.searches_used: The subreddits, searches and time filters you used.

C-RD-REPLY.title: Reply in Reddit threads with a useful, disclosed answer
C-RD-REPLY.purpose: Answer each listed request in its own thread with real help and an honest product mention that the subreddit's rules allow and the owner approved, because a useful reply is what makes the poster answer back or try the product.

steps.do: Reopen each kept thread. Confirm it is not locked, archived or removed, is not solved since, the brand has not replied, the poster has not asked people to stop, and the subreddit's rules still allow a product mention; if the owner already uses a CRM, also check it shows no earlier contact or opt-out for that person. Plan no more than three replies in one subreddit per day.
steps.evidence: The threads still open for a reply, each with its URL and the rule that allows it, and the ones dropped with a reason.

steps.do: Draft one reply per thread. Answer the poster's actual question first with specific help that works even without the product. Then mention the product as one option, with the approved disclosure line, using only claims the product facts support. Write like a person in that subreddit, not like an ad, usually under 800 characters, and never reuse the same text in two threads.
steps.evidence: One draft per thread, each with the facts it relies on and the disclosure line.

steps.do: Add the round's tracked link only if the subreddit allows links and the poster asked for a tool or a link; otherwise name the product without a link. If you test two versions, change one thing and give them ?v=A and ?v=B.
steps.evidence: Each draft marked 'with link' or 'no link', and the tracked link with its version tag where used.

steps.do: Show the owner every reply word for word, next to the thread it answers and the rule that allows it. Nothing is posted until the owner says yes to that exact text.
steps.evidence: The approved texts and the owner's approval message.

steps.do: Post each approved reply in its thread, under the post or the comment that asked, from the agreed username. The agent posts only if its browser is signed in to that account and the owner said yes; otherwise the owner posts. Leave at least 30 minutes between replies, never send it as a private message unless the poster asked for one, and press reply once.
steps.evidence: Who posted each reply and when.

steps.do: Open each reply's link in a signed-out or private window to confirm it shows publicly, because a removed comment can still look normal to its author. If it does not show, record it as removed with any reason given, and never post it again.
steps.evidence: The public URL of each reply, or its 'removed' status with the reason.

steps.do: Plan when to look at each thread again: about 24 and 48 hours after each reply, during the observation window. With the plan, write how answers are handled then: draft replies to follow-up questions and show them to the owner before posting; send no cold private messages and no follow-up to people who did not answer. Hand back this plan as follow_ups; do not wait for the checks before submitting the step.
steps.evidence: Each thread with the times to look again, and the rule for answering follow-ups.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to the exact text, do not post; show them the text and stop until they answer.
If the rules forbid a product mention, either post a helpful answer with no product mention, if the owner wants that, or skip the thread; never move to private messages to get around it.

If a reply is removed, keep its URL and the reason, do not repost or reword it to slip past the filter, and if the subreddit offers a normal way to appeal, draft a short appeal and show it to the owner before anything is sent.
If the thread is solved, locked or archived, drop it and never follow up on it to sell.
If the poster says no thanks or asks not to be contacted, stop replying to them and remove them from the round.
If the signed-in account is not the agreed username, stop and ask the owner to switch or to post themselves.

deliver_help.reply_urls: The public link of each reply that went live, opened signed out and confirmed to show.
deliver_help.replied_text: The exact text of each reply as it appears publicly, with the thread it answers.
deliver_help.removed_or_hidden: Replies that were removed or do not show publicly, with any reason given, or 'none'.
deliver_help.follow_ups: The plan for looking again: each thread URL with the times to check it (about 24 and 48 hours after the reply), and the rule that follow-up answers are shown to the owner before posting.

C-RD-STORY.title: Post a true founder story in a subreddit that allows it
C-RD-STORY.purpose: Post one honest founder story in a community whose rules allow it, so readers who share the problem learn something useful and some of them ask about the product.

steps.do: Find one to three subreddits where the buyer spends time and where the rules allow founder stories or self-promotion. Read each rules page, sidebar, wiki and pinned posts. Note any required flair, set promotion days, a weekly thread to use instead, or a minimum account age or karma. Pick the single best fit for this round.
steps.evidence: Each subreddit with its rules URL, the exact rule that allows this post, any flair or account requirement, and the one chosen.

steps.do: Confirm with the owner which real Reddit account will post. Use one real account only, never a second or fake one. The owner signs in themselves. Check that the account meets the subreddit's age and karma rules.
steps.evidence: The username, and whether it meets each subreddit's requirements.

steps.do: Collect the true story from the owner: what happened, what went wrong, what they learned, and any numbers they can show. If there is no proof of revenue or growth figures, leave those figures out.
steps.evidence: The story outline with each fact and number marked with its source, or marked as left out.

steps.do: Write the post in the owner's voice. Title under 300 characters, honest and without clickbait. Open with the lesson that helps the reader, and say clearly 'I'm the founder of ...'. Do not copy a popular post and never pose as an outside user.
steps.evidence: The title and body draft, with the line that states the founder's relationship to the product.

steps.do: Add a link only if the rules allow links. Use the round's tracked link, with ?v=A or ?v=B if there are two versions, and open it once to confirm it loads.
steps.evidence: The link and its version label, or a note that the rules do not allow links.

steps.do: Show the owner the title, body, chosen subreddit and flair word for word, and get a clear yes.
steps.evidence: The approved post and the owner's approval message.

steps.do: Post it once, in one subreddit, with the right flair. The owner posts it, or the agent's own browser does if it is signed in and the owner said yes.
steps.evidence: Who posted it, the subreddit, and the time.

steps.do: After 10 minutes, open the post's public URL in a signed-out or private browser window and confirm it is visible. If it was removed, record the reason given. Do not repost it, and do not post the same story in any other subreddit this round.
steps.evidence: The public URL and whether it is visible or removed, with any removal reason.

steps.do: For the next 48 hours, read the comments. Draft short answers to real questions for the owner to approve, and do not argue with critics.
steps.evidence: The comments that asked about the product, with their URLs and the approved answers.

blockers.do: If a subreddit's rules do not allow this kind of post, leave it out; never reword the post or switch to DMs to get around the rule.
If the post is removed, record the reason and do not repost; if the rules offer a way to appeal, draft a short note to the moderators for the owner to approve.
If the account does not meet the age or karma rule, tell the owner and choose another subreddit; never use another account.
If the owner has not said yes to this exact post, do not publish; show it to them and wait.
If the owner cannot confirm the facts of the story, do not post it; ask them for one real event to build it on.

C-RD-STORY.title_zh: Reddit創辦人故事與版規適配

deliver_help.post_url: The public URL of the live post, opened in a signed-out or private window.
deliver_help.published_text: The title and body exactly as they appear on the live post.
deliver_help.subreddit_rules: The subreddit, its rules URL, and the rule that allows this post.

C-LINKEDIN-ACCESS.title: Confirm the LinkedIn identity, sign-in, and who does what
C-LINKEDIN-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which LinkedIn profile or Company Page this goal works under, who signs in and publishes, and how research is done within LinkedIn's rules, so the round can run without fake accounts, blocked searches, or the owner being stopped halfway.

steps.do: Ask the owner which LinkedIn identity this goal uses: their personal profile, the Company Page, or both. Get the public URL of each and open it with read_page to confirm it exists and matches the brand. Use the existing profile or Page; do not create a second one.
steps.evidence: The profile and Page URLs, the names shown on them, and the owner's confirmation that they are theirs.

steps.do: If the goal posts as the Company Page, ask the owner to confirm they are an admin of that Page who can post and see its analytics. If they are not, research and drafting go on, and only posting as the Page waits until an existing admin adds them.
steps.evidence: The owner's role on the Page as they stated it or as shown in their screenshot, or a note that the role is missing.

steps.do: The owner signs in to LinkedIn themselves, on the official LinkedIn sign-in screen or their company's single sign-on, and completes any verification code, identity check, or terms screen. Never ask for a password, never copy browser cookies, and never install extensions or tools that pull data from LinkedIn.
steps.evidence: A note of which account the owner is signed in as, and the time it was checked.

steps.do: Agree who does each kind of work. LinkedIn forbids scraping and bots on its site, so the signed-in work inside LinkedIn is done by the owner by hand: searching, posting, sending messages, and opening analytics. The agent drafts, reads single public pages with read_page, checks company websites, and works from the owner's screenshots, pasted URLs, or LinkedIn's own data export. The agent posts or sends only through an official LinkedIn tool the owner has already set up.
steps.evidence: A short plan naming 'owner' or 'agent' for searching, publishing, messaging, and reading numbers, with the route for each.

steps.do: Test the plan once. If the goal needs people research, ask the owner to run one sample search on LinkedIn, such as a job title plus an industry, and send a screenshot of the results. Then use read_page on one public company page or profile URL to see what loads without sign-in.
steps.evidence: The sample search terms, what the screenshot and the public page showed, and the exact text of any limit message.

steps.do: If a sign-in wall or search limit appears, do not switch to another account, create a new one, or try any workaround. Keep the owner's searches few and specific, wait for the limit to clear, or move the research to public company websites and team pages.
steps.evidence: The chosen route for research, with the reason, or a note that no limit appeared.

steps.do: Write down the record rules for the rest of the round: every search keeps its exact terms, date, and URL; an email is recorded only if the person or their company published it, with the source URL, otherwise it stays empty; a job title is a hint, not proof of buying power; a public email is not permission to send marketing, so source, consent, and opt-outs are kept in separate columns of this round's list, or in that tool if the owner already uses a CRM.
steps.evidence: The rules as written, ready for the research and outreach steps.

blockers.do: If a verification code, identity check, or terms screen appears, stop and tell the owner which screen needs them; never enter codes or accept terms for them.
If the owner is not an admin of the Company Page, continue research and drafts, and ask the owner to have an existing admin add them before anything is posted as the Page.
If the signed-in account is not the agreed profile, stop and ask the owner to switch accounts or to do the work on their own device.

If a route would need scraping, bulk extraction, a browser extension, or the agent clicking through LinkedIn while signed in, do not use it; ask the owner to do it by hand or to send LinkedIn's own data export.
If LinkedIn shows a sign-in wall or a search limit, never use or create another account; keep the owner's searches small or research on public company websites.
If LinkedIn shows a warning or restriction on the account, stop all outreach and automation, save the notice word for word with its official link, and tell the owner.

deliver_help.linkedin_identity: The URL of the personal profile and/or Company Page this goal uses, opened and confirmed to exist. Example: 'https://www.linkedin.com/company/yourbrand/'.
deliver_help.page_admin_role: Whether the owner can post as the Company Page, as they stated or as seen, or 'not needed' if the goal uses only the personal profile.
deliver_help.who_does_what: For searching, publishing, messaging, and reading numbers: 'owner' or 'agent', with the route for each in one line.
deliver_help.research_access: What the sample search showed, any limit message word for word, and the research route chosen.
deliver_help.record_rules: The written rules for searches, emails, job titles, and consent that the research and outreach steps will follow.

C-LI-METRICS.title: Read this goal's numbers on LinkedIn
C-LI-METRICS.purpose: Record the exact numbers this goal is judged on, for one LinkedIn identity and one fixed date range, so each round is compared with the last on real counts. record_numbers lists exactly which numbers it needs.

steps.do: Confirm what you are measuring: the goal's metric component names exactly as record_numbers lists them, the one LinkedIn identity (personal profile or Company Page, never both mixed), and the date range with its time zone. The range is the goal's observation window and the same length as the baseline.
steps.evidence: The component names, the profile or Page URL, and the date range with time zone.

steps.do: Find where each of this goal's components lives. Follower totals and post numbers are in the profile's or Page's analytics, which the owner opens and sends as a screenshot or LinkedIn's own export. Inquiries come from comments on the round's posts (read public posts with read_page), LinkedIn messages the owner shares, and any email or form the owner already receives. Meetings come from the owner's calendar or booking tool; roles and emails from the round's reviewed lists.
steps.evidence: A list of each component with the screenshot, export, page, or list it will be read from.

steps.do: Count only the components this goal lists, by their plain meaning. followers: the follower total, read as close to the end of the date range as possible. qualified_inquiries: different people in the range who asked about buying or using the product and fit the buyer definition. confirmed_meetings: demos where the prospect accepted an invite or confirmed a date and time in writing. reviewed_people or reviewed_roles: every unique person checked this round, rejected ones included. verified_public_emails: people whose own business email was published by them or their company, with a source URL. qualified_roles: people whose confirmed current role matches the buyer definition.
steps.evidence: Each count, with the list of items behind it (URLs or names) so it can be checked.

steps.do: Count each person once. Leave out the owner, their team, the agent, test accounts, and bots. For rate goals, never drop rejected people from the reviewed total to lift the rate; if nobody was reviewed, record 0 and say so.
steps.evidence: A note of who was left out and why, and the reviewed total used.

steps.do: Read supporting numbers where LinkedIn or tracking shows them: impressions and reactions from the post's analytics, and clicks per version (?v=A, ?v=B) from tracking. Write 'not shown' for anything not displayed. Treat a difference based on fewer than 20 clicks or inquiries per version as a hint, not a result, and do not credit a change across months to the content alone.
steps.evidence: The supporting numbers as displayed, with 'not shown' where missing and a note on sample size.

steps.do: Add sales only if the owner already has payment records or the round's sale counter. Do not count the owner's own test payments. Where you cannot tell which post or conversation led to a sale, say so plainly.
steps.evidence: Any sales figure with its source, or a note that there is none.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with each of this goal's components under its exact name, and a source that says where and when you read it. For a rate goal, pass both components separately, not the rate. If there is no history for a number, record 0 and say in the source that there is no history. Never estimate a number that you could not read.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call as sent, with every component name, value, and source.

blockers.do: If the analytics cannot be opened, ask the owner for a screenshot or LinkedIn's own export showing the numbers this goal needs, for the agreed identity and date range.
If there is no history for a number, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; this round then sets the baseline.
If the screenshot or screen shows a different profile or Page from the agreed one, do not use those numbers and ask again.
If you cannot tell whether a person fits the buyer definition, list them as unclear, do not count them, and ask the owner to decide.
If the post or outreach is less than 24 hours old, report the numbers as early and read them again at the end of the range.

deliver_help.numbers: Each metric component by its exact name with its value, as passed to record_numbers. Example: 'qualified_roles: 14, reviewed_roles: 25'.
deliver_help.where_read: For each number, the screen, export, calendar, or list it came from and the time you read it.
deliver_help.date_range: The start and end of the measured range, with time zone.

C-LI-POST.title: Publish one approved LinkedIn post and confirm it
C-LI-POST.purpose: Publish the approved post once, under the agreed profile or Company Page, with the round's tracked link, and hand back its public URL, because the post must be live and exactly as approved before followers or inquiries can be measured.

steps.do: Confirm the author is the identity agreed in the access step: the personal profile or the Company Page. Read its last 10 posts, with read_page if they are public or from the owner's screenshot, so this one does not repeat the same content or link.
steps.evidence: The profile or Page URL, and a note on the recent posts you checked.

steps.do: Read the final text from the writing step. Check it is under 3,000 characters and that the hook sits in the first two lines, since LinkedIn cuts longer posts off with a 'see more'. Check every claim against the product facts.
steps.evidence: The final text, its character count, and a note that each claim matches a product fact.

steps.do: Use the round's tracked link from tracking, with ?v=A, ?v=B when there are several versions. Open each link and check it forwards to the product page. If there is an image or PDF, check it reads clearly on a phone and that its text matches the product facts.
steps.evidence: Each tracked link with its version label, confirmation it opened the product page, and any media file.

steps.do: Show the owner the exact text, link, media, and the author it will be posted as, for each version, and get a clear yes. If the plan has two versions, follow its order and spacing; if it gives none, publish them at least 48 hours apart at the same time of day.
steps.evidence: The owner's approval message for each version, the author named in it, and the planned publish times.

steps.do: The owner pastes the approved text, link, and media into LinkedIn's post box, checks the preview and the selected author match, and presses Post once. The agent posts itself only through an official LinkedIn posting tool the owner has already set up, never by clicking through the site. If posting as the Page fails, do not post from another Page or the personal profile instead.
steps.evidence: Who posted and how, when, and confirmation that the preview matched the approved text.

steps.do: Get the post's public URL from the owner or the posting tool, open it with read_page, and check the full text, author name, link, and media. If publishing seemed to fail, ask the owner to check the profile or Page activity before trying again so nothing is posted twice.
steps.evidence: The public URL, the text as it appears there, and the author name shown.

steps.do: After 24 hours, read the post's comments again and list those that ask about the product, with their URLs, for the measuring step. Draft any replies and show them to the owner word for word; nothing is posted without their yes, and the owner posts it.
steps.evidence: The list of product questions in the comments with URLs, and any draft replies awaiting approval.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to this exact text, do not publish; show them the text and stop until they answer.
If the signed-in account or the author selected in the post box is not the agreed profile or Page, stop and ask the owner to switch before posting.
If the account cannot post as the Company Page, do not post elsewhere instead; ask the owner to get admin access from an existing admin.
If the agent has no official LinkedIn posting tool, give the owner the final text, link, and media to paste, and ask them to send back the post URL.
If the post does not show after publishing, check the activity again after a few minutes before any retry, and never post the same text twice.
If the tracked link does not open the product page, stop before publishing and fix the link with the owner.

deliver_help.post_url: The public link to the live post, opened and confirmed to load. Example: 'https://www.linkedin.com/posts/...'.
deliver_help.published_text: The full text exactly as it appears on the live post, copied from the public page.
deliver_help.posted_as: The name and URL of the profile or Company Page shown as the author.
deliver_help.tracked_link: The tracked link used in this post, including its ?v= label if there are versions.

C-LI-ROLES.title: Find people in the right buyer role on LinkedIn
