C-LI-ROLES.purpose: Build a checked list of real people whose current role matches the buyer, each with evidence of need, so content and outreach reach people who can use or approve the product.

steps.do: Write the buyer definition from the earlier segment and motive steps: the problem, industry, company size, and region. Name two kinds of role: the person who would use the product and the person likely to approve the purchase. Add exclusion rules such as competitors, existing customers, students, and recruiters.
steps.evidence: The buyer definition with user roles, approver roles, and exclusion rules.

steps.do: Write three to five searches in the form 'job function + industry + buying trigger' or 'company + department', using the buyer's own words from the quotes, and save each one's exact terms and date. The owner runs them in LinkedIn by hand; the agent runs the same terms in its own web search and on company websites.
steps.evidence: A search log with terms, date, and where each was run: LinkedIn by the owner, web search, or a company site.

steps.do: Collect candidates only by allowed routes: profile URLs or screenshots the owner sends from their own searches, a LinkedIn export the owner provides, single public pages read with read_page, and public company team pages. No scraping tools, no bulk extraction, no extra accounts, and no agent browsing inside LinkedIn while signed in. Remove duplicates by profile URL as you go and stop at 25 unique people this round.
steps.evidence: A deduplicated candidate list with each person's original profile URL and how they were found.

steps.do: For each candidate, confirm the current role from a public page or the owner's screenshot: job title, company, the company's website domain, and the date checked. Where possible, check the company's own site lists them. If the current job cannot be confirmed, mark the person 'unknown', not qualified.
steps.evidence: For each person: title, company, domain, profile URL, date checked, and confirmed or unknown.

steps.do: Look for public evidence of need: the person's own posts, the company website, job ads, or news that show the problem or a buying trigger. Quote it with its URL and date. A job title alone does not prove budget or buying power; mark buying power as 'guess' until the person says so.
steps.evidence: For each qualified person, at least one quote or fact with URL and date, or 'no need evidence found'.

steps.do: Sort every reviewed person into qualified, excluded, or unknown, with a one-line reason each. Qualified means the current role is confirmed and matches the buyer definition. The reviewed total is every unique person checked, rejected and unknown ones included.
steps.evidence: Three lists with reasons, and the counts of qualified people and of everyone reviewed.

steps.do: Rank qualified people with need evidence first, and keep no more than three per company on the final list, holding the rest as reserves. Do not message, connect with, or email anyone in this step; contact only happens in a later step the owner approves.
steps.evidence: The ranked final list with reserves marked, and a note that no one was contacted.

blockers.do: If there is no clear buyer definition from the earlier steps, go back to the segment step before searching.
If a route would need scraping or bulk extraction, do not use it; ask the owner to run the search by hand or provide LinkedIn's own export.
If LinkedIn shows a sign-in wall or search limit, never use or create another account; keep the owner's searches small or switch to public company team pages.
If a title does not show whether the person uses or approves this kind of product, mark the person 'unknown' and do not count them as qualified.
If no public evidence of need turns up, keep the person only if the role matches, mark need as 'not found', and do not invent a reason.
If LinkedIn shows a warning or restriction, stop searching, save the notice word for word, and tell the owner.

C-LI-ROLES.title_zh: LinkedIn依公司與需求找買方角色

deliver_help.qualified_people: Each qualified person: name, profile URL, current title, company and domain, date checked, and the need evidence with its URL.
deliver_help.excluded_people: Each excluded or unknown person with their profile URL and the one-line reason.
deliver_help.search_log: Each search's exact terms, date, and where it was run.
deliver_help.review_counts: How many people were reviewed in total and how many were qualified. Example: 'reviewed 25, qualified 14'.

C-LI-EMAIL.title: Find public business emails for LinkedIn leads
C-LI-EMAIL.purpose: For each qualified LinkedIn lead, find a business email that the person or their company published, with its source, so the owner has real, checkable ways to reach them and the share of leads with a verified email goes up.

steps.do: Start from the qualified list from the role step. For each person, note the profile URL, current company, and the company website domain. If the person has left that company or the role no longer matches, move them to the no-email list with the reason. Never guess an address from a pattern such as first.last@company.
steps.evidence: The list of people to check, each with profile URL and company domain.

steps.do: Ask the owner to open each person's Contact info on LinkedIn, one at a time, and copy any email shown with the profile URL and the date. The agent does not open it itself. Many people show an email there only to their connections, so 'not shown' is a normal result.
steps.evidence: For each person, the email exactly as shown with its source and date, or 'not shown'.

steps.do: If LinkedIn shows none, use web search and read_page on the company's official website: team, about, author, or contact pages, and any personal website linked from the profile. Copy any email exactly with its URL and the date.
steps.evidence: For each person still missing an email, the pages checked and any email found with its URL.

steps.do: Check each address belongs to that person: their name is in it, or the page ties it to them. Shared inboxes such as info@, support@, sales@, or press@ are recorded as company contacts, not as the person's email.
steps.evidence: Each email marked 'personal' or 'shared inbox', with the reason.

steps.do: Mark each person as verified (their own address, shown by them on LinkedIn or published by them or their company, source saved), company inbox only, or none found with the email left empty. Do not buy lists, use email-guessing tools, or use data brokers.
steps.evidence: Every reviewed person with one of the three statuses.

steps.do: Record, for each email, where it was published and what for (for example 'for business inquiries'). A public email is not consent to receive marketing; mark consent as unknown and note any request not to be contacted. Keep this in the round's list, or in that tool if the owner already uses a CRM.
steps.evidence: For each email: source URL, stated purpose, consent 'unknown', and any opt-out noted.

steps.do: Count everyone reviewed and everyone verified. Send nothing in this step; any later email must be personal, say how the owner is connected to the product, offer an easy opt-out, follow anti-spam law, and be approved by the owner first.
steps.evidence: The reviewed and verified counts, and a note that no email was sent.

blockers.do: If the role step produced no qualified people, go back to it before looking for emails.
If neither LinkedIn nor the company site shows an email, leave it empty and mark the person 'none found'; never guess an address.
If only info@ or similar is published, record it as a company contact and do not count it as the person's verified email.
If the email's page does not clearly tie it to this person at this company, do not count it and note why.
If finding emails would need scraping or an email-guessing tool, do not use it; check pages one by one or ask the owner.
If LinkedIn shows a warning or restriction, stop opening profiles, save the notice word for word, and tell the owner.

C-LI-EMAIL.title_zh: LinkedIn候選人的公開商務Email核對

deliver_help.verified_emails: Each verified person: name, profile URL, email exactly as published, source URL, date found, and stated purpose.
deliver_help.no_email_list: Each person with only a company inbox or no email, with the pages checked, plus anyone dropped because their role or company changed, with the reason.
deliver_help.review_counts: How many people were reviewed and how many have a verified email. Example: 'reviewed 14, verified 6'.

C-LI-INBOUND.title: Reply to existing LinkedIn conversations and book demos
C-LI-INBOUND.purpose: Answer people who already wrote to the owner on LinkedIn, solve their question with true product facts, and offer a demo they can confirm, because a prompt, honest reply to an interested person is the shortest path to a confirmed meeting.

steps.do: Ask the owner to share the conversations where the other person reached out or asked something: LinkedIn messages as pasted text or screenshots, comments on the owner's posts (read public ones with read_page), and replies to earlier approved messages. A connection, a like, or a job title is not an invitation to message someone.
steps.evidence: A list of conversations with link or location, the person's name, the date of their last message, and their exact words.

steps.do: Reread each whole thread. Skip anyone who said no or asked not to be contacted, anyone whose question the owner already answered, and anyone whose last message from the owner is still unanswered.
steps.evidence: The conversations to answer, and the skipped ones with the reason for each.

steps.do: Draft one reply per conversation, under 120 words. Answer their question first using only product facts, say the owner makes or sells the product, and offer one next step: a demo with two or three specific time slots or the owner's booking link. Do not move them to email unless they asked.
steps.evidence: Each draft reply with the product facts it relies on.

steps.do: Show the owner every draft word for word and get a clear yes for each one. Change only what the owner asks.
steps.evidence: The approved text of each reply and the owner's approval message.

steps.do: The owner sends each approved reply once, in the same thread, after checking the name and thread. The agent sends only through an official LinkedIn tool the owner has already set up, never by clicking through the site. If sending seems stuck, check the thread before trying again so nothing is sent twice.
steps.evidence: For each reply, the thread, who sent it, the time, and the text as it shows in the thread.

steps.do: When someone picks a time, the owner sends the calendar invite. Count a meeting as confirmed only when the person accepts the invite or confirms the date and time in writing.
steps.evidence: For each meeting: the person, date and time, and how it was confirmed.

steps.do: If there is no answer after three business days, draft at most one short follow-up, get the owner's yes, and have it sent in the same thread. After that, stop. Mark each conversation: booked, confirmed, declined, asked to stop, or no reply; if the owner already uses a CRM, ask them to record these there.
steps.evidence: The status of every conversation, and any follow-ups sent with their time.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to a reply's exact text, do not send it; show it to them and wait.
If the person never wrote to the owner or asked for help, do not message them in this step; leave them out.
If the person said no or asked not to be contacted, send nothing and mark the conversation 'asked to stop'.
If the agent has no official LinkedIn tool for messages, give the owner the approved texts and the threads to reply in, and ask them to confirm when each is sent.
If the owner has no booking link or free times, ask them for two or three time slots before drafting the reply.
If LinkedIn shows a warning or message limit, stop sending, save the notice word for word, and tell the owner.

deliver_help.replies_sent: Each reply sent: thread link, person's name, time sent, and the text as it shows in the thread.
deliver_help.confirmed_meetings_list: Each confirmed demo: person, date and time, and how they confirmed it (invite accepted or written yes).
deliver_help.conversation_status: Every conversation with its status, including skipped ones and the reason.

C-PRODUCTHUNT-ACCESS.title: Confirm the Product Hunt account and who acts on it
C-PRODUCTHUNT-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which real Product Hunt maker account the owner uses, whether the product already has a page, and who presses publish, so research, the launch and replies all run under the right account without stopping halfway.

steps.do: Ask the owner for the URL of their own Product Hunt profile and the product's website. Open the profile with read_page or your browser and confirm it exists, shows a real name, and is the owner's. Product Hunt accounts are for real people: use the owner's one personal account, and never create extra or brand-only accounts to act on Product Hunt.
steps.evidence: The profile URL, the name and handle shown on it, and the owner's confirmation that it is theirs.

steps.do: Search Product Hunt for the product's name and its website domain. If a page for this product already exists, open it and check whether the owner is listed as a maker. Plan to use that page; do not plan a second page for the same product.
steps.evidence: The URL of any existing product page with its listed makers, or a note that a search on the name and the domain found none.

steps.do: Decide who will press publish on Product Hunt: the owner on their own device, or your browser if it is already signed in to the owner's account and the owner agrees. If nobody is signed in, the owner signs in themselves on the official Product Hunt sign-in screen. Never ask for a password. If this goal only researches makers and posts nothing, write 'nobody, research only' and skip sign-in.
steps.evidence: Who will publish, how the owner signed in, and the handle shown after sign-in, or a note that this goal posts nothing.

steps.do: Create a new Product Hunt account only if the owner has none, this goal includes a launch or replies, and the owner asks for one in this conversation. The account must be in the owner's real name. If the owner agrees to sign up with the address from inbox_address, read the verification code with inbox_latest; otherwise the owner reads the code from their own email. Any terms screen or identity check is done by the owner.
steps.evidence: The new profile URL and the owner's request, or a note that the existing account is used.

steps.do: Read Product Hunt's current help pages on launching and community rules, and write down in three to six short lines what is not allowed. In every case: never buy votes, never trade votes, never use extra accounts, and never ask people to upvote; ask for feedback instead.
steps.evidence: A short list of the current rules with the help page URLs they came from.

steps.do: Settle how you will read Product Hunt data. Read public pages one at a time with read_page or your browser; do not bulk-download pages or use scraping tools. Do not use the Product Hunt API as a free lead list; its terms ask for permission before commercial use, so use it only if the owner already has that permission in writing. Profiles do not reliably show an email address, so any business email must later come from the maker's own public website, never from a guess built on a username.
steps.evidence: A one-line note on how data will be read, whether the owner has written API permission, and that emails will only come from makers' own websites.

steps.do: If this goal includes a launch or replies, confirm with the agreed account signed in that whoever publishes can open the screen for submitting a product and can post a comment. Do not submit or post anything in this step. If the goal only researches makers, write 'not needed'.
steps.evidence: Confirmation that the submit screen and the comment box open for the agreed account, with the time checked, or 'not needed'.

blockers.do: If the owner has no Product Hunt account and this goal only researches makers, carry on without one; if it includes a launch or replies, ask whether they want one in their real name and create it only on a clear yes.
If the signed-in account is not the owner's agreed profile, stop and ask the owner to switch accounts or to act on their own device.
If the product already has a page that lists other people as makers, do not create a new one; ask the owner to request maker access for that page through Product Hunt's help pages.
If a verification screen, terms screen or identity check appears, stop and tell the owner which screen and which button; never accept terms for them.
If the owner has no written API permission, read public pages one at a time instead and say so in the hand-back.
If your browser is not signed in to the owner's account, set who_publishes to 'owner' and plan to hand them exact text to paste.

C-PRODUCTHUNT-ACCESS.title_zh: 準備Product Hunt帳號、登入與授權

deliver_help.account_handle: The Product Hunt handle of the owner's own maker account, or 'none' if this goal only researches makers and the owner has no account. Example: '@janedoe'.
deliver_help.profile_url: The public URL of that profile, opened and confirmed to exist, or 'none' with the reason.
deliver_help.existing_product_page: The URL of the product's existing Product Hunt page and whether the owner is a listed maker, or 'none found' with the searches you ran.
deliver_help.who_publishes: 'owner', 'agent browser' or 'nobody, research only', plus one line on why.

C-PH-MAKERS.title: Find Product Hunt makers who fit the product
C-PH-MAKERS.purpose: Build a short, sourced list of real makers whose recent products and public words show a need the product meets, because only checked, well-fitting makers count toward the goal's main number and give later steps someone worth reaching.

steps.do: From the buyer groups and the strongest motive chosen earlier, write who a fitting maker is in two or three lines: the kind of product they launched, how recently (for example, in the last 90 days), and the situation that would make them need this product. Add a one-line guess to test, such as 'makers of B2B tools launched in the last 90 days need X because Y'. Also write who to leave out: competitors, the owner's own products, and people who say they do not want contact.
steps.evidence: The fit definition, the one-line guess, and the leave-out rules.

steps.do: Pick three to five searches: the product category, two or three known alternatives, and the job the buyer is trying to get done. Open Product Hunt search and topic pages for each with read_page or your browser, one page at a time.
steps.evidence: Each search or topic page URL you opened, and the date.

steps.do: From those pages, open each product that matches the fit definition and launched within the chosen time. Record the product page URL, the launch date, the product website, and the people listed as makers. The hunter who posted a product is not its owner unless they are also listed as a maker.
steps.evidence: One row per product with its page URL, launch date, website and maker names.

steps.do: For each maker, open their Product Hunt profile and the product website. Confirm they built or run the product and that the site is still live. Keep one row per company: if several makers run the same company, put them in one row and mark the one whose role fits best as the contact. Review at least 20 rows and stop at 50 per round, so each one gets a real check.
steps.evidence: A list of distinct rows reviewed, one per company, each with the makers' profile URLs, roles, company and a note that the site loads.

steps.do: For each maker, look for a public sign of need that the product meets: a line in their launch comments, a public post asking for help, a job post, or a roadmap item. Copy the exact words with the URL and date. A recent launch on its own is not a need and not a sign they will pay.
steps.evidence: For each maker, either a quoted need with URL and date, or 'no need found'.

steps.do: Keep what you saw separate from what you infer. Write the observed need in one field and your reason for fit in another. Mark a maker 'qualified' only when the fit rests on a quoted need or a clear, sourced fact about their situation.
steps.evidence: Each maker has an observed-need field and a separate fit-reason field.

steps.do: Sort every reviewed row into qualified, unknown or excluded, with one line of reason each. Do not contact anyone and do not guess any email address in this step.
steps.evidence: Three groups whose counts add up to the number of rows reviewed, each row with a reason.

blockers.do: If no buyer group or motive was chosen earlier, go back to those steps before searching.
If the searches turn up fewer than 20 rows, widen the launch time or add two more searches, and say which change you made.
If Product Hunt pages will not open for you, ask the owner to open them and share what they show; do not use a scraping service.
If reading by API would need commercial permission the owner does not have, keep reading public pages one at a time.
If a maker shows no sign of need, mark them unknown or excluded; never mark them qualified only because they launched recently.

deliver_help.fit_definition: The two or three lines describing a fitting maker, the one-line guess, and the leave-out rules.
deliver_help.searches_used: Each search term or topic page URL you opened, with the date.
deliver_help.maker_list: Every reviewed row marked qualified or unknown, with product page URL, profile URLs, role, quoted need with its URL, and fit reason, plus the count of each group.
deliver_help.excluded_makers: Every reviewed row you left out, with the reason. Example: 'hunter only, not a maker' or 'direct competitor'.

C-PH-METRICS.title: Read this goal's numbers for Product Hunt
C-PH-METRICS.purpose: Record the numbers this goal is judged on, for a fixed window before and after the round, from sources you can name, so rounds are compared on real counts and not on guesses. record_numbers lists exactly which numbers it needs.

steps.do: Read the goal's metric components from where_are_we. Set the window: seven days, in the owner's time zone. For a baseline, use the seven days before the round starts; for current, the seven days after it starts. If a launch is involved, note that Product Hunt's launch day runs on Pacific Time and write both times.
steps.evidence: The component names, the start and end of the window with time zone, and whether this is the baseline or the current reading.

steps.do: If the goal counts makers, read the maker list for the window: for the baseline, the last round's list; for current, this round's list. Count each row once (one per company). reviewed_makers is the rows whose profile and product site were actually opened and checked. qualified_makers is the rows marked qualified with a quoted need or sourced fit reason. verified_public_emails is the rows with an address the email step counted as verified, printed on the maker's own site, with the page URL. Never count unknown or excluded rows as qualified.
steps.evidence: Each maker count with the list it came from and the date that list was made, or 'no history' if there was no earlier list.

steps.do: If the goal counts site visits, take the click count of this round's tracked link from tracking for the window. If the listing does not use the tracked link, or for a baseline before any tracked link existed, use visits referred by producthunt.com in the owner's site analytics and name it. Use the same source for baseline and current, and use one source only; never add two sources together.
steps.evidence: The visit count, the tool it came from, and the window it covers.

steps.do: If the goal counts purchases, take the sale counter on the page shown after payment, or the owner's payment records for the window. Count only purchases from outside buyers that can be tied to this round. Leave out the owner's own test payments, refunded orders, and sales you cannot connect to this round, and say how many you left out.
steps.evidence: The purchase count, its source, and the number left out with the reason.

steps.do: If a launch is live, also note the visible upvote and comment counts and the number of different people who asked a real question about the product. Do not count the owner, the hunter, other makers promoting their own products, or simple congratulations. These are context only, not the goal's number.
steps.evidence: The upvote and comment counts and the number of real questions, each with the launch page URL.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with the goal's exact component names and a source for each. If there is no history for a component, record 0 and say in source that there is no history. Never estimate or fill a gap; if a component cannot be read, say which one and why.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call with every component name, value and source.

blockers.do: If there is no history for a component, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline.
If there is no sale counter and the owner has no payment records to share, ask the owner for the sales in the window from their payment tool; if none exists, say so and do not estimate.

If the live listing or replies do not use this round's tracked link, use the owner's site analytics for visits from producthunt.com and say so; if neither exists, record what you can and name the gap.
If the listing is still a draft, scheduled or pending, do not treat it as launched; record the current reading only once it is public.
If the window has not closed, report the numbers as early and read them again when the seven days are over.
If the count a rate is divided by is 0, record the components as they are and do not report any rise or fall.

C-PH-METRICS.title_zh: Product Hunt launch流量與付費結果

deliver_help.numbers: Each of the goal's components by its exact name with its value. Example: 'attributed_sessions: 0 (no history)'.
deliver_help.where_read: For each number, the tool, page or file it came from, such as the tracked link's click count, the maker list from this round, or the owner's payment records.
deliver_help.date_range: The start and end of the window with the time zone, and whether it is the baseline or the current reading.

C-PH-EMAIL.title: Find makers' public business emails from their own sites
C-PH-EMAIL.purpose: For each qualified maker, find a business email the maker has published on their own website and record where it was found, because only sourced, public addresses count and only they can be contacted fairly later.

steps.do: Take the qualified rows from the latest maker list. For each, start at the Product Hunt product page, open the contact maker's profile, and follow the links they list to the product website or their personal site. Write down every URL in that path.
steps.evidence: For each row, the product page URL, profile URL and website URL.

steps.do: Confirm the website belongs to this maker or their product: the domain matches the link on the product page, or the maker is named on the site's about or team page.
steps.evidence: For each website, the page and line that ties it to the maker.

steps.do: Read the site's contact, about, press and legal notice pages and the page footer. Record any email address printed there, the URL of the page it is on, and what the page says it is for, such as partnerships, press or support.
steps.evidence: Each email found, with its page URL and stated purpose, and the date you read it.

steps.do: If no address is printed, record 'none found' and the pages you checked. Never build an address from a name or username, never use email-guessing, lookup or scraping services, and never treat the email used to sign in to Product Hunt, or a field Product Hunt does not show, as known. A contact form may be recorded as a form URL, not as an email.
steps.evidence: Makers with no email marked 'none found', with the pages checked.

steps.do: Mark each address by type: the maker personally, the company's general inbox, customer support, or press and partnerships. Count an address as a verified public business email only if it is on the maker's own site and is not a customer-support-only address.
steps.evidence: Each address with its type and a yes or no for counting as verified.

steps.do: Check the page for signs the maker does not want pitches, such as 'no solicitations'. Note them and exclude that address. A public address is not consent to marketing: do not add anyone to a mailing list. Any later message is one personal email, approved by the owner word for word, that says who is writing, how they relate to the product and why, includes a way to opt out, and follows anti-spam law.
steps.evidence: For each address, a note of any no-contact sign and 'not added to any list'.

steps.do: Hand back one row for each qualified row you checked: verified email with source, none found, or excluded with reason. Do not send anything in this step.
steps.evidence: A list whose rows match the qualified rows checked, each with a result and a source.

blockers.do: If there is no list of qualified makers for this round, go back to the maker search step first.
If a maker lists no website and the product page links nowhere, mark them 'none found' and move on; do not search for private addresses.
If the site shows only a contact form, record the form URL and mark the email as 'none found'; never guess an address.
If you cannot tie the website to the maker, do not use any address from it and mark the row unknown.
If the site asks not to be contacted for sales, exclude that maker and note the page.

C-PH-EMAIL.title_zh: Product Hunt Maker公開商務Email核對

deliver_help.contacts_found: Each verified address with the maker's name, the page URL it is printed on, its type, and the date read.
deliver_help.none_found: Makers with no published business email, with the pages you checked for each.
deliver_help.excluded_contacts: Addresses you did not count, with the reason. Example: 'support address only' or 'site says no solicitations'.

C-PH-LISTING.title: Prepare and publish the Product Hunt launch
C-PH-LISTING.purpose: Put one honest, approved Product Hunt listing live on a chosen launch day with the round's tracked link, because a clear listing that the owner backs in the comments is what sends visitors from Product Hunt to the product.

steps.do: Search Product Hunt again for the product's name and website domain. If a page already exists and the owner is a listed maker, read Product Hunt's current rules on launching an existing product again and use that page. If it lists other makers, stop and ask the owner. Never create a second page for the same product.
steps.evidence: The existing page URL and its makers, or a note that none exists.

steps.do: Open the screen for submitting a product, or Product Hunt's help pages, and write down each field and its current limit: name, tagline, description, topics, images, pricing type and links. Do not rely on old limits from memory.
steps.evidence: A list of the fields with the limits read today and where you read them.

steps.do: Draft the listing from the product facts and the approved copy: a tagline with one specific benefit, a short description of what the product does today, one to three topics where these buyers browse, and a pricing type that matches the real price. Leave out features that are not live, invented numbers, testimonials, scarcity and guarantees.
steps.evidence: The draft text for each field, each within its limit, and a list of claims left out.

steps.do: Choose the images: real screenshots, or images made earlier in this round if there are any. Confirm the owner has the right to use each one and that each shows the product as it is now.
steps.evidence: Each image file with what it shows and a note on who owns it.

steps.do: Use the round's tracked link as the website link only if the form accepts it and the Product Hunt rules read earlier do not forbid redirect links; open it once to check it lands on the product. Otherwise use the plain product URL and tell the numbers step that visits will be read from producthunt.com referrals in the owner's site analytics. Draft the maker's first comment: who built it, why, what it does today, what it does not do yet, and a request for honest feedback, with the tracked link.
steps.evidence: The website link used, confirmation it opens the product, which source will count visits, and the first comment draft.

steps.do: Agree a launch date with the owner. Product Hunt's launch day runs on Pacific Time; pick a day when the owner can answer comments for the full 24 hours. Keep draft, scheduled and live apart; a draft or a scheduled launch is not launched.
steps.evidence: The launch date and start time in Pacific Time and in the owner's time zone, and the owner's agreement.

steps.do: Show the owner every field, the images, the website link and the first comment word for word, and get a clear yes. Any message the owner sends to friends or followers about the launch asks for feedback, not for upvotes. Never buy or trade votes and never use extra accounts.
steps.evidence: The full approved listing and the owner's yes message.

steps.do: The agreed person submits or schedules the listing once: the owner, or your browser if it is signed in to their account and they said yes. If submitting seems to fail, check the owner's drafts and products before trying again so nothing is submitted twice. If it is pending review, wait; do not submit it again.
steps.evidence: Who submitted, when, and the state shown afterwards: scheduled, pending or live.

steps.do: When it is live, open the public page and read back the name, tagline, description, makers and first comment. Click the website link and confirm it reaches the product. Hand back the public URL.
steps.evidence: The public listing URL, the text as it appears there, and confirmation the website link works.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to the exact listing and first comment, do not submit; show them the text and stop until they answer.
If the product already has a page, use it or ask the owner to request maker access; never create a second page.
If a field needs a fact you do not have, remove the claim or ask the owner; never fill it with a guess.
If your browser is not signed in to the owner's account, give the owner the final fields, images and first comment to paste, and ask for the public URL.
If Product Hunt shows the listing as pending, wait and check again later; do not resubmit or treat it as launched.
If the owner cannot answer comments on the chosen day, pick another date with them before scheduling.

C-PH-LISTING.title_zh: Product Hunt既有產品上架／維護

deliver_help.listing_url: The public Product Hunt URL of the live listing, opened and confirmed to load. If it is not live yet, write its state and when it goes live.
deliver_help.published_text: The name, tagline, description and first comment exactly as they appear on the public page.
deliver_help.launch_date: The launch day and start time in Pacific Time and in the owner's time zone.
deliver_help.website_link: The link on the listing, and whether it is the round's tracked link or the plain product URL.

C-PH-ANSWERS.title: Answer real questions on the Product Hunt launch
C-PH-ANSWERS.purpose: Reply quickly and truthfully to people asking about the product on the launch page, in the same thread, because clear answers to price, fit and trust questions are what turn launch visitors into buyers.

steps.do: Open the live launch page and read every comment. List the ones where a person asks about the product: what it does, price, setup, integrations, privacy or how it compares. Skip other makers promoting their own products and plain congratulations.
steps.evidence: A list of questions, each with the commenter's name, the comment URL and the exact question.

steps.do: Put questions about buying first: price, whether it fits their case, setup effort and trust. On launch day check the page every two to three hours; for the rest of the week check once a day.
steps.evidence: The questions in answer order, and the times you checked the page.

steps.do: Draft each answer from the product facts only, in under 100 words, in the owner's voice as the maker. If something is not built yet, say so plainly and give a date only if the owner gives one. Where the answer is about buying or trying the product, add the round's tracked link once. Offer a discount only if the owner has a real one.
steps.evidence: A draft per question, with the product facts each one relies on.

steps.do: Show the owner each reply word for word, alone or as a batch, and get a clear yes. Change nothing after the yes without asking again.
steps.evidence: The approved replies and the owner's yes message.

steps.do: Post each reply once, directly under the comment it answers, from the owner's maker account. The owner posts, or your browser does if it is signed in to their account and they said yes. If a reply seems to fail, check the thread before trying again so nothing is posted twice.
steps.evidence: For each reply, who posted it and when.

steps.do: Open each thread after posting and confirm the reply sits under the right comment, shows the owner's account, and matches the approved text. Copy the public URL of each reply.
steps.evidence: The public URL and visible text of each reply.

steps.do: Keep the talk on Product Hunt. Do not copy commenters or upvoters into an email list and do not message them elsewhere. If someone asks to talk further, answer in the thread or point them to the product's public contact page.
steps.evidence: A note that no commenter was added to any list or contacted outside the thread.

steps.do: List questions still open and any objection raised by three or more different people, so the next round's copy and listing can answer them. Replies are not sales; do not count them as purchases.
steps.evidence: Open questions and repeated objections, each with the comment URLs behind it.

blockers.do: If the listing is not public yet, wait until it is live; there is nothing to answer.
If the owner has not said yes to a reply, do not post it; show them the text and wait.
If an answer needs a fact you do not have, ask the owner and keep the question open; never guess.
If your browser is not signed in to the owner's account, give the owner each approved reply with the comment URL it goes under, and ask for the reply URLs.
If a comment is abusive or spam, do not argue; show it to the owner and let them decide whether to reply or report it.

C-PH-ANSWERS.title_zh: Product Hunt launch留言問題回覆

deliver_help.replies_posted: Each reply's public URL, its text as shown, and the question it answers.
deliver_help.open_questions: Questions not yet answered and why, such as 'waiting for the owner to confirm the price'.
deliver_help.repeated_objections: Doubts raised by three or more different people, with how many people raised each and the comment URLs.

C-META_ADS-ACCESS.title: Confirm the Meta ad account, brand Page and spending limits
C-META_ADS-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which ad account, which brand Page and Instagram account, who operates Ads Manager, and how much the owner allows to be spent, so ads can run under the right brand without the round stopping halfway.

steps.do: Ask the owner for the brand website, the Facebook Page and the Instagram account the ads should run under. Note how you will work: in your own browser already signed in to Meta Ads Manager, or through the owner's screen and screenshots.
steps.evidence: The website, Page URL, Instagram handle, and who will operate Ads Manager.

steps.do: The owner signs in to Ads Manager themselves; never ask for a password. List the business portfolios and ad accounts the owner can see, let the owner pick one, and write down its ad account ID, currency and time zone. If there are several, do not choose for them.
steps.evidence: The chosen ad account ID, its currency and time zone, and the owner's choice in their own words.

steps.do: Check that the brand's own Page and Instagram account are connected to this ad account and can be chosen as the ad's identity. If you open a new ad to see the identity choice, discard that draft afterwards so nothing is left in the account. If they cannot be chosen, stop the ads part of the round; never run the ads under another brand's Page.
steps.evidence: The Page and Instagram account shown as choosable for this ad account, a note that any test draft was discarded, or a note that they are missing.

steps.do: Check the account's health in Account Quality and in the ad account's payment settings. Sort any problem into one type: one rejected ad, a restricted account, a payment problem, or missing permission. Copy the exact wording of each notice.
steps.evidence: Account status, the problem type if any, and the exact notice text with the date it was read.

steps.do: Confirm the signed-in person can create and edit ads and can open the ad account's reporting. Open the reporting for the last 7 days and check that real numbers appear, not a message about a plan limit or missing permission. If only reading works, plan for the owner to make every change by hand from the drafts you prepare.
steps.evidence: What the signed-in person can do (read reports, create drafts, switch ads on and off), and whether real numbers appeared in reporting.

steps.do: If Meta asks for a two-factor code, an identity check, a new payment method or acceptance of terms, stop. Tell the owner which screen and which button, and wait. Resume on the same screen once they are done.
steps.evidence: What the owner had to do, on which screen, and where you resumed.

steps.do: Create a new ad account or business portfolio only if the owner asked for one in this conversation, and only through Meta's own screens. Keep to one real account. If creation seems to fail, check whether it was created before trying again; never make a second one.
steps.evidence: The new account ID with the owner's request, or a note that the existing account is used.

steps.do: Ask the owner to write down the limits for this round: the daily budget, the total for the round, the end date, and the currency. Without a written amount above zero, this round may only prepare ads that stay off.
steps.evidence: The owner's written message with daily budget, round total, end date and currency, or a note that no spend is approved.

blockers.do: If the brand's Page or Instagram account cannot be selected in this ad account, stop the ads part and ask the owner to give the ad account access to the Page; never use another Page instead.
If the account is restricted or has a payment problem, tell the owner the exact notice and Meta's next step shown on screen; never add or pay with a card for them.
If a code, identity check, payment method or terms screen appears, stop and tell the owner which screen and which button; never enter codes or accept terms for them.
If the session expires, ask the owner to sign in once more; if it expires again, switch to the owner operating Ads Manager from your drafts.
If the owner has not written a daily budget and round total, continue preparing drafts that stay off and ask for the two numbers before any ad is switched on.
If the owner can see more than one ad account, list them by ID and name and let the owner choose; never pick one yourself.

C-META_ADS-ACCESS.title_zh: 準備Meta Ads帳號、登入與授權

deliver_help.ad_account: The ad account ID, its currency and its time zone, as shown in Ads Manager.
deliver_help.brand_identity: The Facebook Page and Instagram account the ads will run under, confirmed as selectable in this ad account.
deliver_help.account_health: 'ok', or the problem type and the exact wording of the notice. Example: 'payment problem: card declined on 2026-11-20'.
deliver_help.who_operates: 'agent browser' or 'owner', plus whether that person can only read reports or can also create and switch ads.
deliver_help.approved_limits: The owner's written daily budget, round total, end date and currency, quoted from their message, or 'none approved'.

C-META-BASELINE.title: Map past Meta ad results and how each number will be counted
C-META-BASELINE.purpose: Lay out what past ads spent and returned, and fix the counting rules for this goal once, so the before and after numbers of this round are compared the same way and the weak point is visible.

steps.do: In the ad account's reporting, list the campaigns, ad sets and ads that ran in the last 30 days, with their status, budget, amount spent and the dates they ran. If you cannot open reporting, ask the owner for a screenshot or an export of the same view.
steps.evidence: A table of past campaigns, ad sets and ads with IDs, status, budget, spend and dates, and where it was read.

steps.do: For the same 30 days, read impressions, frequency, link clicks, landing page views and the result each campaign was set to get (purchases, leads or another conversion). Write each number exactly as shown and 'not shown' where it is missing.
steps.evidence: The numbers per campaign as displayed, with the name of the result each campaign counts.

steps.do: Write down the attribution setting (for example 7-day click, 1-day view), the account time zone, and how long after a click sales usually arrive. These must stay the same for the baseline and the current read.
steps.evidence: The attribution setting, time zone and typical delay, stated as the rule for this goal.

steps.do: Find where real sales, leads and refunds are recorded: the payment provider, the order list, the lead form inbox, or a CRM if the owner already uses a CRM. Ask the owner whether the Meta pixel is installed on the product page, because Meta only counts landing page views and website conversions where it is. A purchase reported by Meta is not money received; note how you will match the two and count each order only once.
steps.evidence: The name of each source for sales, leads and refunds, whether the pixel is on the product page, and how a Meta result will be matched to one real order or lead.

steps.do: Propose what counts for this goal and ask the owner to confirm or correct it: what makes a lead qualified, which orders count as outside customers (not the owner, team, tests or bots), and which costs are included in full costs. Write each rule in one sentence.
steps.evidence: The counting rules in plain sentences, confirmed by the owner.

steps.do: List every part of the goal's main number you cannot yet get, such as unknown fees or no sales source, and leave it empty; never estimate. If there is no past ad history, say so; the first round sets the baseline.
steps.evidence: A list of missing pieces and why each is missing, or a note that every piece has a source.

steps.do: From the table, name where results drop most: few impressions, low link click rate, clicks that do not load the page, or page visits that do not buy. Do not change any ad during this step.
steps.evidence: One sentence naming the weakest stage, with the two numbers that show it.

blockers.do: If you cannot open the ad account's reporting, ask the owner for a screenshot or export of the last 30 days by campaign, with the columns you need.
If there is no record of real sales or leads outside Meta, tell the owner the goal cannot be judged on money yet and ask where orders arrive; do not use Meta's numbers as money received.
If a tool returns a message about a plan limit instead of numbers, do not treat it as a number; read the same figures from the ad account's reporting or ask the owner for a screenshot.
If past campaigns used different attribution settings, pick one with the owner and note that older numbers are not directly comparable.
If the account has never run ads, write that there is no history and move on; the first round's read becomes the baseline.

C-META-BASELINE.title_zh: Meta Ads基準、歸因與全成本盤點

deliver_help.past_results: The 30-day table of campaigns, ad sets and ads with IDs, spend, impressions, link clicks, landing page views and results, as displayed.
deliver_help.counting_rules: Attribution setting, time zone, what counts as a qualified lead or outside customer, and which costs are included.
deliver_help.money_sources: Where real sales, leads and refunds are recorded. Example: 'Stripe payments list, refunds tab'.
deliver_help.missing_pieces: Each part of the goal's main number with no source yet, and why. Example: 'delivery cost unknown'.
deliver_help.weakest_stage: The stage where results drop most, with the numbers that show it.

C-META-CREATIVE.title: Diagnose current Meta ads and design a one-change test
C-META-CREATIVE.purpose: Find out why current ads are falling short and design two ad versions that differ in one thing only, so the round shows clearly which change moves the goal's main number.

steps.do: Read the ads that ran most recently: their IDs, impressions, frequency, link click rate, cost per result, and how long they have run. Do not judge any ad with under 1,000 impressions or under 72 hours of delivery.
steps.evidence: A short table of recent ads with these numbers and which ones have enough data to judge.

steps.do: Sort the problem into one type: not delivering, stuck in review or rejected, wrong audience, or tired creative. Call it tired only when frequency is above 3 and the link click rate fell by at least 20% over 7 days or more; one bad day is not enough.
steps.evidence: The problem type and the numbers that support it.

steps.do: If the problem is delivery, review or account health, stop here and send the round back to the account step; if it is the wrong audience, send it back to the buyer group step. A new creative fixes neither. Otherwise continue.
steps.evidence: A note that the problem is in the ad itself, or which step the round was sent back to.

steps.do: From the chosen angle, buyer quotes and buying motive, pick one thing to change: the hook, the image, the format (image, carousel, video) or the offer wording. Write a one-sentence guess of why it will do better.
steps.evidence: The single thing that changes and the one-sentence guess, with the quote or motive it comes from.

steps.do: Write a brief for version A (the current best ad, unchanged) and version B (the one change). For each, list the opening line, the headline, the image or video needed, the button, and the tracked link with ?v=A or ?v=B. Keep the first line of the ad text under 125 characters.
steps.evidence: Two briefs side by side, showing they differ only in the chosen element.

steps.do: Next to each claim in the briefs, name the product fact that supports it. Remove any number, testimonial, deadline or guarantee the facts do not support.
steps.evidence: Each claim paired with its product fact, and a list of claims removed.

steps.do: Set the rule for picking a winner before anything runs: the goal's main number, the goal's observation window (at least 72 hours), at least 1,000 impressions per version, and, when the goal counts purchases or leads, at least 5 of them per version. Call B the winner only if it beats A by 20% or more on the goal's main number; otherwise report 'no clear winner' and keep A. Keep the ad account, Page, audience and total budget the same as already approved; anything beyond that waits for the owner.
steps.evidence: The written winner rule and a note that budget, audience and Page stay within what the owner approved.

blockers.do: If no ad has 1,000 impressions and 72 hours of delivery, or no ad has run at all, write version A from the chosen angle as it stands and design version B with one change, without claiming any old ad is tired.
If ads are not delivering, are rejected or the account is restricted, send the round back to the account step instead of writing new ads.
If no angle or buyer quotes exist yet, go back to the angle test step before writing briefs.
If a claim needs a fact you do not have, remove it or ask the owner; never fill the gap with a guess.
If the test only works with a bigger budget or a new audience, write the request for the owner and keep the round within the current limits until they answer in writing.

C-META-CREATIVE.title_zh: Meta素材疲乏與單一變數測試設計

deliver_help.diagnosis: The problem type with the numbers that show it. Example: 'tired creative: frequency 3.8, link click rate down 31% over 9 days'.
deliver_help.hypothesis: The one thing that changes and why you expect it to do better, in one sentence.
deliver_help.variants: The briefs for version A and version B: opening line, headline, image or video, button, and tracked link with ?v=A or ?v=B, with the product fact behind each claim.
deliver_help.acceptance_rule: How the winner is picked: the goal's main number, the window, the minimum impressions and results per version, and the 20% margin.

C-META-METRICS.title: Read this goal's Meta Ads numbers and check them against real sales
C-META-METRICS.purpose: Record the numbers this goal is judged on, read from the ad account and matched against real sales, leads and costs, so the before and after of the round are compared on real money and not on what the platform reports.

steps.do: Confirm the ad account ID, the ads being measured, the date range, the time zone and the attribution setting. For the baseline read, use the account's ads over the most recent past period as long as the goal's observation window; for the current read, use this round's campaign, ad set and ad IDs from the time they started delivering. Use the same attribution setting for both.
steps.evidence: Ad account ID, ad IDs, date range with time zone, and attribution setting.

steps.do: For the current read, wait until the goal's observation window (72 hours of delivery) has passed since the ads started delivering. If you must read earlier, mark the numbers as early and read again after the window.
steps.evidence: The time delivery started and the time of this read, with 'final' or 'early'.

steps.do: In the ad account's reporting, or from the owner's screenshot or export, read amount spent, impressions, link clicks, landing page views and the result the ads were set to get, for each version (A and B) and in total. Write each exactly as shown; write 'not shown' and do not estimate when a number is missing.
steps.evidence: The numbers per version and in total as displayed, with the screen or file they came from and the time they were read.

steps.do: Check leads, purchases and refunds against the owner's own records: the payment provider, the order list, the lead form inbox, the round's sale counter from tracking, or a CRM if the owner already uses a CRM. Apply the counting rules agreed in the baseline step and count only real outside customers; leave out the owner, team, tests, bots, duplicates and refunded orders.
steps.evidence: The count from the owner's records, the source name, and how many were left out and why.

steps.do: If the goal needs money, add up the money from matched outside sales after refunds, and every cost for the round: ad spend, payment fees, platform fees, commissions, software and tools, product or delivery cost, paid help, and any other cost, plus money held back for work still to deliver. Meta's return on ad spend is not the owner's income.
steps.evidence: Money from matched sales after refunds, and each cost with its amount and source, or 'unknown' where there is no source.

steps.do: Turn money into the currency's smallest unit for any component ending in _minor, using the currency's standard decimal places: multiply by 100 for currencies with two decimals, such as USD, EUR and TWD; use the amount as shown for currencies without decimals, such as JPY and KRW. Say which rule you used.
steps.evidence: Each money amount as shown and in the smallest unit, with the rule used.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with the goal's exact component names, as record_numbers lists them for this goal (for example spend_minor, impressions, link_clicks, landing_page_views, attributed_conversions, qualified_leads, external_purchases, net_after_all_costs_minor), and a source for each. If there is no history, record 0 and say so in source. If a source is incomplete, say what is missing in source. Never estimate, and never change any ad during this step.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call with every component, its value and its source.

blockers.do: If you cannot open the ad account's reporting, ask the owner for a screenshot or export with the columns this goal needs, for the exact date range.
If there is no record of real sales or leads outside Meta, say so in source and leave those components unrecorded; never copy Meta's reported purchases as real ones.
If a cost needed for money after costs has no source, list it as unknown and ask the owner for the figure; do not estimate it.
If the observation window has not passed, record the numbers as early and read them again after the window ends; do not fill conversions that have not arrived yet with 0.
If the attribution setting, time zone or range length differs from the baseline, read again with the baseline's settings before recording.
If the account has no history for these numbers, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline.

C-META-METRICS.title_zh: Meta投放新觀察與付款成本核對

deliver_help.numbers: Each component of the goal's main number by its exact name, with its value as read; money in the currency's smallest unit.
deliver_help.where_read: For each number, the screen, export or record it came from, and the time it was read. Example: 'Ads Manager, campaign level, 2026-11-22 10:00'.
deliver_help.date_range: Start and end of the period measured, with the time zone and the attribution setting.

C-META-DRAFT.title: Build this round's Meta ads switched off
C-META-DRAFT.purpose: Build the approved ad versions in the ad account, switched off and within the owner's budget, so nothing spends until the owner says yes and each version can be measured on its own.

steps.do: Re-check the ad account ID, the brand Page and Instagram account, the campaign objective that fits the goal (sales, leads, or traffic for a goal about clicks or page loads), and the owner's written daily budget, round total and end date. Plan one campaign, one ad set per version with the same audience and placements, and one ad in each, all named with the round name.
steps.evidence: The list of objects to create with their names, and the limits quoted from the owner's message.

steps.do: Show the owner each ad word for word: the ad text, headline, image or video, button, the Page and Instagram account it shows as, and the link. Get a clear yes for each version before building.
steps.evidence: The exact text and image of each version and the owner's approval message.

steps.do: Use the round's tracked link as each ad's website link, with ?v=A or ?v=B to match the version. Open each link on a phone and check the product page loads in about 3 seconds and matches what the ad promises. If the goal counts landing page views or website conversions and the owner has not confirmed the Meta pixel is on that page, tell the owner before building.
steps.evidence: Each tracked link, which version it belongs to, a note that it loaded the right page, and whether the pixel is confirmed on that page.

steps.do: In Ads Manager (your own browser if it is signed in and the owner agreed, otherwise the owner), create the campaign and one ad set per version. Split the approved daily budget equally and set it on each ad set, not on the campaign, so Meta cannot move money from one version to the other; the ad sets together must not exceed the approved daily budget. Set the end date the owner gave and, if the owner agrees, a campaign spending limit equal to the round total.
steps.evidence: The campaign and ad set names with each ad set's budget, the end date and any spending limit as shown on screen.

steps.do: Upload the approved images or videos and create one ad per version in its own ad set. Check the ad preview for each placement shows the right image, text, Page name and link, with nothing cut off that changes the meaning.
steps.evidence: A preview check for each ad, with any placement turned off and why.

steps.do: Turn the campaign, every ad set and every ad off before publishing them, so they are created but spend nothing. Do not use any option that would also publish or switch on other drafts or ads in the account.
steps.evidence: Each new object shown as off, and a note that no other draft or ad was touched.

steps.do: Read back from the ad account each new object's ID, status, budget, end date, Page and link, and confirm spend is 0. If saving seemed to fail, search the account for the round name before trying again; never create a second copy.
steps.evidence: The IDs, status off, budget, end date and link of every new object, and spend of 0.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to the exact text and image of a version, do not build it; show it to them and wait.
If there is no written daily budget and round total, build nothing that can spend; prepare the ads off and ask the owner for the two numbers.
If the brand's Page or Instagram account cannot be selected for the ad, stop building and go back to the account step; never use another Page.
If a tracked link does not open the product page, stop before building that ad and fix the link with the owner.
If you are not sure an object was saved, search the account for the round name and use what exists; never create a duplicate.
If Ads Manager shows a restriction or payment problem, copy the exact notice, tell the owner, and stop; never pay or add a card for them.

deliver_help.ad_ids: The campaign, ad set and ad IDs created this round, with which version (A or B) each ad is.
deliver_help.approved_ads: The exact text, image or video, button and tracked link of each ad, as the owner approved them.
deliver_help.budget_settings: Each ad set's daily budget, the end date and any spending limit as shown in the ad account, next to the owner's approved limits.
deliver_help.status_check: The status of each new object (it should be off) and spend so far, read from the ad account.

C-META-ACTIVATE.title: Switch on only this round's Meta ads within the approved budget
C-META-ACTIVATE.purpose: Switch on exactly this round's ads after the owner's written yes, within the approved daily budget and total, so the test starts spending only what was agreed and its numbers can be read.

steps.do: Open this round's campaign, ad set and ad IDs and check they are still off and unchanged since the owner approved them. List any other drafts or unpublished changes in the account and leave them alone.
steps.evidence: This round's IDs shown as off and unchanged, and a list of other drafts left untouched.

steps.do: Find the owner's written approval to spend: daily budget, round total, end date and currency. Check each ad set budget is a whole amount above zero and that together they are not higher than the approved daily budget. If any of these is missing or zero, stop.
steps.evidence: The owner's approval quoted, and the budget and end date as set in the ad account.

steps.do: Write a short change plan and show it to the owner: which objects go from off to on, the daily budget, the end date, the most it can spend in total, and how to undo it (switch them off). Wait for the owner's yes to this plan.
steps.evidence: The change plan and the owner's yes.

steps.do: Switch on only this round's campaign, ad sets and ads, using your own browser if the owner said yes to that, otherwise the owner does it. Do not use any option that publishes all pending changes, and do not raise any budget.
steps.evidence: Who switched them on, at what time, which objects, and the link to each live ad if the ad preview offers one.

steps.do: After about 15 minutes, read each object's delivery status in the ad account. 'In review' means not delivering yet. If an ad is rejected, copy the reason and tell the owner; do not edit and resubmit without their yes.
steps.evidence: Each object's delivery status with the time it was read, and any rejection reason.

steps.do: Once the ads show as delivering, note the start time; the observation window counts from there. At 24 and 48 hours, check that spend so far is within the daily budget and that both versions are getting impressions.
steps.evidence: The delivery start time, and spend so far and impressions per version at the 24-hour and 48-hour checks.

steps.do: Note the date and time when the observation window ends, so the numbers are read and the ads paused on time and never left running past the approved end date.
steps.evidence: The planned time for the current read and for pausing.

blockers.do: If the owner has not approved a daily budget, total and the change plan in writing, keep everything off and ask them.
If the text, image, link or budget changed after the owner approved, show the new version and get a new yes before switching on.
If an ad is rejected, copy the reason, tell the owner, and wait for their yes before editing or asking for a new review.
If an ad is still in review after 24 hours, tell the owner and do not count review time in the observation window.
If spend runs above the approved daily budget or heads past the round total, switch this round's ads off at once and tell the owner.
If a restriction or payment problem appears, copy the exact notice and tell the owner; never pay or add a card for them.

deliver_help.ad_ids: The campaign, ad set and ad IDs switched on this round, with which version each ad is, and the link to each live ad if one is offered.
deliver_help.delivery_status: Each object's status as shown in the ad account, such as in review, active or rejected, with the time read and any rejection reason.
deliver_help.live_budget: Daily budget, end date and spend so far as shown in the ad account, next to the owner's approved limits.
deliver_help.delivery_start_time: When the ads started delivering, and when the observation window ends.

C-META-STOP.title: Pause only this round's Meta ads when the window ends
C-META-STOP.purpose: Pause exactly this round's ads once the numbers are read, and confirm they stopped spending, so the round costs no more than approved and the next test starts clean.

steps.do: Take the list of campaign, ad set and ad IDs that were switched on this round. Use only that list; never pause by picking from all ads in the account.
steps.evidence: This round's IDs, taken from the switch-on step.

steps.do: Check that the observation window has ended and that the current numbers were recorded. If they were not, record them first so the read covers the full window.
steps.evidence: The window end time and a note that the current numbers are recorded.

steps.do: Tell the owner exactly which ads will be paused. Keep an ad running only if the owner asks for it and writes a new daily budget, total and end date for it; record that it is still spending at their request.
steps.evidence: The list shown to the owner and their answer, with any new written limits for an ad kept running.

steps.do: Switch off only those IDs, using your own browser if the owner agreed, otherwise the owner does it. Do not delete anything, do not edit text, images or budgets, and do not touch other campaigns or brands.
steps.evidence: Who switched them off, at what time, and which IDs.

steps.do: After about 15 minutes, read each object's delivery status and confirm it is off and not delivering. If it is unclear, check again before trying anything else; never report it as stopped without seeing it.
steps.evidence: Each ID with its status as shown and the time read.

steps.do: Read the final amount spent for the round and compare it with the approved total. If it went over, report by how much.
steps.evidence: Final spend in the account currency and in its smallest unit, next to the approved total.

steps.do: Write what the next round should test: one new change, the same account, Page and limits. Pausing never raises the budget or extends the owner's approval.
steps.evidence: One sentence on the next test and a note that the limits stay as approved.

blockers.do: If the current numbers were not recorded yet, record them first, then pause.
If you do not have this round's IDs, search the account for the round name and confirm the list with the owner before pausing anything.
If an ad still shows as delivering after pausing, check again after 15 minutes and then ask the owner to switch it off by hand.
If your browser cannot switch ads off, give the owner the exact list of IDs to switch off and ask for a screenshot after.
If final spend is above the approved total, pause at once and report the amount over to the owner.

C-META-STOP.title_zh: Meta Ads觀察後只暫停本輪測試物件

deliver_help.paused_ids: The campaign, ad set and ad IDs paused this round, plus any the owner chose to keep running under new written limits.
deliver_help.status_after_pause: Each ID's delivery status as shown after pausing, with the time read.
deliver_help.final_spend: Total spent this round, in the account currency and in its smallest unit, next to the approved total.
deliver_help.next_test: The one change the next round should test, within the same approved limits.

C-GOOGLE_ADS-ACCESS.title: Confirm the Google Ads account, who edits it, and the budget cap
C-GOOGLE_ADS-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which Google Ads account the round uses, who signs in and makes changes, what it can already measure, and how much the owner allows to spend, so the draft is built in the right account and never spends more than approved.

steps.do: Ask the owner for the 10-digit customer ID (shown as 123-456-7890) of the account that will run the ads, and the website it advertises. If the account sits under a manager account, write down both IDs. Identify the brand by customer ID, never by account name, because two accounts can share a name.
steps.evidence: The customer ID, any manager account ID, the website, and the owner's confirmation that this account belongs to this brand.

steps.do: Decide who makes changes: the owner in their own browser, or the agent's browser if it is already signed in to a Google account with access to this customer ID. The owner signs in themselves; never ask for a password. Note the access level of the signed-in user. Read only access cannot create drafts.
steps.evidence: Who makes changes, the signed-in Google account, and its access level for this customer ID.

steps.do: If the owner has no Google Ads account yet, the owner creates exactly one on the official Google Ads sign-up page and enters billing details themselves. Do not create extra accounts, and never create a new one to get around a suspension. Advertiser verification and identity checks are done by the owner.
steps.evidence: The new customer ID and the owner's note that they created it, or a note that an account already existed.

steps.do: Read the account's currency, time zone, billing status and advertiser verification status. The currency cannot be changed after the account is made, so every budget and report in this round uses this currency and time zone. Do not add, change or use a payment method.
steps.evidence: Currency, time zone, billing status and verification status, as shown in the account.

steps.do: Open the account's list of conversion actions. For each, write down the name, where it comes from (website, import, app or phone), whether it is primary or secondary, its status as shown, and how many it recorded in the last 30 days. Pick the one that matches the goal's main number. Do not add tags or change the website in this step.
steps.evidence: The list of conversion actions with their status and 30-day counts, and the one this goal will be judged on, or a note that none fits.

steps.do: List the existing campaigns with their status, daily budget, keyword match types and negative keywords. Agree with the owner that this round only creates one new search campaign, and that no existing campaign, keyword or negative list is changed.
steps.evidence: The existing campaigns that stay untouched, and the owner's agreement on what this round may create.

steps.do: Ask the owner to write, in this conversation, the most the round may spend per day and in total, in the account currency, and the last day of the round. Check whether recommendations are set to apply automatically; if they are, tell the owner they can change the test without asking and ask whether to turn that off. Never accept a recommendation as part of this round.
steps.evidence: The owner's written daily cap, total cap and end date, plus the auto-apply setting and the owner's choice.

blockers.do: If the ID belongs to a manager account or another brand, stop and ask the owner for the exact customer ID of this brand; never change settings at the manager level.
If the signed-in user has read only access, set who_changes to 'owner' or ask the owner to grant standard access to that user themselves.
If no conversion action fits the goal, do not install tags; plan to count results with the round's sale counter and site analytics, and tell the owner.
If billing is not set up or verification is pending, tell the owner which screen needs them and wait; the agent never enters payment details.
If the owner has not written a daily cap, total cap and end date, stop here and ask for them; never guess a budget.
If the account is suspended, stop and tell the owner; never create another account to get around it.

C-GOOGLE_ADS-ACCESS.title_zh: 準備Google Ads帳號、登入與授權

deliver_help.customer_id: The 10-digit customer ID the round uses, plus any manager account ID above it.
deliver_help.who_changes: 'owner' or 'agent browser', the signed-in Google account, and its access level.
deliver_help.currency_and_time_zone: The account currency and time zone exactly as shown. Example: 'TWD, Asia/Taipei'.
deliver_help.conversion_to_judge: The conversion action name the goal is judged on, primary or secondary, and its last 30 days count, or 'none'.
deliver_help.approved_caps: The owner's written daily cap, total cap and end date, quoted from their message.

C-GA-KEYWORDS.title: Sort real Google search terms into keep, test and negative lists
C-GA-KEYWORDS.purpose: Turn the search terms people actually typed into keep, test and negative lists with one fixed review rule, so the round's money goes to searches with buying intent and the goal's main number can move.

steps.do: Open the search terms report for the agreed customer ID and campaigns. Use the last 30 days ending yesterday, or the days since the campaign started if shorter, in the account time zone. If the account has never run search ads, skip to step 6.
steps.evidence: The customer ID, campaign names, date range with time zone, and how many search terms the report lists.

steps.do: Copy each search term with its impressions, clicks, cost and conversions, plus the keyword and match type that triggered it. Keep keywords and search terms apart: a keyword is what the account bids on, a search term is what the person typed.
steps.evidence: A table of search terms with those columns and the keyword that triggered each.

steps.do: Mark each term as brand (contains the brand or product name) or non-brand. Then put each non-brand term in one class: buying (wants the product's job done, compares options, asks price), research (how-to or free information), job seeker (jobs, salary, careers), free seeker (free, download, crack), or unrelated (a different meaning). Add a one-line reason when the class is not obvious.
steps.evidence: Every term with its brand mark, class and, where needed, a reason.

steps.do: Write down the review rule and keep it the same in every round: review every term with at least one click, or the top 100 by cost if there are more. Count the terms reviewed, the terms marked buying, and the total cost of terms marked job seeker, free seeker or unrelated. The measurement step uses this same rule.
steps.evidence: The written review rule and the three counts it gives for this date range.

steps.do: Propose negative keywords only with clear evidence: a job seeker, free seeker or unrelated term that spent money, or a word that repeats in at least three such terms. Use phrase or exact match for multi-word negatives. Never add a generic negative list, never block a word that also appears in a term that converted, and never delete keywords just because their volume is low. If the window has fewer than 30 clicks in total, mark every negative as a candidate only.
steps.evidence: Each proposed negative with its match type, the terms that justify it, and a check against converting terms.

steps.do: Propose the keywords to keep or add, at most 20, grouped so each group serves one buyer situation from the segments and the chosen angle. Use phrase or exact match for a small budget. With no search history, build them from the buyer quotes and patterns such as '{job} software', '{category} price' and '{category} alternative', search each one on Google and note whether the results show buying intent.
steps.evidence: Keyword groups with match types, each keyword tied to the quote or search result it came from.

steps.do: Write the one change this round tests, for example 'the same keywords plus these 12 negatives' or 'one new ad group for situation X'. The change goes into this round's new campaign only, never into an existing one, and everything else stays the same. Do not change the sales page or tracking here. Show the owner the keep list, the negative list and the test change, and get a yes before the draft step uses them.
steps.evidence: A one-sentence test plan, the final lists, and the owner's approval message.

blockers.do: If the account has never run search ads, build the lists from buyer quotes and Google search results and mark every keyword as untested.
If you cannot open the search terms report, ask the owner for an export or screenshot of it for the agreed date range.
If the range has fewer than 30 clicks, propose negatives only as candidates and do not remove any keyword.
If a proposed negative would block a term that converted, drop that negative and note why.
If the report shows a different customer ID from the agreed one, do not use it and ask the owner again.

C-GA-KEYWORDS.title_zh: Google Ads實際搜尋字詞與排除詞

deliver_help.search_terms_reviewed: The table of reviewed search terms with clicks, cost, conversions and class, plus the date range.
deliver_help.keep_keywords: The keywords to keep or add, grouped by buyer situation, each with its match type.
deliver_help.negative_keywords: The negatives with match type and the terms that justify each; label candidates as candidates.
deliver_help.review_rule: The exact rule for which terms are reviewed and which classes count as irrelevant spend. Example: 'every term with 1+ click; irrelevant = job seeker, free seeker, unrelated'.
deliver_help.test_change: The single change this round tests, in one sentence, and the owner's yes.

C-GA-METRICS.title: Read this goal's numbers from Google Ads
C-GA-METRICS.purpose: Record the exact numbers this goal is judged on, for the period before the round and for the round itself, from Google Ads and the owner's payment records, so rounds are compared on real numbers. record_numbers lists exactly which numbers it needs.

steps.do: Confirm the customer ID, the currency and the time zone. For the baseline, use the same number of days as the round lasts, ending the day before this round's ads are switched on, and count the account's existing search campaigns.
