For the current reading, use the days since this round's ads were switched on and count only this round's campaign. Use the same conversion action, review rule and sources for both. If you cannot open the ad account's reporting, ask the owner for an export or screenshot.
steps.evidence: Customer ID, the campaigns counted, date range with time zone, currency, and how the numbers will be obtained.

steps.do: Check which components record_numbers asks for and use those exact names. Goals that use this step ask for: spend_minor and attributed_conversions (cost per conversion), irrelevant_spend_minor and spend_minor (share of wasted spend), qualified_queries and reviewed_queries (search term fit), or external_purchases and attributed_sessions (purchase rate of ad visitors).
steps.evidence: The list of component names this goal needs, copied from record_numbers.

steps.do: Read cost for the range and convert it to the currency's smallest unit without rounding. Example: US$12.34 is 1234. For a currency shown without decimals, such as JPY, use the figure as shown. Never convert to another currency.
steps.evidence: Cost as shown, and the same figure in the smallest unit.

steps.do: For conversions, count only the conversion action agreed for this goal, and write down the click-through conversion window shown in its settings. Google can add conversions days after the click. If the range ended less than 7 days ago, say in source that the number is early and read it again 7 days later if the round is still open. Google's conversion value or return on ad spend is not the owner's income.
steps.evidence: The conversion action name, its conversion window, its count for the range, and whether it is early.

steps.do: For search term numbers, apply the saved review rule and classes from the keywords step to this range: reviewed_queries is the count of terms reviewed, qualified_queries the count marked buying, irrelevant_spend_minor the cost of terms marked job seeker, free seeker or unrelated. If the report shows cost not tied to any visible term, say how much and leave it out.
steps.evidence: The three counts with the rule used, and any cost from hidden terms.

steps.do: For purchases and visits, take external_purchases from the owner's payment records or the round's sale counter, counting each order once and only real outside buyers: leave out the owner's, test and refunded purchases. Count only purchases you can tie to Google Ads, and say how many other sales were left out. Take attributed_sessions from the site analytics' sessions from Google Ads (paid search) and name the report; use the same source for baseline and current.
steps.evidence: Purchases and sessions, each with its source, what was left out, and how many sales could not be tied to the ads.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with each component's exact name, its value, and a source naming the report or export, the customer ID, the date range, the time zone and any 'early' note. If there is no history, record 0 and say 'no history' in source. Never estimate; a number that is not shown is not recorded. Do not change any ad, keyword or budget in this step.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call with names, values and sources.

blockers.do: If you cannot open the ad account's reporting, ask the owner for an export or screenshot covering the exact date range.
If the account has no history for these numbers, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline.
If the range ended less than 7 days ago, record the numbers as early and read them again after 7 days.
If the agreed conversion action does not exist or recorded nothing, use the payment records or sale counter and say so; never fill the gap with a guess.
If the screen or export shows a different customer ID, do not use those numbers and ask again.
If the report currency differs from the account currency agreed earlier, stop and confirm the currency with the owner; never convert to make it fit.

C-GA-METRICS.title_zh: Google Ads轉換、延遲與全成本核對

deliver_help.numbers: Each component name exactly as record_numbers asks for it, with its value as an integer, spend in the currency's smallest unit.
deliver_help.where_read: The report, export or screenshot each number came from, the account ID, and the time it was read.
deliver_help.date_range: The first and last day counted, with the account's time zone. Example: '2026-11-01 to 2026-11-30, Asia/Taipei'.

C-GA-DRAFT.title: Build the Google search ad as a paused draft
C-GA-DRAFT.purpose: Create this round's search campaign, keywords and ad in the account, switched off, exactly as the owner approved, so it can be switched on later with no surprises in budget, wording or link.

steps.do: Before building, check again: the customer ID, the owner's written daily cap, total cap and end date in the account currency, the target locations and language agreed with the owner from the buyer segments, and the conversion action. If any cap is missing, stop.
steps.evidence: Customer ID, caps quoted from the owner's message, end date, locations, language and conversion action.

steps.do: Plan the structure: one new search campaign for this round only, on Google Search with the Display Network switched off; one ad group per keyword group from the keywords step, with those keywords, match types and the approved negatives. Pick the bid strategy with the owner: if the agreed conversion action recorded fewer than 15 conversions in the last 30 days, use Maximize clicks with a maximum cost per click limit; otherwise use Maximize conversions. Daily budget no higher than the owner's daily cap, and an end date on the last day of the round.
steps.evidence: A written plan of campaign, ad groups, keywords, negatives, bid strategy, budget and dates.

steps.do: Write one responsive search ad per ad group from the approved copy: 8 to 15 headlines of 30 characters or fewer, and 2 to 4 descriptions of 90 characters or fewer; Chinese, Japanese and Korean characters count as two each. Each line must be backed by the product facts. No invented prices, discounts, ratings, 'best' or '#1' claims, scarcity or guarantees.
steps.evidence: Every headline and description with its character count and the fact it relies on.

steps.do: Google Ads does not accept a final URL that forwards to a different domain, so do not use the round's tracked link here. Set each ad's final URL to the product page with ?v=A, ?v=B when ads differ, plus utm_source=google&utm_medium=cpc so site analytics can count the visits. Open each URL and see the product page load. Tell the owner that sales from this round are counted with the sale counter and site analytics.
steps.evidence: The final URL for each ad, opened and confirmed to load the product page.

steps.do: Show the owner word for word: campaign name, locations, language, daily budget, end date, keywords, negatives, every headline and description, and the final URLs. Get a clear yes before creating anything.
steps.evidence: The full draft as shown to the owner and their approval message.

steps.do: Create only this round's campaign, ad groups and ads, in the owner's browser or the agent's own browser if the owner said yes. Set the campaign start date to a day in the future while building, and set the campaign to Paused as soon as the screen allows, at the latest right after publishing. Touch nothing that already exists. If a save seems to fail, check the campaign list before trying again so nothing is created twice.
steps.evidence: The names and IDs of the new campaign, ad groups and ads, all paused, and the start date as set.

steps.do: Open the draft again and check: status Paused, start date, daily budget, currency, end date, locations, language, Display Network off, bid strategy, keywords, negatives, final URLs, and each ad's policy status. A paused draft is not live. If an ad is disapproved, read the reason, fix only that line, and show the change to the owner.
steps.evidence: Each setting as it appears in the account, and each ad's policy status.

blockers.do: If the owner has not written a daily cap, total cap and end date, stop and ask for them before building.
If the owner has not said yes to this exact draft, do not create it; show it and wait.
If an ad is disapproved, read the stated reason and rewrite only that line; if the product or page itself must change, stop that ad and tell the owner.
If the product page does not load or shows an error, do not build the ads; tell the owner which URL failed.
If the signed-in user cannot create campaigns, hand the owner the full draft to enter themselves and ask for the IDs back.
If a second copy of the campaign appears, remove the extra paused copy only after the owner agrees, and keep one.

deliver_help.campaign_id: The new campaign's name and ID, with its status Paused.
deliver_help.ad_ids: The ID of every ad group and ad created this round.
deliver_help.daily_budget: The daily budget as set in the account, in the account currency, next to the owner's written cap.
deliver_help.final_urls: Each ad's final URL with its ?v= and utm tags, opened and confirmed to load.
deliver_help.policy_status: Each ad's policy status as shown, and the reason for any disapproval.

C-GA-ACTIVATE.title: Switch on only this round's Google ads, within the approved cap
C-GA-ACTIVATE.purpose: Turn on only the approved paused campaign, at a budget the owner wrote down, so real searches reach the ad and the goal's main number gets new data without risking more money than allowed.

steps.do: Open the paused draft and confirm the customer ID and the campaign, ad group and ad IDs from the draft step. These are the only items this step may switch on.
steps.evidence: The list of IDs to switch on, matching the draft step.

steps.do: Check the money against the owner's written caps: the daily budget times the number of days is at or below the total cap, and the end date is set. Google can spend up to twice the daily budget on a single day, so either set the daily budget to half the owner's daily cap or get the owner to write that a single day may reach twice the budget. A zero or missing cap means do not switch on.
steps.evidence: Daily budget, number of days, planned total, end date, the owner's caps side by side, and how the two-times rule was handled.

steps.do: Check each ad's policy status. If it is under review, wait and check again; never edit an ad to get around review. If it is disapproved, go back to the draft step.
steps.evidence: Each ad's policy status at the time of the check.

steps.do: Ask the owner for a yes in this conversation to switch on now, stating the campaign name, daily budget, total cap and end date.
steps.evidence: The owner's message saying yes to these exact figures.

steps.do: Switch on only this round's campaign, ad groups and ads, and set the start date to today if it was set in the future. Do not switch on any other paused item, raise any budget, or accept any recommendation.
steps.evidence: The time the campaign was switched on and who switched it on.

steps.do: Within 3 hours, check the status and whether impressions have started. Then check spend once a day: it must stay under the daily cap, and when total spend comes within one daily budget of the total cap, run the stop step. If the status says limited, write down the reason Google gives.
steps.evidence: Status, impressions, daily spend and total spend at each check, with the times read.

steps.do: Write down the stop date and the total cap, and plan the stop step for whichever comes first. Since a search ad has no public post URL, hand back the ad IDs, the final URL and a screenshot of the ad as shown in the account.
steps.evidence: The stop date, the planned stop trigger, and the ad IDs with final URL and screenshot.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to switching on at these figures, do not switch on; ask and wait.
If the daily budget or planned total is above the owner's cap, lower the budget to fit or ask the owner for a new written cap.
If an ad is still under review, keep the same ad and check again later; never create a copy to skip review.
If an ad is disapproved, leave it paused, read the reason and go back to the draft step.
If Google shows a billing problem, stop and tell the owner which screen needs them; never touch payment details.
If there are no impressions after 24 hours, read the status reason Google shows and report it; do not raise the budget.

deliver_help.switched_on_ids: The campaign, ad group and ad IDs that were switched on, and nothing else.
deliver_help.live_since: The date and time the campaign was switched on, in the account time zone.
deliver_help.delivery_status: Status, impressions and spend at the latest check, with the time read.
deliver_help.stop_plan: The stop date and total cap, and which comes first.

C-GA-STOP.title: Pause only this round's Google ads and close the round
C-GA-STOP.purpose: Pause exactly the campaign this round switched on, confirm spending has stopped, and record the final spend, so the round's result is clean and no money leaks after the test.

steps.do: Take the list of IDs from the switch-on step. This list is the only thing this step may pause. Never use 'all enabled campaigns' as the list.
steps.evidence: The campaign, ad group and ad IDs this round switched on.

steps.do: Confirm why the round ends: the end date arrived, the total cap was reached, or the owner asked. Make sure the current numbers were read for the full window before pausing; if not, read spend and conversions now.
steps.evidence: The reason the round ends, and the time the current numbers were read.

steps.do: Save the ads as they ran: headlines, descriptions, keywords, negatives, budget and final URLs, so the next round can change one thing from a known start.
steps.evidence: A saved copy of the round's ads and settings.

steps.do: Tell the owner which items will be paused, by name and ID. If the owner wants to keep them running, stop here and ask for a new written daily cap, total cap and end date.
steps.evidence: The message to the owner listing the items to pause, and their answer.

steps.do: Pause only those IDs. Do not delete or remove any campaign, do not touch other campaigns or other brands, and do not change billing.
steps.evidence: The time each item was paused and who paused it.

steps.do: Open the account again and confirm each item shows Paused. Compare spend at the time of pausing with spend 24 hours later; a small late charge can appear, but new clicks should stop. If the status did not change, check again before trying a second time.
steps.evidence: Status of each item and spend at pause time and 24 hours later.

steps.do: Record the final spend in the currency's smallest unit and write the one change the next round will test. The next round starts from a new draft; pausing never extends the budget or the owner's approval.
steps.evidence: Final spend in the smallest unit and the next round's single change.

blockers.do: If you do not have the IDs from the switch-on step, find the round's campaign by its exact name and creation date and confirm it with the owner before pausing.
If the status does not show Paused, wait 15 minutes and check again before retrying; tell the owner if it still runs.
If the owner wants the ads to keep running, ask for a new written daily cap, total cap and end date before doing anything.
If spend keeps rising 24 hours after the pause, check the status of every item and tell the owner the exact figures.
If the signed-in account shows a different customer ID, stop and switch to the agreed account before pausing anything.

C-GA-STOP.title_zh: Google Ads觀察後只暫停本輪測試物件

deliver_help.paused_ids: The IDs that were paused, each confirmed as Paused in the account.
deliver_help.paused_at: The date and time of the pause, in the account time zone.
deliver_help.final_spend_minor: Total spend for the round in the currency's smallest unit. Example: US$85.40 is 8540.
deliver_help.next_change: The one thing the next round will change, in one sentence.

C-TIKTOK_ADS-ACCESS.title: Confirm the TikTok Ads account, video rights and budget cap
C-TIKTOK_ADS-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which TikTok ad account the round uses, who makes changes, which identity and videos may run, what it can measure, and how much the owner allows to spend, so the test runs on the right account with rights in place and never overspends.

steps.do: Ask the owner for the advertiser ID of the TikTok Ads Manager account and the Business Center it belongs to, if any. Identify the brand by advertiser ID, never by account name.
steps.evidence: The advertiser ID, any Business Center, and the owner's confirmation that it belongs to this brand.

steps.do: Decide who makes changes: the owner in their own browser, or the agent's browser if it is already signed in with access to this advertiser ID. The owner signs in themselves; never ask for a password. Note the signed-in user's role; an analyst role can only read.
steps.evidence: Who makes changes, the signed-in user, and their role on this ad account.

steps.do: If the owner has no TikTok ad account, the owner creates exactly one on the official TikTok for Business sign-up page. If the owner chooses an address from inbox_address for the sign-up, read the verification code with inbox_latest. Business documents, identity checks and payment details are entered by the owner. Never create extra accounts.
steps.evidence: The new advertiser ID and how the sign-up was verified, or a note that an account already existed.

steps.do: Read the account's country, currency, time zone, payment status and account review status. These decide every budget and report in the round. Do not add or change a payment method.
steps.evidence: Country, currency, time zone, payment status and review status, as shown in the account.

steps.do: Check the account's existing pixel and events: which events fired in the last 7 days, for example a completed payment or a submitted form, and which one matches the goal's main number. Do not create a new pixel or change the website in this step.
steps.evidence: The events that fired in the last 7 days, and the one this goal will be judged on, or 'none'.

steps.do: Decide the identity the ad runs under. For Spark Ads (an existing TikTok post), get the authorization code from the post's creator and write down its expiry date; it must last past the round's end. For any video, confirm the owner has commercial rights to the footage, voices and music, or uses music from TikTok's Commercial Music Library.
steps.evidence: The identity, any Spark code expiry date, and a rights note for each video.

steps.do: Ask the owner to write, in this conversation, the most the round may spend per day and in total, in the account currency, and the last day. Check the minimum daily budget TikTok shows for an ad group, and tell the owner if it is above their daily cap.
steps.evidence: The owner's written daily cap, total cap and end date, and the minimum daily budget shown.

blockers.do: If the ID belongs to another brand or another Business Center, stop and ask the owner for the exact advertiser ID.
If the signed-in user can only read, set who_changes to 'owner' or ask the owner to change the role themselves.
If the account is under review or needs documents, tell the owner which screen needs them and wait.
If no event fits the goal, do not invent purchases; use the tracked link and sale counter and tell the owner.
If the Spark code is missing or ends before the round does, use a video the owner has rights to or wait for a new code from the creator.
If TikTok's minimum daily budget is above the owner's cap, show both figures and ask the owner for a new written cap or to skip TikTok.

C-TIKTOK_ADS-ACCESS.title_zh: 準備TikTok Ads帳號、登入與授權

deliver_help.advertiser_id: The advertiser ID the round uses, and its Business Center if any.
deliver_help.who_changes: 'owner' or 'agent browser', the signed-in user, and their role.
deliver_help.currency_and_time_zone: The account currency and time zone exactly as shown. Example: 'USD, America/Los_Angeles'.
deliver_help.event_to_judge: The event name the goal is judged on and its last 7 days count, or 'none, use tracked link and sale counter'.
deliver_help.approved_caps: The owner's written daily cap, total cap and end date, quoted from their message.

C-TA-METRICS.title: Read this goal's numbers from TikTok Ads
C-TA-METRICS.purpose: Record the exact numbers this goal is judged on, for the period before the round and for the round itself, from TikTok Ads and the owner's own records, so rounds are compared on real numbers. record_numbers lists exactly which numbers it needs.

steps.do: Confirm the advertiser ID, the currency and the time zone. For the baseline, use the same number of days as the round lasts, ending the day before this round's ads are switched on, and count the account's existing campaigns. For the current reading, use the days since this round's ads were switched on and count only this round's campaign. Use the same event, click figure and qualification rule for both. If you cannot open the ad account's reporting, ask the owner for an export or screenshot.
steps.evidence: Advertiser ID, the campaigns counted, date range with time zone, currency, and how the numbers will be obtained.

steps.do: Check which components record_numbers asks for and use those exact names. Goals that use this step ask for: spend_minor and attributed_conversions (cost per conversion), spend_minor and qualified_leads (cost per qualified lead), or link_clicks and impressions (link click rate).
steps.evidence: The list of component names this goal needs, copied from record_numbers.

steps.do: Read spend for the range and convert it to the currency's smallest unit without rounding. Example: US$12.34 is 1234. For a currency shown without decimals, such as JPY, use the figure as shown. Never convert to another currency.
steps.evidence: Spend as shown, and the same figure in the smallest unit.

steps.do: Read impressions and link clicks. Record only clicks that went to the destination link, not all clicks on the ad such as profile visits or likes, and use the same click figure in baseline and current. If the report shows only one click figure, say which kind it is. Compare it with the tracked link's own click count as a check and report both.
steps.evidence: Impressions, destination clicks, the tracked link's click count, and which figure was recorded.

steps.do: For conversions, count only the event agreed for this goal and note the attribution window the report uses. Conversions can arrive days late; if the range ended less than 3 days ago, say in source that the number is early. Check purchases against the owner's payment records or the sale counter, count each order once, and leave out the owner's, test and refunded orders.
steps.evidence: The event name, attribution window, count, the payment record check, and whether it is early.

steps.do: For qualified leads, use the qualification rule agreed for this goal, for example 'business owner in the target country who left a working email'; if none was written, write one with the owner before counting and keep it for every round. Count each person once from the lead form responses, the owner's lead list, or a CRM if the owner already uses a CRM. Leave out the owner, tests, duplicates and spam.
steps.evidence: The qualification rule, the count, and what was left out.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with each component's exact name, its value, and a source naming the report or export, the advertiser ID, the date range and the time zone. If there is no history, record 0 and say 'no history' in source. Never estimate. Do not change any ad or budget in this step.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call with names, values and sources.

blockers.do: If you cannot open the ad account's reporting, ask the owner for an export or screenshot covering the exact date range.
If the account has no history for these numbers, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline.
If the agreed event recorded nothing or does not exist, use the payment records, lead list or sale counter and say so; never invent purchases.
If the range ended less than 3 days ago, record the numbers as early and read them again after 3 days.
If the screen or export shows a different advertiser ID, do not use those numbers and ask again.
If destination clicks and the tracked link's clicks differ by more than half, still record TikTok's destination clicks and report both figures in source.

C-TA-METRICS.title_zh: TikTok Ads轉換歸因與全成本核對

deliver_help.numbers: Each component name exactly as record_numbers asks for it, with its value as an integer, spend in the currency's smallest unit.
deliver_help.where_read: The report, export or screenshot each number came from, the account ID, and the time it was read.
deliver_help.date_range: The first and last day counted, with the account's time zone. Example: '2026-11-01 to 2026-11-30, Asia/Taipei'.

C-TA-DRAFT.title: Build the TikTok video ad as a switched-off draft
C-TA-DRAFT.purpose: Create this round's TikTok campaign, ad group and video ad, switched off, exactly as the owner approved, so it can be switched on later with no surprises in budget, wording, rights or link.

steps.do: Before building, check again: the advertiser ID, the identity (Spark code valid past the round's end, or the account's own identity), the rights note for each video, and the owner's written daily cap, total cap and end date. If any cap is missing, stop.
steps.evidence: Advertiser ID, identity, rights note, and caps quoted from the owner's message.

steps.do: Check each video: vertical, the first two seconds show the buyer's situation, captions readable without sound, and length and file size within the limits the upload screen shows. If you test more than one video, change only the first two seconds between them.
steps.evidence: Each video file with its length, orientation, opening line, and what differs between versions.

steps.do: Plan the structure: one new campaign with the objective that matches the goal's main number, using the names the objective list shows: traffic for link clicks, lead generation for leads, website conversions or sales for purchases. A purchase objective needs the event chosen in the account step; if there is none, use traffic. One ad group with locations and language from the buyer segments, a daily budget no higher than the owner's cap, and a schedule ending on the round's last day. Do not copy settings from another platform.
steps.evidence: A written plan of objective, ad group targeting, budget and schedule.

steps.do: Write the ad text from the approved copy, under 100 characters, and pick one call-to-action button; a Spark Ad uses the post's own caption instead. Set the destination to the round's tracked link with ?v=A, ?v=B per video. Open the link and see the product page load. No invented numbers, testimonials, scarcity or guarantees.
steps.evidence: Ad text with character count, the button, and each destination URL confirmed to load.

steps.do: Show the owner word for word: each video, ad text, button, destination URL, objective, locations, daily budget and schedule. Get a clear yes before creating anything.
steps.evidence: The full draft as shown to the owner and their approval message.

steps.do: Create only this round's campaign, ad group and ads so that nothing can spend yet: set the ad group's schedule to start on a future day, and switch the campaign off before submitting if the screen allows it, otherwise right after submitting. Use the owner's browser, or the agent's own browser if the owner said yes. Touch nothing that already exists, and check the campaign list before any retry so nothing is created twice.
steps.evidence: The names and IDs of the new campaign, ad group and ads, that the campaign is off, and the schedule start as set.

steps.do: Open the draft again and check: campaign off, daily budget, currency, schedule, identity, destination URLs, video processing and review status. A processed or approved video is not live. If review is pending, keep the same ad ID and wait. If rejected, read the reason and fix only that part with the owner's yes.
steps.evidence: Each setting as it appears in the account, and each ad's review status.

blockers.do: If the owner has not written a daily cap, total cap and end date, stop and ask for them before building.
If the owner has not said yes to this exact draft, do not create it; show it and wait.
If the Spark code has expired or ends before the round, stop that ad and use a video the owner has rights to, or wait for a new code.
If an ad is still in review, keep its ad ID and check again later; never create a second copy of the same ad.
If an ad is rejected, read the stated reason and fix only that part with the owner's yes; if the product itself must change, stop that ad.
If the owner cannot confirm rights to a video's footage, voices or music, leave that video out.

deliver_help.campaign_id: The new campaign's name and ID, confirmed switched off.
deliver_help.ad_ids: The ID of the ad group and every ad created this round.
deliver_help.daily_budget: The daily budget as set, in the account currency, next to the owner's written cap.
deliver_help.destination_urls: Each ad's destination URL with its ?v= tag, opened and confirmed to load.
deliver_help.review_status: Each ad's processing and review status as shown, and the reason for any rejection.

C-TA-ACTIVATE.title: Switch on only this round's TikTok ads, within the approved cap
C-TA-ACTIVATE.purpose: Turn on only the approved switched-off campaign, at a budget the owner wrote down, so real viewers see the video and the goal's main number gets new data without risking more money than allowed.

steps.do: Open the draft and confirm the advertiser ID and the campaign, ad group and ad IDs from the draft step. These are the only items this step may switch on. Check that any Spark code is still valid past the round's end.
steps.evidence: The list of IDs to switch on, matching the draft step, and the Spark code expiry if used.

steps.do: Check the money against the owner's written caps: the daily budget is at or below the daily cap, the daily budget times the number of days is at or below the total cap, and the schedule ends on the round's last day. A zero or missing cap means do not switch on.
steps.evidence: Daily budget, number of days, planned total, end date, and the owner's caps side by side.

steps.do: Check each ad's review status. If it is still in review, wait and check again; never edit or copy an ad to get around review. If it is rejected, go back to the draft step.
steps.evidence: Each ad's review status at the time of the check.

steps.do: Ask the owner for a yes in this conversation to switch on now, stating the campaign name, daily budget, total cap and end date.
steps.evidence: The owner's message saying yes to these exact figures.

steps.do: Switch on only this round's campaign, ad group and ads, and move the schedule start to today if it was set in the future. Do not switch on any other item, raise any budget, or turn on automatic budget increases.
steps.evidence: The time the campaign was switched on and who switched it on.

steps.do: Within 3 hours, check the status and whether impressions have started. Then check spend once a day: it must stay under the daily cap, and when total spend comes within one daily budget of the total cap, run the stop step. If an ad shows as not delivering, write down the reason TikTok gives.
steps.evidence: Status, impressions, daily spend and total spend at each check, with the times read.

steps.do: Write down the stop date and total cap, and plan the stop step for whichever comes first, or the Spark code's expiry if that is sooner. Hand back the ad IDs, destination URLs, and an ad preview link or screenshot.
steps.evidence: The stop date, the planned stop trigger, and the ad IDs with preview link or screenshot.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to switching on at these figures, do not switch on; ask and wait.
If the daily budget or planned total is above the owner's cap, lower the budget to fit or ask the owner for a new written cap.
If an ad is still in review, keep the same ad ID and check again later; never create a copy to skip review.
If the Spark code has expired, leave that ad off and use a video the owner has rights to, or wait for a new code.
If TikTok shows a payment problem, stop and tell the owner which screen needs them; never touch payment details.
If there are no impressions after 24 hours, read the reason TikTok shows and report it; do not raise the budget.

deliver_help.switched_on_ids: The campaign, ad group and ad IDs that were switched on, and nothing else.
deliver_help.live_since: The date and time the campaign was switched on, in the account time zone.
deliver_help.delivery_status: Status, impressions and spend at the latest check, with the time read.
deliver_help.stop_plan: The stop date, total cap and any Spark code expiry, and which comes first.

C-TA-STOP.title: Pause only this round's TikTok ads and close the round
C-TA-STOP.purpose: Switch off exactly the campaign this round switched on, confirm spending has stopped, and record the final spend, so the round's result is clean and no money leaks after the test.

steps.do: Take the list of IDs from the switch-on step. This list is the only thing this step may switch off. Never use 'all active campaigns' as the list.
steps.evidence: The campaign, ad group and ad IDs this round switched on.

steps.do: Confirm why the round ends: the end date arrived, the total cap was reached, the Spark code expired, or the owner asked. Make sure the current numbers were read for the full window before pausing; if not, read spend, clicks and conversions now.
steps.evidence: The reason the round ends, and the time the current numbers were read.

steps.do: Save the ads as they ran: video files, ad text, button, targeting, budget and destination URLs, so the next round can change one thing from a known start.
steps.evidence: A saved copy of the round's ads and settings.

steps.do: Tell the owner which items will be switched off, by name and ID. If the owner wants to keep them running, stop here and ask for a new written daily cap, total cap and end date.
steps.evidence: The message to the owner listing the items to switch off, and their answer.

steps.do: Switch off only those IDs. Do not delete any campaign, do not touch other campaigns or brands, and do not change payment settings.
steps.evidence: The time each item was switched off and who did it.

steps.do: Open the account again and confirm each item shows as off and not delivering. Compare spend at the time of pausing with spend 24 hours later; new impressions should stop. If the status did not change, check again before trying a second time.
steps.evidence: Status of each item and spend at pause time and 24 hours later.

steps.do: Record the final spend in the currency's smallest unit and write the one change the next round will test, for example a new first two seconds. The next round starts from a new draft; pausing never extends the budget or the owner's approval.
steps.evidence: Final spend in the smallest unit and the next round's single change.

blockers.do: If you do not have the IDs from the switch-on step, find the round's campaign by its exact name and creation date and confirm it with the owner before switching anything off.
If the status does not show off, wait 15 minutes and check again before retrying; tell the owner if it still runs.
If the owner wants the ads to keep running, ask for a new written daily cap, total cap and end date before doing anything.
If spend keeps rising 24 hours after the pause, check the status of every item and tell the owner the exact figures.
If the signed-in account shows a different advertiser ID, stop and switch to the agreed account before pausing anything.

C-TA-STOP.title_zh: TikTok Ads觀察後只暫停本輪測試物件

deliver_help.paused_ids: The IDs that were switched off, each confirmed as not delivering.
deliver_help.paused_at: The date and time of the pause, in the account time zone.
deliver_help.final_spend_minor: Total spend for the round in the currency's smallest unit. Example: US$85.40 is 8540.
deliver_help.next_change: The one thing the next round will change, in one sentence.

C-LINKEDIN_ADS-ACCESS.title: Confirm the LinkedIn ad account, Page, and spending limits
C-LINKEDIN_ADS-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which LinkedIn ad account and Company Page this goal uses, who works in Campaign Manager, and the owner's written spending limits, so ads can be drafted, run and measured without stopping halfway.

steps.do: Ask the owner for the URL of the LinkedIn Company Page the ads will run under and the ad account they want to use. Open the Page URL as a public page and confirm it is the owner's brand. If an ad account already exists, use it; do not create a second one.
steps.evidence: The Company Page URL, the ad account name and ID as Campaign Manager shows them, and the owner's confirmation that both are theirs.

steps.do: Decide who works in Campaign Manager: the owner, or the agent in a browser where the owner is already signed in, if the owner allows it. If nobody is signed in, the owner signs in themselves on LinkedIn's own sign-in screen and handles any code or identity check. Never ask for a password. If the owner already reaches the ad account through a tool that uses LinkedIn's advertising API, use only the access it already has; if that access is still waiting for LinkedIn's review, wait and work in Campaign Manager instead.
steps.evidence: Who will operate the ad account, and how sign-in was done.

steps.do: Check the role the operator has on the ad account (it must allow creating and editing campaigns, for example Account manager or Campaign manager) and that the operator is allowed to run ads under the Company Page. If either is missing, the owner adds it from a Page or ad account admin login.
steps.evidence: The operator's role on the ad account, and whether ads can run under the Company Page.

steps.do: Read the ad account's currency, time zone, and whether a payment method is already set up. Ask the owner to write down the daily budget and the total budget for this round in that currency. The agent never enters card details; if billing is missing, the owner adds it.
steps.evidence: Currency, time zone, billing status, and the owner's written daily and total limits.

steps.do: List the conversions already set up in the ad account, what each one counts, and its attribution window, and whether the product site already has LinkedIn's Insight Tag. Do not add a tag or a new conversion here; if one is needed, write down exactly what and ask the owner.
steps.evidence: Each existing conversion with what it counts and its window, or a note that none exist.

steps.do: If the round will use a Lead Gen Form, confirm the form will belong to this ad account, that the owner has a privacy policy URL for it, and who can download the leads. A filled form only allows a reply about that request, not adding the person to every mailing.
steps.evidence: The privacy policy URL opened and confirmed, who can download leads, or a note that the round sends people to the product site instead.

steps.do: Write down the round's limits: the one campaign group and campaign this round may create or change, and that nothing else in the account will be switched on, paused or edited. Leave audience expansion and any automatic budget increase off unless the owner asks for them.
steps.evidence: The list of what this round may touch, with the owner's okay in writing.

blockers.do: If the operator cannot run ads for the Company Page, ask the owner to add the role from a Page admin login, and keep working on the copy meanwhile.
If LinkedIn asks for a verification code, terms, or an identity check, stop and tell the owner which screen needs them; never enter codes or accept terms for them.
If the ad account has no payment method, ask the owner to add one themselves; never type card details.
If the owner has not written down both a daily and a total budget, do not prepare any campaign and ask for both numbers in the account's currency.
If nobody can download the form's leads, say so and plan to send people to the product site with the round's tracked link; never guess email addresses.
If no conversion is set up, mark it unknown and rely on the round's tracked link and sale counter; add nothing to the site without the owner's yes.

C-LINKEDIN_ADS-ACCESS.title_zh: 準備LinkedIn Ads帳號、登入與授權

deliver_help.ad_account_id: The ad account name and ID exactly as Campaign Manager shows them.
deliver_help.company_page_url: The public URL of the Company Page the ads run under, opened and confirmed to be the owner's.
deliver_help.who_operates: 'owner' or 'agent browser', plus the operator's role on the ad account.
deliver_help.budget_limits: The owner's written daily and total budget for this round, with the currency. Example: 'USD 20 per day, USD 140 total'.
deliver_help.conversion_sources: Each conversion already set up and what it counts, or 'none', plus whether a Lead Gen Form will be used.

C-LA-METRICS.title: Read this goal's numbers from LinkedIn Ads
C-LA-METRICS.purpose: Record the numbers this goal is judged on, from the ad account's reporting and the owner's own lead or sales records, for a fixed date range, so the baseline and the current round are compared on real numbers.

steps.do: Confirm the ad account ID, the campaigns being measured, the date range, the time zone, and the currency. For the baseline, use the account's earlier campaigns with the same objective over a range of the same length. For the current reading, start when this round's ads went live and cover at least the goal's 168 hours.
steps.evidence: Ad account ID, campaign names and IDs, date range with time zone, and currency.

steps.do: Find this goal's metric components and use those exact names with record_numbers: spend_minor and attributed_conversions for cost per conversion, spend_minor and qualified_leads for cost per qualified lead, link_clicks and impressions for link click rate.
steps.evidence: The list of component names this goal needs, copied exactly.

steps.do: In the ad account's reporting, filter to only the measured campaigns and the date range, then read spend, impressions, and landing page clicks. Write spend in the currency's smallest unit: USD 123.45 is 12345; for a currency without cents, such as JPY, 1 yen is 1.
steps.evidence: Each figure as shown, with the filter used and the time it was read.

steps.do: For attributed_conversions, read the chosen conversion and note its attribution window. Check it against the sale counter and the owner's payment records; never count the owner's or the agent's test purchases, and leave out refunded orders. If the window is still open, mark the number as early.
steps.evidence: The conversion count, its window, and how it matches the sales records.

steps.do: For qualified_leads, take the leads from the form download or the site form and count only those that meet the rule written before the round, such as job role, company size, or stated need. Count each person once. A lead is not a sale, and no lead is ever invented.
steps.evidence: The qualified count, the rule used, and how many leads were left out and why.

steps.do: For link_clicks, use landing page clicks from the reporting or the round's tracked link count, and name which one. Use the same source for the baseline and the current reading.
steps.evidence: The click count and its source, the same as in the other reading.

steps.do: Write down refunds and the round's other costs if known, such as tools or the owner's hours, or 'unknown'. The return the ad account reports is not the owner's net income. Use the same definitions and sources for the baseline and the current reading, and never borrow a number from another goal.
steps.evidence: Refunds and other costs, or 'unknown', and a note that both readings use the same definitions.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with each component by its exact name and a source naming the screen, export, or file and the read time. If there is no history, record 0 and say so in source. Never estimate a missing number, and change nothing in the ads while reading.
steps.evidence: The recorded numbers, each with its source, and any number left out with the reason.

blockers.do: If you cannot open the ad account's reporting, ask the owner for an export or a screenshot filtered to the measured campaigns and date range.
If the account has no earlier campaigns for this metric, record 0, say in source that there is no history, and let this round set the baseline.
If no conversion is set up, use the sale counter and payment records only, and say in source that the ad account has no conversion.
If the leads cannot be downloaded, ask the owner to export them; never count qualified leads you cannot see.
If the ads have run less than 168 hours or conversions may still arrive, record the numbers as early and read them again later.
If an export or screenshot shows a different ad account or campaigns from the agreed ones, do not use it and ask again.

C-LA-METRICS.title_zh: LinkedIn Ads表單到合格商機核對

deliver_help.numbers: Each component by its exact name with its value. Spend is in the smallest currency unit.
deliver_help.where_read: Where each number came from: the ad account's reporting, the form download, the sale counter, or the owner's payment records, with the time read.
deliver_help.date_range: Start and end date with time zone. Example: '2026-11-01 to 2026-11-08, Asia/Taipei'.

C-LA-DRAFT.title: Build this round's LinkedIn ads as drafts, not running
C-LA-DRAFT.purpose: Set up this round's campaign and ads in Campaign Manager without switching them on, so the owner can check every word, the audience, and the budget before any money is spent.

steps.do: Re-check the ad account ID, the Company Page, the operator's role, and the owner's written daily and total budget. If any of these is missing, stop here.
steps.evidence: The four items, confirmed on the day of drafting.

steps.do: Pick the objective that fits the goal's main number: website visits or conversions when people should reach the product page, lead generation when the goal counts leads. Read the audience options the ad account shows today; do not copy audience settings or typical costs from old guides.
steps.evidence: The objective chosen and why, and the audience options available today.

steps.do: Build the audience from the chosen buyer group: one job situation, such as a job function plus seniority and company size. Note the audience size estimate shown. If it is too small to run, adjust within the same buyer group; never widen to people who do not fit.
steps.evidence: The audience settings and the size estimate shown.

steps.do: Prepare each ad from the approved copy and image. The destination is the round's tracked link, with ?v=A, ?v=B for each version, and only one thing differs between versions. For a Lead Gen Form, keep it to at most four fields, add one question that tests the qualification rule, and add the privacy policy URL. Check every claim against the product facts; no invented numbers, testimonials, scarcity, or guarantees.
steps.evidence: Each ad's text, image, and link or form, with what differs between versions.

steps.do: Show the owner, word for word: each ad's text, headline, image, destination link or form questions, the audience, the objective, the daily and total budget, and the start and end dates. Get a clear yes before saving.
steps.evidence: The full draft as shown, and the owner's approval message.

steps.do: The operator agreed in the account step creates only this round's campaign and ads, saved as draft or paused. Set a daily budget and a total budget at or below the owner's limits, and an end date. Do not edit any other campaign. If saving seemed to fail, check the campaign list before trying again so nothing is created twice.
steps.evidence: One campaign and its ads in draft or paused status, and their IDs.

steps.do: Open the campaign again and check that the status, audience, budget, end date, and each ad's link or form match the approved draft. Report no leads or clicks yet; nothing has run.
steps.evidence: Campaign and ad IDs, their status, and a line-by-line match with the approved draft.

blockers.do: If the owner has not written a daily and a total budget, do not create anything and ask for both numbers.
If the owner has not said yes to this exact draft, do not save it in the ad account; show it and wait.
If the audience is too small to run, adjust it within the same buyer group or tell the owner; never widen to people who do not fit.
If the ads cannot run under the Company Page, ask the owner to fix the role, and keep the draft text ready.
If the tracked link does not open the product page, fix it before saving the draft.
If leads from the form cannot be downloaded, switch to the product page with the tracked link and tell the owner.

deliver_help.campaign_id: The campaign name and ID as Campaign Manager shows them.
deliver_help.ad_ids: Each ad's ID with its version label (A, B) and its tracked link or form name.
deliver_help.draft_status: The status shown for the campaign and each ad. It must be draft or paused.
deliver_help.budget_set: The daily budget, total budget, end date, and currency as saved.
deliver_help.owner_approval: The owner's yes, quoted with the time it was given.

C-LA-ACTIVATE.title: Switch on only this round's LinkedIn ads
C-LA-ACTIVATE.purpose: Start delivery of the approved draft ads, and nothing else, within the owner's written budget, so the round collects real numbers for the goal.

steps.do: Open the campaign and ads by the IDs from the draft step. Confirm the text, image, audience, link or form, and budget are the same as approved. If anything changed, show the owner again before going on.
steps.evidence: Campaign and ad IDs, and a check that each matches the approved draft.

steps.do: Get the owner's written yes to switch on, naming the daily budget, the total budget, and the end date in the account's currency. With no budget, a zero budget, or no yes, nothing is switched on.
steps.evidence: The owner's message approving the switch-on with the amounts and end date.

steps.do: Open the tracked link of each ad and confirm it reaches the product page, or preview the Lead Gen Form and confirm its questions and privacy link.
steps.evidence: Each link or form checked, with the page or form it showed.

steps.do: Switch on only this round's campaign and ads, by the operator agreed earlier. Do not switch on any other draft, raise the budget, or turn on audience expansion.
steps.evidence: Who switched on what, and when.

steps.do: Open the campaign again and read each ad's status and review state. If an ad is in review, wait; do not edit it to get around review. If an ad is rejected, read the reason and bring a fix to the owner.
steps.evidence: Status and review state of each ad, with the time read.

steps.do: Write down the start time and the planned stop: after the goal's 168 hours or when the total budget is spent, whichever comes first. Set the campaign's end date to match if the owner agreed.
steps.evidence: Start time, planned stop time, and whether an end date is set in the campaign.

blockers.do: If the owner has not approved switching on with a budget and end date, do not switch anything on; ask and wait.
If the ads no longer match the approved draft, show the owner the difference and get a new yes.
If an ad is still in review, wait and check again later; do not edit it to get around review.
If an ad is rejected, read the reason, draft a fix that keeps to the facts, and show the owner before resubmitting.
If the ad account shows a billing problem, ask the owner to fix it themselves; never enter card details.

deliver_help.campaign_id: The campaign name and ID that was switched on.
deliver_help.ad_ids: Each ad ID with its version label, its status, and its review state.
deliver_help.live_status: What the ad account shows now for the campaign, such as active, in review, or rejected.
deliver_help.started_at: The date and time delivery was switched on, with time zone.
deliver_help.planned_stop: When this round's ads will be paused, and the total budget that ends it sooner.

C-LA-STOP.title: Pause only this round's LinkedIn ads after the test
C-LA-STOP.purpose: Stop spending on this round's ads once the observation time is over, without touching anything else in the account, so the result is fixed and the next round starts clean.

steps.do: List the campaign and ad IDs that this round switched on, taken from the switch-on step. Use only these; never take the whole account's campaign list.
steps.evidence: The IDs this round switched on.

steps.do: Confirm the round is over: at least 168 hours since start, or the total budget is spent. Confirm this round's numbers have been read and recorded; if not, read them first.
steps.evidence: Start time, time now or budget reached, and a note that the numbers were recorded.

steps.do: Tell the owner which campaign and ads will be paused, then pause only those. Do not delete or archive them, and do not change text, images, audience, or budget, so the round stays on record. Do not touch other campaigns or other brands.
steps.evidence: The IDs paused, who paused them, and when.

steps.do: Open each campaign and ad again and confirm the status shows paused and nothing is still delivering. If the pause seemed to fail, check the status before trying again, and do not call it stopped until the screen shows it.
steps.evidence: Status of each ID as shown after pausing, with the time read.

steps.do: Read the round's final spend from the ad account's reporting, in the currency's smallest unit, and compare it with the owner's total limit. If it went over, tell the owner the exact amount.
steps.evidence: Final spend in the smallest unit, and whether it stayed within the owner's limit.

steps.do: Write the one change the next round will test, such as a different job function or one different form question, with the same budget and qualification rule. Pausing does not give permission for a bigger budget.
steps.evidence: The single change planned for the next round.

blockers.do: If you do not know which IDs this round switched on, ask the owner or check the switch-on step; never pause by guessing.
If this round's numbers are not recorded yet, read and record them first, then pause.
If the status does not show paused, check again after a few minutes and ask the owner to pause it by hand if it still runs.
If spend went over the owner's total limit, pause at once and tell the owner the exact amount.
If the owner wants to keep the ads running, get a new written daily budget, total budget, and end date instead of pausing.

C-LA-STOP.title_zh: LinkedIn Ads觀察後只暫停本輪測試物件

deliver_help.paused_ids: The campaign and ad IDs this round paused, and nothing else.
deliver_help.status_shown: The status each one shows after pausing, with the time read.
deliver_help.final_spend_minor: Total spend for the round in the currency's smallest unit, with the currency. Example: '13850 USD'.
deliver_help.next_change: The one thing the next round will change, in one sentence.

C-EMAIL-ACCESS.title: Confirm the brand's sender address, sending tool and who sends
C-EMAIL-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which brand address sends, through which tool the owner already uses, who presses send and how unsubscribes work, so the email goes out under the right name to people who agreed to it without the owner being stopped halfway.

steps.do: Ask the owner which brand address will send and which address replies should go to. Check both are on the brand's own domain. Never borrow another brand's or a personal sender address.
steps.evidence: The From name, From address and Reply-To address, confirmed by the owner.

steps.do: Ask which tool the owner already uses to send email (for example the brand's mailbox or an email marketing tool), where the contact list and its unsubscribes are kept, and whether that list records how each contact signed up. Use that tool; do not sign up for a new one unless the owner asks in this conversation.
steps.evidence: The name of the sending tool, where the list and unsubscribes live, and whether signup sources are recorded.

steps.do: Decide who presses send: the owner in their own tool, or the agent's own browser if it is already signed in to that account. If nobody is signed in, the owner signs in on the tool's official screen and enters any two-step code themselves. Never ask for a password.
steps.evidence: Who will send, and the account name shown after sign-in.

steps.do: If the owner asks for a new sending tool, create one account only, in the brand's name, on a free plan, following the tool's rules. Sign up with the brand's own address and let the owner read the code; use inbox_address, with inbox_latest for the code, only if the owner prefers that. Terms screens, payment details and identity checks go to the owner.
steps.evidence: The new account's name and sign-in address, or a note that no new account was needed.

steps.do: Check that the sending domain is verified where the sending tool shows domain authentication (SPF and DKIM passing), or ask the owner for a screenshot of it. If it is not verified, keep all emails as drafts and tell the owner which records their domain manager must add; do not switch to another sender.
steps.evidence: The domain's verification status as the tool shows it, with the time it was checked.

steps.do: Find the limits for this round: the tool's daily sending limit, the most the owner wants sent per day, and the date of the last promotional email to this list. If the list got one in the last 72 hours, plan this send for later. When sending from the brand's normal mailbox instead of an email tool, keep to 50 emails a day, sent one by one.
steps.evidence: The daily cap for this round, the last send date, and the earliest send date.

steps.do: Confirm how people unsubscribe: an unsubscribe link the tool adds automatically, or a 'reply STOP' line the owner will honour within 2 days. Check where unsubscribes are recorded, and that the footer can carry the sender's postal address where the law asks for it. Agree that only emails shown in Sent count as sent; drafts and scheduled emails do not.
steps.evidence: The unsubscribe method, where unsubscribes are recorded, and the footer that will be used.

steps.do: Agree on test sends: tests go only to an address the owner names as their own, never to contacts on the list. Any link or attachment in the email must be the brand's own; open each one before the test to check it loads and is the right file.
steps.evidence: The test address the owner named and the list of links and attachments checked.

blockers.do: If the sending domain is not verified, keep the emails as drafts, tell the owner which records are missing, and do not send from a different address.
If the owner has no way to send to their list, ask whether they want one sending tool set up in the brand's name; do not send bulk email from a personal mailbox.
If a two-step code, terms screen or identity check appears, stop and tell the owner which screen and which button; never enter their codes or accept terms for them.
If the signed-in account is a personal address or another brand, stop and ask the owner to switch to the agreed brand account.
If nobody knows where the contact list and its unsubscribes are kept, ask the owner for an export before any segment or send step.
If the tool's plan cannot send this round's volume, show the owner the limit and either send fewer or wait; never upgrade or pay without the owner's written yes.

C-EMAIL-ACCESS.title_zh: 準備已同意Email帳號、登入與授權

deliver_help.sender_address: The From name, From address and Reply-To address. Example: 'Ana at Brand <ana@brand.com>, replies to hello@brand.com'.
deliver_help.sending_tool: The tool the email will be sent from, where the list lives, and whether the sending domain is verified.
deliver_help.who_sends: 'owner' or 'agent browser', plus one line on why.
deliver_help.send_limits: The daily cap for this round, the last promotional send date to this list, and the earliest date this round can go out.
deliver_help.unsubscribe_method: How a reader unsubscribes, where that is recorded, and the footer text that will appear on every email.

C-EM-SEGMENT.title: Pick the opted-in email contacts for this round
C-EM-SEGMENT.purpose: Produce a clean group of contacts who agreed to hear from the brand and match this round's buyer situation, with everyone who must not be emailed removed, because the right readers move the goal's main number and the wrong ones only add unsubscribes and spam reports.

steps.do: Ask the owner for an export or a view of the contact list, and for where each group of contacts came from (signup form, purchase, free trial, event, inquiry). Use only contacts the brand collected itself; never bought, scraped or copied lists, and never addresses found on public pages. Use the export only for this round and do not paste it anywhere public.
steps.evidence: Each source with its contact count and the date it was exported.

steps.do: For each source, write down what people agreed to receive, as stated on the form, checkbox or terms they saw. If a source has no record of what people agreed to, mark it 'consent unknown' and keep it out of this round.
steps.evidence: Each source marked with what was agreed, or 'consent unknown'.

steps.do: Merge duplicates by email address, ignoring upper and lower case. If any copy of a person is unsubscribed, bounced or marked the brand as spam, that person stays out; an import never overrides an unsubscribe.
steps.evidence: Contact counts before and after merging, and how many were kept out by an earlier unsubscribe.

steps.do: Build the exclusion list: unsubscribed, hard bounced, spam complaints, people who replied 'not interested', the owner, the team and test addresses. Leave out people who already bought this product when the email is an offer to buy it.
steps.evidence: The exclusion list with a count per reason.

steps.do: Group the remaining contacts by what they actually did, matching the buyer groups from the earlier segment step: bought before, signed up or tried but did not buy, asked a question or showed clear interest, or subscribed only. Never guess sensitive traits such as health, money trouble, religion or politics.
steps.evidence: Each group with its count and the action that put people in it.

steps.do: Pick the one group that fits this round's chosen angle. If two versions will be tested, split that group at random into two halves labeled A and B (use the tool's own A/B split if it has one, or sort the export at random and take alternate rows). If the group has fewer than 200 contacts, send one version only and note that the result will be noisy.
steps.evidence: The chosen group, its count, and how it was split, if it was.

steps.do: Show the owner the chosen group, its count, the exclusion counts and the 'consent unknown' count, and get their confirmation before anything is written or sent to it. If the group has to be saved as a segment or tag in the owner's tool, do that only after their yes, and never re-subscribe anyone.
steps.evidence: The owner's confirmation of the group to email this round, and the name of the saved segment if one was made.

blockers.do: If you cannot tell what a group of contacts agreed to, keep them out of promotional email and ask the owner where the signup record is.
If the owner cannot export or show the list, ask for a screenshot of the tool's audience page with group counts and stop until it arrives.
If any contacts come from a bought, rented or scraped list, leave them out entirely and tell the owner why.
If you cannot see who has unsubscribed or bounced, do not build the group; ask the owner to export the unsubscribe and bounce list first.
If the chosen group has fewer than 50 contacts, tell the owner the result will not be readable as a rate and ask whether to merge it with the next closest group.

C-EM-SEGMENT.title_zh: 依來源與同意分已可聯絡Email名單

deliver_help.list_sources: Each place contacts came from, what people agreed to receive there, and the count. Example: 'Website newsletter form, agreed to product news, 640 contacts'.
deliver_help.chosen_segment: The group picked for this round, what put people in it, its count, and the A and B split if there is one.
deliver_help.excluded: How many contacts were left out and why, one line per reason.
deliver_help.consent_unknown: How many contacts have no record of agreeing to email, and from which sources; these are kept aside, not sent to.

C-EM-METRICS.title: Read this goal's email numbers
C-EM-METRICS.purpose: Record the numbers this goal is judged on, for the send before this round and for this round's send, so rounds are compared on real counts. record_numbers lists exactly which numbers it needs.

steps.do: Confirm what you are measuring: the sender, which email or campaign, the date range and the time zone. For the baseline use the last comparable send to a similar group before this round; for the current reading use this round's send, read once the goal's observation window has passed (7 days after sending for these goals).
steps.evidence: The email or campaign name, send date, date range with time zone, and whether this is the baseline or the current reading.

steps.do: Read the sending tool's report for that send: sent, bounced, delivered, unsubscribes, spam complaints and unique link clicks. If the tool does not show delivered, use sent minus bounced and say so. If you cannot open the report, ask the owner for a screenshot or an export. Do not use opens; they are not reliable and an open is not a reader.
steps.evidence: The numbers exactly as the tool shows them, the screen or export they came from, and when they were read.

steps.do: Take out the owner's, the team's and test addresses, and count each person once for clicks, unsubscribes and replies. If many clicks arrive within a minute of delivery from the same company domain, note that mail security scanners may have made them.
steps.evidence: What was removed and why, with counts before and after.

steps.do: Read the replies to this send in the mailbox for the same date range. Count a qualified reply once per person who asks about buying, price, fit or a demo. Do not count auto-replies, out-of-office notes, bounces, unsubscribe requests or the owner's own messages.
steps.evidence: The number of qualified replies, with sender, date and one-line summary for each.

steps.do: Read clicks and sales for each version from the round's tracked link (per ?v= label) and its sale counter, and from the owner's payment records for the same dates. Count each order once, take out refunds and test or owner payments, and say plainly where you cannot tell whether a sale came from this email. For unique_link_clicks use the sending tool's unique clicks per recipient where it shows them, otherwise the tracked link's count; use the same source for the baseline and the current reading, and never add the two together.
steps.evidence: Clicks and purchases per version, each with its source, and any sale whose link to the email is unclear.

steps.do: Write down what this send cost: the sending tool's fee for the period and any other cost the owner reports. Keep costs separate from the goal's numbers.
steps.evidence: Each cost with its amount, currency and source, or 'not given by the owner'.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with the exact component names this goal lists: delivered plus one of qualified_replies, unique_link_clicks, external_purchases or unsubscribes. Give each value its source. If there is no earlier send, record 0 and say 'no history' in the source. If delivered is 0 or the delivery data is incomplete, do not work out a rate; report which number is missing. Never estimate a number.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call with every component, its value and its source.

blockers.do: If you cannot open the sending tool's report, ask the owner for a screenshot or export of that send's report and wait for it.
If there is no earlier comparable send, record 0 and say in the source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline.
If sent or delivered counts are missing or still changing, do not work out a rate; report the missing number and read again later.
If the goal's observation window has not passed since the send, report the numbers as early and read them again when it has.
If you cannot separate the owner's or team's test clicks, replies or payments from real ones, say so in the source and do not count them.
If payments cannot be matched to this send, record only what the sale counter shows and state that the rest is unknown; never assign sales by guess.

C-EM-METRICS.title_zh: Email回覆、退訂與付款結果核對

deliver_help.numbers: Each of this goal's metric components by its exact name with the value read, plus any number you could not get, marked missing.
deliver_help.where_read: Where each number came from: the sending tool's report, the mailbox, the round's tracked link, the sale counter or the owner's payment records, with the time it was read.
deliver_help.date_range: The start and end of the period measured, with time zone, and whether it is the baseline or the current reading.

C-EM-SEND.title: Send the approved email to the opted-in group once
C-EM-SEND.purpose: Send the owner-approved email, with the round's tracked link and a working unsubscribe, once to the chosen group, and stop follow-ups to anyone who replied, bought or opted out, because the goal's number can only be read on a send that went out exactly as approved.

steps.do: Gather the approved text from the copy step, the chosen group from the segment step, and the round's tracked link from tracking, with ?v=A and ?v=B if there are two versions. Open each link and see it load the product page.
steps.evidence: The text, the group and its count, and each tracked link you opened.

steps.do: Turn the text into an email: a subject under 60 characters, one main link (the tracked link), the sender name, and a footer with the unsubscribe link or line and the postal address where the law asks for it. Do not put 'Re:' or 'Fwd:' in the subject, and keep only claims the product facts support, with no invented deadlines, stock limits or guarantees.
steps.evidence: The full email for each version: subject, body, link and footer.

steps.do: Show the owner, word for word, the From and Reply-To, subject, body, links, footer, which group and how many people, and the send day and time with time zone. Nothing is sent without their clear yes to this exact email.
steps.evidence: The exact email shown and the owner's approval message.

steps.do: Send one test to the owner's own address only. Check the sender name, subject, that every link opens through the tracked link, that the unsubscribe link or line is there, and that it reads well on a phone. Fix and re-show the owner any change. The test is not counted.
steps.evidence: The test result: what was checked and anything fixed.

steps.do: Right before sending, read the latest unsubscribes, bounces, spam complaints, replies and purchases since the group was built. Remove anyone who unsubscribed, bounced, said no, has no record of agreeing to email, or already bought, and stop any older automatic follow-up to them. The approved count can only go down at this point, never up.
steps.evidence: How many people were removed and why, and which older follow-ups were stopped.

steps.do: The owner sends, or the agent sends with its own browser if it has the tool open and the owner said yes. Send once, only to the approved group, within the daily cap; split across days if needed. Never put many addresses in To or CC. If sending seems to fail, check Sent or the campaign status before trying again; never send twice and never resend through another channel.
steps.evidence: Who sent, when, and to how many people.

steps.do: Open the sent copy or the campaign page and copy the exact subject and body as sent, the number of recipients and the send time. Drafts and scheduled emails do not count as sent. If the tool gives a 'view in browser' link, keep it as the email's public URL.
steps.evidence: The subject and body as sent, the recipient count, the send time, and the web view link if there is one.

steps.do: Do not send a follow-up inside this round's 7-day reading window, so the round's numbers stay clean. If the owner wants one, plan at most one for after the reading, only to people who did not reply, click, buy or unsubscribe, with its own owner yes. Remove anyone who hard bounced and never retry them with a changed spelling.
steps.evidence: The follow-up plan with date and audience, or a note that none will be sent, and the list of bounced addresses removed.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to this exact email, do not send; show them the email and stop until they answer.
If the sending domain is not verified, keep the email as a draft and do not switch to another sender address.
If you cannot tell whether the email went out, check Sent and the campaign status in the sending tool; never send again, or through another channel, until you know.
If an address hard bounces, remove it from this and later sends; never retry it with a changed spelling.
If the group is larger than the daily cap, send the rest on the following days at the same time; never go over the cap the owner set.
If someone in the group has no record of agreeing to email, take them out of this send and tell the owner.

C-EM-SEND.title_zh: 已同意Email序列送出與停止

deliver_help.sent_record: When it was sent, by whom, to which group and how many people, plus the campaign page or web view link if the tool gives one.
deliver_help.sent_text: The exact subject and body of each version as they appear in the sent copy.
deliver_help.owner_approval: The owner's message saying yes to this exact email, with its date.
deliver_help.tracked_links: Each tracked link used in the email, with its version label. Example: 'https://.../r/abc?v=A'.
deliver_help.stopped_contacts: How many people were removed or had follow-ups stopped, and why (unsubscribed, bounced, replied, bought, said no).

C-WEBINAR-ACCESS.title: Confirm the meeting tool, host account and live presenter
C-WEBINAR-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which brand account hosts the live demo, what its plan allows, who presents and where attendance numbers will come from, so the event can run under the right name without upgrades or surprises mid-way.

steps.do: Ask the owner which meeting or webinar tool the brand already uses and which account will host. The host must be the brand's account, not someone else's personal one. Use what exists; do not sign up for a new tool unless the owner asks in this conversation.
steps.evidence: The tool's name and the host account, confirmed by the owner.

steps.do: Decide who creates the event: the owner, or the agent's own browser if it is already signed in to the host account. If nobody is signed in, the owner signs in on the tool's official screen or company sign-in and enters any code themselves. Never ask for a password.
steps.evidence: Who will create the event, and the account name shown after sign-in.

steps.do: Read the plan's limits from the account's plan or billing page, or ask the owner: maximum participants, maximum meeting length, whether registration pages are included, whether recording is included, and whether this host account is allowed to create events. Do not buy an upgrade to get past a limit.
steps.evidence: Each limit with where it was read, or 'not known'.

steps.do: Confirm a real person will present the live demo: their name, role, and two or three dates and times they can do, with time zone. The agent cannot host or present a live session for people.
steps.evidence: The presenter's name and their available slots with time zone.

steps.do: Ask the owner whether the event will be recorded. Record only if the owner agrees and attendees are told at the start; if the tool has its own recording notice, leave it on. Write down where a replay would be shared, if anywhere.
steps.evidence: The recording decision and how attendees will be told.

steps.do: Confirm how people register: the tool's own registration page or a signup form the owner already has. Do not change the product's own signup or its tracking codes. Write down that registrations, people who join and purchases are read later from the tool's registration and attendee reports and the owner's payment records, never before the event happens.
steps.evidence: The registration route and the reports that will be used for the numbers.

blockers.do: If the plan cannot hold the event, show the owner the limit and either plan a smaller event or wait; never upgrade or pay without the owner's written yes.
If no real person has agreed to present, prepare the details but do not create or announce the event.
If a sign-in code, terms screen or identity check appears, stop and tell the owner which screen and which button; never enter codes or accept terms for them.
If the brand has no meeting tool, ask the owner which one they want; set up one free account in the brand's name only after they say so, and leave terms screens and any payment to the owner.
If the signed-in account is personal or belongs to another brand, stop and ask the owner to switch to the agreed host account.

C-WEBINAR-ACCESS.title_zh: 準備線上示範活動帳號、登入與授權

deliver_help.host_account: The meeting tool and the brand account that will host. Example: 'Zoom, events@brand.com'.
deliver_help.who_creates_event: 'owner' or 'agent browser', plus one line on why.
deliver_help.plan_limits: Maximum participants, maximum length, and whether registration and recording are included, each with its source.
deliver_help.presenter: The real person who will present, and the dates and times they can do, with time zone.
deliver_help.attendance_source: Where registrations and attendance will be read after the event, such as the tool's attendee report.

C-WB-METRICS.title: Read this goal's live demo numbers
C-WB-METRICS.purpose: Record the numbers this goal is judged on, for the event before this round and for this round's event, so rounds are compared on real registrations, attendance, meetings and sales. record_numbers lists exactly which numbers it needs.

steps.do: Confirm which event you are measuring: its link or ID, date, time zone, and the date range. For the baseline use the owner's last comparable live event before this round; for the current reading use this round's event, read once the goal's observation window has passed (7 days after the event for these goals). If the event has not happened yet, do not record attendance.
steps.evidence: The event link or ID, its date and time zone, the date range, and whether this is the baseline or the current reading.

steps.do: Read the tool's registration report and attendee report for that event, or ask the owner for an export or screenshot. Count each person once by email, even if they joined twice. Take out the host, presenter, owner, team and any test registration.
steps.evidence: Registrations and attendees as counted, with the report they came from, the time read, and what was removed.

steps.do: Count attendees only as people who joined the live event. Where the attendee report shows time in session, note separately how many stayed at least 10 minutes, and how many watched a replay; replay views are not attendees.
