steps.evidence: Live attendees, those who stayed 10 minutes or more, and replay views, each with its source.

steps.do: List every question asked in the chat or Q&A and every request for a one-to-one demo. Count a confirmed meeting only when a date and time are accepted by both sides in writing or by an accepted calendar invite; requested, unanswered or cancelled meetings do not count. Signing up for the event is not agreement to marketing email.
steps.evidence: Each question, each meeting request, and each confirmed meeting with its date, time and confirmation.

steps.do: Read sales from the round's sale counter and the owner's payment records for the date range. Count each order once, take out refunds and test or owner payments, and match buyers to attendees by email where possible. Say plainly where you cannot tell whether a sale came from the event.
steps.evidence: Purchases with their sources, how many were matched to attendees, and any sale whose link to the event is unclear.

steps.do: Write down what the event cost: the tool's fee for the period, any paid promotion, and presenter time if the owner gives it. Keep costs separate from the goal's numbers.
steps.evidence: Each cost with its amount, currency and source, or 'not given by the owner'.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with the exact component names this goal lists: registrations and attendees, confirmed_meetings, or external_purchases and attendees. Give each value its source. If there is no earlier event, record 0 and say 'no history' in the source. If the number you would divide by is 0, do not work out a rate; report it. Never estimate a number.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call with every component, its value and its source.

blockers.do: If the event has not happened or its attendee report is not ready, report attendance as pending and read again later; never fill it in by guess.
If you cannot open the tool's reports, ask the owner for an export or screenshot of the registration and attendee reports for that event.
If there is no earlier comparable event, record 0 and say in the source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline.
If there were no registrations, record 0, do not work out a rate, and report that the invite step needs attention.
If a meeting request has no accepted date and time, list it as requested and leave it out of confirmed meetings.
If payments cannot be matched to the event, record only what the sale counter shows and state that the rest is unknown; never assign sales by guess.

C-WB-METRICS.title_zh: 活動報名到實際出席及成交核對

deliver_help.numbers: Each of this goal's metric components by its exact name with the value read, plus any number you could not get, marked missing.
deliver_help.where_read: Where each number came from: the tool's registration or attendee report, the mailbox or calendar for meetings, the sale counter or the owner's payment records, with the time it was read.
deliver_help.date_range: The event date and the period measured, with time zone, and whether it is the baseline or the current reading.

C-WB-SCHEDULE.title: Create the live demo event and its registration page
C-WB-SCHEDULE.purpose: Create one real, owner-approved live demo of what the product does today, with a working registration page, because people can only register, attend and buy if a real event with a real presenter exists.

steps.do: Write a short event brief: who it is for (the chosen buyer group), the problem the demo solves (the chosen angle), what will be shown live, the presenter, a length of 30 to 45 minutes, and at least 10 minutes for questions. Show only features the product has today.
steps.evidence: The event brief, with each feature checked against the product facts.

steps.do: Pick a date and time at least 7 days ahead, in the main time zone of the buyer group, avoiding public holidays there. The owner and the presenter both confirm the slot.
steps.evidence: The date, time and time zone, and the owner's and presenter's confirmation.

steps.do: Look in the host account for an event already scheduled for this demo. If one exists, update that event instead of creating a second one.
steps.evidence: A note that no matching event exists, or the link of the existing one that will be used.

steps.do: Draft the event page: title, a short description of what attendees will see, date and time with time zone, length, presenter, and registration questions (name, email, and one optional 'what do you want to see?'). State facts only; no invented seat limits, bonuses or results. Show the owner the page text word for word and get a clear yes.
steps.evidence: The exact event page text and the owner's approval message.

steps.do: Create the event once in the host account: the owner does it, or the agent's own browser if signed in and the owner said yes. Turn registration on, keep capacity within the plan limit, and turn on the tool's reminder emails if it has them. If creating seems to fail, check the event list before trying again.
steps.evidence: The event ID and the registration page URL.

steps.do: Open the registration page as a visitor and check that it loads with the right title, date, time zone and presenter. If you make a test registration, use the owner's own address, check the confirmation carries the join link, and note it so it is taken out of the counts.
steps.evidence: Confirmation that the page loads correctly and the join link arrives, and any test registration noted.

steps.do: Hand over the event as 'waiting for the event'. Do not report any attendance, recording or replay until the event has happened and the tool's attendee report exists. If the time must change later, update this same event and tell registrants once.
steps.evidence: The event status, its date, and where attendance will be read after it.

blockers.do: If no presenter has confirmed the slot, keep the event as a draft and do not open registration.
If the plan cannot hold the expected number of people, show the owner the limit and set a smaller capacity; never upgrade without the owner's written yes.
If the owner has not said yes to the event page text, do not create or publish the event; show them the text and stop until they answer.
If an event for this demo already exists, update it instead of creating another, so registrants do not get two invitations.
If a feature in the brief is not live in the product, remove it from the agenda and the page; never demo or promise what does not exist.

C-WB-SCHEDULE.title_zh: 建立既有產品線上示範活動

deliver_help.event_id: The event's ID or link inside the host account.
deliver_help.registration_url: The public registration page, opened and confirmed to load.
deliver_help.event_details: Title, date, start time with time zone, length and capacity, exactly as the event page shows them.
deliver_help.presenter_confirmed: The presenter's name and the message where they confirmed the slot, or 'pending'.
deliver_help.attendance_source: The report that will give registrations and attendance after the event, such as the tool's attendee report.

C-WB-INVITE.title: Invite opted-in people to the live demo and follow up
C-WB-INVITE.purpose: Invite only people who agreed to hear from the brand or asked for a demo, with a personal, owner-approved message and the registration link from the first step, then remind registrants and follow up on questions, because the right invitations decide who registers, who shows up and who books or buys after.

steps.do: Open the event's registration page and confirm it exists and shows the right title, date, time zone and presenter. Ask tracking for the round's tracked link; use it only if it can point at the registration page, with ?v=A and ?v=B if there are two invite versions. Otherwise use the registration page URL itself and read registrations from the tool's report.
steps.evidence: The registration page URL you opened and the link each invite version will carry.

steps.do: Choose who to invite: contacts who agreed to hear from the brand, people who asked for a demo in an existing conversation, and communities whose rules allow event posts. Leave out anyone who unsubscribed, said no, already registered, or already bought (unless the demo is for customers). Keep to the owner's cap; for personal messages, at most 30 a day.
steps.evidence: The invite list or groups, the reason each is included, and the counts.

steps.do: Write one invite under 120 words that names the reader's problem, what they will see, the date and time in their time zone, the length, the presenter, and the registration link from the first step. Say who is sending and that they run the product. No invented seat limits, deadlines or results. Emails carry the unsubscribe link or line.
steps.evidence: The invite text for each version, with its word count.

steps.do: Show the owner, word for word, each invite version, the channel, and who will receive it, and get a clear yes before anything is sent or posted.
steps.evidence: The exact invites shown and the owner's approval message.

steps.do: Send through the brand's own channel: the owner's email tool, or a reply in the existing conversation. The agent sends only with its own tools and the owner's yes; otherwise the owner sends. Send each invite once; if status is unclear, check Sent before retrying, and never resend through another channel. A community post ends with its public URL.
steps.evidence: Who sent, when, how many invites went out, and the public URL of any post.

steps.do: Remind registrants once 24 hours before and once at the start, unless the tool already sends reminders. Send non-registrants at most one follow-up, no sooner than 3 days after the first invite and never after the event. The owner approves the reminder and follow-up text.
steps.evidence: Each reminder or follow-up with its text, date, audience and the owner's approval.

steps.do: After the event, within 24 hours, draft a short personal reply for each attendee who asked a question or asked for a one-to-one demo: answer from the product facts and offer two times the presenter has confirmed, or the owner's booking link. Only these people get it, and only after the owner approves the text. Any link to the product uses the round's tracked link.
steps.evidence: The list of people followed up, each message as sent, and any times they accepted.

steps.do: Keep invites sent, registrations, attendees, replay views, meetings and purchases separate. Never report invites as registrations; pass the event to the measuring step.
steps.evidence: A short record of what was sent and what is still waiting for the event or its reports.

blockers.do: If the registration page does not load or shows the wrong details, stop and go back to the event step before inviting anyone.
If the owner has not said yes to this exact invite, do not send or post; show them the text and stop until they answer.
If you cannot tell whether a person agreed to hear from the brand, leave them out of the invite.
If you cannot tell whether an invite went out, check Sent or the conversation first; never send it again or through a different channel.
If someone replies no or asks to stop, remove them from all reminders and follow-ups at once and record it.
If the presenter cancels, do not send invites; tell the owner and move the event to a new confirmed time first.

C-WB-INVITE.title_zh: 向可聯絡對象邀請既有示範活動

deliver_help.invite_text: The exact text of each invite, reminder and follow-up as sent.
deliver_help.recipients: Who was invited, by group, with the reason they could be contacted and the counts.
deliver_help.owner_approval: The owner's message saying yes to these exact texts, with its date.
deliver_help.sent_record: When each invite, reminder and follow-up went out, how many, by whom, and the public URL of any community post.
deliver_help.tracked_links: Each link used in the invites, with its version label, and whether it is a tracked link or the registration page itself. Example: 'https://.../r/abc?v=B'.

S02.title: Find who buys and why now
S02.purpose: Find the groups of people most likely to buy and what makes them start looking now, so later copy speaks to a real situation instead of to everyone.

steps.do: Read the product and this round's goal: first users, trials, purchases, or repeat purchases.
steps.evidence: The research goal matches what is actually on offer.

steps.do: List candidate situations of use: propose groups by the real task, what they use instead today, and the kind of user.
steps.evidence: Each group describes a concrete situation.

steps.do: Collect what people say about the need in their own words: public discussions, questions, reviews, interviews, and the context of past purchases.
steps.evidence: Each quote has a date, a source, and its situation.

steps.do: Separate who uses it from who pays: work out who operates it, who benefits, and who pays or approves.
steps.evidence: Each role has a source; unknown roles stay unknown.

steps.do: Write down the result each group wants: time saved, money saved, income, convenience, peace of mind, status, or another real motive.
steps.evidence: Each motive links to a quote and a situation.

steps.do: Find why they start looking for a solution now: an event, a deadline, more work, or a current solution that stopped working.
steps.evidence: Each group has a trigger that can be observed.

steps.do: List hesitations and reasons not to buy: trust, price, effort to learn, habits, and risk.
steps.evidence: Each hesitation matches a real question someone asked.

steps.do: Mark the buying stage: just noticed the problem, comparing options, ready to buy, or already bought.
steps.evidence: Content and follow-up can be chosen by stage.

steps.do: Compare the groups on strength of need, ways to reach them, cost, and fit with the product.
steps.evidence: The order of priority has a stated reason.

steps.do: Hand over a table of groups and messages: for each group the situation, motive, evidence, hesitations, and angles worth testing.
steps.evidence: Later steps can use the table directly.

steps.do: Revise the groups when real results come in: new replies, trials, and payments.
steps.evidence: Earlier versions are kept with the reason for each change.

blockers.do: If you cannot find people describing the need in their own words, ask the owner for customer messages or reviews, and label every group as a guess.
If all you have is age, gender, or job title, do not build groups from it; ask the owner what happened just before recent customers bought.

S02.title_zh: 找出誰會買、為什麼現在買

deliver_help.sourced_segments: The groups, each with its situation, trigger, motive and the quotes behind it.
deliver_help.hypotheses: What you believe about each group that is not yet proven.
deliver_help.unknowns: What is still unknown, such as who pays or how big each group is.

S33.title: Read the goal's numbers and check them against payments and costs
S33.purpose: Record the goal's real numbers for one period, with test activity, duplicates and refunds removed and costs listed, so each round is judged on what truly happened.

steps.do: Get the goal's exact metric component names from record_numbers (for example qualified_inquiries and eligible_exposures). Set the date range, time zone and currency. For the baseline, use a period of the same length just before this round; for the current reading, use the round's own observation period.
steps.evidence: The component names, the date range with time zone, and the currency.

steps.do: List every source the owner already has: post insights, the ad account's reporting, the round's tracked link and sale counter from tracking, form responses, the inbox, and payment records such as the payment provider's dashboard. Note who can open each one. Do not install new tracking code.
steps.evidence: Each source, what it covers, and whether you or the owner can read it.

steps.do: Read each component from those sources, with the time you read it. For an exposures component, use the reach or views number the channel shows for this round's posts, and say which one you used. If you cannot open a source, ask the owner for a screenshot or export.
steps.evidence: The raw number for each component, its source, and the time it was read.

steps.do: Match each result to the post, ad or version it came from (for example ?v=A or ?v=B). If you cannot tell where a result came from, mark it unknown; do not give it to the version that seems most likely.
steps.evidence: Results split by version, with unknown results listed apart.

steps.do: Remove duplicates and tests. Count each person and each order once. Leave out the owner's, the team's and the agent's own messages and purchases, test-mode payments, and bots.
steps.evidence: What was removed and why, with the count before and after.

steps.do: Qualify the results. An inquiry or response counts only when the person states a real need or a wanted outcome that the product meets, not just praise or a like. A purchase counts only when it is paid, in the date range, and not refunded; unpaid invoices and abandoned checkouts do not count.
steps.evidence: The list of counted inquiries, responses or purchases, each with its link or order reference.

steps.do: List the round's costs: ad spend, platform and payment fees, tools, and delivery costs, each with its source. If a payment covers work not yet delivered, note the delivery cost still owed and keep that money apart from money that is free to use. An unknown cost stays unknown, never zero. Keep different currencies separate unless you have a stated rate.
steps.evidence: The cost list with sources, any money held for future delivery, and any unknown items named.

steps.do: Pass each component to record_numbers under its exact name, with the source in source. If there is no history, record 0 and say so in source. Never estimate a number; if a component cannot be read, say which and why.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call with every component and its source.

steps.do: Note the limits of what the numbers show: what the platform reports, what the tracked link and sale counter show, and what the payment records confirm. Without a comparison group, do not claim the round caused the change.
steps.evidence: A short note on where each number comes from and what it cannot prove.

blockers.do: If no source shows a component, ask the owner whether they have one; if not, say so plainly and do not estimate.
If there is no history for these numbers, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline.
If you cannot open payment records, ask the owner for an export or screenshot of payments and refunds for the date range.
If you cannot tell test or owner activity from real buyers, leave those items out and list them as unverified.
If sources use different currencies and there is no stated rate, keep them separate and do not add them together.
If the denominator component is 0, record the real numbers and say the rate cannot be worked out yet; never report it as 0% or 100%.

S33.title_zh: 彙整成效並核對付款與成本

deliver_help.numbers: Each metric component under its exact name with its value, as passed to record_numbers.
deliver_help.where_read: For each number, the source it came from and the time you read it, or 'no history' or 'not available' with the reason.
deliver_help.date_range: The start and end of the period measured, with the time zone.

C-X-REPLY.title: Reply helpfully to a public request on X
C-X-REPLY.purpose: Post one approved, helpful reply under a public X post where someone asked for help the product gives, because a useful answer in the original thread is what turns a public request into a real conversation.

steps.do: Take one post from the list of public requests and open it again with read_page, or ask the owner to open it if it does not load. Confirm it is still up, less than 7 days old, that replies are open to the owner's account, and that the owner's account has not already replied there.
steps.evidence: The post URL, its date, and confirmation that a reply is allowed and none was sent yet.

steps.do: Re-read the person's exact words and the rest of the thread. Check whether they or anyone in the thread said they do not want product suggestions, and whether they already found a solution; if so, skip this post.
steps.evidence: The person's exact words, and a note that they still need help and have not opted out.

steps.do: Draft a reply that first answers their actual question with one concrete, useful tip. Mention the product only if it truly fits, and say plainly that the owner makes it, for example 'I built X'. Keep it under 280 characters unless the account can post longer.
steps.evidence: The draft reply with its character count.

steps.do: Check every claim against the product fact sheet. Add a link only if the person asked for a tool or recommendation; then use the round's tracked link, with ?v=A or ?v=B if several reply versions are being compared. Do not offer to move to DMs or email unless they asked.
steps.evidence: The claims checked against facts, and the exact link used or 'no link'.

steps.do: Show the owner the original post and the exact reply text and get a clear yes before anything is posted.
steps.evidence: The owner's approval message for this exact reply.

steps.do: Keep volume small and personal: at most 5 replies a day from the account, each written for its post, never the same text twice, and at least 10 minutes apart. Follow X's rules on automation and spam.
steps.evidence: The count of replies sent today, including this one.

steps.do: Post the reply once: the owner posts it, or the agent posts it after the owner's yes only through a posting tool that uses X's official API, never by driving x.com in a browser. If posting seemed to fail, check the thread before trying again so nothing is posted twice.
steps.evidence: Who posted the reply and when.

steps.do: Open the reply's public URL and confirm the text, the author handle, and that it sits under the right post.
steps.evidence: The reply URL, its text as shown, and the parent post URL.

steps.do: Check the thread again after 48 hours and record whether the person answered and what they said. If they ask a question, draft one answer and get the owner's yes before it is posted; if they say no or do not answer, do not post in that thread again.
steps.evidence: The person's response word for word, or 'no response after 48 hours'.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to this exact reply, do not post it; show them and wait.
If the author limits who can reply, skip the post; never mention them in a new post or send a DM instead.
If the owner's account already replied to this person about this need, or they asked not to be contacted, skip them.
If 5 replies were already sent today or X shows a limit message, stop and continue the next day.
If the agent has no posting tool that uses X's official API, give the owner the reply text and post link, and ask them to send back the reply URL.
If the reply does not show under the post, check the thread and the account's replies again after a few minutes before any retry, and never post the same text twice.

deliver_help.reply_url: The public link to the live reply, opened and confirmed to load.
deliver_help.published_text: The full reply text exactly as it appears on X.
deliver_help.parent_post_url: The URL of the post the reply answers.
deliver_help.response: What the person said back, word for word, or 'no response after 48 hours'.

C-SE-ACCESS.title: Check what search data, analytics, and outlets the owner has
C-SE-ACCESS.purpose: Find out which search reports and site analytics the owner can show, which product pages search engines can index, and which outside places can carry content, so the round measures real numbers and only uses outlets that already exist.

steps.do: Ask the owner whether the product site is in Google Search Console, and if so for the exact property: a whole domain (example.com) or one URL prefix (https://example.com/). Confirm the property matches the product's own site, not another brand or an old domain.
steps.evidence: The property address, its type (domain or URL prefix), and the owner's confirmation that it is the product's site, or a note that there is no Search Console property.

steps.do: If a property exists, the owner signs in themselves and sends a screenshot or export of the Performance report, or gives read-only access to a person they choose. Never ask for a password. If the site still needs verification or a DNS change, write it down as an owner task and do not change the site yourself.
steps.evidence: How the search numbers will reach you (screenshot, export, or read-only access), or the exact verification task left for the owner.

steps.do: Ask the owner which site analytics they already use, and whether it can show visits by source (organic search, and each outside site that links in) and visits that reached the pricing or sign-up page. Do not install analytics or add tracking code yourself.
steps.evidence: The analytics tool's name, whether it splits visits by source, and how the owner will share it (screenshot or read-only access), or a note that there is none.

steps.do: Fix the settings every later reading will use: country, language, device, search type (web), and time zone. The most recent days of Search Console data are often incomplete, so plan to read only dates at least 3 days old.
steps.evidence: One line with country, language, device, search type, time zone, and the 3-day settling delay.

steps.do: Decide which AI answer tools will be sampled (for example Google's AI answers, ChatGPT search, or Perplexity), in which region and language, and who runs each one: the agent in its own browser if it has one, or the owner by screenshot. Keep AI answer samples separate from Search Console totals; one is never used as the other.
steps.evidence: The list of AI answer tools, the region and language, and who will run each one.

steps.do: Use read_page to open the product's main pages and its /robots.txt. List the pages a buyer would land on, and mark any page that robots.txt blocks or that shows a noindex tag where you can see it. Do not add structured data or new pages; report problems to the owner as product tasks.
steps.evidence: A list of product URLs, each marked indexable, blocked, or unknown, with the reason for any block.

steps.do: List the outside places that can already carry content about the product: the owner's own blog or newsletter, the owner's profiles on publishing sites, and publications that have run the owner's writing before or publicly invite contributions.
steps.evidence: A list of outlet URLs, each with how content gets published there and who controls it.

blockers.do: If the site has no Search Console property, continue with public search research only and record search report numbers as not available, never guessed.
If adding the property needs a site file or DNS record, submit the step as blocked and tell the owner exactly which record or file Search Console asks for; do not change the site yourself.

If the owner has no site analytics that split visits by source, tell them visit-based numbers will rest only on the tracked link's click count, and let them decide whether to add analytics themselves.
If key product pages are blocked by robots.txt or noindex, write down the page and the reason and hand it to the owner as a product fix; do not promise any ranking or citation.
If the property the owner shows belongs to another site or brand, do not use its numbers and ask the owner for the property of the product's own site.

C-SE-ACCESS.title_zh: 搜尋與AI答案能見度身分、資格與可用工具核對

deliver_help.search_property: The Search Console property address and type, or 'none' if the owner has no property.
deliver_help.report_access: How search numbers and site analytics will be obtained (screenshot, export, read-only access, or none), plus the fixed country, language, device, and time zone.
deliver_help.indexable_pages: Each product URL a buyer would land on, marked indexable, blocked, or unknown, with the reason for any block.
deliver_help.outlets: Each outside place that can carry content about the product, with its URL and who publishes there.

C-SE-QUERY.title: Find the searches buyers type before they buy
C-SE-QUERY.purpose: Build a list of real buyer searches, grouped by problem, comparison, alternative, and purchase, and checked against live results and the product's facts, so outside articles target searches that bring buyers who can actually use the product.

steps.do: Fix the market for the research before searching: country, language, and the date you search. Use the same settings for every search so results can be compared.
steps.evidence: One line with country, language, and search date.

steps.do: Start from the buyer quotes and product facts already collected. Write searches in the buyers' own words, sorted into four groups: problem ('how to ...'), comparison ('X vs Y'), alternative ('X alternative'), and purchase ('X price', 'best X for ...'). Write at least 20 searches with at least 3 in each group, not just category words.
steps.evidence: A table of at least 20 searches in four groups, each with the buyer quote or fact it came from.

steps.do: Check each search against the product facts. Remove any search that needs a feature, price, or market the product does not have today, and list it as excluded with the reason.
steps.evidence: An excluded list, each search with the missing fact that ruled it out.

steps.do: Run the 10 most promising remaining searches with your own web search. Look at the first 10 results of each and open the top 3. Note what kind of page ranks (guide, comparison, forum thread, product page), whether the product or a competitor appears, and what question the top results leave unanswered.
steps.evidence: For each of the 10 searches, the result URLs, the page types, and one unanswered question or 'fully answered'.

steps.do: Where a search shows demand only through forum posts or comments, count how many different people asked it. The same person asking twice, or the same thread seen twice, counts once.
steps.evidence: For forum-based searches, the number of different people and the thread URLs.

steps.do: Pick 3 to 5 searches where the product is a true answer and the current results leave a gap. For each, write a short brief for an outside article or guest post: the search, the reader's situation, the gap to fill, the product facts to use, and the product page to link with the round's tracked link.
steps.evidence: Three to five article briefs, each tied to one search and one tracked product link.

steps.do: If a search shows the product's own site is missing a page, list it as a site gap for the owner. Do not edit the site.
steps.evidence: A list of site gaps, or a note that none were found.

blockers.do: If there are no buyer quotes to start from, go back to the buyer quote step before writing searches.
If you cannot run web searches, ask the owner to run the 10 searches and send screenshots of the first page of results.
If you cannot see how often a search is made, say so in limitations and rank by fit with the product, never by an invented volume.
If almost every search needs features the product lacks, stop and tell the owner which searches buyers make and which facts are missing.
If the round has no tracked link yet, call tracking to get one before writing the briefs.

C-SE-QUERY.title_zh: 搜尋買方問題、替代與比較情境

deliver_help.query_groups: The searches in four groups (problem, comparison, alternative, purchase), each with the quote or fact it came from.
deliver_help.source_urls: The result URLs you read for each checked search, with the country, language, and search date.
deliver_help.excluded_queries: Searches you dropped because the product cannot answer them today, each with the reason.
deliver_help.article_briefs: Three to five briefs for outside articles, each naming the search, the gap, the facts to use, and the tracked link.
deliver_help.limitations: What this research cannot show, such as search volume you could not see, demand seen in only one forum, or questions that still need buyer interviews.

C-PR-ACCESS.title: Confirm the pitch address, routes and story kit for press
C-PR-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which address sends pitches, which kinds of coverage are on the table, and which true facts and stories the brand can offer, so every pitch that follows is credible and costs nothing the owner did not approve.

steps.do: Ask the owner which email address will send pitches and reply to editors. Prefer an address on the brand's own domain, and check that the domain matches the product site. The owner signs in to that mailbox themselves; never ask for a password.
steps.evidence: The sending address, the brand domain, and who will press Send (the owner, or the agent's own email tool if it has one).

steps.do: Ask the owner whether they already have contacts or past coverage: outlets that featured them, podcasts they joined, newsletters that mentioned them, or a contributor profile on a publication. Open each public page that shows it.
steps.evidence: A list of existing relationships and past coverage, each with its URL, or a note that there are none.

steps.do: Ask the owner which kinds of coverage this round may use: editorial (a writer covers the story for free), guest (guest article, podcast guest, newsletter feature) and paid (sponsorship, paid placement). Paid routes are only listed for the owner, never bought.
steps.evidence: The kinds of coverage allowed this round, each labeled editorial, guest or paid.

steps.do: Build a story kit from things the brand owns: product facts, any original data or research, a short demo, the founder's real background, and images the owner holds the rights to. Ask the owner for a founder bio under 100 words. Never borrow another company's numbers.
steps.evidence: The story kit, with the source of every fact and the owner's confirmation that each image may be used.

steps.do: Ask the owner what must stay private or wait: launch dates, unreleased features, customer names. Use a customer's name or result only if that customer has agreed to it.
steps.evidence: A short list of what can be shared now and what cannot, in the owner's words.

steps.do: Ask the owner for the spending limit in writing. The default is zero. If any outlet quotes a fee for a slot, write down the outlet, the price and what it includes, and bring it to the owner as a decision.
steps.evidence: The owner's written spending limit, and any quotes listed as open decisions.

steps.do: Get the round's tracked link from tracking and open it once to confirm it reaches the product page. This is the link every pitch and every published piece should carry.
steps.evidence: The tracked link and confirmation that it loads the product page.

blockers.do: If the owner has no address on the brand's domain, ask which address they want to use; do not create a new mailbox unless the owner asks for one.
If the story kit has no fact, data or story a journalist would find new, tell the owner plainly and suggest what could be built first, instead of pitching with nothing.
If a route only works by paying, list the price and terms for the owner and do not buy anything.
If you are unsure whether a fact, name or image may be shared, leave it out until the owner confirms.
If signing in asks for a code, a terms screen or an identity check, tell the owner which screen needs them and wait; never enter it for them.

C-PR-ACCESS.title_zh: 客座、媒體與電子報曝光身分、資格與可用工具核對

deliver_help.sending_address: The email address pitches go from, and who presses Send.
deliver_help.routes: Each kind of coverage the round may use, labeled editorial, guest or paid, with any existing contact or past coverage.
deliver_help.story_kit: The facts, data, demo, founder bio and images that may be used, each with its source.
deliver_help.spend_limit: The owner's written spending limit (zero by default) and any paid quotes waiting for a decision.

C-PR-FIND.title: Find outlets whose audience matches the buyer and invites pitches
C-PR-FIND.purpose: Produce a short list of active newsletters, podcasts and publications that reach the buyer and publicly invite pitches or guests, because a pitch only moves the goal's main number when the outlet's readers are the people who buy.

steps.do: Write 5 to 10 search phrases from the buyer's situation and problem, such as '<buyer situation> newsletter', '<problem> podcast', '<topic> write for us' or '<topic> be a guest'. Run them with web search and note each phrase and the date.
steps.evidence: The list of phrases used, each with the date it was run.

steps.do: For each candidate outlet, open its three most recent issues, episodes or articles. Keep it only if it published something in the last 60 days and its recent topics match the buyer's problem. Do not judge an outlet by its subscriber count.
steps.evidence: Each outlet's URL, the three recent pieces read, their dates, and a one-line note on who they are for.

steps.do: Find how the outlet asks to be contacted: a 'write for us' page, a pitch or guest form, or an editor's address published on the outlet's own site. Record that URL. If there is no public invitation, exclude the outlet. Never guess an address pattern or collect personal emails.
steps.evidence: For each kept outlet, the URL of its public contact or submission page.

steps.do: Label each route: editorial pitch, guest article, podcast guest, newsletter feature, or paid sponsorship. Put paid sponsorships in a separate list for the owner to decide on.
steps.evidence: Each outlet labeled by route, with paid options listed apart.

steps.do: For each outlet, write one fit reason that links a recent piece of theirs to a real story, demo or data point from the story kit. Keep what the outlet says it wants separate from your own guess about fit. Drop outlets where the brand has nothing new to add.
steps.evidence: A fit reason per outlet, with the outlet's stated wish and your inferred fit written separately.

steps.do: Check whether the brand has already pitched each outlet: ask the owner, search the sending mailbox, and, if the owner already uses a CRM, look there too. Exclude any outlet that said no or asked not to be contacted, and any outlet pitched in the last 30 days that has not answered.
steps.evidence: Each outlet marked new, already pitched, declined, or waiting, with the source of that status.

steps.do: Keep at most 15 outlets, ranked by fit. Hand back three groups: qualified, excluded, and unknown, each with a reason. If fewer than three qualify, report the true number.
steps.evidence: The ranked list of up to 15 qualified outlets, plus the excluded and unknown groups with reasons.

blockers.do: If an outlet has no public way to pitch or apply as a guest, exclude it; do not guess an email address.
If the only contact covers a different topic or section, look for the right page on the outlet's own site, and exclude the outlet if there is none.
If the brand pitched this outlet before, keep its status and do not add it again this round.
If the only route is paid, list the price and terms for the owner and move on; never buy a slot.
If the searches find no fitting outlet, change the phrases once using the buyer's own words, then report the true zero.

C-PR-FIND.title_zh: 媒體、Podcast與電子報適配窗口研究

deliver_help.outlets: The qualified outlets in rank order, each with its URL, route type and public contact or submission page.
deliver_help.fit_reasons: For each qualified outlet, the recent piece it published and the true story or data from the kit that fits it.
deliver_help.exclusions: Outlets left out and why. Example: 'no public contact page' or 'declined in March'.
deliver_help.search_phrases: The phrases you searched and the date of each.

C-SE-METRICS.title: Read this goal's search numbers for the round
C-SE-METRICS.purpose: Record the numbers this goal is judged on, with the same settings and counting rules before and after the round, so search visits or AI answer citations are compared on real numbers. record_numbers lists exactly which numbers it needs.

steps.do: Read the goal's metric components in where_are_we and use those exact names. Confirm whether this is the baseline or the current reading, the date range (the goal watches 168 hours, so 7 full days), the time zone, and the country, language, and device settings fixed earlier.
steps.evidence: The component names, baseline or current, the date range with time zone, and the fixed settings.

steps.do: At the baseline, write one counting rule per component and keep it unchanged for the current reading. For a qualified visit, use a rule such as 'reached the pricing or sign-up page, or stayed 30 seconds or more'. For an AI answer citation, reuse the eligible and verified citation rules written in the AI answer audit.
steps.evidence: One sentence per component saying exactly what counts, identical for baseline and current.

steps.do: For visit components, count clicks on the round's tracked links with tracking, and read site visits from the analytics the owner already uses, split into organic search and visits from outside articles. Ask the owner for a screenshot if you cannot open the analytics. Never add the same visit to two sources; if the source cannot be told apart, mark it unknown and leave it out.
steps.evidence: Visit numbers per source, with the screen or counter each was read from and the time it was read.

steps.do: For citation components, ask the same fixed question list from the AI answer audit again, in the same tools, region, language, and number of runs per question. Count the eligible questions and the verified citations under the written rules, and save each answer's text and cited URLs.
steps.evidence: The questions asked, each marked eligible or not and cited or not, with the date, tool, and saved answer.

steps.do: Check the data is complete: search report days that have not settled, rows hidden for low volume, or tracking that started mid-range. Never fill a gap with an estimate. If a number is missing only because it has not settled, read again later instead of recording it.
steps.evidence: A note on each gap and why it exists, or 'complete'.

steps.do: If a goal component counts sales, read them only from the sale counter or the owner's payment records, or from their CRM if the owner already uses a CRM. Remove refunds, test payments, the owner's own purchases, and duplicate orders. Search clicks are never counted as sales.
steps.evidence: Sales figures with their source and what was removed and why, or 'not used by this goal'.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with each component under its exact name and a source that names the report, link counter, analytics screen, or answer log and the date range. If there is no history for a component (for example, no outside article has run yet), record 0 and say so in source. If a denominator is 0, report no rate change.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call with every component, its value, and its source.

blockers.do: If a visit component needs site analytics and you cannot open it, submit blocked and ask the owner for one screenshot of their analytics for the date range; do not estimate.
If the last days of the range have not settled in the search report, read again three days later instead of reporting partial numbers as final.
If there is no history for a component, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline.
If the counting rule or the question list differs from the baseline, do not compare; redo the reading with the baseline rule and list.
If a tool gives no AI answer for a question, save the question, region, and time and count it under the written rule; never treat one answer as a lasting placement.

C-SE-METRICS.title_zh: 搜尋曝光到合格流量與既有付款核對

deliver_help.numbers: Each goal component under its exact name with the value you recorded.
deliver_help.where_read: For each number, the report, link counter, analytics screen, or answer log it came from, and the counting rule used.
deliver_help.date_range: The start and end date with time zone, and whether this is the baseline or the current reading.

C-PR-PITCH.title: Send one tailored, approved pitch to each chosen outlet
C-PR-PITCH.purpose: Send a short, personal pitch to each qualified outlet through the route it invites, and follow it until it goes live or closes, because accepted pieces that carry the tracked link are what bring visitors and inquiries.

steps.do: For each outlet on the list, open its contact or submission page again and confirm it is still open to this kind of pitch. Search the sending mailbox for any earlier pitch, reply, refusal or opt-out. Skip any outlet that declined or asked not to be contacted.
steps.evidence: Each outlet marked ready or skipped, with the reason.

steps.do: Write one pitch per outlet. Subject line under 60 characters. Body under 200 words: name a recent piece of theirs, give the angle, two or three facts from the story kit, what you can deliver (an article draft, an interview, data, a demo), and the sender's real name, the brand and their role in it. Follow any word limit or form fields the outlet sets.
steps.evidence: One draft per outlet, with its word count and the outlet's own requirements noted.

steps.do: Where the pitch links to the product, use the round's tracked link. If you are testing two angles across similar outlets, add ?v=A to one angle and ?v=B to the other, and change only the angle.
steps.evidence: Each draft's link, with its version label if there are two angles.

steps.do: Check every sentence against the story kit. Remove any number, result, customer name or promise you cannot support, and never promise the outlet traffic or sales. Respect anything the owner said must stay private.
steps.evidence: Each draft with its claims listed and the source for each.

steps.do: Show the owner each pitch word for word, with the address or form it goes to. Send no more than 10 pitches in a round. Nothing goes out without the owner's yes.
steps.evidence: The approved drafts and the owner's approval message.

steps.do: Send each pitch once, to one person or form per outlet. The owner sends it from the sending address, or the agent sends it with its own email tool only if it has one and the owner said yes. For a form, submit it once. If sending seems to fail, check the sent folder or confirmation page before trying again.
steps.evidence: For each pitch: recipient or form URL, subject, time sent, and any confirmation number or message link.

steps.do: Wait at least 7 days, or the response time the outlet states, before one short follow-up in the same email thread, approved by the owner. Send no more than one follow-up, and never resend the pitch with a new subject line.
steps.evidence: For each outlet: waiting, replied, declined, or followed up once, with dates.

steps.do: When an outlet says yes, share only approved material and bring any fee, contract or paid slot to the owner as a decision. When the piece goes live, open its public URL, note the publish or air date, and check that it carries the tracked link.
steps.evidence: For each accepted pitch: what was agreed, the public URL once live, the date, and the link it carries.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to a pitch's exact text and recipient, do not send it; show it to them and wait.
If the outlet or person declined or asked not to be contacted, stop and record it; never contact them again this round.
If the outlet replies that this is the wrong contact, use only a contact they name or one on their own site; never guess an address.
If the outlet says it is reviewing, keep the date and their stated timeline, and do not resend or follow up early.
If the outlet asks for payment, give the owner the exact price and terms and do not pay or agree to anything.
If the outlet wants material the owner has not cleared, ask the owner before sending it.

C-PR-PITCH.title_zh: 限定窗口的客座、受訪與電子報提案

deliver_help.pitches_sent: Each pitch sent: outlet, recipient or form URL, subject, time sent, and version label if any.
deliver_help.approved_text: The exact text of each pitch as the owner approved it.
deliver_help.replies: Each outlet's status: waiting, declined, accepted, or followed up, with the date and a one-line summary.
deliver_help.live_urls: Public URLs of any piece that went live, with its date and whether it carries the tracked link.

C-SE-AI.title: Audit how AI answers mention and cite the product
C-SE-AI.purpose: Ask a fixed set of buyer questions in AI answer tools, record whether each answer cites the product correctly, and list true content that could earn a citation, so the goal's main number is measured and moved on facts.

steps.do: Before looking at any answer, write a fixed list of 10 to 20 buyer questions from the buyer quotes and search research, plus the tools, region, language, and device you will use. This list stays the same for every later reading.
steps.evidence: The numbered question list and the sampling settings, dated before the first answer was read.

steps.do: Write the counting rules: which questions are eligible (the product is a true answer to them), what counts as a mention (the name appears), and what counts as a verified citation (the answer links to a page about the product and states its facts correctly). Ask each question 3 times per tool and count a result only if it appears in at least 2 of the 3 answers.
steps.evidence: Three one-sentence rules (eligible, mention, verified citation) and the 2-of-3 rule.

steps.do: Ask each question in each chosen tool, in your own browser if you have one, or ask the owner to run them and send screenshots of each full answer. Save the full answer text, every cited URL, the tool, and the time.
steps.evidence: Three saved answers per question per tool, with their cited URLs and times.

steps.do: Sort each question into: no AI answer, answer without the product, product mentioned without a link, or verified citation. Note which competitors and which outside pages are cited instead.
steps.evidence: A table of every question with its class and the pages cited in its place.

steps.do: Check every statement about the product in the answers against the current product facts, such as price, features, and who it is for. List each wrong or outdated statement and the page it seems to come from.
steps.evidence: A list of wrong statements, each with the correct fact and the source page, or 'none found'.

steps.do: Open the 3 to 5 outside pages the answers cite most and note what they offer: a comparison, a how-to, or original data. Suggest 2 to 4 true pieces the owner could publish through outlets they already have, such as an honest comparison or a guide with real results. Never plan fake reviews, mass-produced pages, or posts that pretend to be independent.
steps.evidence: Two to four content ideas, each with the questions it targets, the outlet, and the facts it will use.

steps.do: Write a limitations note: the sample size, that a share of sampled answers is not market share, that one answer is not a lasting placement, and that total search traffic cannot be read as traffic from AI answers.
steps.evidence: A limitations note with the sample size and what the sample cannot show.

blockers.do: If you cannot get AI answers yourself, ask the owner to run the questions in the agreed tools and send screenshots of each full answer.
If a tool gives no AI answer, save the question, region, and time and mark it 'no answer'; do not promise that one will appear.
If you do not have the product's current price and features, go back to the product reading step before checking claims.
If the product pages that answers should cite are blocked from indexing, tell the owner which page and why; do not change the site yourself.

C-SE-AI.title_zh: 搜尋AI答案與可引用事實查核

deliver_help.question_list: The fixed numbered questions, tools, region, language, and the counting rules.
deliver_help.answer_samples: For each question and tool, the class (no answer, no product, mention, verified citation), the cited URLs, and the times read.
deliver_help.wrong_claims: Each wrong or outdated statement about the product, the correct fact, and the page it seems to come from.
deliver_help.content_ideas: Two to four true pieces to publish through existing outlets, with the questions each one targets.
deliver_help.limitations: The sample size and what this sample cannot show.

C-PI-ACCESS.title: Confirm the Pinterest account, board, and who publishes
C-PI-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which Pinterest business account and public board will carry the Pin and who presses publish, so the Pin goes out under the right brand and its numbers can be read later.

steps.do: Ask the owner for the URL of the Pinterest profile that will post. Open it as a public page and confirm the username, the display name, and the website shown match the product's brand. Do not use a personal account for the brand.
steps.evidence: The profile URL, username, and website shown, with the owner's confirmation it is the brand's account.

steps.do: Ask the owner whether it is a business account; Pin analytics such as impressions and outbound clicks need one. If it is personal, the owner decides whether to switch it to business and does the switch themselves.
steps.evidence: Business or personal, and the owner's decision if a switch is needed.

steps.do: If the brand has no Pinterest account, create one only if the owner asks. Use the brand's real name and website approved by the owner; you may use inbox_address for the sign-up email and inbox_latest for the code. Never create a second or extra account.
steps.evidence: The owner's request and the account details they approved, or a note that the existing account is used.

steps.do: Decide who presses publish: the owner on their own device, or the agent's own browser if it is already signed in to this account. If nobody is signed in, the owner signs in on the official Pinterest screen. Never ask for a password.
steps.evidence: Who will publish, and the username seen after sign-in.

steps.do: Pick the board for the Pin. It must belong to this account and be public; a secret board gives no public reach. If no board fits the product's topic, propose one board name and description and create it only after the owner says yes.
steps.evidence: The board URL, confirmation that it is public and owned by the account, or the approved new board.

steps.do: Ask the owner whether the product's website is claimed on this Pinterest account and check what the profile shows. Do not assume shopping ads or product catalogs are available; a normal Pin is the plan unless the owner shows otherwise.
steps.evidence: Claimed, not claimed, or unknown, and the Pin format this round will use.

steps.do: Confirm how numbers will be read later: the agent's browser if signed in, or owner screenshots of the account's analytics. If Pinterest shows a verification code, terms screen, or identity check, stop and tell the owner exactly which screen needs them.
steps.evidence: How analytics will be obtained, and any screen left for the owner with where to resume.

blockers.do: If the account is personal, tell the owner that analytics need a business account and let them decide whether to switch; do not switch it for them.
If the chosen board belongs to someone else or cannot be posted to, use another public board of the brand; if none exists, keep the Pin as a draft and ask the owner about a new board.
If a verification code you cannot read with inbox_latest, a terms screen, or an identity check appears, stop and tell the owner which screen and which button; never accept terms for them.
If the agent's browser is not signed in to the right account, set who_publishes to 'owner' and plan to hand them the final Pin to post.
If the signed-in account shows a different brand or website, stop before any posting and ask the owner which account to use.

C-PI-ACCESS.title_zh: Pinterest身分、資格與可用工具核對

deliver_help.account_handle: The Pinterest username that will post, and whether it is a business account.
deliver_help.profile_url: The public profile URL, opened and confirmed to show the brand's website.
deliver_help.board_url: The public board the Pin will go on, owned by this account.
deliver_help.who_publishes: 'owner' or 'agent browser', plus one line on why.
deliver_help.analytics_access: How impressions and outbound clicks will be read: owner screenshots, the agent's browser, or not available.

C-PI-RESEARCH.title: Research what buyers search and save on Pinterest
C-PI-RESEARCH.purpose: Find the Pinterest searches, boards, and Pins around the product's use, separate saving for ideas from ready-to-buy moments, and turn that into a one-variable brief, so the next Pin earns clicks and visits from people likely to buy.

steps.do: From the buyer quotes and product facts, write 5 to 8 Pinterest searches in the form people use there, such as '{task} ideas', '{product type} guide', or '{situation} inspiration'. Run them in Pinterest search in your own browser, or have the owner send screenshots, and note any suggested searches Pinterest shows, plus the date and country.
steps.evidence: The searches run, the suggested searches shown, and the date and country.

steps.do: Collect at least 10 Pins and 3 boards that closely match the product's use. For each Pin, save its URL, the account that posted it, the date if shown, its title and description as written, where its link goes, and only the numbers Pinterest shows publicly.
steps.evidence: A list of at least 10 Pin URLs and 3 board URLs with author, date or 'unknown', text, and destination.

steps.do: Sort the examples by the buyer's situation: saving ideas for later, or ready to act now (looking for a tool, a price, or a how-to to do today). Saves alone do not show buying intent; say so where you have only saves.
steps.evidence: Each example marked 'ideas' or 'ready to act', with the words or link that show it.

steps.do: For at least 5 Pins that lead to a product or sign-up page, open the destination and compare it with the image, title, and description. Note where the page keeps the Pin's promise and where it does not.
steps.evidence: A short comparison of at least 5 linked Pins: image, title, destination, and whether the page keeps the promise.

steps.do: Write down 2 to 4 patterns worth borrowing, such as layout, text on the image, or the kind of headline. Borrow structure only; never copy another person's image, photo, or text.
steps.evidence: Two to four patterns, each with the example Pins it comes from.

steps.do: Write a brief for the next Pin that changes one thing only: the image or the headline. Keep the destination page the same and use the round's tracked link with ?v=A and ?v=B. Name the buyer situation, the hook, and the product facts it rests on.
steps.evidence: A one-variable brief with versions A and B, the hook, the facts used, and the tracked links.

blockers.do: If you cannot open Pinterest search, ask the owner for screenshots of the first screen of results for each search.
If fewer than 10 relevant Pins exist, say so and widen the searches to the buyer's broader situation, not to unrelated topics.
If the buyer situation needs a page the product does not have, note the gap for the owner and pick a situation the existing page serves.
If the round has no tracked link yet, call tracking to get one before writing the brief.

C-PI-RESEARCH.title_zh: Pinterest買方搜尋與保存意圖研究

deliver_help.example_pins: Each Pin or board URL with author, date or 'unknown', the text as written or empty, the destination, and only publicly shown numbers.
deliver_help.buyer_situations: The examples sorted into 'ideas' and 'ready to act', with the evidence for each.
deliver_help.patterns: Two to four structures worth borrowing, each with its example Pins; no copied images or text.
deliver_help.pin_brief: The next Pin's single changed variable, versions A and B, the hook, facts used, and the tracked links.

C-PI-METRICS.title: Read this goal's Pinterest numbers for the round
C-PI-METRICS.purpose: Record the numbers this goal is judged on, for the same Pins and dates before and after the new Pin, so rounds are compared on real numbers. record_numbers lists exactly which numbers it needs.

steps.do: Read the goal's metric components in where_are_we and use those exact names. Confirm whether this is the baseline or the current reading, which Pins are measured (by Pin URL), the date range (the goal watches 168 hours, so 7 full days), and the time zone.
steps.evidence: The component names, baseline or current, the Pin URLs, and the date range with time zone.

steps.do: For Pin components such as impressions, saves, and outbound clicks, read them per Pin from the account's analytics in your own browser, or ask the owner for screenshots. Keep impressions, saves, and outbound clicks apart; each is a different number.
steps.evidence: Each Pin's numbers exactly as displayed, with where they were read and the time.

steps.do: If any Pin was promoted as an ad, read paid and organic numbers separately and use only the ones the goal is about. Never add the same click or purchase to both.
steps.evidence: A note that no Pin was promoted, or the paid and organic numbers side by side.

steps.do: For visit components, use the click count of the round's tracked link from tracking, per version (?v=A, ?v=B). Use the owner's analytics for visits from Pinterest only if they already have it, and pick one source at the baseline and keep it for the current reading. Where there is no source, say so; do not estimate.
steps.evidence: Visit numbers per version with the one source used, or a note that the source is missing.

steps.do: For purchase components, count only purchases the sale counter or the owner's payment records tie to this round's tracked link, or their CRM if the owner already uses a CRM. Remove refunds, test payments, the owner's own purchases, and duplicates. A purchase you cannot tie to the Pin is not counted, and Pin clicks are never counted as sales.
steps.evidence: Purchase figures with their source, and what was removed or left out and why, or 'not used by this goal'.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with each component under its exact name and a source naming the screen or counter and the date range. If there is no history, record 0 and say so in source. If a denominator is 0, report no rate change.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call with every component, its value, and its source.

steps.do: Write one line on where the drop-off is largest (seen but not clicked, clicked but no visit, or visited but no purchase) to guide the next round's image or hook.
steps.evidence: One sentence naming the weakest step, based only on the numbers recorded.

blockers.do: If you cannot open the account's analytics, ask the owner for a screenshot showing the Pins and date range this goal needs.
If the account has no history for these numbers, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline.
If the Pin is less than 48 hours old, report the numbers as early and read them again when the 7-day window ends.
If a report mixes promoted and organic results, ask the owner for the split; if it cannot be split, say so and do not count the same conversion twice.
If the goal needs purchases and there is no sale counter or payment record, submit blocked and ask the owner to add the sale counter to the page shown after payment.

C-PI-METRICS.title_zh: Pinterest外連點擊到外部購買核對

deliver_help.numbers: Each goal component under its exact name with the value you recorded.
deliver_help.where_read: For each number, the Pinterest analytics screen, link counter, sale counter, or payment record it came from.
deliver_help.date_range: The start and end date with time zone, and whether this is the baseline or the current reading.

C-PI-PUBLISH.title: Publish one Pin and confirm it is live
C-PI-PUBLISH.purpose: Publish the approved Pin once, on the right account and public board, with the round's tracked link, and hand back its public URL, because the Pin has to be live and exactly as approved before any click can be measured.

steps.do: Check the image: a vertical 2:3 ratio (for example 1000 x 1500 pixels), and the owner owns it or has the right to use it. Check the title is under 100 characters and the description under 500, and that every claim matches the product facts.
steps.evidence: The image file with its size, the owner's confirmation of rights, and the title and description with their character counts.

steps.do: Set the destination to the round's tracked link with the version label (?v=A, or ?v=B for the second version). Open it and confirm it lands on the intended product page.
steps.evidence: The tracked link with its version label, and the page it opened.

steps.do: Look at the account's recent Pins so you do not post the same image again. Show the owner the exact image, title, description, link, and board, and get a clear yes before publishing.
steps.evidence: A note on the recent Pins checked, and the owner's approval message for this exact Pin.

steps.do: The agreed person creates the Pin once on the agreed public board: the agent's own browser if it is signed in and the owner said yes, otherwise the owner with the approved content you hand them. If the image is still uploading or processing, wait and do not press publish again.
steps.evidence: Who published, on which board, and when.

steps.do: If publishing seemed to fail or the result is unclear, check the board and profile for the Pin before any retry, so nothing is posted twice.
steps.evidence: A note that the Pin appears once, or that it did not appear and a single retry was made.

steps.do: Open the Pin's public URL, with read_page or a signed-out view if you can. Check the image, title, description, board, that it is public, and that the link opens the tracked link and lands on the product.
steps.evidence: The public Pin URL, the text as it appears there, the board, and the page the link opened.

steps.do: Note the publish time as the start of the 7-day watch window. The next version changes only one thing, and the same image is never posted again to push it.
steps.evidence: The window start and end times, and the one variable planned for the next version.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to this exact Pin, do not publish; show them the Pin and stop until they answer.

If Pinterest rejects the link, read the reason and tell the owner; never swap in another short link to get around it, and use the plain product page only if the owner agrees, noting that clicks and purchases can then be read only from Pinterest's own numbers.
If the Pin is still processing, wait and check the board again later; do not create a second copy.
If the agreed board cannot be posted to, use another public board of the brand; if none exists, keep the Pin as a draft and ask the owner.
If the owner cannot confirm the right to use the image, do not publish; go back to the image step for one the owner owns.
If the agent's browser cannot post, give the owner the image, text, link, and board, and ask them to send back the Pin URL.

deliver_help.pin_url: The public link to the live Pin, opened and confirmed to load. Example: 'https://www.pinterest.com/pin/...'.
deliver_help.published_text: The title and description exactly as they appear on the live Pin.
deliver_help.board_url: The public board the Pin is on.
deliver_help.tracked_link: The tracked link the Pin opens, with its version label.
deliver_help.window_start: The date and time the Pin went live, with time zone, which starts the 7-day window.

C-FG-ACCESS.title: Confirm the Facebook identity and which groups allow answers
C-FG-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which Facebook profile or Page will answer, in which groups, and what each group's rules allow, so replies go out under the right name and are not held or removed.

steps.do: Ask the owner which Facebook profile or Page will speak for the product, and for the links of the groups they are already in or want to use. Use the owner's one real account; never create a second or fake profile to get into a group.
steps.evidence: The name of the profile or Page that will answer, and a list of group links.

steps.do: Have the owner sign in to Facebook themselves, on their own device or in the agent's browser. Never ask for a password. If Facebook shows a code, a security check, or new terms, stop and tell the owner exactly which screen needs them.
steps.evidence: Who is signed in, on which device or browser, and the time it was checked.

steps.do: Open each group while signed in and note the owner's status there: admin, moderator, member, request pending, or not a member. Also note whether a Page can take part in the group or only personal profiles can comment.
steps.evidence: One row per group with the owner's status and whether a Page may answer.

steps.do: Read each group's rules and description. Write down in plain words whether self-promotion is allowed anywhere, only in a set promotion thread or on set days, or not at all; whether links are allowed in comments; and whether posts need admin approval.
steps.evidence: A short rules summary per group, quoting the exact rule lines about promotion and links.

steps.do: If the owner is not yet a member of a useful group, show them the group's joining questions and draft honest answers that say who they are and what they make; the owner sends the request. A pending request is not permission to post, so mark that group as waiting and carry on with the others.
steps.evidence: The groups with pending requests, the answers the owner sent, and the date sent.

steps.do: Decide per group who will post the replies: the agent's own browser, if it is signed in as the agreed identity and the owner allows it, or otherwise the owner. Facebook no longer lets outside apps post into groups, so plan on the Facebook site or app only.
steps.evidence: For each group, who will post and from which device or browser.

steps.do: Keep only the groups where the agreed identity can comment and the rules allow a helpful answer that mentions a product, in any thread or in a set thread. Put every other group on a skip list with the reason.
steps.evidence: The final list of usable groups and a skip list with one reason per group.

blockers.do: If the join request is still waiting, do not post there; finish research in other groups and check the request again after 24 hours.
If a group bans any mention of products, put it on the skip list; do not try to slip the product in through hints or private messages.
If the group does not let Pages comment, ask the owner whether to answer from their personal profile with a clear note that they make the product, or skip the group; never pose as an ordinary user.
If Facebook asks for a code, an identity check, or new terms, stop and tell the owner which screen and which button; never enter codes or accept terms for them.
If the owner has no groups in mind, search Facebook for groups on the buyer's problem, list up to 10 with their member count and rules, and let the owner choose which to join.

C-FG-ACCESS.title_zh: Facebook Groups身分、資格與可用工具核對

deliver_help.identity: The Facebook profile or Page that will answer, with its link. Example: 'Page: Acme Notes, facebook.com/acmenotes'.
deliver_help.usable_groups: Each usable group's link, the owner's status there, and its rule on promotion and links in one line.
deliver_help.skipped_groups: Each group left out, with the reason. Example: 'No promotion of any kind, rule 3'.
deliver_help.who_posts: 'owner' or 'agent browser' for each group, plus one line on why.

C-FG-FIND.title: Find recent buyer requests in Facebook groups
C-FG-FIND.purpose: Build a checked list of recent group posts where someone asks for what the product does, because each one is a request a reply can answer and this round's results are counted from these threads.

steps.do: Turn the buyer quotes and the chosen segment into 5 to 10 search phrases in the language the groups use, shaped like real requests: 'any recommendation for', 'looking for an alternative to', 'how do you handle', 'budget for'.
steps.evidence: The list of search phrases, each tied to the buyer quote or segment it came from.

steps.do: In each usable group, run every phrase in the group's own search and also scroll the posts from the last 14 days. Group posts usually need sign-in, so work in the agent's browser signed in as the owner, or ask the owner to paste post links; read_page only reads public pages.
steps.evidence: A search log per group: phrases used, date searched, and how many posts were looked at.

steps.do: Open each candidate post itself, not the search preview. Write down the post link, its date, the author's name as shown, the exact words of the request, and whether it is already solved, for example the author thanked someone, chose an option, or turned comments off.
steps.evidence: One row per candidate post with link, date, author, quoted request, and solved or open.

steps.do: Keep a post only if it is under 14 days old, still open, asks for something the product does today according to the fact sheet, and sits where the group's rules allow an answer. Leave out people selling their own product, people recruiting sellers or agents, competitors, posts that ask for no recommendations, and the owner's own posts.
steps.evidence: A kept list and an excluded list, each post with a one-line reason.

steps.do: For each kept post, write two things separately: what the person said they need, quoted, and why you think the product fits, as your own judgment. Mark the fit 'strong' or 'possible'.
steps.evidence: Each kept post shows a quoted need, a separate fit reason, and a fit mark.

steps.do: Remove duplicates: the same person asking in two groups counts once, keeping the newest post. A public request is not permission to email or privately message the person, so mark every kept post 'answer in the thread only'.
steps.evidence: The de-duplicated list, each post marked 'answer in the thread only'.

steps.do: Aim for at least 10 kept requests per round. If fewer than 5 remain after all phrases and groups, report that instead of stretching the fit, so the round can change groups or phrases. The final count is the round's number of eligible requests.
steps.evidence: The final count of eligible requests, or a note that fewer than 5 were found and why.

blockers.do: If the agent cannot open the group's posts, ask the owner to sign in in the agent's browser or to paste the links of recent posts that ask for help.
If the join request is still waiting, search the other usable groups and check the pending one again after 24 hours.
If fewer than 5 requests fit, say so and suggest two new phrases or groups; never count a weak fit to reach the target.
If a group's rules forbid any product mention, drop its posts from the kept list and note the group for the skip list.

C-FG-FIND.title_zh: Facebook群組查找適配需求與宣傳入口

deliver_help.requests: Each kept post: link, date, quoted request, fit reason, and fit mark.
deliver_help.excluded: Each post you looked at and left out, with its link and the reason. Example: 'Seller looking for resellers'.
deliver_help.search_log: The phrases searched in each group, the date, and how many posts were checked.
deliver_help.eligible_count: The number of kept, de-duplicated requests that can be answered this round.

C-FG-METRICS.title: Read this goal's numbers for Facebook group replies
C-FG-METRICS.purpose: Record the numbers this goal is judged on, for a fixed 7-day window before and after the replies, so rounds are compared on real counts from the threads and payment records. record_numbers lists exactly which numbers it needs.

steps.do: Take the goal's exact metric component names, for example qualified_replies and eligible_requests, or external_purchases, and count only those; skip the counting steps below for components this goal does not use. Set the window: for the baseline, the 168 hours before this round's first reply; for the current reading, the 168 hours after it. Write down the time zone.
steps.evidence: The component names, the start and end of the window, and the time zone.

steps.do: List the threads in the window with their links: for the baseline, the threads answered before this round; for the current reading, the threads this round found or answered. Open each one and mark its state: reply visible, reply waiting for admin approval, reply removed, or not answered. Only visible replies count as delivered.
steps.evidence: The thread list with a state for each link, checked on a stated date.

steps.do: Count eligible requests as the checked requests from the find step that fall inside the window and where an answer was allowed. Do not use group member counts or reach; most of those numbers are shown only to admins and are not this goal's base.
steps.evidence: The eligible request count with the links it was counted from.

steps.do: Count qualified replies: different people, not the owner, the agent, or a moderator, who answered our reply or messaged the owner about it inside the window with a buying signal, such as asking the price, how to get it, a question about using it, or saying they will try it. Count each person once per thread; a like or 'thanks' alone does not count.
steps.evidence: The qualified reply count, with the link of each counted comment or a note of each private message.

steps.do: Count external purchases for the same window from the round's tracked link sale counter and the owner's payment records. Leave out test, owner, and team purchases, and purchases refunded inside the window. If you cannot tell which purchases came from the groups, say so plainly.
steps.evidence: The purchase count, the source of each purchase, and a note of anything left out.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with the goal's exact component names and a source that says where each number came from, for example 'hand count of 12 thread links on 22 Nov; tracking sale counter'. If there is no history, record 0 and say 'no history' in source. Never estimate a number you could not read, and if eligible_requests is 0, do not report a rate.
steps.evidence: The numbers as recorded, each with its source.

steps.do: Write down why requests did not turn into replies or purchases: answer held or removed, no response, weak fit, or already solved, and the owner's hours spent on this round, so the next round can change the groups, the phrases, or the answer.
steps.evidence: A short list of reasons, each with the number of threads it applies to, and the hours spent.

blockers.do: If there are no earlier replies or purchases for this goal, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline.
If the agent cannot open the threads, ask the owner to sign in in the agent's browser or to send screenshots of each thread.
If a reply is still waiting for admin approval, count it as not delivered and check it again after 24 hours; never post it again.
If there is no sale counter and the owner cannot share payment records, report purchases as missing; do not estimate them.
If fewer than 168 hours have passed since the first reply, report the numbers as early and read them again when the window closes.

C-FG-METRICS.title_zh: Facebook群組有效對話與付款核對

deliver_help.numbers: Each of the goal's components by its exact name with the value read. Example: 'qualified_replies: 3, eligible_requests: 11'.
deliver_help.where_read: Where each number came from: the thread links counted, the tracking sale counter, or the owner's payment records.
