deliver_help.date_range: The start and end of the window with the time zone. Example: '15 Nov 09:00 to 22 Nov 09:00, Taipei time'.

C-FG-REPLY.title: Answer buyer requests in Facebook group threads
C-FG-REPLY.purpose: Post one helpful, honest answer under each checked request, with the tracked link where the rules allow it, because a useful answer in the thread is what earns a buyer's reply and click.

steps.do: Before each reply, open the thread again. Confirm the request is still open, read every comment so you do not repeat an answer already given, check the group rules have not changed, and check the owner has not already answered this person.
steps.evidence: For each thread, its link, the time it was checked, and 'still open' or the reason to skip it.

steps.do: Write the answer to the person's exact question first, in 2 to 5 sentences that help even if they never buy. Then mention the product in one sentence with a clear note of the relationship, such as 'I make this, so I am biased'. Use only claims from the fact sheet and the approved copy; no invented results, reviews, or discounts.
steps.evidence: A draft answer per thread, with the facts it relies on.

steps.do: Add the round's tracked link only if the group allows links in comments, with ?v=A or ?v=B matching the answer's version. If links are not allowed, leave the link out and name the product so people can find it; never send the link by private message to someone who did not ask for it.
steps.evidence: Each draft shows either the tracked link with its version or a note that links are not allowed there.

steps.do: Show the owner each reply word for word, with the thread link and the identity that will post it, up to 5 at a time. Nothing is posted without the owner's yes to that exact text.
steps.evidence: The exact texts shown and the owner's approval message for each.

steps.do: Post each approved reply once, in the original thread only, as the agreed profile or Page: by the agent's own browser if it is signed in and the owner said yes, otherwise by the owner. Post at most one reply per thread and at most 5 replies a day across all groups; do not paste the same text into several groups or message people who did not ask.
steps.evidence: Who posted each reply and when.

steps.do: After posting, open the thread and confirm the reply is visible and matches the approved text, then copy the comment's link. If the group holds it for admin approval, mark it pending and check again after 24 hours without posting again. If it was removed, note it and stop answering in that group this round.
steps.evidence: For each reply, its public comment link, or the state 'pending' or 'removed' with the time checked.

steps.do: Check each thread every 24 hours for 7 days. If the person asks a question, draft an answer and show the owner before posting. If they say no or that it is solved, stop. Never add a second sales message to the same thread; if they ask to talk privately, the owner takes over the conversation.
steps.evidence: A log per thread of each response received and what was done about it.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to this exact text, do not post; show them the text and stop until they answer.
If the group holds the reply for admin approval, wait and check after 24 hours; never post the same reply again.
If the rules or an admin say no product mentions, remove the product sentence and the link, and post only a helpful answer if the owner still wants to.
If the agent's browser is not signed in as the agreed identity, give the owner the approved text and thread link, and ask them to send back the comment link.
If the person has already chosen a solution or closed the thread, skip it and do not reply.
If the tracked link does not open the product page, stop before posting and fix the link with the owner.

C-FG-REPLY.title_zh: Facebook群組相關答案與審核續接

deliver_help.reply_urls: The public link of each live reply, opened and confirmed to show the reply.
deliver_help.published_text: The text of each reply exactly as it appears in the group, copied from the thread.
deliver_help.pending_or_removed: Each reply that is waiting for approval or was removed, with the thread link and the time checked.
deliver_help.follow_ups: Each response from a buyer, with its link, and what was answered or why the thread was closed.

C-DC-ACCESS.title: Confirm the Discord servers, account, and who posts
C-DC-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which Discord servers and channels this goal may use, which real account speaks for the brand, and who presses send, so answers go out under the right name and inside each server's rules.

steps.do: Ask the owner which Discord account speaks for the brand and which servers they are already a real member of where buyers ask for help or gather. Use the owner's existing account; do not create extra accounts.
steps.evidence: The account name, and the list of servers with their invite links or names.

steps.do: For each server, read the rules channel and any rules on self-promotion. Note whether members may mention their own product, in which channels, whether links are allowed, whether the relationship must be stated, and whether direct messages to members are forbidden. If a rule is unclear, the owner asks a moderator.
steps.evidence: For each server, the rules on product mentions, links, and direct messages, quoted.

steps.do: Pick the channels to use: help, questions, or forum channels where answering is welcome and the product fits. Mark channels that forbid product mentions as answer-only with no link, or leave them out.
steps.evidence: The channel list, each marked 'answer with link', 'answer only', or 'not used'.

steps.do: Decide who posts: the owner by hand in Discord, or a bot that the server's admins already added and the owner controls. The agent never drives the owner's personal account with automated tools, because Discord forbids self-bots, and never posts from any other account.
steps.evidence: Who will post, and for a bot, the admin's okay for it in each channel.

steps.do: In each chosen channel, check that the posting account can see the channel, read earlier messages, and send messages. Note any slowmode, membership screening, or phone check; the owner completes those. Never ask for a password.
steps.evidence: For each channel, can see, can read history, can send, and any slowmode.

steps.do: Agree how the agent will read messages: the owner shares message links or screenshots, the allowed bot reads only the channels it was added to, or the agent opens a public web copy of the server's help forum if the server publishes one. A bot without permission to read message text sees only messages that mention it; do not ask for wider access to scan the whole server. Never collect member lists or read channels the account cannot see.
steps.evidence: The reading method for each channel.

steps.do: If the owner has no Discord account and asks for one, the owner signs up with their own real details and completes any captcha or phone check. The agent may give inbox_address for the sign-up and read the code with inbox_latest. One account only.
steps.evidence: The new account name and the owner's request, or a note that an existing account is used.

blockers.do: If a server forbids any product mention, use it for answers only with no product or link, or leave it out.
If the account cannot see or post in a channel, drop that channel and continue with the allowed ones.
If Discord or the server asks for a phone check, screening answers, or a code, stop and tell the owner which screen needs them; never complete it for them.
If the owner is not a member of any server where buyers ask for help, list two or three public servers that fit and let the owner decide whether to join with their own account.

If server admins have not approved a bot, or the bot cannot read message text, set who_posts to 'owner by hand' and read through message links or screenshots the owner shares; never widen access to scan the server.
If the signed-in account is not the agreed brand account, stop and ask the owner to switch before anything is posted.

C-DC-ACCESS.title_zh: Discord身分、資格與可用工具核對

deliver_help.brand_account: The Discord account name that will post for the brand.
deliver_help.servers_and_channels: Each server and channel to use, marked 'answer with link' or 'answer only'.
deliver_help.server_rules: Each server's rule on product mentions, links, and direct messages, quoted with where it was read.
deliver_help.who_posts: 'owner by hand' or 'admin-approved bot', plus how the agent reads messages.

C-DC-FIND.title: Find open Discord help requests the product can answer
C-DC-FIND.purpose: Collect a short list of real, unsolved help requests in allowed channels where the product truly fits, because a useful answer to an open question is what earns a reply and a click.

steps.do: Re-read the channel list and rules from the account step and use only those channels. Never take names from member lists to message people.
steps.evidence: The channels searched, with their rules on answers and links.

steps.do: Turn the buyer situation into 3 to 5 search phrases in the words buyers use in their quotes, such as 'how do I', 'any tool for', or 'recommend'. The owner runs Discord's search in each channel and shares the message links, the allowed bot reads recent messages in the channels it was added to, or the agent reads the public forum copy.
steps.evidence: The search phrases used, the channels they were run in, and who ran them.

steps.do: Collect requests from the last 14 days unless the owner set another range. For each, keep the message link, the date, the author's name, and the shortest quote that shows the need.
steps.evidence: A list of requests, each with message link, date, author, and quote.

steps.do: Read each whole thread and the replies after it. Leave out requests that are solved, where the person says they found an answer, where the thread is closed, where the post asks for no promotion, or where the person already said no to the brand.
steps.evidence: The excluded requests, each with the reason.

steps.do: For each remaining request, write two things separately: what the person said they need, quoted, and why you think the product fits, as your own view. Mark the fit strong, weak, or unknown, and drop the weak ones.
steps.evidence: For each request, the quoted need, your fit reason, and the fit mark.

steps.do: Keep only people who openly asked for help or a recommendation, in a channel that allows answers. Being in the same server is not permission to pitch. Count each person once, even if they asked twice.
steps.evidence: The final list, one line per person.

steps.do: Hand over at most 10 requests per round, strongest fit first, together with the excluded list.
steps.evidence: Up to 10 open requests in order, and the excluded list with reasons.

blockers.do: If no one can read a channel, skip it and say so; never read it through another account or tool.
If nothing fits, try new phrases from the buyer quotes or extend to 30 days; do not move into channels that were not approved.
If a channel's rules forbid product mentions, keep its requests only as answer-only, with no link.
If a thread is closed or archived, leave it out; do not open a new thread to answer it.
If the same person asked in several places, keep one request, the most recent, and note the others.

C-DC-FIND.title_zh: Discord已授權社群的產品需求整理

deliver_help.open_requests: Up to 10 requests, each with message link, date, author, the quoted need, and your separate reason the product fits.
deliver_help.excluded: Requests left out, each with its link and the reason, such as 'already solved'.
deliver_help.search_phrases: The phrases searched and the channels they were run in.

C-DC-METRICS.title: Read this goal's numbers from Discord
C-DC-METRICS.purpose: Record the numbers this goal is judged on, counted message by message and person by person in the allowed channels and the owner's sales records, so the baseline and the current round are compared on real numbers.

steps.do: Confirm the servers and channels being measured, the date range, and the time zone. For the baseline, use a range of the same length just before this round's first answer or task post. For the current reading, start when that first answer or post went live and cover at least the goal's 168 hours.
steps.evidence: Servers, channels, and date range with time zone.

steps.do: Find this goal's metric components and use those exact names with record_numbers: qualified_replies and eligible_requests for qualified reply rate, external_purchases for purchases, completed_participants and eligible_members for task completion.
steps.evidence: The list of component names this goal needs, copied exactly.

steps.do: For eligible_requests, count the open help requests in range that fit the product, invited answers, and got a brand answer that is still visible in the thread, one per person. For qualified_replies, count those where the person wrote back to the brand's answer with a real follow-up: a question about the product, a request for the link or a demo, or saying they tried it. Reactions and a plain 'thanks' do not count, and the owner's or agent's own messages never count.
steps.evidence: Both counts, with the message link for each request and each qualifying reply.

steps.do: For external_purchases, count purchases from the sale counter on the page shown after payment and the owner's payment records that came through this round's tracked link or where the buyer said they came from Discord. Leave out test purchases by the owner or the agent and refunded orders. If you cannot tell where a sale came from, do not count it and say so.
steps.evidence: The purchase count, each with its order date and how it was traced to Discord.

steps.do: For eligible_members, count members who joined the task in range in the way the task post set out. For completed_participants, count those who posted the finished work as defined. Each person once; a reaction is neither a join nor a completion.
steps.evidence: Both counts, with a message link per member.

steps.do: Never use the server's member count as reach or as a denominator. Note the owner's time spent answering and any refunds if known, or write 'unknown'. List what held numbers back, such as no replies, poor fit, or a rule that blocked links.
steps.evidence: Time spent, refunds or 'unknown', and the list of what held numbers back.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with each component by its exact name and a source naming where it was counted and when. If there is no history, record 0 and say so in source. Never estimate a missing number.
steps.evidence: The recorded numbers, each with its source, and any number left out with the reason.

blockers.do: If you cannot see the messages, ask the owner for the message links or screenshots of the threads; never count what you have not seen.
If there were no earlier answers, sales, or tasks from Discord, record 0, say so in source, and let this round set the baseline.
If there is no sale counter or payment record to check, say so and record no purchases you cannot trace; do not estimate.
If less than 168 hours have passed since the round started, record the numbers as early and read them again later.
If a counted message was deleted, keep the count only if you recorded its link and text before; otherwise drop it and say so.

C-DC-METRICS.title_zh: Discord社群答案到合格商機核對

deliver_help.numbers: Each component by its exact name with its value.
deliver_help.where_read: Where each number was counted: message links, the sale counter, the owner's payment records, with the time read, plus time spent and refunds or 'unknown'.
deliver_help.date_range: Start and end date with time zone. Example: '2026-11-01 to 2026-11-08, Asia/Taipei'.

C-DC-REPLY.title: Answer one Discord help request in its own thread
C-DC-REPLY.purpose: Post one helpful, owner-approved answer in the thread where the person asked, with the brand relationship stated, because a real answer is what earns a qualified reply and later a purchase.

steps.do: Open the request again by its message link. Confirm it is still open, the person has not said they solved it or said no to the brand, and the channel rules still allow the answer. Check the posting account can send there and note any slowmode.
steps.evidence: The request link, a note that it is still open, and the rule check.

steps.do: Write the answer to solve the problem first, so it helps even if the person never buys: two to four concrete steps, under 1,000 characters.
steps.evidence: The draft answer and its character count.

steps.do: Mention the product only if it truly fits, in one sentence that says plainly how you are related to it, such as 'I make this'. If the channel allows links, add the round's tracked link, with ?v=A or ?v=B when there are several versions. Use only claims the product facts support.
steps.evidence: The product sentence, the link with its version, and the facts it relies on, or a note that no product was mentioned.

steps.do: Show the owner the exact text, word for word, with the request link, and get a clear yes before anything is posted.
steps.evidence: The final text and the owner's approval message.

steps.do: Post once, as a reply to the original message in the same thread, by the owner by hand or by the admin-approved bot. If you are unsure it went out, check the thread before posting again; never post the same answer twice and never resend it in a direct message or a new thread.
steps.evidence: Who posted, and when.

steps.do: Open the thread, copy the message link of the live answer, and confirm the text and the author match what was approved.
steps.evidence: The public message link, the text as it appears, and the author.

steps.do: Wait 48 hours for a reply. If the person asks a question, draft one answer and show the owner. If they say no, ask to stop, or have already bought, stop contacting them. Send a direct message only if they ask for one, and never chase silence.
steps.evidence: The follow-up state: replied, no reply, stopped, or bought, with message links.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to this exact text, do not post it; show it and wait.
If the request is solved or the person said no, do not answer; move to the next request.
If the channel forbids links or product mentions, post the answer only, without the product sentence or link.
If the thread is closed or archived, do not open a new thread or message the person; move to the next request.
If slowmode blocks sending, wait the time shown and post once; never switch accounts to get around it.
If no approved bot can post, give the owner the final text and request link, and ask them to send back the message link.

C-DC-REPLY.title_zh: Discord求助原串回答與同人停止

deliver_help.reply_url: The message link of the live answer, opened and confirmed.
deliver_help.posted_text: The full text exactly as it appears in Discord.
deliver_help.request_url: The message link of the help request being answered.
deliver_help.follow_up_state: 'replied', 'no reply after 48 hours', 'asked to stop', or 'bought', with the link to any reply.

C-LN-ACCESS.title: Confirm the LINE Official Account, limits, and who sends
C-LN-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which LINE Official Account sends, who presses send, how many messages are free this month, and the spend the owner allows, so the message goes out from the right account without surprise costs.

steps.do: Ask the owner for the LINE Official Account name and its ID that starts with @, and the brand it belongs to. Open its public add-friend page if one exists and confirm it matches the brand. Make sure it is the account customers actually follow, not a test account or a personal LINE.
steps.evidence: The account name, its @ ID, and a note that it matches the brand.

steps.do: Have the owner sign in to the LINE Official Account Manager themselves. Never ask for a password or for any access token. Check that their role can send messages and see statistics; if not, ask the account's admin to change the role.
steps.evidence: Who signed in, their role, and whether it can send and see statistics.

steps.do: If the owner or a developer sends messages through LINE's developer tools, note only that this exists and who controls it. Never paste a channel token into the chat or any deliverable. A LINE Login channel cannot send messages; only the Official Account can.
steps.evidence: A note of how messages are sent today and who controls it, with no token written anywhere.

steps.do: Read, from the account's plan or billing page, the plan name, how many messages it includes each month, how many are already used this month, and what extra messages cost, if the plan allows extra messages at all. Write down the remaining free messages and the cost per extra message in local currency.
steps.evidence: The plan name, messages used and remaining this month, the extra-message price, and where these were read.

steps.do: Ask the owner, in writing, for the most messages and the most extra spend this goal may use. Do not upgrade the plan or buy extra messages; if the send would need either, the owner decides.
steps.evidence: The owner's written limits: a message count and a spend amount, which may be zero.

steps.do: Read the friend count, the count that can be targeted, and the blocked count from the account's friend statistics. Ask the owner how friends joined, such as a QR code in the shop, after a purchase, an ad, or a website button, and whether anyone was promised a type or rate of message when they joined.
steps.evidence: The three friend counts with the date read, how friends joined, and any promise made to them.

steps.do: Decide who presses send: the owner in the LINE Official Account Manager, or the agent's own browser if it is signed in and the owner allows it. If LINE asks for a verification code or new terms, stop and tell the owner which screen needs them.
steps.evidence: Who will send, from which device or browser, and the time this was confirmed.

blockers.do: If no free messages are left and the owner has not approved extra spend, stop new sends, say when the count resets, and do not upgrade the plan.
If the signed-in account is a test account or a different brand, stop and ask the owner which account customers follow.
If the signed-in role cannot send or see statistics, tell the owner which account admin needs to change the role.
If LINE asks for a code, an identity check, or new terms, stop and tell the owner which screen and which button; never enter codes or accept terms for them.
If the owner pastes a token or password into the chat, do not use or repeat it, and tell them to issue a new one because it has been exposed.

C-LN-ACCESS.title_zh: LINE官方帳號身分、資格與可用工具核對

deliver_help.account_id: The Official Account's name and @ ID, confirmed to match the brand. Example: 'Acme Tea, @acmetea'.
deliver_help.send_limits: Free messages left this month, the extra-message price, and the owner's written limits on count and spend.
deliver_help.friend_counts: Friends, targetable friends, and blocked friends, with the date read and how friends joined.
deliver_help.who_sends: 'owner' or 'agent browser', plus one line on why.

C-LN-SEGMENT.title: Choose the LINE friends this message is for
C-LN-SEGMENT.purpose: Pick one small, clearly defined group of LINE friends who agreed to hear from the account and have a reason to care, because the right audience is what turns a delivered message into replies and purchases.

steps.do: List the audience sources the owner already has: audiences the account can already target, chat tags, people who clicked earlier messages, and any customer list the owner exported with LINE user IDs. Write down each source and its date. Never invent or guess LINE user IDs.
steps.evidence: A list of audience sources, each with its date and how many people it holds.

steps.do: Sort the sources by how people joined and where they are in buying: new friends who never bought, people who asked in chat but did not buy, past buyers who could buy again or add something. Use what people did, never names or guesses about age or gender.
steps.evidence: Two to four segments, each defined by how people joined and their buying stage.

steps.do: Pick the one segment whose situation best matches the chosen buying motive and sales angle. Write one sentence on why this group would care about this message now.
steps.evidence: The chosen segment and the one-sentence reason.

steps.do: Remove people who blocked the account, people who asked to stop or not get promotions, past buyers when the message sells the same thing again, anyone messaged by this goal or another campaign in the last 7 days, and the owner's, staff, and test accounts. Use the sending screen's exclude option where LINE offers one; if a group cannot be removed, say how many people it holds.
steps.evidence: The count removed for each reason, and any group that could not be removed with its size.

steps.do: Count the people left and check the count fits both the free messages left and the owner's written limit. Aim for at least 50 people per version so a few replies mean something; if fewer, say the round's result will be noisy.
steps.evidence: The final count, checked against the free messages left and the owner's limit.

steps.do: If the round tests two versions and you have a list of LINE user IDs or two audiences you can split, split them into two halves of similar size, for example by alternating rows, and label them A and B; never split by join date or anything else that could change the result. If the segment cannot be split, send one version this round and compare it with the last round.
steps.evidence: Halves A and B with their counts and how they were split, or a note that one version will be sent.

steps.do: Write the segment in a form the sender can use: the audience name in LINE or the exact filter settings, and the exact count. Share no personal data beyond what sending needs.
steps.evidence: The audience name or filter settings and the count, ready for the send step.

blockers.do: If the account cannot target any segment smaller than all friends, tell the owner and ask whether to build an audience from chat tags or past clicks first; never broadcast to everyone instead.
If fewer than 20 people remain, report it and ask the owner whether to widen the segment by one rule or wait for more friends.
If the free messages left cannot cover the segment and no extra spend is approved, shrink the segment to fit or wait for the monthly reset.
If people joined with a promise of a certain kind of message, such as coupons only, leave them out unless this message matches that promise.

C-LN-SEGMENT.title_zh: LINE依來源、同意與購買狀態分群

deliver_help.segment_definition: Who is in the segment and why, in one or two sentences. Example: 'Friends who asked about prices in chat in the last 60 days and have not bought'.
deliver_help.recipient_count: The number of people after removals, split into A and B if there are two versions.
deliver_help.exclusions: Each removal reason with its count. Example: 'Messaged in last 7 days: 34'.
deliver_help.audience_source: The audience name in LINE or the filter settings, and where the underlying list came from.

C-LN-METRICS.title: Read this goal's numbers for a LINE message
C-LN-METRICS.purpose: Record the numbers this goal is judged on, for the message before and after the change over the same 7-day window, so rounds are compared on real delivery, reply, and payment counts. record_numbers lists exactly which numbers it needs.

steps.do: Take the goal's exact metric component names, for example qualified_replies and delivered, or external_purchases and delivered, and count only those; skip the counting steps below for components this goal does not use. Set the window: for the baseline, the last comparable message before this round, read 168 hours after it was sent; for the current reading, this round's message, 168 hours after sending. Write down the time zone.
steps.evidence: The component names, the message or messages measured, the window, and the time zone.

steps.do: Open the account's message statistics for the measured message, or ask the owner for a screenshot. Read the delivered count, and opens and clicks if shown; write 'not shown' for anything missing. A message accepted for sending is not the same as delivered.
steps.evidence: The delivered count and any other numbers exactly as displayed, with the screen they came from and the time read.

steps.do: Count qualified replies in the account's chats inside the window: different people who wrote about this message's offer and asked the price, how to buy, whether it is available, or a real question about the product. Count each person once. Stickers, 'thanks', automatic keyword replies, and stop requests do not count.
steps.evidence: The qualified reply count, with the date and a short quote of each counted reply.

steps.do: Count purchases in the window from the round's tracked link sale counter and the owner's payment records, and read clicks per version from tracking. Leave out test, owner, and staff purchases and purchases refunded inside the window. If you cannot tell which purchases came from the message, say so. Also note any extra-message cost paid for this send, in local currency.
steps.evidence: The purchase count, clicks per version, and any message cost, each with its source and a note of anything left out.

steps.do: Read the change in blocked friends and any stop requests in the window. If blocks rose by more than 2% of delivered, flag it so this message is not sent again unchanged.
steps.evidence: Blocks and stop requests in the window, and whether the 2% line was crossed.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with the goal's exact component names and a source for each, for example 'message statistics read on 22 Nov; tracking sale counter'. If there is no earlier message, record 0 and say 'no history' in source. Never estimate; if delivered is 0 or cannot be read, do not report a rate.
steps.evidence: The numbers as recorded, each with its source.

steps.do: Write down the one thing that changed from the baseline message: the text, the audience, or the send time. If more than one thing changed, say so, because the result then cannot be credited to a single change.
steps.evidence: The one change between the baseline and this round, or a note that several things changed.

blockers.do: If no comparable message was sent before, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline.
If LINE does not show statistics for this message, for example because the send was small, take the delivered count from the send record and say so in source; do not estimate.
If the agent cannot open the statistics, ask the owner for a screenshot of the message's statistics.
If there is no sale counter and the owner cannot share payment records, report purchases as missing; do not estimate them.
If fewer than 168 hours have passed since sending, report the numbers as early and read them again when the window closes.

C-LN-METRICS.title_zh: LINE訊息到有效詢問與外部付款核對

deliver_help.numbers: Each of the goal's components by its exact name with the value read. Example: 'qualified_replies: 6, delivered: 180'.
deliver_help.where_read: Where each number came from: the account's message statistics, the chats, the tracking sale counter, or the owner's payment records.
deliver_help.date_range: The send time and the end of the window with the time zone. Example: '15 Nov 11:00 to 22 Nov 11:00, Taipei time'.

C-LN-SEND.title: Send one LINE message to the chosen friends
C-LN-SEND.purpose: Send the approved message once, only to the chosen segment and within the agreed limits, and confirm its delivery, because a message delivered to the right people is the base that replies and purchases are counted on.

steps.do: Right before sending, check again: free messages left this month, the owner's written limits on count and spend, and the segment count after removing anyone who blocked the account, asked to stop, or was messaged in the last 7 days.
steps.evidence: The free messages left, the owner's limits, and the final recipient count, with the time checked.

steps.do: Choose how it goes out: a chat reply only to people who wrote to the account first, otherwise a message to the chosen audience. Never send to all friends when the goal is for one segment.
steps.evidence: The send method and the audience name or filter it will use.

steps.do: Prepare the final message from the approved copy: about 300 characters or less, one clear action, and the round's tracked link with ?v=A or ?v=B for each version. Keep any stop-messages wording the account normally uses. Open the link on a phone and check it loads.
steps.evidence: The final text of each version, its character count, and confirmation the link loaded.

steps.do: Show the owner the exact text, any image, the link, the audience and count, the send time, and any cost. Nothing is sent without the owner's yes; any cost beyond the free messages needs the owner's written approval of the amount.
steps.evidence: What was shown and the owner's approval message, including the approved amount if there is a cost.

steps.do: Send a test to the owner's own LINE if the sending screen offers one, or use its preview. Check the text, image, and link look right on a phone before the real send.
steps.evidence: A screenshot of the test or preview, and a note that the link opened.

steps.do: Send once, between 10:00 and 20:00 in the recipients' time zone, by the agreed sender: the agent's own browser if signed in and the owner said yes, otherwise the owner. If there are two versions, send A and B at the same time. If the screen errors or hangs, check the list of sent messages before trying again; never send twice.
steps.evidence: Who sent it, the exact send time, and the sent message as it appears in the sent list.

steps.do: After sending, open the sent message's record and note its audience, target count, and delivered count once shown, with a screenshot. If it is still processing, check again after an hour. Delivered means LINE delivered it, not that anyone read or bought.
steps.evidence: The send record with target and delivered counts, and the time read.

steps.do: Check the account's chats every 24 hours for 7 days. Draft answers to buying questions and show the owner before sending. If someone asks to stop, honour it and note it. If blocks rise by more than 2% of delivered, stop any further sends in this test and tell the owner.
steps.evidence: A log of replies, answers sent, stop requests, and the block count.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to this exact message, audience, and cost, do not send; show them and stop until they answer.
If the free messages left cannot cover the send and no extra spend is approved, shrink the audience to fit or wait for the monthly reset; never upgrade the plan.

If a reply to someone who wrote earlier can now only go out as a counted message, for example through LINE's developer tools after the reply window closed, send it only within the owner's approved message count and spend; otherwise leave it.
If someone blocked the account or asked to stop, send them nothing more, on LINE or anywhere else.
If the send record shows it is still processing, wait and check again after an hour; do not send again.
If the tracked link does not open the product page, stop before sending and fix the link with the owner.

C-LN-SEND.title_zh: LINE限定名單訊息與配額對帳

deliver_help.sent_text: The exact text of each version as sent, with its tracked link and version label.
deliver_help.audience_and_count: The audience name or filter used and how many people it targeted, split into A and B if there are two versions.
deliver_help.delivery_record: The send time and the delivered count from the sent message's record, with where it was read.
deliver_help.replies_log: Each reply received in the 7 days, what was answered, and any stop requests.

C-WA-ACCESS.title: Confirm the WhatsApp Business number and who sends
C-WA-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which WhatsApp Business number sends, who presses send, which templates are approved, where contacts agreed to be messaged and the most the owner will spend, so the round reaches real opted-in buyers without stopping halfway.

steps.do: Ask the owner how the brand uses WhatsApp: the WhatsApp Business Platform, run from WhatsApp Manager in their Meta business account or through a messaging provider; the WhatsApp Business app on a phone; or a personal account. This goal sends template messages, and only the Platform sends those.
steps.evidence: The setup type in the owner's words, and the provider's name if one is used.

steps.do: Get the sending phone number and the business display name. Check that both match the brand on its website or profile, and that only one business number will be used for this round.
steps.evidence: The number, the display name, and the page where the brand shows that number.

steps.do: Decide who presses send: the owner, or the agent only if it already has a working tool signed in to this exact number and the owner says yes. The owner signs in to WhatsApp Manager or the provider themselves. Never ask for a password; a code sent by text message stays with the owner.
steps.evidence: Who sends, how they are signed in, and the number they see after signing in.

steps.do: Read from WhatsApp Manager or the provider's dashboard, or from the owner's screenshot, the number's quality rating, its current messaging limit, and every approved template with its category and language.
steps.evidence: Quality rating, messaging limit and the approved templates with category and language, each with the date read.

steps.do: Ask the owner where contacts agreed to get WhatsApp messages from the brand, such as a checkout box, a sign-up form, or the contact writing first, and what they agreed to receive. A number that is public, bought, copied from a website or given for another purpose is not agreement. Note how people opt out.
steps.evidence: The opt-in source, its wording if visible, what it covers, and how opt-outs are recorded.

steps.do: Note when each likely recipient group last wrote to the business. More than 24 hours after a contact's last message, only an approved template may be sent to them; free-form messages are allowed only inside that window.
steps.evidence: For each recipient group, whether it is inside the 24-hour window or needs a template.

steps.do: Read the current message charges from the account's billing page or the provider's price list, not from memory, and ask the owner in writing for the most they will spend on messages this round.
steps.evidence: The price source with the date read, and the owner's written spending cap in the account currency.

blockers.do: If the brand has only the WhatsApp Business app or a personal account, stop and tell the owner that template messages need the WhatsApp Business Platform, which they set up themselves; never message buyers from a personal account.
If the signed-in number is not the brand's agreed number, stop before anything is sent and ask the owner to switch to the right number.
If the owner cannot show where contacts agreed to WhatsApp messages, stop and message nobody until there is a real opt-in source.
If WhatsApp or Meta asks for a code, a business verification, a payment method or acceptance of terms, tell the owner which screen needs it and wait; never enter it for them.
If the quality rating is low or the number is restricted, plan no sending; tell the owner and read the reasons the account shows.
If messages cost money and the owner has not given a written cap, stop before any send is planned and ask for one.

C-WA-ACCESS.title_zh: WhatsApp Business身分、資格與可用工具核對

deliver_help.sending_number: The business number with country code, the display name recipients see, and whether it runs from WhatsApp Manager or a named provider.
deliver_help.who_sends: 'owner' or 'agent tool', plus one line on why.
deliver_help.account_status: The quality rating, the messaging limit, and each approved template's name, category and language, with the date read.
deliver_help.opt_in_source: Where contacts agreed to WhatsApp messages, what they agreed to, and how they opt out. Example: 'checkbox at checkout for offers; reply STOP'.
deliver_help.spending_cap: The owner's written maximum for message charges this round in the account currency, plus the price source and the date it was read.

C-WA-PLAN.title: Pick opted-in recipients and the approved template
C-WA-PLAN.purpose: Build a small list of people who agreed to WhatsApp messages and pick the approved template that can reach them, because the goal's main number only counts messages that were allowed and delivered.

steps.do: Ask the owner to export the contacts who opted in to WhatsApp messages from the brand, with opt-in date, source and purpose, from where they already keep them: the provider's contact list, a spreadsheet, or the CRM if the owner already uses a CRM. Use only the brand's own contacts.
steps.evidence: Contact count, where the list came from, and the date it was exported.

steps.do: Remove anyone who opted out, blocked the business, asked not to be contacted, agreed only to a different kind of message (for example order updates only when this is an offer), already bought this product if the message is a sales offer, appears twice, or has a number without a valid country code.
steps.evidence: The count removed for each reason and the count left.

steps.do: Keep the contacts whose situation fits the chosen buyer group and angle, using what the owner knows: past purchase, a question they asked, or why they signed up. Mark fit you can see in their history separately from fit you are guessing.
steps.evidence: The kept list with a fit reason per contact or group, marked 'seen' or 'guessed'.

steps.do: Keep the first round small: at most 100 recipients, and never above the messaging limit or what the spending cap covers. Split the list at random into two equal halves, A and B, only if at least 60 contacts remain; otherwise send one version.
steps.evidence: The final recipient count, and the A and B halves if any.

steps.do: Choose one approved template for every recipient in the round, so everyone gets the same kind of message. Its language must match the recipients' language, and its variables (such as name, product and link) should be able to carry the new angle.
steps.evidence: The template name, category and language chosen, and why it fits the angle.

steps.do: If no approved template can carry the angle, draft a new one for the owner under its true category; a sales offer is marketing. Never label a promotion as a utility message to get around the rules. The owner submits it, and nothing is sent until it shows as approved.
steps.evidence: The draft template text, its category and its review status, or a note that an existing template is used.

steps.do: Write down which variables are filled for each recipient. Confirm the template has a place for the round's full tracked link with ?v=A or ?v=B, such as a body variable; a link button with a fixed address cannot hold it.
steps.evidence: A variable map per version, with the tracked link for each and where it sits in the template.

blockers.do: If the owner has no list of opted-in contacts, stop; never find numbers elsewhere or use a bought list.
If the template is not approved, keep the draft and its review status and wait; never switch category to get around review.
If any part of the plan relies on a free-form message to someone who last wrote more than 24 hours ago, replace it with the approved template or leave that person out.
If fewer than 20 contacts remain after removals, tell the owner the result will be noisy and ask whether to go ahead or grow opt-ins first.
If the number's quality rating has dropped, plan no new sends; tell the owner and read the reasons the account shows.

C-WA-PLAN.title_zh: WhatsApp訊息資格與模板變數核對

deliver_help.recipient_list_summary: Where the list came from, the final count, and the A and B split if any.
deliver_help.fit_reasons: Why each kept contact or group fits the angle, each marked 'seen' in their history or 'guessed'.
deliver_help.exclusions: How many contacts were removed for each reason. Example: '12 opted out, 4 duplicates, 3 order updates only'.
deliver_help.template_plan: Template name, category, language, review status, and the variables and tracked link per version.

C-WA-METRICS.title: Read this goal's WhatsApp numbers
C-WA-METRICS.purpose: Record the numbers this goal is judged on for a fixed window before and after the send, so rounds are compared on real delivered messages, replies and sales rather than guesses.

steps.do: Confirm the sending number, the templates in this round, the time zone, and the window: for the baseline, the 168 hours before this round's send; for the current reading, the 168 hours starting at the send.
steps.evidence: The number, template names, time zone and the exact start and end of the window.

steps.do: Read how many messages were sent, delivered and failed in the window, per template and per version, from the template insights in WhatsApp Manager, the provider's dashboard, or the owner's screenshot. Count as delivered only what WhatsApp shows as delivered, and leave out the test message sent to the owner.
steps.evidence: Sent, delivered and failed counts as displayed, with the screen and the time read.

steps.do: Note blocks, opt-outs and any change in the quality rating during the window. If the rating dropped or opt-outs reach 2% of delivered messages, tell the owner and stop further sends.
steps.evidence: Opt-out and block counts, the quality rating, and whether sending must stop.

steps.do: If the goal counts replies, go through the chats and count each person once only if they ask about the product, its price or how to buy, or say they want it. Do not count 'stop', auto-replies, emoji-only replies, or the 'read' status.
steps.evidence: The qualifying reply count with the date of each, and the counts left out by reason, or a note that the goal does not count replies.

steps.do: If the goal counts purchases, count them only from a real record: the round's sale counter from tracking, or the owner's payment records matched to recipients or to the round's tracked link in the window. Leave out refunds and the owner's own tests, and say which sales could not be tied to this round.
steps.evidence: The purchase count with its source and what was left out, or a note that the goal does not count purchases.

steps.do: Read what this round's messages cost from the account's billing in the account currency and note it next to the numbers. Keep it out of the goal's components unless the goal lists a cost component.
steps.evidence: The message charges for the window, with the billing screen and the date read.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with the goal's exact metric component names as listed for this goal (delivered together with qualified_replies or with external_purchases, whichever the goal lists), each with its value, source and window. Never estimate a missing number.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call with component names, values and sources.

steps.do: If there is no history for a number, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline. If delivered is 0, report no rate change.
steps.evidence: Any zero values, each with the note on why.

blockers.do: If you cannot open the account's template insights, ask the owner for a screenshot of the sent, delivered and failed counts for the window.
If the account has no history for these numbers, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline.
If the numbers come from a different business number than the agreed one, do not use them and ask again.
If fewer than 24 hours have passed since the send, report the numbers as early and read them again at the end of the 168-hour window.
If there is no sale counter or payment record for the window, say there is no source and do not estimate purchases.
If the quality rating dropped or opt-outs spiked, record the numbers, tell the owner, and stop any further sends this round.

C-WA-METRICS.title_zh: WhatsApp模板到合格回覆與付款核對

deliver_help.numbers: Each of the goal's metric components by exact name with its value, as passed to record_numbers; 0 with a note where there is no history.
deliver_help.where_read: The screen, report, screenshot or record each number came from, and when it was read.
deliver_help.date_range: The exact start and end of the window, with the time zone.

C-WA-SEND.title: Send the approved WhatsApp template to the agreed list
C-WA-SEND.purpose: Send the approved template once to the agreed opted-in recipients and confirm what was delivered, because only delivered messages can turn into replies and sales.

steps.do: Right before sending, check again: the template still shows as approved, nobody on the list has opted out since it was made, the quality rating has not dropped, the count is within the messaging limit, and the expected message cost is under the owner's written cap.
steps.evidence: The time of the check and the final recipient count per version.

steps.do: Show the owner, word for word, the final message for each version with the variables filled for one example recipient, the tracked link with ?v=A or ?v=B, the sending number, the recipient count and the expected cost. Send nothing until the owner says yes to this exact text.
steps.evidence: The exact text per version and the owner's yes message.

steps.do: Send one test from the sending number to the owner's own WhatsApp. Check the name, the line breaks, and that the link opens the product through the round's tracked link. This test is left out of the round's counts.
steps.evidence: A note or screenshot of the test as received, and the page the link opened.

steps.do: Send once to the approved list. The agent sends only if it has a tool signed in to this number and the owner said yes; otherwise the owner sends from WhatsApp Manager or the provider. Each person gets one message; if a send seems to fail, check its status before trying again so nobody gets it twice.
steps.evidence: Who sent, the send time, and the count sent per version.

steps.do: After 1 hour and again after 24 hours, read each message's status: sent, delivered, read or failed. Count as delivered only what WhatsApp shows as delivered, and note the reason given for each failure.
steps.evidence: Counts by status per version, with the time read.

steps.do: Do not resend failed messages to another number or through another channel. If the reason says the number is not on WhatsApp, remove it from the list.
steps.evidence: The failed list and what was done with each.

steps.do: When someone opts out or says stop, stop all messages to them at once and add them to the do-not-message list.
steps.evidence: The do-not-message list with the time each person was added.

steps.do: When someone replies, draft an answer within 24 hours using product facts only and show it to the owner; the owner sends it, or the agent sends it after the owner's yes. Send no automatic follow-up sequence.
steps.evidence: Each reply, the answer sent, and the time it was sent.

steps.do: After 24 hours, read the actual message charges from the account's billing and compare them with the owner's cap.
steps.evidence: The charges in the account currency, the date read, and whether they stayed under the cap.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to this exact text, list and cost, send nothing; show it to them and wait.
If the template is not approved, keep the draft and its review status and wait; never use another template category to get around review.
If the sending number is not the agreed brand number, stop before sending and ask the owner to switch.
If the expected cost is above the owner's written cap, cut the list to fit or ask the owner for a new cap in writing.
If the quality rating drops or many people block during sending, stop the rest of the send and tell the owner.
If the agent has no tool signed in to this number, give the owner the exact text, list and link, and ask them to send and report the counts.

C-WA-SEND.title_zh: WhatsApp限定模板發送與狀態讀回

deliver_help.sent_text: The exact text of each version as sent, including the tracked link.
deliver_help.sent_count: How many messages were sent per version, by whom, and when.
deliver_help.delivery_status: Sent, delivered, read and failed counts per version, with the time read.
deliver_help.opt_outs: How many people opted out or blocked, and confirmation they were added to the do-not-message list.
deliver_help.message_cost: The charges shown in billing for this send, in the account currency, compared with the owner's written cap.

C-AS-ACCESS.title: Confirm the App Store app and who can edit its page
C-AS-ACCESS.purpose: Confirm the live app, the owner's App Store Connect access, and what can change on its product page right now, so the test plan only uses changes the owner can actually make this round.

steps.do: Ask the owner for the app's public App Store link and open it. Confirm the app is live and that its name and developer match the brand, and note the countries and languages shown. Work only on an app that is already live.
steps.evidence: The App Store URL, app name, developer name, and the date it was opened.

steps.do: Record the app's Apple ID, which is the number after 'id' in the App Store URL. Ask the owner for the bundle ID and the App Store Connect team the app belongs to.
steps.evidence: Apple ID, bundle ID and team name.

steps.do: The owner signs in to App Store Connect themselves, including any two-factor check on their own device. Never ask for the password or the code. Check that the owner's role can edit the product page and see App Analytics; if not, the account holder must grant it.
steps.evidence: The owner's role and whether it can edit the page and see analytics.

steps.do: Decide who makes changes: the owner, or the agent's own browser only if it is already signed in to this team and the owner says yes.
steps.evidence: Who acts, and one line on why.

steps.do: Read the app's current state in App Store Connect or from the owner's screenshots: whether a product page optimization test is already running, whether a version is waiting for or in review, and which locales get product page views.
steps.evidence: Test running or not, review state, and the locales with traffic, with the date read.

steps.do: List what a product page optimization test can change without a new build: screenshots, app previews, and an icon only if that icon is already in the live build. Promotional text can also change without a new build, but it changes the page for everyone and is not part of a test.
steps.evidence: A list of what can be tested now, what can change outside a test, and what needs a new build.

steps.do: Write anything that needs a new build, a new feature or a price change as a separate to-do for the owner, outside this round. Do not plan it as if it could be submitted now.
steps.evidence: The to-do list, or a note that none is needed.

blockers.do: If the app is not live on the App Store, stop; this goal only works on a live product page.
If the owner's role cannot edit the product page or see App Analytics, ask the account holder to grant that access and wait.
If App Store Connect asks for a two-factor code, a new agreement or a terms screen, tell the owner which screen needs it and wait; never accept or enter it for them.
If a product page optimization test is already running, do not start another; wait for it to end or ask the owner whether to stop it.
If the change needs a new build, drop it from this round and pick a change that can be tested on the current page.
If a version or test is waiting for review, note its status and wait; do not resubmit it.

C-AS-ACCESS.title_zh: App Store身分、資格與可用工具核對

deliver_help.app_store_url: The public App Store link, opened and confirmed live.
deliver_help.app_ids: The Apple ID, bundle ID and App Store Connect team name.
deliver_help.who_acts: 'owner' or 'agent browser', plus one line on why.
deliver_help.page_state: The owner's role, whether a test is running, the review state, and the locales with traffic, with the date read.
deliver_help.changeable_now: The product page parts that can be tested this round without a new build, and what needs a build later.

C-AS-PLAN.title: Plan one product page test in one locale
C-AS-PLAN.purpose: Plan a test of a single change to the product page, built from the chosen angle and real app screens, because one clear difference is the only way to know what moved the goal's main number.

steps.do: Open the public product page in the chosen locale and write down what a visitor sees first: icon, subtitle, the first three screenshots with their captions, and any preview video.
steps.evidence: A short description of the current first screen, with the URL and the date.

steps.do: Read the last 7 days of impressions, product page views and first-time downloads for that locale from App Analytics, or the owner's screenshot, by source if shown. Pick one locale; do not mix countries.
steps.evidence: Impressions, page views and first-time downloads for the locale, with the date range.

steps.do: If that locale had fewer than 500 product page views in those 7 days, tell the owner a test may end without a clear result in 168 hours, and offer a bigger locale or a longer window.
steps.evidence: The traffic check and the owner's choice.

steps.do: Choose one thing to change: the first screenshots, the app preview, or an icon already in the live build. Tie it to the chosen angle and buyer situation. Never change features or price, or show anything the app does not do.
steps.evidence: The one variable, the angle it carries, and the buyer quote or situation behind it.

steps.do: Write a brief for the treatment: which real screen of the live app each screenshot shows, and a draft caption of at most 8 words per screenshot built from the chosen angle. The copy step finalizes the words.
steps.evidence: The brief per screenshot, with the app screen and the draft caption.

steps.do: Check the brief: no invented ratings, awards, rankings, user counts or prices in any caption; the owner holds the rights to every image, font and photo it will use; and the required sizes for each device the app supports, read from App Store Connect's current screenshot specifications.
steps.evidence: A claim check per caption, a rights note per asset, and the list of required sizes.

steps.do: Set the test: the original against one treatment, half the traffic each, one locale, at least 168 hours, judged on the goal's main number. The treatment wins only if App Store Connect shows it ahead at its stated confidence; otherwise keep the original.
steps.evidence: The test settings and the written rule for picking a winner.

steps.do: Show the owner the plan, the brief and the winner rule, and get a yes before any images are made.
steps.evidence: The owner's yes to the plan.

blockers.do: If the chosen change needs a new build, drop it and choose screenshots or a preview that can be tested now.
If the traffic numbers or assets belong to a different locale than the test, go back to the round's one locale.
If the locale gets too few page views for a result in 168 hours, tell the owner and agree on a bigger locale or a longer window.
If current screens of the live app are not available, ask the owner for them; never mock up screens the app does not have.
If a caption needs a fact you do not have, remove it or ask the owner; never fill the gap with a guess.

C-AS-PLAN.title_zh: App Store現有產品頁單一素材測試

deliver_help.hypothesis: One sentence: what changes, for which buyer situation, and why it should move the goal's main number.
deliver_help.test_variable: The single thing that differs from the original, and the locale it runs in.
deliver_help.treatment_brief: Per screenshot or preview: the real app screen it shows, the draft caption, and the fact behind the caption.
deliver_help.winner_rule: How long the test runs, the traffic split, and the result needed to keep the treatment.

C-AS-METRICS.title: Read this goal's App Store numbers
C-AS-METRICS.purpose: Record the numbers this goal is judged on, for the same locale and window before and after the test, so rounds are compared on App Store Connect's own figures.

steps.do: Confirm the app, the round's locale or territory, the time zone, and the window: for the baseline, the last full 7 days before the test is submitted; for the current reading, the 168 hours from the test start. Use the same filters both times.
steps.evidence: App, locale, time zone and the exact start and end of the window.

steps.do: Open App Analytics in App Store Connect, or ask the owner for screenshots, and read product page views and first-time downloads for exactly that window and locale. Leave out redownloads.
steps.evidence: The numbers as displayed, with the screen, filters and time read.

steps.do: App Store figures can arrive a day or two late. If the window ended less than 48 hours ago, report the numbers as early and read them again later.
steps.evidence: A note on whether the numbers are final or early.

steps.do: If a product page optimization test is running, read the original and the treatment separately from the test's results, and copy the result status and confidence exactly as shown. Do not compute your own significance.
steps.evidence: Per-version numbers and the status App Store Connect shows.

steps.do: A download is not a purchase. If the owner wants sales noted, read them separately from App Store Connect's sales reports or the owner's payment records, and keep them out of this goal's numbers.
steps.evidence: Sales noted separately with their source, or a note that none were read.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with the goal's exact metric component names as listed for this goal (for this goal: first_downloads and product_page_views), each with its value, source and window. Never estimate a missing number.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call with component names, values and sources.

steps.do: If there is no history for a number, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline. If product page views are 0, report no rate change.
steps.evidence: Any zero values, each with the note on why.

blockers.do: If you cannot open App Analytics, ask the owner for a screenshot showing product page views and first-time downloads for the window and locale.
If the app has no history for these numbers, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline.
If the window ended less than 48 hours ago, report the numbers as early and read them again later.
If the numbers are for all countries or a different locale, filter again to the round's locale before recording.
If the test shows it does not have enough data, record the numbers as they are and let the test run to the end of its window; do not declare a winner.
If the screenshot or screen shows a different app, do not use those numbers and ask again.

C-AS-METRICS.title_zh: App Store產品頁到首次下載與付費核對

deliver_help.numbers: Each of the goal's metric components by exact name with its value, as passed to record_numbers; 0 with a note where there is no history.
deliver_help.where_read: The screen, report, screenshot or record each number came from, and when it was read.
deliver_help.date_range: The exact start and end of the window, with the time zone.

C-AS-LISTING.title: Submit the product page test and confirm it runs
C-AS-LISTING.purpose: Set up and submit the approved product page test exactly as planned and confirm it is running, because the goal's main number can only move once real visitors see the treatment.

steps.do: Gather the approved plan, the final treatment images, the locale, and the app's current live version. Check each image against the approved brief and the required sizes, and confirm nothing in this round touches the build, the price or the app's features.
steps.evidence: The plan, the image files and the locale, with a note that the build and price stay as they are.

steps.do: Show the owner the treatment images and captions next to the current page, plus the test settings, and get a clear yes to these exact files before anything is entered.
steps.evidence: The files shown and the owner's yes message.

steps.do: In App Store Connect's product page optimization area, the owner, or the agent's browser if signed in and the owner said yes, creates the test: a clear name, one treatment, the agreed traffic share and the one locale. Upload the treatment files for that locale only and check the preview matches the approved files.
steps.evidence: The test name, settings, and confirmation that the preview matched.

steps.do: Submit the treatment for review once. If the submit seems to fail, check the test's status before trying again so nothing is submitted twice.
steps.evidence: The submit time and the status shown afterwards.

steps.do: While the status shows waiting for review or in review, treat the test as not live. Check once a day, and do not resubmit or change the files while it is in review.
steps.evidence: The review status with the date of each check.

steps.do: If Apple rejects it, read the reason, fix only what it names, show the owner the change, and submit again only with the owner's yes.
steps.evidence: The rejection reason, the fix, and the owner's yes, or a note that it was approved.

steps.do: Once approved, start the test if it does not start by itself and note the exact start time; the 168-hour window counts from there. Ask the owner not to edit the original page or release a new app version while the test runs, so the comparison stays clean and ending the test brings the original back.
steps.evidence: The start time, the running status, and the owner's note that nothing else will change during the test.

steps.do: Open the public App Store page for that locale and confirm it loads. Visitors see the original or the treatment at random, so also confirm the running status in App Store Connect.
steps.evidence: The public App Store URL and the running status, with the time checked.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to these exact files and settings, enter nothing; show them and wait.
If App Store Connect says the change needs a new build, stop this change and go back to the plan for one that can be tested now.
If the test is still in review, wait and check once a day; never resubmit it.
If Apple rejects the treatment, fix only the stated reason and resubmit only after the owner approves the change.
If the files were added to a different locale, remove them there and add them to the round's locale before submitting.
If another product page test is running, do not create a new one; ask the owner whether to wait or stop it.

C-AS-LISTING.title_zh: App Store既有產品頁測試提交與審核續接

deliver_help.test_name: The name of the test in App Store Connect and its one locale.
deliver_help.review_state: Waiting for review, in review, rejected with the reason, or approved and running.
deliver_help.start_time: The exact time the test started running, with the time zone.
deliver_help.app_store_url: The public App Store link for the locale, opened and confirmed to load.

C-GP-ACCESS.title: Confirm the Google Play app and who can change its listing
C-GP-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which live app is being worked on, who signs in to Play Console, and what this round may change, so the listing test runs on the right app without the owner being stopped halfway.

steps.do: Ask the owner for the app's public Google Play URL. Open it with read_page and write down the package name (the part after id=), the app name, and the developer name. Confirm with the owner that the developer name is their brand.
steps.evidence: The Play URL, package name, app name, developer name, and the owner's confirmation that it is their app.

steps.do: Check that the app is live to the public: the Play URL loads the app page instead of a 'not found' message. If the app is only in internal or closed testing, stop here; store listing experiments need a published app.
steps.evidence: A note that the public page loads, and the time you checked.

steps.do: Decide who works in Play Console: the owner on their own device, or your browser if it is already signed in to the owner's developer account and the owner agrees. The owner signs in themselves. Never ask for a password. Developer identity checks, terms, and payment settings are done only by the owner.
steps.evidence: Who will work in Play Console, and how the owner signed in.

steps.do: If the owner wants someone else to make the changes, the owner invites that person's Google account in Play Console with permission to manage the store presence and view app information for this one app only. Do not ask for admin access to the whole developer account.
steps.evidence: The access that was granted and to whom, or a note that the owner will make the changes themselves.

steps.do: With Play Console open, check that whoever works in it can open this app's main store listing, the store listing experiments page, and the reports that show store listing visitors. Change nothing in this step.
steps.evidence: A list of which of these pages opened, and the time this was checked.

steps.do: Write down the current state: the default language, the translated languages, any custom store listings, and whether an experiment is already running. Open the Publishing overview and note whether managed publishing is on and whether other changes, such as a new app version, are waiting there.
steps.evidence: Default language, other languages, running experiments, managed publishing on or off, and any changes already waiting.

steps.do: Agree the limits of this round with the owner: only store listing text and graphics change (icon, screenshots, feature graphic, short and full description). Anything that needs a new app version, a new feature, or a price change goes on the owner's to-do list and is not done now.
steps.evidence: The owner's agreement to those limits, and a to-do list of product changes, or 'none'.

blockers.do: If the app is not published to the public, stop this channel and tell the owner a listing test can start only after the app is live; do not publish a new build to get there.
If the signed-in developer account does not show this package, stop and ask the owner to switch to the account that owns the app.
If Play Console asks for identity verification, a terms screen, or a payment profile, stop and tell the owner exactly which screen needs them; never do it for them.
If an experiment is already running on the same language, do not start another; wait for it to end or ask the owner to stop it.
If other changes are waiting in the Publishing overview, tell the owner, because publishing the listing test may also publish those changes.

C-GP-ACCESS.title_zh: Google Play身分、資格與可用工具核對

deliver_help.app_package: The package name of the app. Example: 'com.yourbrand.app'.
deliver_help.play_url: The public Google Play URL, opened and confirmed to load the app page.
deliver_help.who_changes_listing: 'owner' or 'agent browser', plus one line on why.
deliver_help.listing_state: Default language, other languages, any running experiment, managed publishing on or off, and anything already waiting to publish.

C-GP-PLAN.title: Plan one Google Play listing test in one language
C-GP-PLAN.purpose: Turn the chosen angle into one listing change with clear test settings, because a single change tested on a share of real visitors shows whether more of them press install.

steps.do: Open the public listing in each language you may test (add hl= and the language code to the Play URL, for example hl=en) and copy the title, short description, full description, and the order of the screenshots. Save a screenshot of what a visitor sees before scrolling.
steps.evidence: The current text and image list per language, with the date read.

steps.do: Ask the owner for the store listing visitors in the last 28 days for each language, from Play Console's reports or a screenshot. If there were fewer than about 1,000, a small text change may never show a clear result, so plan a more visible change such as the icon or first screenshot, and only one variant.
steps.evidence: The last 28 days of visitors per language, with where they were read.

steps.do: Pick one thing to change: the icon, the first two screenshots, the feature graphic, or the short description. Choose the most visible part that does not yet say the chosen angle and that the traffic allows. Change only that one thing.
steps.evidence: The chosen asset, and one sentence on why it is the weak point.

steps.do: Write one variant of that asset from the chosen angle and buyer quotes; write a second only if the listing had more than about 10,000 visitors in the last 28 days. For images, write a brief for each screen or icon. Keep the title at most 30 characters and the short description at most 80. Check every claim against the product fact sheet and what the current app version really does.
steps.evidence: The variant texts or image briefs, each with the facts it relies on.

steps.do: Remove anything Play's store listing rules or the facts do not allow: no 'best', '#1', 'top', 'free', prices, or calls to action such as 'Download now' in the title, icon, or graphics; no unnamed user quotes; no download counts, rankings, or awards that cannot be proven; and no features the app does not have.
steps.evidence: A list of words or claims removed, or a note that none were needed.

steps.do: Choose the experiment type. A default graphics experiment tests graphics in the default language only. A localized experiment tests text or graphics in a chosen language. Test one language at a time and do not mix languages in one test.
steps.evidence: The experiment type and the one language it covers.

steps.do: Set the test: an experiment audience of 50%, so half the visitors see a variant and half see the current listing. Keep Play's default confidence level and recommended target metric, pick the smallest detectable effect Play offers that its time estimate allows, and run for at least 7 days. Stop rule: apply the variant only if Play marks it better; if there is no clear result after 28 days, keep the current listing.
steps.evidence: The audience share, target metric, detectable effect, confidence level, minimum run time, and stop rule, written in one place.

steps.do: Show the owner the full plan: the exact text of each variant or the image brief, the audience share, the run time, and the stop rule. Get a clear yes before anything is made or set up; the finished images are shown again before the experiment starts.
steps.evidence: The plan as shown to the owner, and their approval message.

blockers.do: If no angle has been chosen, go back to the angle test step before planning the listing change.
If a variant needs a claim the facts do not support, drop that claim or ask the owner for proof; never fill the gap with a guess.
If the idea only works with a new feature, new build, or new price, put it on the owner's to-do list and pick a listing change that is true today.
If Play Console does not offer the experiment type you need, keep the variants and the reason, and ask the owner whether to use the other experiment type.
If the test language has no proper translation, test in a language the listing already uses well instead of machine-translating new text.

C-GP-PLAN.title_zh: Google Play語言與單一listing素材測試

deliver_help.hypothesis: One sentence: which change, for which visitors, should raise the goal's main number, and why.
deliver_help.test_asset: The one asset being changed and the language it covers. Example: 'short description, English (United States)'.
deliver_help.variants: The exact text or image brief for each variant, with the facts each one relies on.
deliver_help.test_settings: Experiment type, language, audience share, target metric, detectable effect, confidence level, minimum run time, and stop rule.

C-GP-METRICS.title: Read this goal's Google Play listing numbers
C-GP-METRICS.purpose: Record how many store listing visitors pressed install, before and after the listing change, so rounds are compared on Play's own numbers and not on guesses.

steps.do: Confirm the app package, the language of the test, the date range, and the time zone Play Console uses. Use the same length of range for baseline and current, at least 7 days. Baseline ends the day before the change went live; current starts the day it went live.
steps.evidence: Package, language filter, date range with time zone, and who will read the numbers.

steps.do: Open Play Console's reports on store listing performance, or ask the owner for a screenshot. Filter to the same language as the test. Read the store listing visitors and the number of visitors who pressed install, and write down the exact label Play shows for each.
steps.evidence: The two numbers exactly as displayed, the labels Play uses, the filter applied, and the time read.

steps.do: If an experiment is running, also open its results. For the current listing and each variant, copy the audience share, the installer counts, and Play's result with its range and status. Use the whole test period, never a single good day.
steps.evidence: The experiment numbers per variant and Play's stated result, or a note that no experiment is running.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with exactly these components: unique_install_clicks and store_visitors, for the whole listing in the agreed language. Name the report, filter, and date range in source, and say if an experiment split the visitors. If there is no history for a number, record 0 and say 'no history' in source. Never estimate a number Play does not show.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call with both components and their source.

steps.do: Keep these listing numbers apart from people who opened the app and from payments. If the owner already tracks app revenue, add revenue, refunds, and Play fees for the same range as separate lines in where_read. Leave anything unknown as unknown.
steps.evidence: A note that install numbers were not counted as active users or sales, and any revenue lines with their source.

steps.do: State the outcome. If the variant did worse, or Play shows no clear result, say the current listing stays. Never apply a variant because one day looked good.
steps.evidence: One sentence on whether the variant won, lost, or has no clear result yet.

blockers.do: If you cannot open Play Console, ask the owner for a screenshot of the store listing visitors report with the agreed filter and date range.
If Play does not show visitors or install clicks for this filter, say 'not shown' and ask the owner; do not estimate.
If the listing has no history for these numbers, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; this round sets the baseline.
If the change has been live for less than 7 days, or Play says the experiment is still collecting data, report the numbers as early and read them again later.
If the screenshot or report shows a different package or a different filter from the agreed one, do not use those numbers and read again.
If Play shows no clear winner when the stop rule is reached, record the numbers, keep the current listing, and suggest a bigger change next round.

C-GP-METRICS.title_zh: Google Play listing到取得用戶與外部付費核對
