deliver_help.numbers: unique_install_clicks and store_visitors exactly as passed to record_numbers, plus experiment results per variant if one ran.
deliver_help.where_read: The Play Console report and filters used, or 'owner screenshot', and the time the numbers were read.
deliver_help.date_range: Start and end date with the time zone. Example: '2026-11-01 to 2026-11-07, Pacific Time'.

C-GP-LISTING.title: Start the approved Google Play listing experiment
C-GP-LISTING.purpose: Put the owner-approved variant live as a Play store listing experiment on the right app, because visitors have to see the variant before any change in install clicks can be measured.

steps.do: Confirm the owner said yes to this exact plan: the asset, every variant word for word or image, the split, and the run time. Open Play Console for the agreed package and check that no other experiment is running on the same language.
steps.evidence: The owner's approval message, the package name, and a note that no other experiment overlaps.

steps.do: On the store listing experiments page, create one experiment. Name it with the round and asset, for example 'R3 short description A'. Choose the experiment type and language from the plan, and enter the audience share, target metric, detectable effect, and confidence level as planned.
steps.evidence: The experiment name and its settings as entered.

steps.do: Enter only the planned variant. Leave every other asset the same as the current listing. Check limits before saving: icon 512 x 512 pixels, feature graphic 1024 x 500 pixels, title at most 30 characters, short description at most 80.
steps.evidence: The variant as entered, with its sizes or character count.

steps.do: Preview each variant and compare it word for word with the approved version. Fix any difference before going further.
steps.evidence: Confirmation that the preview matches the approved text or images.

steps.do: The agreed person starts the experiment once: your browser only if it is signed in to the owner's account and the owner said yes, otherwise the owner. If managed publishing is on, open the Publishing overview first. If other changes are waiting there, such as a new app version, stop and ask the owner before publishing, because they would go out together.
steps.evidence: Who started the experiment, when, and what else, if anything, was published with it.

steps.do: Check the status. If it shows in review or waiting to publish, check again after 24 hours. Do not resubmit or create a second experiment. If Play rejects it, read the reason, tell the owner, and change only the flagged part with their yes.
steps.evidence: The status as Play shows it, with the time checked.

steps.do: When the experiment shows as running, note the start date and audience share, and open the public Play URL to confirm the page still loads (it may show the current listing, since only some visitors see the variant). Do not stop the test early or apply the variant; that waits for the measurement step and the owner's yes.
steps.evidence: The running status, start date, audience share, and the public Play URL.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to this exact variant and setup, do not start anything; show them the plan and stop until they answer.
If Play Console does not let you create the experiment, write down the message shown, keep the variants, and tell the owner which permission or setting is missing.
If the change is waiting under managed publishing, it is not live; tell the owner it needs their publish and check again after they do.
If other unpublished changes would go out with this one, stop and ask the owner whether to publish them together or wait.
If Play rejects the variant, show the owner the stated reason and fix only that part with their yes; never resubmit the same content unchanged.
If an image or text does not meet Play's size or length limits, resize or shorten it and show the owner the new version before entering it.

C-GP-LISTING.title_zh: Google Play既有listing實驗與發布讀回

deliver_help.experiment_name: The name given to the experiment in Play Console. Example: 'R3 short description A'.
deliver_help.experiment_status: The status as Play shows it, such as 'in review' or 'running', with the time checked.
deliver_help.store_url: The public Google Play URL of the app, opened and confirmed to load.
deliver_help.started_at: The date and time the experiment started running, with the time zone.

C-MC-ACCESS.title: Confirm the Merchant Center account and which products qualify
C-MC-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which Merchant Center account, website, countries, and products can appear in Google's free listings, so the round does not spend time on products or places Google will not show.

steps.do: Ask the owner for their website and whether they already have a Google Merchant Center account. The owner signs in themselves; your browser works in it only if it is already signed in and the owner agrees. Never ask for a password. Write down the account ID and business name shown, and confirm they match the brand.
steps.evidence: The website, the Merchant Center account ID and business name, and the owner's confirmation.

steps.do: If there is no account, create one only if the owner asks for it, with the owner's own Google account and the owner signed in. The owner accepts the terms and completes any verification. Use one real account; never create a second one.
steps.evidence: The new account ID and the owner's request, or a note that the existing account is used.

steps.do: Check that the website is verified and claimed by this account. If it is not, add it to the owner's to-do list with the exact screen that asks for it. Do not try to pass verification any other way.
steps.evidence: Website status: verified and claimed, or the to-do item for the owner.

steps.do: Read Google's current Merchant Center policy pages on what can be listed. Mark each product as qualifies, does not qualify, or unclear, with the policy URL. Google limits products that are not physical goods, such as services, subscriptions, and some software; check each one and do not assume it qualifies.
steps.evidence: A list of products with their status and the policy URL behind each.

steps.do: Check the countries the owner sells and delivers to, and whether free listings are offered there according to Google's help pages. Drop any country where they are not offered.
steps.evidence: The list of target countries, each marked offered or not, with the help page URL.

steps.do: Open the website and check for what Google asks of sellers: contact details, a return and refund policy, delivery costs and times, and a working checkout. Anything missing goes on the owner's to-do list. Never write a fake policy to get approved.
steps.evidence: A list of these items, each found (with its URL) or missing.

steps.do: Note where the product data comes from today (added by hand, a file, the store platform's app, or Google reading the website) and whether free listings are turned on. Agree with the owner: only existing products at their real price and stock; no new paid Shopping campaigns, price, or checkout changes this round.
steps.evidence: The product data source, free listings on or off, and the owner's agreement to these limits.

blockers.do: If no product qualifies under Google's policy, stop this channel, tell the owner why with the policy URL, and suggest a channel that suits the product.
If free listings are not offered in the owner's country, stop for that country and keep the help page URL as the reason.
If the website lacks a return policy, delivery details, or contact details, give the owner the exact list to add; never invent a policy.
If a terms screen, website verification, or identity check appears, stop and tell the owner which screen needs them.
If the signed-in Merchant Center account shows a different business or website, stop and ask the owner which account to use.

C-MC-ACCESS.title_zh: 商品免費曝光身分、資格與可用工具核對

deliver_help.merchant_account_id: The Merchant Center account ID and business name, confirmed by the owner.
deliver_help.website_status: Whether the website is verified and claimed by this account, and the date checked.
deliver_help.eligible_products: Each product marked qualifies, does not qualify, or unclear, with the countries and policy URL.
deliver_help.missing_requirements: Anything Google needs that the owner must add, such as a return policy or delivery details, or 'none'.

C-MC-AUDIT.title: Match each listed product to its real price, stock, and page
C-MC-AUDIT.purpose: Check every product's listing details against its live page and Google's stated issues, so the round only changes what is true and allowed, and fixes what stops products from showing.

steps.do: List every product that is, or will be, in the product data: its ID, title, link, price, availability, and main image. Read it from Merchant Center's product list, or ask the owner for the product file or a screenshot.
steps.evidence: A table of products with these fields and where they were read.

steps.do: Open each product link with read_page and write down the price, currency, stock status, title, and main image shown on the page, with the time read.
steps.evidence: The same table with the live page values and read times added.

steps.do: Compare them field by field. The price and currency must match exactly. Stock status must match. The title and image must show the same item. List every mismatch.
steps.evidence: A list of mismatches, or a note that every field matches.

steps.do: Read each product's issues in Merchant Center and its status per country (approved, limited, or not approved), with Google's stated reason. Approved does not mean the product is being shown.
steps.evidence: Status and issues per product and country, in Google's words.

steps.do: Drop products that do not qualify under Google's policy, with the reason. Do not reword a product to get around a policy.
steps.evidence: The list of dropped products, each with its reason.

steps.do: Split the fixes. Listing details you can change this round go on one list: title wording, description, choice of image, product category, and brand or barcode numbers the owner already has. Website changes such as price, checkout, or policies go on the owner's to-do list.
steps.evidence: Two lists: listing fixes for this round, and the owner's website to-do list.

steps.do: Write the proposed change for each chosen product: current value, new value, and the fact on the product page that supports it. Change one kind of field per round, such as titles only. Keep titles under 150 characters with the words buyers use first, and no promotional text like 'free shipping' or 'best price'. Use images without added text or watermarks.
steps.evidence: A change list with current value, new value, and supporting fact for each product.

blockers.do: If a product does not qualify, drop it with the policy reason; if none qualify, stop this channel and tell the owner.
If the listing price differs from the page price, put it at the top of the owner's to-do list; never change the shop's price to win a listing.
If you cannot see the product list in Merchant Center, ask the owner for a screenshot of it or for the product file.
If a product link does not load, mark that product as blocked and tell the owner which link fails.
If an issue points at a missing website requirement, add it to the owner's to-do list and do not work around it.
If a product is limited only in some countries, keep the countries where it shows and note why the others are out.

C-MC-AUDIT.title_zh: 商品feed資格、價格與庫存核對

deliver_help.product_check: Each product with its listing values next to the live page values, and the time read.
deliver_help.issues_found: Each product's status and Google's stated issues per country, plus any mismatch found.
deliver_help.listing_changes: The proposed changes per product: field, current value, new value, and the supporting fact.
deliver_help.owner_todo: Website or product changes only the owner can make, such as a price fix or a missing return policy, or 'none'.

C-MC-METRICS.title: Read this goal's numbers from Google free listings
C-MC-METRICS.purpose: Record the goal's main number from Google's free listings and the owner's own site and payment records, before and after the listing change, so rounds are compared on real numbers.

steps.do: Confirm the Merchant Center account, the products in this round, the countries, the date range, and the time zone. Use the same products and the same length of range for baseline and current, at least 7 days. Baseline ends the day before the change; current starts the day the change was approved.
steps.evidence: Account ID, product IDs, countries, date range with time zone, and who will read the numbers.

steps.do: Open Merchant Center's performance reports, or ask the owner for a screenshot. Filter to free listings only, this round's products, and the agreed countries. Read impressions and clicks. Keep paid Shopping ads out of these numbers.
steps.evidence: Impressions and clicks exactly as displayed, the filter used, and the time read.

steps.do: If the goal counts site visits or purchases, read visits from free listings in the site analytics the owner already uses, filtered by the round's tag on the product link, and read purchases from the round's sale counter or the owner's payment records. Never infer sales from approved status or from clicks.
steps.evidence: Visits and purchases with the tool each came from, or a note that the goal does not need them.

steps.do: Take out purchases that were refunded or cancelled within the range, if the payment records show them. If the owner has records of delivery or payment fees, list them in where_read; leave anything unknown as unknown.
steps.evidence: Purchases after refunds, and any cost lines with their source.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with exactly the components this goal lists: listing_clicks and listing_impressions when the goal lists those, or external_purchases and attributed_sessions when it lists those. Name the report, filter, and range in source. If there is no history, record 0 and say 'no history' in source. Never estimate.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call with the goal's components and their source.

steps.do: Note anything that makes the range unfair to compare, such as products not approved for part of it, a country dropped, or a price change. Say so plainly next to the numbers.
steps.evidence: A list of such events with dates, or a note that there were none.

blockers.do: If you cannot open Merchant Center, ask the owner for a screenshot of the performance report with free listings, the products, and the date range shown.
If the report cannot separate free listings from paid ads, say so and do not use mixed numbers as free listing numbers.
If the owner has no site analytics or tagged link for these visits, record 0 with 'not tracked' in source, add setting up site analytics to the owner's to-do list, and do not estimate.
If there is no history for these numbers, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; this round sets the baseline.
If the change was approved less than 7 days ago, report the numbers as early and read them again later.
If the products show no impressions at all, check their status and countries before recording, and report that they are not being shown.

C-MC-METRICS.title_zh: 商品免費曝光點擊到外部購買核對

deliver_help.numbers: The goal's components exactly as passed to record_numbers, with any refunds already taken out.
deliver_help.where_read: The Merchant Center report and filters, the analytics or payment tool, or 'owner screenshot', and the time read.
deliver_help.date_range: Start and end date with the time zone. Example: '2026-11-01 to 2026-11-07, Taipei time'.

C-MC-LISTING.title: Update the approved product details for Google free listings
C-MC-LISTING.purpose: Put the owner-approved listing changes live on existing products, with a tagged link back to the site, because buyers have to see the new details before clicks or purchases can change.

steps.do: Show the owner, for every product, the exact current and new value of each field from the change list. Get a clear yes. Change only existing products at their real price and stock.
steps.evidence: The change list as shown to the owner, and their approval message.

steps.do: Prepare each product link on the owner's own verified website. Add this round's tag to it, for example '?utm_source=google&utm_medium=free_listing&utm_campaign=round3&v=A'. Do not replace it with a link on another domain, because Google rejects links that lead off the verified site. Open the tagged link and check it loads the right product.
steps.evidence: Each tagged link, opened and confirmed to load the right product page.

steps.do: Check the round's sale counter from tracking is on the page shown after payment, so purchases from this round are counted. If it is not, ask the owner to add it before the change goes live.
steps.evidence: A note that the sale counter is in place, or the owner's to-do item.

steps.do: Make the changes where the product data comes from: the store platform's app, the product file, or Merchant Center itself; if Google reads the products from the website, the owner changes them on the website. Otherwise the next update will overwrite them. Make them yourself only if your browser is signed in to the account and the owner said yes; otherwise give the owner the change list. Change only the approved fields, and save the old values so they can be restored.
steps.evidence: Who made the changes, the fields changed per product, the old values saved, and the time of the change.

steps.do: Wait for Google to process the change. Check each product's status after a few hours and again each day for up to 3 days. A product that is submitted or approved is not yet proof it is being shown.
steps.evidence: Each product's status per country after processing, with the time checked.

steps.do: If a product is not approved, read Google's stated issue, tell the owner, and fix only that field with their yes. Never turn on paid Shopping ads to get around it, and never change the shop's price to fit the listing.
steps.evidence: The issue, the fix the owner approved, and the new status, or a note that every product was approved.

steps.do: When products are approved, search Google Shopping for one product's title, with your browser if it has one or by asking the owner, from a target country, and look for the listing. If you find it, open it and confirm the title, price, and image match the approved version.
steps.evidence: The public listing URL with what it shows, or a note that it was not found yet and when you searched.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to these exact changes, do not change anything; show them the list and stop until they answer.
If Google rejects a product, read the item's issue and fix only the field it names, with the owner's yes.
If the changes disappear after the next sync, make them again in the source the product data comes from, not in Merchant Center alone.
If the rejection is about the website, such as a missing return policy, add it to the owner's to-do list; never invent a policy.
If a country is not offered, keep the change for the other countries and note the reason from Google's help page.
If products are approved but cannot be found, wait at least 3 days and check impressions in the measurement step before changing anything else.

C-MC-LISTING.title_zh: 既有商品免費listing提交與審核續接

deliver_help.changed_products: Each product ID with the field changed, the old value, the new value, and the tagged link.
deliver_help.approval_status: Each product's status per country after processing, in Google's words.
deliver_help.public_listing_url: The Google Shopping URL where a changed product was seen live, or 'not found yet' with the date searched.
deliver_help.changed_at: The date and time the changes were saved, with the time zone; the current measurement starts from approval.

C-RV-ACCESS.title: Confirm the directory listing and who can edit it
C-RV-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which review directory and which existing listing this round works on, who controls it, and what its rules allow, so later edits and review requests land on the right page without breaking the directory's rules.

steps.do: Search the directories buyers of this product category use to compare options, such as G2, Capterra, Trustpilot or AlternativeTo, for the product name and the brand domain. Propose one directory to the owner with a one-line reason, preferring one where the product already has a listing, and get the owner's confirmation.
steps.evidence: The directories searched, what was found on each, and the owner's message confirming the chosen one.

steps.do: If a listing already exists on the chosen directory, open it with read_page and write down its URL, product name, website link and whether it shows as claimed. Never create a second listing for the same product.
steps.evidence: The listing URL with its name, website link and claim status, or a note that no listing exists.

steps.do: Confirm with the owner that the listing is theirs and that they can sign in to the directory's vendor or business account that manages it. If no listing exists, create one only if the owner asks for it in this conversation.
steps.evidence: The owner's confirmation that the listing is theirs and which account manages it.

steps.do: Read the directory's current public rules for claiming a listing, editing it, and asking customers for reviews, and save the URL of each rule page. Note especially: no rewards in exchange for reviews, no asking only happy customers, and no reviews from the owner, staff or test accounts.
steps.evidence: A short list of the rules that apply, each with the URL it came from and the date read.

steps.do: Decide who will make edits: the owner in their own browser, or the agent's browser if it is already signed in to the managing account. The owner signs in themselves; never ask for a password. If the owner asked for a new vendor account and the directory accepts any email, the agent may sign up with inbox_address and read the code with inbox_latest; if it needs an email on the brand's domain, the owner signs up.
steps.evidence: Who will edit the listing and how they are signed in.

steps.do: List which listing features are free and which need a paid plan or new terms, such as a premium profile or lead forms. Do not upgrade, pay or accept terms; put each one in front of the owner as a separate choice.
steps.evidence: A free versus paid list, with any decision left to the owner.

steps.do: Ask the owner what real customer proof already exists that may be used: published reviews, customer messages, or case notes, and whether each customer agreed to be quoted. Do not borrow reviews or case studies from other brands or products.
steps.evidence: A list of real customer proof with where each piece came from and whether permission to quote exists.

blockers.do: If the product already has a listing, or more than one, work on the existing one the owner controls and never create another.
If the directory is still verifying the owner's claim, record the date it was started and keep preparing facts and customer proof until it is approved.
If a code sent to the owner's email, an identity check or a terms screen appears, stop and tell the owner which screen and which button; never accept terms for them.
If the change the round needs only works on a paid plan, tell the owner the price shown and stop that part until they decide.
If the listing belongs to another company or a reseller, do not touch it and ask the owner how they want to proceed.

C-RV-ACCESS.title_zh: 第三方目錄與真實評價身分、資格與可用工具核對

deliver_help.listing_url: The public URL of the existing listing, opened and confirmed to be the owner's product, or 'none' with the owner's decision.
deliver_help.claim_status: Whether the listing is claimed by the owner, waiting for the directory to verify, or unclaimed.
deliver_help.who_edits: 'owner' or 'agent browser', plus one line on why.
deliver_help.rules_noted: The directory's rules on editing and asking for reviews that matter this round, each with its URL, plus any feature that needs a paid plan or new terms, left for the owner to decide.
deliver_help.proof_sources: The real customer proof that exists, where each piece came from, and whether the customer agreed to be quoted, or 'none yet'.

C-RV-PROOF.title: Ask real customers for honest reviews and quotes
C-RV-PROOF.purpose: Collect honest reviews and quotes from real paying customers, with permission to use each one, because believable proof from real buyers is what turns directory visitors into inquiries and purchases.

steps.do: Ask the owner for customers who actually paid and used the product, from their payment or delivery records. Leave out the owner, staff, friends who did not buy, and test accounts. If there are more than 10, take the 10 most recent buyers by a neutral rule such as purchase date, never by how happy they seem.
steps.evidence: A list of up to 10 real customers, the record that shows each one paid, and the rule used to pick them.

steps.do: For each person, check they can be contacted for this purpose: they are an existing customer reached through the channel they used with the owner, and they have not opted out. Remove anyone who unsubscribed or asked not to be contacted.
steps.evidence: The final contact list, with anyone removed and why.

steps.do: Draft one short request under 120 words, sent from the owner by name. Ask neutral questions: what they used it for, what changed, and what could be better. Ask every customer on the list the same way, offer no reward tied to a review, and include the directory's direct review link if they want to post there. If it goes by email, send it from the owner's normal address and include a line saying they can reply 'no more emails'.
steps.evidence: The exact request text and the review link it uses.

steps.do: Show the owner the exact request text and the list of recipients and get a clear yes. The owner sends it, or the agent sends it with its own tools only after that yes. Send each one personally, not as a bulk blast.
steps.evidence: The owner's approval message and the date each request was sent.

steps.do: Wait 72 hours. Send at most one polite reminder to people who have not answered, using text the owner approved. Never contact anyone a third time.
steps.evidence: Who answered, who got one reminder, and the dates.

steps.do: Save every answer word for word, including negative ones. Never rewrite, shorten in a way that changes meaning, or write a review for a customer. Record the URL of any review they posted on the directory.
steps.evidence: Each customer's original words with date and source, and the URL of each published review.

steps.do: Before using any quote outside the directory, ask the customer in writing where it may appear (website, listing, posts), how their name should show (full name, first name and company, or anonymous), and tell them they can withdraw it at any time.
steps.evidence: For each quote, the customer's written permission with the places and name format they allowed.

steps.do: If a customer offers to introduce someone else, accept only an introduction that person agreed to, and let the customer make it. Never ask customers for other people's contact details.
steps.evidence: Each introduction offered, with confirmation the person agreed, or a note that there were none.

blockers.do: If the owner has no paying customers yet, stop this step and say so; never use the owner's own tests or friends' opinions as reviews.
If the owner has not said yes to the exact request text and list, do not send anything; show them and wait.
If the request offers a reward for a review or is aimed only at happy customers, remove the reward, keep everyone on the list, and show the owner the corrected text before anything is sent.
If a customer has not agreed in writing to a use, do not use their words there; use only reviews they posted themselves.
If the directory removes a review, save the reason and the rule it cites, and never replace it with a made-up one.

C-RV-PROOF.title_zh: 真實客戶心得來源與推薦範圍核對

deliver_help.customer_quotes: Each customer's answer word for word, with the date and where it came from.
deliver_help.use_permission: For each quote, where it may be used and how the customer's name may appear, as they wrote it.
deliver_help.published_reviews: The URL of each review real customers posted on the directory this round, or 'none yet'.
deliver_help.referrals: Introductions customers offered with the other person's agreement, or 'none'.

C-RV-METRICS.title: Read this goal's numbers from the directory listing
C-RV-METRICS.purpose: Record the numbers this goal is judged on for visits, inquiries or purchases that came from the directory listing, for a fixed range before and after the change, so rounds are compared on real numbers.

steps.do: Confirm the listing URL, whether this is the baseline or the current reading, the date range and the time zone. Use the same range length for both readings; this goal watches results for 168 hours (7 days).
steps.evidence: Listing URL, baseline or current, date range with time zone.

steps.do: For attributed_sessions, use the click count of the round's tracked link from tracking if the listing's website link is that tracked link. Otherwise ask the owner for visits referred by the directory's domain in the site analytics they already use, and name that source. If the directory's vendor reporting shows listing views or website clicks, note them in source as a cross-check, not as the count.
steps.evidence: The visit count, the tool it came from and the range it covers.

steps.do: If the goal needs qualified_inquiries, count different people who contacted the owner through the listing in the range (the directory's contact or lead form, messages that name the directory, or the lead source field if the owner already uses a CRM) and showed a real need the product fits. Leave out spam, vendors, job seekers and the owner's own tests.
steps.evidence: The inquiry count, with one line per person on why they qualify.

steps.do: If the goal needs external_purchases, count paid orders from real outside customers in the range that came through the listing, using the sale counter from tracking or the owner's payment records with the directory as source. Leave out owner tests and orders refunded in the range.
steps.evidence: The purchase count, its source, and any orders left out with the reason.

steps.do: Count published reviews separately from reviews still waiting for moderation, and never count a review as an inquiry or a purchase. Note any listing or sponsorship fee paid in the range in source, so the round's cost is visible.
steps.evidence: Published and pending review counts, and any fees paid, written in the source note.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with the goal's exact metric component names as listed for this goal, each with its source and range, using the same sources for baseline and current. If there is no history, record 0 and say so in source. Never estimate a missing number; if a number cannot be read, say which one and why.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call with each component, its value and its source.

blockers.do: If the listing's website link is not the round's tracked link and the owner has no site analytics, record visits as unavailable in source and do not estimate them.
If the listing has no history for these numbers, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline.
If no payment record can show which orders came from the directory, say so plainly and record only what the sale counter or records prove.
If visits are 0, record it and say the rate cannot be compared yet; do not report a percentage change.
If less than 168 hours have passed since the change, report the numbers as early and read them again when the range ends.

C-RV-METRICS.title_zh: 目錄與真實評價帶來的外部購買核對

deliver_help.numbers: Each of the goal's metric components by exact name with its value, 0 with a note where there is no history.
deliver_help.where_read: For each number, the tool or report it came from, such as the tracked link, site analytics or payment records.
deliver_help.date_range: The start and end of the range with time zone, and whether it is the baseline or the current reading.

C-RV-LISTING.title: Update the existing directory listing with proven facts
C-RV-LISTING.purpose: Rewrite the owner's existing directory listing so every field is true, specific and points to the round's tracked link, because a clear, credible listing is what makes directory visitors click through and get in touch or buy.

steps.do: With whoever edits signed in, open the listing's edit page, or ask the owner for screenshots of it if they edit. Write down every field the directory asks for, such as category, short description, long description, features, pricing, screenshots, website link and support contact, with each field's length limit and current value.
steps.evidence: A table of fields with their current values and length limits.

steps.do: Draft new values for each field from the product fact sheet and the approved copy. Every claim must match a current fact; do not add customer counts, ratings, awards or integrations you cannot show. Keep each field under its limit.
steps.evidence: The new value for each field, with the fact each claim relies on.

steps.do: Use customer quotes only from people who gave written permission for this use, word for word, with the name format they allowed. Set the website link field to the round's tracked link if the directory accepts it and it does not break the domain check used for the claim; otherwise use the plain product URL and note it.
steps.evidence: The quotes used with their permission, and the link placed in the website field.

steps.do: Change only what this round tests, such as the description's opening or the order of real customer quotes, and keep the rest as it was so the result can be compared.
steps.evidence: An old versus new table that shows which fields changed and why.

steps.do: Show the owner the old and new text for every changed field word for word and get a clear yes. Anything that needs a paid plan, new terms or a new promise to buyers stays out unless the owner decides it separately.
steps.evidence: The owner's approval message for the exact new text.

steps.do: The owner, or the agent's signed-in browser after that yes, saves the changes once on the existing listing. Never create a new listing. If the directory sends the edit to moderation, do not resubmit it while it waits.
steps.evidence: Who saved the changes, when, and the status the directory showed right after.

steps.do: Check the status again within 48 hours, and every 48 hours while it waits, without resubmitting. When the edit is live, open the public listing URL, compare the text with the approved version, and click the website link to confirm it opens the product.
steps.evidence: The public listing URL, the text as shown there, and confirmation the website link works.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to the exact new text, do not save anything; show them and wait.
If the edit page belongs to a different listing than the one confirmed earlier, stop and edit only the confirmed listing.
If the listing cannot be edited until the claim is approved, keep the approved text ready and check the claim again in 48 hours.
If a field can only be changed on a paid plan, leave it as it is and tell the owner the price shown.
If the directory rejects the edit, save its reason, fix only what it names, and show the owner the corrected text before saving again.

C-RV-LISTING.title_zh: 第三方目錄現有產品listing更新

deliver_help.listing_url: The public URL of the updated listing, opened and checked after the change.
deliver_help.changes_made: Each changed field with its old and new text exactly as approved.
deliver_help.review_status: 'live', 'waiting for moderation' or 'rejected', with the date checked and any reason the directory gave.

C-PT-ACCESS.title: Confirm the sales accounts, offer and partner terms
C-PT-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which account contacts partners and buyers, which offer and terms can be used today, and how referrals are counted, so every later message goes out from the right place and every sale can be counted.

steps.do: Ask the owner which account will send messages to partners and buyers, for example the business email address or a partner program dashboard. Ask where past conversations are kept: the inbox, a spreadsheet, or, if the owner already uses a CRM, that CRM. Write down where you will read conversations and, separately, which account will send.
steps.evidence: The sending account, where past conversations are kept, and who can open each.

steps.do: Have the owner sign in to the sending account themselves, or confirm the agent's browser is already signed in to it. Check that the name and address shown match the brand. Never ask for a password. If the owner asked for a new sign-up, for example on an affiliate platform they chose, use inbox_address for the email and inbox_latest for the verification code, create only one real account, and follow that platform's rules.
steps.evidence: The signed-in account name and address, who signed in, and any new account the owner asked for.

steps.do: Use read_page on the product's pricing page and write down the offer that can be sold today: plans, prices, currency, trial length, refund policy, and any discount that already exists. Have the owner confirm it. Do not create new plans, discounts, bundles or billing.
steps.evidence: An offer sheet with each line linked to the page it came from, and the owner's confirmation.

steps.do: Ask the owner for existing partner terms: the commission or referral reward, when it is paid, how long a referral counts, and which logos, screenshots and claims partners may use. If no terms exist, write 'no terms yet' and list two or three options for the owner to decide. Never promise a commission yourself.
steps.evidence: The existing terms quoted from their source, or 'no terms yet' with the options shown to the owner.

steps.do: Check how referrals will be counted. If the owner already runs an affiliate or referral program, record its link format. If not, do not set up a new program; call tracking for this round's tracked link and plan one label per partner (?v=A for the first, ?v=B for the second, and so on). Confirm with the owner that the sale counter from tracking is on the page shown after payment.
steps.evidence: The referral link format, or the round's tracked link with its labels, and whether the sale counter is in place.

steps.do: List who this round may contact and why: partners who publicly invite partnership requests, and buyers who asked a question, started a trial, or bought before. Get the list of people who unsubscribed or said no, and remove them. Having worked with someone before is not permission to send them bulk messages.
steps.evidence: The contact list with the reason each person may be contacted, and the opt-out list that was applied.

steps.do: Agree with the owner on limits for this round, for example at most 10 new partner contacts and at most 2 follow-ups per person, and on who presses send. Write the summary in five lines and get the owner's yes.
steps.evidence: The five-line summary and the owner's approval message.

blockers.do: If the signed-in account is personal or belongs to another brand, stop and ask the owner to switch accounts or to send the messages themselves.
If a verification step, terms screen or identity check appears that inbox_latest cannot answer, stop and tell the owner which screen and which button.
If there are no partner terms, give the owner options to choose from; do not sign anything or promise a commission.
If the sale counter is not on the after-payment page, ask the owner to add it before any outreach, or to name the payment report that will be used instead.
If the price or plans on the page do not match what the owner says, use neither until the owner confirms which one is correct.
If nobody can say who unsubscribed or said no, contact only people who wrote to the owner in the last 90 days and did not ask to stop.

C-PT-ACCESS.title_zh: 合作、推薦與銷售接力身分、資格與可用工具核對

deliver_help.sending_account: The account that sends messages, who signed in, and who presses send. Example: 'sales@example.com, signed in by the owner, owner sends'.
deliver_help.current_offer: Plans, prices, trial and refund terms exactly as shown on the product page, with that page's URL.
deliver_help.partner_terms: The existing commission or referral terms with their source, or 'no terms yet' plus the options shown to the owner.
deliver_help.referral_tracking: The tracked link or referral link format, the label for each partner, and whether the sale counter is on the after-payment page.
deliver_help.contact_rules: Who may be contacted and why, the opt-out list applied, and the limits agreed for this round.

C-PT-FIND.title: Find partners whose audience already needs this product
C-PT-FIND.purpose: Produce a short, checked list of partners whose real audience matches the buyer and who publicly invite partnership requests, because the right partner is what turns referrals into qualified buyers.

steps.do: Write a short partner brief from the earlier steps: the buyer group, their strongest motive, what the product does, and the current offer. Pick which partner types fit: creators, newsletters, affiliate or review sites, resellers or agencies, and products used alongside this one.
steps.evidence: The brief in five lines or fewer, and the partner types chosen with one reason each.

steps.do: Search the web with queries such as '{related product} partner program', '{buyer group} newsletter sponsor', '{niche} affiliate' and '{buyer group} agency', with the brackets replaced by this product and buyer. Collect at least 15 candidates. Skip direct competitors.
steps.evidence: The queries used, the date, and at least 15 candidate names with URLs.

steps.do: For each candidate, use read_page on at least three pieces of their content from the last 90 days. Note who they write for and whether those readers have the problem the product solves. Do not rank by follower count alone.
steps.evidence: For each candidate, the URLs read and one line on how their audience matches the buyer, or why it does not.

steps.do: Check whether each candidate publicly invites partnership contact: a 'work with us', sponsor, partner or affiliate page, or a public partner program. Record that page and the contact route it gives. Drop candidates with no public invitation.
steps.evidence: The invitation page URL and contact route for each remaining candidate, and the list of dropped ones.

steps.do: Read each candidate's public terms: sponsorship prices, affiliate rules, required disclosure, and anything they will not promote. If a term is not published, write 'unknown'; do not guess.
steps.evidence: Terms per candidate, quoted with their URL, or marked unknown.

steps.do: For each candidate, write the one thing they would do (a newsletter mention, a review, a referral link, reselling) and what the owner can offer in return under existing terms only.
steps.evidence: A role and an offer for each candidate, each within the existing terms.

steps.do: Rank candidates by audience match first, then by how clearly they invite contact, then by fit with existing terms. Keep 5 to 10, and note any conflict, such as also promoting a competitor.
steps.evidence: A ranked shortlist of 5 to 10 partners with the reason for each rank and any conflicts.

steps.do: Show the shortlist to the owner and ask which partners to contact this round, within the contact limit agreed earlier. Send nothing in this step.
steps.evidence: The owner's reply naming the approved partners.

blockers.do: If no buyer group or motive was chosen earlier, go back to the buyer grouping step before searching.
If fewer than five candidates match the audience, widen to nearby topics or buyer groups and tell the owner the list is thin.
If a strong candidate does not publicly invite contact, leave them off the list; do not hunt for private emails.
If a candidate sells or promotes a direct competitor, mark the conflict and leave the choice to the owner.
If the owner has no partner terms to offer, show the shortlist with the open terms question and promise nothing.

C-PT-FIND.title_zh: 合作夥伴受眾、需求與交付適配研究

deliver_help.shortlist: The 5 to 10 ranked partners with name, URL, role, and the owner's yes or no for each.
deliver_help.fit_evidence: For each partner, the content URLs you read and one line on why their audience matches the buyer.
deliver_help.contact_route: For each partner, the public page that invites partnership contact and the address or form it gives.
deliver_help.partner_terms_or_unknown: Each partner's published terms quoted with the URL, or 'unknown'.

C-PT-METRICS.title: Read this goal's partner and sales numbers
C-PT-METRICS.purpose: Record the two numbers this goal is judged on for a fixed window, counted once per real buyer and net of refunds and tests, so rounds are compared on real sales rather than interest.

steps.do: Call where_are_we and copy this goal's exact metric component names and its observation window. Each goal has its own pair, for example qualified_referrals and referred_people. Use only the names this goal lists, and never borrow numbers from another goal.
steps.evidence: The goal id, its component names copied exactly, and its observation window in hours.

steps.do: Fix the window and time zone. For the baseline, use the window just before this round started; for the current reading, use the same length of time since the round started (168 hours for these goals). Do not take the current reading before the window ends.
steps.evidence: Start and end of the window with time zone, and whether it is the baseline or the current reading.

steps.do: Gather the sources: clicks and sales from tracking, the payment system's report, the inbox threads, the partner program's own report if one exists, and, if the owner already uses a CRM, that CRM. If you cannot open a source, ask the owner for a screenshot or export of that exact window.
steps.evidence: Each source named, with the time you read it or the file the owner sent.

steps.do: Build one list with one row per person or company, merging duplicates by email or company name; a sale that shows in both the payment report and a partner report counts once. Before counting, write the rule for each component, for example 'qualified means matches the buyer group and had a real two-way conversation or started a trial', or 'dormant means no reply for 21 days or more'.
steps.evidence: The deduplicated list and the written counting rule for each component.

steps.do: Remove anything that is not a real outside buyer: the owner's and team's own purchases, test payments, bots, the agent's own messages, refunded orders and duplicates. Credit a sale to a partner or follow-up only if a partner link, a label, or the buyer's own words show it; otherwise mark its source unknown.
steps.evidence: The count removed for each reason, and how many sales have an unknown source.

steps.do: Count money as received, not promised: a signed contract or an unpaid invoice is not a purchase. Note refunds, delivery costs, and commissions owed in the window; an unpaid commission is owed, not paid.
steps.evidence: Paid, unpaid and refunded amounts listed separately, with commissions owed.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with each component under its exact name and a source that says where each number was read. If there is no history, record 0 and say 'no history' in source. Never estimate. If the denominator is 0, say so in source and do not report a rate change.
steps.evidence: The values and sources passed to record_numbers, as accepted.

steps.do: Write one line on where the numbers stall: too few people entering, people not qualifying, or qualified people not acting or paying. This points the next round at the partner, the message, or the follow-up.
steps.evidence: One line naming the stalled stage and the numbers behind it.

blockers.do: If there is no history for these numbers, record 0 and say 'no history' in source; the first round then sets the baseline.
If you cannot open the payment report, ask the owner for an export or screenshot of the exact window; never estimate sales.
If a sale cannot be tied to a partner or follow-up, count its source as unknown and do not credit the partner.
If the owner's, team's or test payments are mixed in and cannot be separated, ask the owner to mark them before you record anything.
If the window has not ended, report the reading as early and read again when it ends.
If the denominator is 0, record 0, say so in source, and do not claim any rate.

C-PT-METRICS.title_zh: 合作、喚回與採購的外部成交淨貢獻核對

deliver_help.numbers: Each component under its exact name with its value, for example 'qualified_referrals: 4, referred_people: 11'.
deliver_help.where_read: Each source and when it was read, what was removed and why, and any sale whose source is unknown.
deliver_help.date_range: Start and end of the window with time zone, and whether it is the baseline or the current reading.

C-PT-ENABLE.title: Ask approved partners, then give each a kit and own link
C-PT-ENABLE.purpose: Send one honest partnership request to each approved partner, then hand those who say yes a short, accurate kit with their own tracked link, so their audience hears a true message and every referral is counted.

steps.do: From the shortlist the owner approved, split partners into two groups: those who already agreed in writing to promote the product, and those not asked yet. Note the terms that apply to each, from the earlier account check.
steps.evidence: The two groups, a quote of or link to each existing yes, and the terms that apply.

steps.do: For each partner not asked yet, write one personal partnership request under 150 words, for the contact route their public page gives. Name their audience and one piece of their recent content, say plainly that you write for the owner's brand, say the one thing you ask them to do, and offer only existing terms.
steps.evidence: Each draft request with its recipient, contact route, and the content it mentions.

steps.do: Show the owner each request word for word and get a clear yes. Send once per partner from the agreed account; the agent sends only if it has the tools and the owner said yes, otherwise the owner sends. Wait 5 business days, send at most one short owner-approved follow-up, then stop. A no ends contact.
steps.evidence: For each request, the recipient, send time, who sent it, and the partner's reply or 'no answer'.

steps.do: Give each partner who agreed their own link: their existing referral link if a program exists, or this round's tracked link with their label (?v=A, ?v=B, and so on). Open each link and confirm it lands on the product page.
steps.evidence: One link per agreed partner, each opened and confirmed to load the product.

steps.do: Write a one-page kit: who the product is for, the problem it solves, three benefits taken from the proven benefits list, the price as shown on the product page, the partner's link, and a disclosure line such as 'affiliate link' or 'sponsored'. Add only images and screenshots the owner owns.
steps.evidence: The kit text, the images attached, and the source for each claim.

steps.do: Add a short 'please do not say' list: no invented results, no guarantees, no fake urgency, and no discount that does not exist. Check every sentence of the kit against the product facts.
steps.evidence: The 'do not say' list and a sentence-by-sentence fact check of the kit.

steps.do: Write a short delivery message for each agreed partner that restates the terms plainly. Show the owner each message and the kit word for word, and get a clear yes.
steps.evidence: Each final message with its recipient, and the owner's approval.

steps.do: Send the kit once per partner from the agreed account, the same way as the request. If it is unclear whether a message went, check the sent folder before sending again.
steps.evidence: For each partner, the recipient, subject line, send time, and who sent it.

steps.do: Record each partner's link, terms and send date. Count a commission as owed only when a counted sale exists, and as paid only when it has actually been paid.
steps.evidence: A partner record with link, terms, send date, and commission status.

steps.do: If a partner has not confirmed the kit after 5 business days, send at most one owner-approved check-in, then stop. When a partner or a referred buyer asks a buying question, pass it to the sales follow-through step.
steps.evidence: Each partner's status (active, declined, or no answer) and any buyer questions passed on.

blockers.do: If a partner has not agreed in writing, send only the partnership request, never the kit or their link.
If the owner has not said yes to the exact request, kit or message, do not send; show them the text and wait.
If there are no agreed terms, mention no commission in any request or kit; ask the owner to decide the terms first.
If a partner's link does not load the product page, fix it with tracking before sending anything.
If the owner has no images they own, send a text-only kit; never use images taken from elsewhere.
If a partner does not reply after one follow-up, stop and mark them 'no answer'; do not try another channel.

C-PT-ENABLE.title_zh: 既有合作夥伴銷售資料與推薦連結交付

deliver_help.partners_contacted: Each partner asked or given the kit, with their status: agreed, active, declined, or no answer.
deliver_help.kit_text: The exact kit as sent, including the disclosure line and the 'do not say' list.
deliver_help.partner_links: Each agreed partner's link with its label, opened and confirmed to load the product.
deliver_help.sent_messages: Recipient, subject line, send time and who sent it, for every request, kit and follow-up.
deliver_help.buyer_handoffs: Any buyer question or referred buyer passed to the sales follow-through step, or 'none yet'.

C-PT-CLOSE.title: Move each open buyer to their next real step
C-PT-CLOSE.purpose: Sort every open inquiry, trial, stalled deal, past customer and company lead by where they really are, and move each forward by one buyer action, because only confirmed buyer actions turn into paid sales.

steps.do: Collect every open buyer in the inbox and, if the owner already uses a CRM, that CRM: people who asked a question, started a trial, went quiet, or are a company lead in the last 90 days, plus customers who bought in the last 12 months. Write one row each with the last message date and who wrote last.
steps.evidence: A buyer list with one row per person or company, the last message date, and who wrote last.

steps.do: Give each row one stage: new inquiry, active trial, stalled (no reply for 21 days or more), past customer, or company deal. Remove anyone who said no or unsubscribed.
steps.evidence: Each row with its stage, and the removed people with the reason.

steps.do: For each buyer, copy from their own messages what they need, their problem, budget, timing, and who decides. Mark a field 'not asked yet' when they have not said it; never fill it with a guess.
steps.evidence: Each buyer's needs in their own words, with missing fields marked.

steps.do: Compare each need with what the product does today, using the product fact sheet. If the product cannot do it, mark 'no fit', write the reason, and note it as a product request for the owner. Do not promise future features.
steps.evidence: Each buyer marked fit or no fit, with the reason and the fact it rests on.

steps.do: Choose one next buyer action for each fit: answer their question, a short follow-up, a tailored demo, a business case, a small pilot, or help with company purchasing. Pick the one that removes what is stopping them now.
steps.evidence: One next action per buyer and the obstacle it removes.

steps.do: Draft any direct replies needed, answering the buyer's actual question with existing offers only and the round's tracked link when pointing to the product. Show the owner each reply word for word and get a yes. The agent sends only if it has the tools and the owner said yes; otherwise the owner sends.
steps.evidence: Each approved reply, its recipient, the send time, and who sent it.

steps.do: Count a milestone only when the buyer acts: books a call, starts a trial, asks for a quote, or pays. 'Sounds interesting' or a proposal you sent is not a milestone.
steps.evidence: Milestones per buyer, each with the message or record that shows the buyer's action.

steps.do: Update the buyer list with each next step, its date, and who does it. Pass each buyer to the matching step: the follow-up step, the demo step, the business case step, the pilot step, or the company purchase step.
steps.evidence: The updated list with next step, date and person for every open buyer.

blockers.do: If the product cannot do what the buyer needs, close the lead with the reason and do not push.
If there are no open buyers or recent customers, tell the owner and go back to finding partners or buyers.
If the owner has not said yes to a reply, do not send it; show them the text and wait.
If a buyer asks for a discount or terms that do not exist, pass the question to the owner and promise nothing.
If you do not know who decides, ask the buyer that one question in the next approved reply.
If a buyer has unsubscribed or said no, remove them and never contact them again.

C-PT-CLOSE.title_zh: 既有詢問、試用、喚回與公司採購接力

deliver_help.buyer_stages: How many buyers are in each stage, plus the full list with stage and last message date.
deliver_help.next_actions: For each buyer, the one next action chosen and the step it goes to.
deliver_help.replies_sent: Each reply the owner approved, with recipient, send time and who sent it, or 'none'.
deliver_help.milestones: Each confirmed buyer action with the message or record that shows it.

C-PT-NUDGE.title: Send one approved follow-up that fits the buyer's stage
C-PT-NUDGE.purpose: Send a short, useful follow-up only to buyers who may be contacted, at the right time and in the existing thread, because a timely answer to their real question is what restarts the conversation or the purchase.

steps.do: Re-read each buyer's thread. Confirm their stage and the date of the last message to them. Skip anyone who said no, unsubscribed, already bought (unless the goal is a repeat purchase), or was messaged in the last 3 business days.
steps.evidence: The buyers kept and skipped, each with the reason and last contact date.

steps.do: Confirm each remaining buyer may be contacted: they asked a question, are in a trial, are a stalled deal who wrote to the owner before, or are a customer who did not opt out. Do not message cold contacts or anyone from a bought list.
steps.evidence: The reason each buyer may be contacted.

steps.do: Write one message per buyer, under 120 words, that answers their last question or offers one helpful next step, such as a short demo or a how-to link. Use only existing offers: no new discounts, invented deadlines or promised features. Add one line saying how to stop receiving messages.
steps.evidence: The draft message for each buyer and the product facts it relies on.

steps.do: When the message links to the product, use the round's tracked link. If you test two versions, change only one thing between them and label the links ?v=A and ?v=B.
steps.evidence: The link in each message and its version label.

steps.do: Show the owner each message and its recipient word for word, and get a clear yes.
steps.evidence: The owner's approval for each message.

steps.do: Send once, as a reply in the existing thread, from the agreed account. The agent sends only if it has the tools and the owner said yes; otherwise the owner sends. If you are unsure whether it went, check the sent folder first; never resend through another channel.
steps.evidence: For each buyer, the recipient, subject line, send time, and who sent it.

steps.do: Watch for replies for 72 hours. If a buyer replies with interest or a question, pass them to the sales follow-through step. If they say no, stop and add them to the opt-out list.
steps.evidence: Each buyer's reply or silence, and where replies were passed.

steps.do: If there is still no reply after 7 days, send at most one more owner-approved follow-up, then stop. Never send more than two follow-ups to one person in a round.
steps.evidence: The final status of each buyer: replied, declined, or closed after the follow-up limit.

blockers.do: If the buyer unsubscribed or said no, do not message them and keep them on the opt-out list.
If the person never asked, never tried the product and never bought, do not message them.
If the owner has not said yes to the exact text and recipient, do not send; show them the text and wait.
If the buyer was messaged in the last 3 business days, wait until that time has passed.
If you cannot tell whether the message went, check the sent folder and the thread before any retry, and never send it twice.
If the buyer asks for a discount or terms that do not exist, pass the question to the owner and promise nothing.

C-PT-NUDGE.title_zh: 依真實買方階段送出限定跟進

deliver_help.messages_sent: Recipient, subject line, send time, version label and who sent it, for every message.
deliver_help.approved_text: The exact text of each message as the owner approved it.
deliver_help.replies: Each reply quoted with its date and the step it was passed to, or 'no reply'.
deliver_help.stopped_contacts: Everyone skipped or stopped this round, with the reason: declined, unsubscribed, bought, or follow-up limit reached.

S26.title: Show the product working on the buyer's own task
S26.purpose: Prepare and run a short demo of what the product already does, built around the one task the buyer cares about most, because seeing their own case handled is what moves a trial or a company lead to buy.

steps.do: Read the buyer's messages or call notes and pick the one task they care about most and how they will judge success. If the need is not clear, go back to the sales follow-through step to ask.
steps.evidence: The buyer's main task and how they judge success, quoted from their own words.

steps.do: List each part of that task and check that the product does it today. Mark any part it cannot do as a limit; do not promise future work.
steps.evidence: A list of task parts, each marked 'works today' or 'limit'.

steps.do: Choose the demo form: a live screen share by the owner, an existing recorded video, screenshots, or a demo account the owner already has. Open it and confirm it works. Never present mock-ups or edited images as the real product.
steps.evidence: The demo form chosen and its link or file, opened and confirmed to work.

steps.do: Prepare the sample data and the order of the demo. Use only data the buyer gave for this purpose or sample data clearly labeled as made up; never show another customer's private data, and never change the buyer's live data.
steps.evidence: The demo order in steps and the data used, with its source.

steps.do: For each part of the demo, write the one thing it proves for the buyer, plus answers to the two or three questions they are most likely to ask. Drop any claim the demo cannot show. Keep the whole demo under 15 minutes.
steps.evidence: A demo script linking each part to what it proves, plus the likely questions and answers.

steps.do: Rehearse once: open every screen, link and video in demo order. Fix or replace anything that fails.
steps.evidence: A rehearsal note listing what was checked and anything fixed.

steps.do: Write the invitation or the message with the recorded demo, using the round's tracked link if it points to the product. Show the owner the message word for word and send only after their yes; the agent sends only if it has the tools, otherwise the owner sends. Count the demo as given only if it took place or the buyer replied about it.
steps.evidence: The approved message, its send time, and whether the demo took place or the buyer replied about it.

steps.do: Record the buyer's actual reactions and questions in their own words. Silence is not agreement.
steps.evidence: The buyer's reactions and questions, quoted, with the date.

steps.do: Choose the next step from the result: a business case, a pilot, a follow-up, or closing the lead with the reason.
steps.evidence: The next step chosen and the buyer reaction it rests on.

blockers.do: If you do not know the buyer's main task, go back to the sales follow-through step and ask them before building a demo.
If the product cannot do the buyer's main task, tell the owner and mark the lead as no fit; do not promise it.
If no demo form works, ask the owner to run a live screen share; never show mock-ups as the product.
If the demo would need another customer's data or the buyer's live data, use labeled sample data instead or ask the data owner.
If the owner has not said yes to the invitation, do not send it; show them the text and wait.
If the buyer missed the demo, offer one new time in an approved message and do not mark the demo as given.

S26.title_zh: 依客戶情境示範現有產品

deliver_help.demo_link: The link or file of the demo shown or sent, and whether it took place or the buyer replied about it.
deliver_help.demo_script: The demo order, what each part proves, and the prepared answers to likely questions.
deliver_help.buyer_feedback: The buyer's reactions and questions in their own words, or 'no response yet'.
deliver_help.limits: Parts of the buyer's task the product cannot do today, stated plainly.

S27.title: Build a business case the buyer can forward
S27.purpose: Turn the buyer's own figures and the current price into a clear cost and benefit calculation and a one-page proposal, because company buyers need a reason they can show their manager and finance before they pay.

steps.do: Find out who will read the proposal and what each person must decide: the user, their manager, finance, purchasing. If the buyer's need is not clear, return to the sales follow-through step first.
steps.evidence: Each reader and the decision they make.

steps.do: Write down the plan and price that fit, as shown on the product page or in existing terms: price, currency, billing period, what is delivered, and any trial. Do not invent discounts or bundles.
steps.evidence: The plan, price and terms, with their source.

steps.do: Ask the buyer for their own starting figures: hours spent on the task, people involved, current tool costs, and their target. Mark each number as 'from buyer' or 'assumption'; leave missing numbers blank, never zero.
steps.evidence: A table of inputs, each marked 'from buyer' or 'assumption', with blanks noted.

steps.do: Set up the calculation: the same period and currency for every figure, the unit, and the comparison (today versus with the product). Time saved is not new revenue unless the buyer says how it turns into money.
steps.evidence: The formula written in plain words, so anyone can redo it.

steps.do: Work out a low case and an expected case. Keep facts and estimates apart, and describe in words anything you cannot estimate in numbers.
steps.evidence: Low and expected results, with facts and estimates labeled.

steps.do: Check that no benefit, cost or commission is counted twice and that the totals add up. Fix any mismatch before writing.
steps.evidence: A check note confirming the sums and no double counting.

steps.do: Write a one-page proposal: the buyer's problem in their words, what the product does about it, the calculation, the price, the next step (an existing trial, a pilot or an order) with what their purchasing will need, and the limits. No made-up certifications, client names or guaranteed returns.
steps.evidence: The proposal text and the source for each claim.

steps.do: Show the owner the proposal and its cover message word for word and get a yes. Send one version from the agreed account; the agent sends only if it has the tools and the owner said yes, otherwise the owner sends.
steps.evidence: The approved version, its recipient, and the send time.

steps.do: Record the buyer's reply. Answer their questions, update the calculation only with numbers the buyer confirms, and move to the pilot step or the company purchase step when they ask for it.
steps.evidence: The buyer's reply quoted, and the version number of any update.

blockers.do: If the buyer's need or decision makers are unclear, go back to the sales follow-through step before writing any figures.
If the buyer has not given their figures, ask for them; show ranges with clearly labeled assumptions and never fill gaps with zero.
If the buyer wants a price or terms that do not exist, pass the request to the owner and do not put it in the proposal.
If the totals do not match, fix the calculation before sending; never cover a gap with sales wording.
If the owner has not said yes to the exact proposal, do not send it; show them the text and wait.

S27.title_zh: 試算效益並準備購買提案

deliver_help.calculation: The formula in plain words with the low and expected results, in one currency and one period.
deliver_help.inputs_and_assumptions: Each input marked 'from buyer' or 'assumption', with missing numbers left blank.
deliver_help.proposal_text: The exact proposal and cover message as approved and sent, with the version number.
deliver_help.buyer_reply: The buyer's reply in their own words, or 'no reply yet'.

S28.title: Run a small pilot with success the buyer agreed
S28.purpose: Run a short, clearly bounded trial of the existing product against success measures the buyer agreed to, because real results on the buyer's own work are what justify a paid contract.

steps.do: Decide whether a pilot helps: it must answer one specific doubt the buyer has, and the product must already do the task. If it needs new features, do not run a pilot this round.
steps.evidence: The buyer's doubt the pilot answers, and confirmation the product does the task today.

steps.do: Write the pilot terms from existing offers only: what is included, how it is used, the price or the existing free trial it uses, its length (for example 14 days), and who delivers. Never invent free services or extra work.
steps.evidence: The pilot terms with their source.

steps.do: Agree the success measures with the buyer: one to three measures, where the data comes from, and the decision date. Until the buyer agrees in writing, the pilot has not started.
steps.evidence: The measures and the buyer's written agreement.

steps.do: List milestones: who uses the product, what result they report, and by when. Check each one can be done with the product as it is.
steps.evidence: A dated milestone list with a named person for each.

steps.do: Write the message with the pilot plan. Show the owner the message word for word and send only after their yes; the agent sends only if it has the tools, otherwise the owner sends. Confirm the start date and participants with the buyer.
steps.evidence: The approved message, its send time, and the buyer's confirmation of start date and participants.

steps.do: Track progress at each milestone from what the buyer or the delivering person reports. The buyer uses the product; the agent never uses it on the buyer's behalf to make results look better.
steps.evidence: A progress note per milestone with the source of each update.

steps.do: When something stalls, sort it as a usage, data or product problem. Fix usage and data problems with an explanation or a short demo; for a product problem, note it and stop promising that result.
steps.evidence: Each problem, its type, and what was done about it.

steps.do: At the end, mark each success measure met, not met, or unknown, with the evidence. Do not drop failed items.
steps.evidence: A results table with evidence for each measure.

steps.do: Recommend the next step from the results: the business case step or the company purchase step if the measures were met, or closing the pilot with the reason. Never call an unmet pilot a success.
steps.evidence: The recommendation and the results it rests on.

steps.do: Close the pilot: note payment received, amounts still unpaid, and delivery costs separately, and stop reminders that are no longer needed.
steps.evidence: Paid, unpaid and cost figures, and the pilot marked closed.

blockers.do: If the pilot would need features the product does not have, do not run it this round and tell the owner why.
If the buyer has not agreed the success measures in writing, keep the pilot as not started and ask them to confirm.
If the owner has not said yes to the pilot plan message, do not send it; show them the text and wait.
If the buyer has not used the product by the first milestone, send one approved check-in; if there is still no use, close the pilot as not met.
If the data for a measure cannot be obtained, agree a measurable replacement with the buyer before the end date.
If the buyer asks for free extras or new terms, pass the request to the owner and promise nothing.

S28.title_zh: 安排小規模試辦並整理結果

deliver_help.pilot_plan: The pilot terms, length, participants and dated milestones, as approved and sent.
deliver_help.success_measures: The one to three measures, their data source and decision date, and the buyer's written agreement.
deliver_help.results: Each measure marked met, not met or unknown, with its evidence.
deliver_help.recommendation: The next step chosen from the results, with paid and unpaid amounts stated separately.

S29.title: Guide a company purchase through to payment
S29.purpose: Track who must approve, which documents are needed, and what the owner must decide, all the way to money received, because a company deal only counts when it is paid.

steps.do: From the buyer's messages and the proposal, write down where the purchase stands and who still has to approve: user, manager, finance, purchasing, legal. A user liking the product is not company approval.
steps.evidence: The approval chain with each person's role and status.

steps.do: Ask the buyer for their actual process: required documents, forms, deadlines, and the order of steps. List anything not yet known as a question to ask; do not assume another company's process.
steps.evidence: The buyer's purchase steps and deadlines, with open questions listed.

steps.do: Collect real documents the owner already has, such as company details, tax forms, an invoice template, the product description, and security or privacy answers. Never create or claim a certification the owner does not hold.
steps.evidence: Each document, its source, and whether it is current.

steps.do: Sort each buyer question: answered by a document, answered by existing terms, or needing the owner's decision. Give each one a person and a next step.
steps.evidence: The question list with type, person and next step for each.

steps.do: For negotiation, lay out options only within limits the owner has given in writing, with the effect of each on price, delivery and dates. Anything outside those limits goes to the owner; never offer a discount yourself.
steps.evidence: The options, each tied to an owner-set limit, and the items waiting for the owner.

steps.do: Prepare the documents and answers for the right person at the buyer. Show the owner the message and attachments word for word and send only after their yes; the agent sends only if it has the tools, otherwise the owner sends. A draft the buyer has not accepted is still a draft.
steps.evidence: The approved message, attachments, recipient, and send time.

steps.do: Follow up on approvals at the pace the buyer set, at most once a week unless they ask for more. When the buyer delays, update the expected date; never announce the deal as closed.
steps.evidence: Each follow-up date and the buyer's latest status.

steps.do: Hand anything that signs a contract, accepts new terms, or creates a duty to pay to the owner, with the exact text to decide on. The agent never signs or accepts terms.
steps.evidence: The items sent to the owner, the exact text, and the owner's decision or 'waiting'.

steps.do: Check the order, contract, invoice and payment separately. Count the deal as paid only when the money has arrived, net of refunds.
steps.evidence: Signed, invoiced and paid status with amounts and dates.

steps.do: Close the deal record. After payment, pass the customer on for delivery and later repeat-purchase follow-up; if the buyer walks away, record why and stop following up.
steps.evidence: The closed record with the outcome and the reason.

blockers.do: If you do not know who approves the purchase, ask the buyer that one question in the next approved message.
If the buyer asks for a document or certification the owner does not have, tell the owner and the buyer plainly; never create one.
If a step signs a contract, accepts new terms or changes the price, stop and send the exact text to the owner to decide.
If the owner has not said yes to a message or attachment, do not send it; show them and wait.
If the buyer misses their own deadline, update the expected date and follow up once a week at most; do not report the deal as won.
If a signed contract is not yet paid, record it as unpaid and do not count it as a paid contract.

S29.title_zh: 推進商務協商與公司採購

deliver_help.approval_chain: Each person who must approve, their role, and their current status.
deliver_help.documents_sent: Each document and answer sent, with recipient, send time and the owner's approval.
deliver_help.owner_decisions: Each item that needs the owner (signing, new terms, discounts), the exact text, and the decision or 'waiting'.
deliver_help.paid_vs_unpaid: Signed, invoiced and paid amounts with dates, listed separately and net of refunds.

C-PR-METRICS.title: Read the goal's numbers from press, podcast and newsletter coverage
C-PR-METRICS.purpose: Record the visits, inquiries and purchases that came from coverage that is actually live, for the goal's exact components, so the round is judged on real buyers and not on how many pitches were accepted.

steps.do: Get the goal's exact metric component names from record_numbers (for example qualified_inquiries or external_purchases, and attributed_sessions). Set the date range and time zone. For the baseline, use a period of the same length just before this round; for the current reading, use the round's observation period.
steps.evidence: The component names and the date range with time zone.

steps.do: List every piece that was publicly live in the date range: for the baseline, coverage from the earlier period; for the current reading, this round's coverage. Open each URL and note the publish or air date. An accepted pitch is not live coverage. Record an outlet's audience size only if it states it publicly or told the owner; never estimate it.
steps.evidence: Each live piece with its URL, date, and stated audience if any.

steps.do: For a visits component such as attributed_sessions, check which link each live piece carries. For pieces with the tracked link, read clicks from tracking. For pieces without it, use visits referred from that outlet's site in the owner's site analytics, if the owner has them. Use one source per visit and do not add overlapping sources.
steps.evidence: Visits per piece, with the source each number came from.
