steps.do: For an inquiry component, count people who contacted the brand in the date range by email, form or message, who said they heard about it from that outlet or can be tied to the tracked link, and who state a real need the product meets. List inquiries with no known source apart and do not count them.
steps.evidence: The counted inquiries, each with its date and how its source is known, plus the unknown-source list.

steps.do: For a purchase component, check the sale counter and the payment records: count orders that are paid, in the date range, not refunded, not test mode, and not made by the owner or team, and that are tied to the tracked link or a buyer's stated source.
steps.evidence: The counted purchases with order references, and the ones left out with reasons.

steps.do: Note any money spent on this coverage, such as a sponsorship fee or production cost, and the hours the owner spent, each with its source. Unknown costs stay unknown.
steps.evidence: The cost list for the round, with sources.

steps.do: Pass each component to record_numbers under its exact name, with the source in source. If there is no history, record 0 and say so in source. Never estimate a number.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call with every component and its source.

steps.do: Write one line per outlet on what it produced, as input for the next round's choice of outlets and angles. Coverage alone does not prove sales.
steps.evidence: A short per-outlet summary of visits, inquiries and purchases.

blockers.do: If no piece is live in the date range, record the real counts, which may be 0, and say in source that no coverage was live yet.
If there is no history for these numbers, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline.
If a piece did not use the tracked link and the owner has no site analytics, say its visits are unknown; do not estimate them.
If you cannot open the site analytics or payment records, ask the owner for a screenshot or export for the date range.
If visits, inquiries or orders came from the owner, the team or tests, leave them out and say how many were removed.
If a piece went live less than 48 hours ago, report its numbers as early and read them again at the end of the observation period.

C-PR-METRICS.title_zh: 客座、Podcast與電子報曝光到買方核對

deliver_help.numbers: Each metric component under its exact name with its value, as passed to record_numbers.
deliver_help.where_read: For each number, the source it came from and the time you read it, or 'no history' or 'not available' with the reason.
deliver_help.date_range: The start and end of the period measured, with the time zone.

C-MA-ACCESS.title: Confirm the Microsoft Ads account and who makes changes
C-MA-ACCESS.purpose: Settle which Microsoft Advertising account this round uses, who signs in and edits it, and what billing and tracking it already has, so the test ads are built in the right place and their numbers can be trusted.

steps.do: Ask the owner which Microsoft Advertising account belongs to this brand: the account name, account ID or number, and customer ID. If they reach it through a manager account, write down which client account under it is this brand's. All later steps work in that one account only.
steps.evidence: The account name and ID, the customer ID, and whether it sits under a manager account.

steps.do: If the brand has no Microsoft Advertising account, create one only if the owner asks for it in this conversation. The owner enters the business details and payment method and accepts the terms. If the owner agrees to sign up with a new email address, you may get one from inbox_address and read the code with inbox_latest. Never create a second account for the same business.
steps.evidence: The new account ID and the owner's request, or a note that an account already existed.

steps.do: The owner signs in on the official Microsoft Advertising site, on their own device or in the agent's browser if they choose. Never ask for a password. Check that the signed-in user's role can create and edit campaigns; a view-only role cannot.
steps.evidence: Who signed in, on which device, and the role the account shows for that user.

steps.do: Decide who will build, switch on, and pause the ads: the agent, if its own browser or ad tool is signed in to this account and the owner says yes, or the owner, following the agent's written drafts step by step.
steps.evidence: 'agent' or 'owner', with the owner's yes if it is the agent.

steps.do: Read the account's currency and time zone and write them down. Every budget and spend figure in later steps uses this currency, and spend is reported in its smallest unit (USD 12.34 is 1234).
steps.evidence: The currency code and the time zone, as the account shows them.

steps.do: Read billing: whether an active payment method is on file and whether the account shows any hold or unpaid balance. Do not enter or change payment details; if billing is missing, the owner adds it.
steps.evidence: Billing status in one line, and what the owner must fix, if anything.

steps.do: Read the existing conversion tracking: whether a UET tag exists, which conversion goals are set up, and whether any of them recorded a conversion in the last 30 days. Do not install a new tag or change goals in this round; the round's tracked link and sale counter will count clicks and sales.
steps.evidence: The tag and goal names with their last-30-day conversion counts, or a note that there are none.

steps.do: List the account's existing campaigns with their status, IDs and the networks each runs on (search only, or search plus audience ads). Mark every active one so later steps never touch it, and mark any campaign imported from Google Ads, since imports can arrive switched on. Agree a name prefix for this round's objects with the owner, for example 'NE-G093-R1'.
steps.evidence: A list of existing campaigns with IDs, status and networks, the imported ones marked, and the agreed name prefix.

blockers.do: If the signed-in account or client account is not this brand's, stop and ask the owner to switch to the right one; never change anything across a whole manager account.
If the user's role cannot create or edit campaigns, ask the owner to give that user an editing role or to make the changes themselves.
If there is no active payment method or the account is on hold, tell the owner to fix it in the account's billing settings and wait; never enter card or bank details.
If a verification code, terms screen, or identity check appears that needs the owner, stop and tell them which screen and which button; never accept terms for them.
If a campaign imported from Google Ads is active and the owner did not mean it to run, tell the owner at once and pause it only if they say yes.
If the agent's browser or tool cannot open the account, set who_makes_changes to 'owner' and plan to hand them exact drafts and settings.

C-MA-ACCESS.title_zh: Microsoft Ads身分、資格與可用工具核對

deliver_help.account_id: The account name, account ID and customer ID, plus the manager account name if there is one.
deliver_help.who_makes_changes: 'agent' or 'owner', and one line on why.
deliver_help.currency_and_time_zone: The account currency code and time zone. Example: 'USD, (GMT+08:00) Taipei'.
deliver_help.billing_and_tracking: Whether billing is active, and which conversion tag and goals exist with their last-30-day counts.
deliver_help.campaigns_not_to_touch: IDs and names of the existing campaigns this round must leave alone, active ones first.

C-MA-METRICS.title: Read this goal's numbers for Microsoft Ads
C-MA-METRICS.purpose: Record the goal's numbers for one fixed date range, from the ad account's reporting and the round's own click and sale counters, so the baseline and the test round are compared on the same real numbers.

steps.do: Confirm whether this is the baseline or the current reading. Baseline: a period of the same length just before the round, for this product's existing Microsoft Ads campaigns. Current: only this round's campaign, ad group and ads, found by their IDs and name prefix. Write the date range in the account's time zone.
steps.evidence: Baseline or current, the campaign IDs measured, and the date range with time zone.

steps.do: Open the ad account's reporting for exactly those campaigns and that date range, and read impressions, clicks and spend as shown. If the agent cannot open it, ask the owner for a report export or screenshot that shows the account name, the date range and the campaign names.
steps.evidence: Impressions, clicks and spend exactly as displayed, with where they were read and when.

steps.do: If the goal counts qualified clicks, take the round's tracked link click count from tracking for the same range, split by ?v=A and ?v=B. These are people who actually reached the product page. If the ads did not use the tracked link, use the platform's clicks and say so in source.
steps.evidence: The tracked click count per version, or the platform click count with a note on why.

steps.do: If the goal counts purchases, take sales from the round's sale counter and check each one against the owner's payment records, and, if the owner already uses a CRM, against that CRM's records too. Remove refunds, test payments, the owner's own purchases and duplicates. Conversions the ad platform reports are a cross-check only.
steps.evidence: The purchase count, with each sale's date and amount and every removed sale named with the reason.

steps.do: Convert spend to the currency's smallest unit. List any other cost of the round, such as tools or fees, separately in source with its amount; write 'unknown' for a cost you cannot find and never guess it.
steps.evidence: Spend in the smallest unit, and a list of other costs with amounts or 'unknown'.

steps.do: Clicks and conversions can arrive late. For the current reading, read the final numbers at least 48 hours after the date range ends; if you must report sooner, mark the numbers as early in source.
steps.evidence: The time the numbers were read, and whether they are final or early.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with the goal's exact metric component names as listed for this goal, for example spend_minor and external_purchases for a cost per purchase goal, or qualified_clicks and impressions for a click rate goal. In source, name each screen or file and the date range. If there is no history, record 0 for each component and say 'no history' in source. Never estimate a missing number.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call with every component name, value and source.

steps.do: Note anything that makes this reading not comparable with the last one: a different range length, a changed attribution setting, ads paused part way, or a report still processing. The next round changes only one thing: audience, keywords, or ad text.
steps.evidence: A short list of comparability notes, or 'none', and the one thing the next round could change.

blockers.do: If you cannot open the ad account's reporting, ask the owner for an export or screenshot showing the account name, date range and campaign names.
If the report shows a different account or other campaigns mixed in, do not use it and ask again for this round's campaigns only.
If the report is still processing or the range ended less than 48 hours ago, record the numbers as early and read them again later; never fill purchases in from clicks.
If a sale cannot be tied to this round's tracked link or sale counter, leave it out of the count and list it in source as unattributed.
If there is no history for these numbers, record 0 for each component and say in source that there is no history; this round then sets the baseline.

C-MA-METRICS.title_zh: Microsoft Ads同窗轉換與全成本核對

deliver_help.numbers: Each metric component by its exact name with its value, for example spend_minor 4250 and external_purchases 3.
deliver_help.where_read: The screen, report file, tracked link or payment record each number came from, and the time it was read.
deliver_help.date_range: The start and end date with the account's time zone, and whether this is the baseline or the current reading.

C-MA-DRAFT.title: Build the Microsoft Ads test as paused drafts
C-MA-DRAFT.purpose: Turn the chosen angle into one paused search campaign with keywords and ads the owner approved word for word, so nothing runs or spends until the owner switches it on.

steps.do: If the account has past search ads for this product, open the search terms report for the last 30 to 90 days and sort the terms into three groups: buying intent, research only, and irrelevant. If there is no history, build the keyword list from the buyer quotes and the chosen angle.
steps.evidence: The three lists with each term's clicks and cost, or a note that there is no history and where the keywords came from.

steps.do: Pick 5 to 20 keywords for one ad group that match the chosen buyer situation, and a negative keyword list from the irrelevant terms. Keep the match types the account already uses for proven keywords; for new keywords use phrase match unless the owner prefers another.
steps.evidence: The keyword list with match types, and the negative keyword list.

steps.do: Write one responsive search ad from the approved copy and the product facts: at least 5 headlines of up to 30 characters and at least 2 descriptions of up to 90 characters. Make only claims the facts support; no invented numbers, discounts, scarcity or guarantees. For two versions, change one thing only and label them A and B.
steps.evidence: Every headline and description with its character count, labeled by version, and the fact behind each claim.

steps.do: Set each version's final URL to the round's tracked link from tracking, with ?v=A or ?v=B added. Open each link and check it lands on the product page.
steps.evidence: The final URL per version, each opened and seen to load the product page.

steps.do: Write the settings: campaign name with the agreed prefix, one ad group, location, language, the search network setting, and a daily budget no higher than the amount the owner approved in writing. Show the owner the full draft word for word, including keywords, negatives, headlines, descriptions, URLs and budget, and get a clear yes.
steps.evidence: The full draft as shown to the owner, and the owner's approval message.

steps.do: Create the campaign, ad group, keywords and ad with status Paused, using the agent's tool if it has one and the owner said yes, or have the owner build it from the draft. Build new objects; do not copy or import an active campaign. Check spend still reads 0 after saving.
steps.evidence: Who created the objects, when, and the spend shown after saving.

steps.do: Read back what now exists: the ID of each object, status Paused at campaign, ad group and ad level, the budget, the final URLs and the ad's review status. Fix any difference from the approved draft before moving on.
steps.evidence: Each object's ID, status, budget and review status, matching the approved draft.

blockers.do: If the owner has not said yes to this exact draft, do not create anything; show them the draft and wait.
If the owner has not written down a daily budget and a total for the round, ask for both before building the campaign.
If any campaign, ad group or ad shows as active after creation, set it to Paused at once and tell the owner.

deliver_help.usable_pins: The Pins or images the brand owns or may use in ads, with URLs or file names, and any excluded ones with the reason.
deliver_help.tracking_status: Whether a Pinterest tag or other conversion source already reports purchases, the attribution windows shown, and whether a catalog exists.

C-PA-METRICS.title: Read this goal's numbers for the Pinterest ads
C-PA-METRICS.purpose: Record the numbers this goal is judged on, for this round's Pinterest ads in a fixed date range, so the baseline and the new round are compared on the same real numbers. record_numbers lists exactly which numbers it needs.

steps.do: Confirm the ad account, the date range, the time zone, and the account currency. For a baseline, use the brand's earlier Pinterest ads over a range of the same length as this round; for current, use only this round's campaign, ad group, and ad IDs over this round's range.
steps.evidence: The ad account ID, the ad IDs measured, and the date range with time zone and currency.

steps.do: Pass only this goal's metric components, by these exact names: spend_minor and external_purchases for cost per purchase; qualified_clicks and impressions for qualified click rate. Decide where each is read before reading anything: spend and impressions from the ad account's reporting, qualified_clicks from the round's tracked link, external_purchases from the sale counter or the owner's payment records. Never borrow a number from another goal.
steps.evidence: A list of each component name and the source it will be read from.

steps.do: Read the numbers in the ad account's reporting, filtered to the ads above, exactly as displayed. Keep the same attribution windows for baseline and current, and if the windows differ, say so. If the agent cannot open reporting, ask the owner for a screenshot or export.
steps.evidence: The raw numbers as displayed, the attribution windows, the screen or file they came from, and the time they were read.

steps.do: Write spend in the account currency's smallest unit, without converting to another currency. For USD that is cents: 12.34 USD is 1234. Note separately any other cost the owner paid for this round, such as design help or tools, without adding it to spend_minor.
steps.evidence: Spend in the smallest unit with the currency named, and a list of any other costs for the round.

steps.do: Count qualified_clicks as clicks on the round's tracked link, split by ?v=A and ?v=B if there are versions, and make sure that link was used only in this round's ads. Do not count saves, closeups, or Pin opens. Use the same source for baseline and current: if the earlier ads had no tracked link, read outbound clicks from the ad account's reporting for both and give the tracked-link count in source as a cross-check.
steps.evidence: Click counts per version with the source named, the same for baseline and current.

steps.do: Count external_purchases from the sale counter or the owner's payment records, once per order. Leave out refunded orders, the owner's own test payments, and duplicates. Use purchases reported by Pinterest only as a cross-check; if they are the only source, record them and say plainly in source that they are Pinterest-reported and not matched to payments.
steps.evidence: The purchase count with its source, and a list of any orders excluded and why.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with each component by its exact name and a source naming the screen, export, or record and the time read. If the account has no earlier ads, record 0 and say in source that there is no history. If a number is not shown anywhere, say so and never estimate it. If impressions or purchases are 0, still record both numbers and claim no improvement. Read current numbers only after the round has run its full 7 days; anything read sooner is labeled early.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call with every component, its value, and its source.

steps.do: For a current reading, name the one thing the next round should change, such as the audience, the image, or the search topic, and keep everything else the same.
steps.evidence: One sentence naming the single change suggested for the next round, or a note that this was a baseline reading.

blockers.do: If you cannot open the ad account's reporting, ask the owner for a screenshot or export covering the exact ads and date range.
If the report is still being prepared or the data is less than 24 hours old, wait and read the same report again later; do not request many new reports.
If the brand has no earlier Pinterest ads, record 0 and say in source that there is no history; the first round then sets the baseline.
If a screenshot or export shows a different ad account or other ads, do not use it and ask again for the agreed ad account and ad IDs.
If baseline and current were read with different attribution windows, read them again with the same windows before recording.
If there is no sale counter and no payment record, say so in source, use only Pinterest-reported purchases labeled as unconfirmed, and use that same source for baseline and current.

C-PA-METRICS.title_zh: Pinterest Ads同窗轉換與全成本核對

deliver_help.numbers: Each goal component by its exact name with its value, with spend in the currency's smallest unit, and 0 marked as 'no history' where that applies.
deliver_help.where_read: For each number, the screen, export, tracked link, or payment record it came from, the attribution windows, and the time it was read.
deliver_help.date_range: The start and end of the range measured, with the time zone. Example: '2026-11-01 00:00 to 2026-11-07 23:59, America/Los_Angeles'.

C-PA-DRAFT.title: Build the Pinterest ad test as paused drafts
C-PA-DRAFT.purpose: Build this round's Pinterest campaign, ad group, and ads in the owner's ad account, switched off and matching an approved plan, so the test can start the moment the owner approves the budget.

steps.do: Read the chosen angle, the approved ad text, and the images made for this round. Pick one thing to test, either the audience or the opening hook, based on what buyers actually search on Pinterest, and keep everything else the same between versions.
steps.evidence: The single thing being tested, the versions labeled A and B, and the search phrases or buyer quotes it is based on.

steps.do: For each ad, prepare the Pin image, a title, a description, and the destination URL, kept within the length limits the ad screen shows. The destination is the round's tracked link with ?v=A or ?v=B for each version. Open each link and check it lands on the product page. Use only the brand's own or licensed images, and keep these paid Pins apart from the brand's ordinary Pins.
steps.evidence: A list of ads with image, title, description, and tracked link, each link opened and confirmed to load.

steps.do: Check every claim in the titles and descriptions against the product facts. Remove any number, testimonial, scarcity, or guarantee the facts do not support.
steps.evidence: The final ad text with each claim checked, and a list of anything removed.

steps.do: Write the campaign plan: the objective that fits the goal's main number, the audience, the daily budget, the total budget for the round, the start and end dates of at least 7 days, and the account currency. Pick a conversion objective only if a conversion source already reports purchases; otherwise pick the objective that drives clicks to the site. Show the owner the plan and every ad word for word, and get their written approval of the daily budget and the total.
steps.evidence: The full plan, the ad text, and the owner's written approval with the daily and total amounts.

steps.do: Build the campaign, ad group, and ads in the agreed ad account with every item paused. The agent builds them only if its own browser is signed in and the owner said yes; otherwise hand the owner the plan to build themselves. Do not switch anything on in this step.
steps.evidence: Who built the ads, and a statement that every item was saved as paused.

steps.do: Open the campaign in the ad account and read back each item's name, ID, status, budget, dates, and destination URL. Compare them with the approved plan and fix any difference before moving on.
steps.evidence: The campaign, ad group, and ad IDs, each shown as paused, with budgets and links matching the plan.

steps.do: Write down that only these IDs belong to this round, and keep the brand's ordinary unpaid Pins out of this round's numbers.
steps.evidence: A list of this round's ad IDs labeled as the only ads in this test.

blockers.do: If the owner has not approved the daily and total budget in writing, do not build anything; show them the plan and wait for their answer.
If an image or Pin belongs to another creator, replace it with one the brand owns or has rights to use.
If the plan needs a product catalog that does not exist, switch to standard image ads and do not call the test a shopping ad.
If a destination link does not open the product page, stop and fix the link before building the ad.
If the agent's browser is not signed in to the ad account, give the owner the full plan and ad text to build as paused, and ask them to send back the IDs.
If any item shows as active after saving, ask the owner to pause it right away and report any spend it made.

C-PA-DRAFT.title_zh: Pinterest Ads限定物件PAUSED測試建立

deliver_help.ad_ids: The campaign, ad group, and ad IDs created for this round, each with its version label.
deliver_help.status_shown: The status each item shows in the ad account after saving. It should read paused.
deliver_help.approved_plan: The objective, audience, daily budget, total budget, dates, and currency, plus the owner's approval message quoted word for word.
deliver_help.tracked_links: The destination URL used in each ad, with its ?v= label. Example: 'https://.../r/abc?v=A'.

C-PA-ACTIVATE.title: Switch on only this round's Pinterest ads
C-PA-ACTIVATE.purpose: Switch on this round's paused Pinterest ads within the budget the owner approved in writing and confirm they actually start delivering, because the goal's number cannot move until the approved ads run.

steps.do: List this round's campaign, ad group, and ad IDs from the draft step. Open them in the ad account and confirm each is still paused and still matches the approved plan. Leave every other campaign in the account untouched.
steps.evidence: This round's IDs, each shown as paused and matching the plan.

steps.do: Compare the daily and total budget set in the ad account with the amounts the owner approved in writing, in the account currency. If the set amount is higher, lower it to the approved amount first. Confirm billing is ready; the owner handles any payment details.
steps.evidence: The set daily and total budget next to the approved amounts, and a note that billing is ready.

steps.do: Show the owner the exact list of ads to switch on, the daily budget, the total budget, and the end date, and ask for a final yes. Do not switch anything on without that yes in this conversation.
steps.evidence: The list shown to the owner and their yes quoted word for word.

steps.do: Switch on only the listed items, the agent with its own browser if the owner agreed, otherwise the owner. Note the time they were switched on.
steps.evidence: Who switched them on and the date and time.

steps.do: Within 24 hours, check each ad's review status and whether it has started to show. Active does not mean money has been spent or a sale has happened. If an ad is rejected, tell the owner the reason shown and fix only that ad.
steps.evidence: Each ad's review status, impressions so far, and any rejection reason.

steps.do: Agree the stop rule with the owner: pause this round's ads when spend reaches the approved total, when the end date arrives, when an ad is rejected, or when spend reaches half the approved total with no clicks on the tracked link. Check spend against the approved total at least once a day until then.
steps.evidence: The stop rule in one sentence and the date of the first spend check.

blockers.do: If the owner has not given a final yes to switch on these exact ads and budgets, do not switch anything on; show them the list and wait.
If the budget set in the account is higher than the approved amount, lower it to the approved amount before switching on, or ask the owner to.
If billing is not set up or a payment failed, ask the owner to fix it in the ad account's billing settings; never enter payment details.
If an ad is rejected, show the owner the reason Pinterest gives and fix only that ad within the product facts; do not resubmit it unchanged.
If the ads are approved but show no impressions after 24 hours, check the dates, budget, and audience against the plan and tell the owner; do not raise the budget.

C-PA-ACTIVATE.title_zh: Pinterest Ads已授權單組啟用與有效狀態核對

deliver_help.ad_ids: The campaign, ad group, and ad IDs that were switched on, and nothing else.
deliver_help.switched_on_at: The date, time, and time zone the ads were switched on, and who did it.
deliver_help.review_status: Each ad's review status and whether it has started showing. Example: 'Ad A approved, 1,240 impressions; Ad B in review'.
deliver_help.approved_caps: The daily and total budget the owner approved, in the account currency, with the owner's approval quoted.

C-PA-STOP.title: Pause this round's Pinterest ads when the test ends
C-PA-STOP.purpose: Pause only this round's Pinterest ads once the test window ends or a stop rule is hit, and confirm spend has stopped, so the round's cost is final and the next round starts from a clean, honest number.

steps.do: Take this round's campaign, ad group, and ad IDs from the switch-on step. Do not use the full list of ads in the account.
steps.evidence: This round's IDs, copied from the switch-on step.

steps.do: Confirm the reason to stop: the round's end date has passed, spend has reached the approved total, an ad was rejected, or another part of the stop rule agreed at switch-on was hit. Confirm this round's current numbers have already been recorded, unless spend has reached the approved total, in which case pause first.
steps.evidence: The stop reason, the date, and whether the current numbers were recorded.

steps.do: Show the owner the exact list of items to pause. If the stop rule agreed at switch-on was hit, pause right away and tell the owner; otherwise wait for their yes. Pause only those items, the agent with its own browser if the owner agreed, otherwise the owner. Do not delete campaigns, change budgets, edit ads, or touch any other ads or brands.
steps.evidence: The list shown, the stop rule or the owner's yes that allowed the pause, who paused the ads, and when.

steps.do: Open each item and confirm it now shows as paused. If pausing seemed to fail, check the status again before trying a second time.
steps.evidence: Each ID with the status shown after pausing.

steps.do: Check spend again 24 hours later to confirm no new spend appeared after the pause. Write the round's final spend in the currency's smallest unit. If it differs from the spend recorded as current, tell the owner both numbers.
steps.evidence: The final spend in the smallest unit, read at least 24 hours after the pause, with the currency named.

steps.do: Keep the ads, images, and settings as they are so the next round can reuse them. Note the one change the next round will test, and do not raise the budget without a new written approval from the owner.
steps.evidence: A note of what was kept and the single change proposed for the next round.

blockers.do: If no agreed stop rule was hit and the owner has not said yes to pausing these exact items, show them the list and wait before pausing.
If you cannot find this round's IDs from the switch-on step, ask the owner to confirm them; never pause ads you cannot tie to this round.
If an item still shows as active or spend keeps growing after the pause, tell the owner right away and ask them to pause it in the ad account.
If the final spend is not yet shown, wait and read the same report again later before writing the final number.
If this round's current numbers have not been recorded, record them first unless spend has hit the approved total, in which case pause first.

C-PA-STOP.title_zh: Pinterest Ads觀察後只暫停本輪測試物件

deliver_help.paused_ad_ids: The campaign, ad group, and ad IDs from this round that were paused, and nothing else.
deliver_help.status_after: The status each item shows after pausing, and the time it was checked.
deliver_help.final_spend_minor: The round's total spend in the currency's smallest unit with the currency named. Example: '18450 USD cents'.
deliver_help.next_change: The single change the next round should test, such as a new image or a different audience.

C-DC-PROGRAM.title: Run one opt-in product task in a Discord channel
C-DC-PROGRAM.purpose: Invite members of an approved channel to try the product in one short, clearly defined task, and record who joins and who finishes, because members who complete a real task are the ones most likely to buy.

steps.do: Through the owner, ask the server's admins whether a product task may be run, in which channel, and under which rules, such as stating the relationship or offering a reward. Keep their written okay.
steps.evidence: The admin's okay, quoted, with the channel named.

steps.do: Design one task a member can finish in one sitting, about 15 to 30 minutes, with the product as it is today. Write what to do, what to post as proof (a screenshot, a result, or a link), how to join (for example, reply 'in' in the thread), how to leave, and a deadline within 7 days. Offer a reward only if the owner really gives one, and state it plainly.
steps.evidence: The task with its join, proof, leave, and deadline rules.

steps.do: Write the task post: short, with the relationship to the product stated and the round's tracked link, with ?v=A or ?v=B when there are several versions. Use only claims the product facts support. Show the owner the exact text, word for word, and get a clear yes.
steps.evidence: The final post text and the owner's approval message.

steps.do: Post it once in the approved channel, by the owner by hand or by the admin-approved bot. Do not send direct messages to members, and do not mention everyone in the server unless the admins approved it. Copy the message link of the live post.
steps.evidence: The public message link of the task post.

steps.do: Record each member who joins in the way the post set out, once per person, with the message link. These are the eligible members.
steps.evidence: The list of members who joined, with links.

steps.do: Record a completion only when a member posts the finished work as the task defined. A reaction or 'will do' is an interaction, not a completion.
steps.evidence: The list of members who completed, each with the link to their proof.

steps.do: Answer questions in the thread with owner-approved text, and offer a product demo only when a member asks. If a member says they want out or asks to stop, stop contacting them and mark them as left.
steps.evidence: Questions answered with links, demos given on request, and members who left.

blockers.do: If the admins have not approved the task, do not post it; run it only in a server or channel the owner runs or where admins agreed.
If the account cannot post in the channel, stop and ask the admins through the owner; do not post it elsewhere.
If the owner has not said yes to the exact task post, do not post; show it and wait.
If nobody joins within 48 hours, make the task shorter or clearer as one change for the next round; never message members one by one.
If slowmode blocks replies, answer in one combined message after the wait; never switch accounts.
If the task thread is closed before the deadline, ask the owner or admins to reopen it; do not start a duplicate thread.

C-DC-PROGRAM.title_zh: Discord已同意成員體驗與作品任務

deliver_help.task_post_url: The message link of the live task post.
deliver_help.joined_members: Each member who joined, once, with the link to their join message.
deliver_help.completed_members: Each member who posted the finished work, with the link to their proof.
deliver_help.left_members: Members who asked to leave or stop, or 'none'.

C-CR-ACCESS.title: Settle the creator offer, the contact account and how sales are counted
C-CR-ACCESS.purpose: Agree with the owner, before any creator is contacted, what creators are offered, which account contacts them, how many may be contacted a day and how each creator's sales are counted, so every message promises only what the owner approved and every sale can be credited.

steps.do: Ask the owner which account contacts creators: the brand's business email, or the brand's own social account for creators who publish only a message route. Have the owner sign in, or confirm the agent's browser already is; never ask for a password. Check that the name and address shown match the brand.
steps.evidence: The contact account, who signed in, and the name shown on it.

steps.do: Write down what can be offered, from terms the owner already has or decides now: free access (which plan, for how long), an affiliate or referral share (percentage, how long a referral counts, when it is paid, minimum payout), a discount code for the creator's audience if one exists, and a paid sponsorship only if the owner sets a budget. If there are no terms, show the owner two or three options with what each costs and wait for a decision. Never promise money yourself.
steps.evidence: The offer the owner approved, quoted from their message, or the options shown and 'waiting for the owner'.

steps.do: Decide how each creator's sales are counted: the affiliate program the owner already runs (its link format), or, if there is none, call tracking for this round's tracked link and plan one label per creator (?v=creator-name). Confirm with the owner that the sale counter from tracking is on the page shown after payment, so purchases are counted by the engine.
steps.evidence: The link format with one example label, and whether the sale counter is in place.

steps.do: Agree the limits: how many creators may be contacted a day (start at 10 or fewer), at most one follow-up per creator after 5 business days, and who presses send. Platform rules come first: no bulk messages, and no contact through a route the creator did not publish.
steps.evidence: The daily cap, the follow-up rule and who sends, approved by the owner.

steps.do: Write the disclosure line creators will be given: they label the content as sponsored or affiliate as their platform and local law require (for example YouTube's paid promotion setting, or #ad), and the brand never asks them to hide it.
steps.evidence: The disclosure line.

steps.do: Ask the owner how free access is handed out (accounts or codes, how many, which plan, how they are activated) so creators can really try the product. If none can be issued, the offer is affiliate only and says so.
steps.evidence: How free access is given and how many are available, or 'affiliate only'.

steps.do: Put it in five lines (offer, contact account, link format, daily cap, disclosure) and get the owner's yes.
steps.evidence: The five-line summary and the owner's approval message.

blockers.do: If the owner has not decided what creators get, contact nobody; show the options and wait for the answer.
If the signed-in account is personal or belongs to another brand, stop and ask the owner to switch or to send the messages themselves.
If the sale counter is not on the after-payment page, ask the owner to add it, or name the payment report that will be used instead.
If the owner cannot give creators free access, make the offer affiliate only and say so in every message.
If a verification screen, terms screen or identity check appears, stop and tell the owner which screen and which button; never accept terms for them.

C-CR-ACCESS.title_zh: 確認創作者合作方案、聯絡帳號與成交計算方式

deliver_help.offer_terms: What creators get, quoted from the owner's approval, for example 'free Pro for 3 months plus 30% of each sale for 12 months'.
deliver_help.contact_account: The account that contacts creators, who signed in, and who presses send.
deliver_help.creator_tracking: The link format per creator and whether the sale counter is in place. Example: 'https://.../r/abc?v=anna-piano'.
deliver_help.limits: The daily contact cap, the follow-up rule and the disclosure line.
deliver_help.owner_approval: The owner's message approving the five-line summary, with its date.

C-CR-FIND.title: Find creators whose audience already wants the product
C-CR-FIND.purpose: Build a checked shortlist of creators whose recent content draws exactly the buyers this product serves (for example piano cover channels for a sheet-music tool), each with a business contact they published, because fit with the audience sells far more than follower count.

steps.do: From the buyer group and motive chosen earlier, write who the creator's viewers must be and what they watch or read, for example 'people learning songs on piano watch tutorial and cover videos'. List 3 to 5 content types and the platforms where they live (YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, blogs, newsletters, podcasts).
steps.evidence: The audience description, the content types and the platforms.

steps.do: Search each platform and the web for those content types, for example 'piano tutorial {song}', '{niche} review' or '{niche} newsletter', with the brackets replaced. Collect at least 30 candidates with about 1,000 to 200,000 followers or subscribers; smaller creators answer more often and their audiences trust them. Skip direct competitors and accounts that only repost.
steps.evidence: The searches used, the date, and at least 30 candidates with profile URLs and follower counts as shown.

steps.do: For each candidate, use read_page on at least three posts or videos from the last 90 days. Note the views on recent posts (not only followers), what viewers ask in the comments, and whether those questions are what the product answers.
steps.evidence: For each candidate, the URLs read, typical recent views, and one line on audience fit with one comment quoted.

steps.do: Find each candidate's published business contact: the email on their channel's About page, their website's contact page, a 'work with me' or sponsorship page, or a creator marketplace profile. Use only contacts they published for business; never guess an address or use a personal one found elsewhere. Drop candidates with no published route.
steps.evidence: The contact route and the page it is published on, for each remaining candidate, and the list of dropped ones.

steps.do: Check what each candidate promoted before and how they disclosed it, and whether they work with a competitor now. Note any rate card or sponsorship terms they publish; if none are published, write 'unknown'.
steps.evidence: Past sponsors or 'none seen', how they disclose, any conflict, and published terms or 'unknown'.

steps.do: Rank by audience fit first, then recent views, then how clearly they invite business contact. Keep the top 10 to 20 for this round, each with one line on why their audience would buy.
steps.evidence: The ranked shortlist with the reason for each rank.

steps.do: Show the owner the shortlist and ask them to strike anyone they do not want linked to the brand. Contact nobody in this step.
steps.evidence: The owner's reply and the final list.

blockers.do: If fewer than 10 creators fit, widen to nearby content types or platforms and tell the owner the list is thin.
If a strong candidate publishes no business contact, leave them off; never guess an email or message someone whose profile says no business requests.
If a creator promotes a direct competitor now, mark the conflict and leave the choice to the owner.
If read_page cannot open a profile, use the platform's public web page or skip the candidate; never log in to collect pages.
If the owner has not reviewed the shortlist, submit the step as blocked and say what they need to check.

C-CR-FIND.title_zh: 找出受眾正需要這個產品的創作者

deliver_help.shortlist: The 10 to 20 ranked creators with name, profile URL, platform, typical recent views and the owner's yes or no.
deliver_help.fit_evidence: For each creator, the posts read and one line on why their audience matches the buyer, with a comment quoted.
deliver_help.contact_routes: For each creator, the published business contact and the page it appears on.
deliver_help.excluded: Candidates dropped and why: no published contact, competitor conflict, poor fit, or struck by the owner.

C-CR-METRICS.title: Read paid customers from creator links
C-CR-METRICS.purpose: Record how many real outside customers paid through creators in a fixed window, credited to a creator only where a link, label or code shows it, so the next round keeps the creators who sell and drops the ones who do not.

steps.do: Call where_are_we (with lane in a month target) and copy this goal's component name (external_purchases) and observation window. For the baseline use the same length of time just before this round's first invitation; for the current reading use the window since creators started publishing.
steps.evidence: The component name, the window with start, end and time zone, and whether this is the baseline or the current reading.

steps.do: Read the engine's own counts first: tracking shows clicks per creator label and the sale counter's purchases in the window. If the step says the engine already counted external_purchases, leave it out of record_numbers; the engine's count is the one used.
steps.evidence: Clicks per label and the engine's purchase count, with the time read.

steps.do: Read the payment records for the same window (the payment tool's report or the owner's export) and the affiliate program's report if there is one. Match each purchase to a creator by label, code or the buyer's own words; anything else is 'source unknown'.
steps.evidence: Each purchase with its creator or 'source unknown', and the report it came from.

steps.do: Remove the owner's, team's and test payments, refunds inside the window, duplicates, and the free accounts given to creators; a creator's own free access is never a sale.
steps.evidence: What was removed and why, with counts before and after.

steps.do: Write one line per creator: post URL, public views, clicks, purchases, and whether a commission is now owed.
steps.evidence: One line per creator with these numbers and their sources.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with external_purchases (unless the engine counted it) and a source naming each report and when it was read. If there is no history, record 0 and say 'no history'. In a month target lane also pass paid_customers (paying customers since the month started, from the payment records), and visits and signups if you have them; they update the month progress and are not judged here. Never estimate.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call as accepted.

blockers.do: If you cannot open the payment report, ask the owner for an export of the exact window; never estimate sales.
If there is no earlier window to compare, record 0 and say 'no history'; the first round then sets the baseline.
If a sale cannot be tied to a creator, count its source as unknown and credit no one.
If the window has not ended, report the reading as early and read again when it ends.
If the owner's, team's or test purchases cannot be separated, ask the owner to mark them before recording.

C-CR-METRICS.title_zh: 核對創作者連結帶來的付費客戶

deliver_help.numbers: external_purchases with its value, for example 'external_purchases: 7', plus any number you could not get, marked missing.
deliver_help.where_read: Each source and when it was read, what was removed and why, and purchases whose source is unknown.
deliver_help.date_range: Start and end of the window with time zone, and whether it is the baseline or the current reading.
deliver_help.per_creator: One line per creator: post URL, views, clicks, purchases and commission owed.

C-CR-OUTREACH.title: Send the approved creator invitation within the daily cap
C-CR-OUTREACH.purpose: Invite each shortlisted creator once, through the contact they published, with a short personal message built from one owner-approved template, so the owner approves the wording and the daily volume once and every creator still gets a message about their own work.

steps.do: Write one invitation template under 120 words with placeholders in curly brackets, for example {first_name}, {their_video} (a recent piece of theirs) and {why_their_audience} (one line on why their viewers fit). Say plainly who you write for, the offer exactly as approved, what you ask (try it free and post only if they like it), and how to say no. Everything outside the brackets stays word for word the same in every message. Each placeholder value is one line of at most 80 characters (40 for a name); where one needs more, write its limit, for example {why_their_audience:120} (200 at most). Values carry no links; a link goes in the fixed text or a {link} placeholder.
steps.evidence: The template text and the list of its placeholders.

steps.do: Write the audience rule in one sentence, for example 'creators on this round's approved shortlist, through their published business contact', and the daily cap agreed in the offer step.
steps.evidence: The audience rule and the daily cap.

steps.do: Get the template approved. In a month target, send it with submit_batch as one item of kind 'template' with text, audience_rule and daily_cap, and tell the owner to approve it on their owner page or with the approve command. Outside a month target, show the owner the template, the audience rule and the cap, and get a clear yes. Never approve it yourself.
steps.evidence: The template's id and the owner's approval, or the owner's yes message.

steps.do: Fill the placeholders for each creator from what you read on their own pages; each value is true and one line, at most 80 characters (40 for a name) unless the template sets its own limit such as {their_video:120}, with no link except in a {link} placeholder. If a value does not fit naturally, leave that creator out of this round rather than changing the fixed text.
steps.evidence: Each filled message with its recipient.

steps.do: Send at most the daily cap per day, one message per creator, from the approved account; the owner sends if the agent has no tool for it. Never put several creators in one email, never switch to another channel, and if you are unsure whether a message went, check Sent before trying again. When today's messages are out, submit this step with approved_item set to the template's id (in a month target) and the sent texts in output; the engine checks each one against the approved template and the day's cap. Fill each placeholder with a true value: one line, at most 80 characters (40 for a name) unless the template sets its own limit, with no link except in a {link} placeholder.
steps.evidence: For each message, the recipient, the send time and who sent it.

steps.do: After 5 business days with no answer, send at most one short follow-up that is part of the approved templates, then stop. A no or a request to stop ends contact for good and goes on the do-not-contact list.
steps.evidence: Follow-ups sent, replies received, and the do-not-contact list.

steps.do: Record each reply in one list: yes, maybe (with their questions), no, or no answer. Pass each yes to the next step with what they asked for.
steps.evidence: The reply list with each creator's status.

blockers.do: If the owner has not approved the template, send nothing; show them the template, rule and cap and wait.
If the shortlist is larger than the daily cap, send the rest on the following days; never go over the cap.
If you cannot fill a placeholder with something true from their own pages, leave that creator out of this round.
If an address bounces, remove it; never retry with a guessed spelling or another route.
If the platform limits or flags the messages, stop for the day and tell the owner.

C-CR-OUTREACH.title_zh: 在每日上限內寄出已核准的創作者邀請

deliver_help.template: The approved template word for word, with its placeholders.
deliver_help.owner_approval: The template's id and the owner's approval with its date, or the owner's yes message.
deliver_help.sent_messages: For every message and follow-up: recipient, send time, who sent it, and the filled text.
deliver_help.replies: Each creator with yes, maybe, no or no answer, and any question they asked.
deliver_help.do_not_contact: Creators who said no or asked to stop, or 'none'.

C-CR-ENABLE.title: Give each creator who said yes free access, their own link and a short brief
C-CR-ENABLE.purpose: Turn each yes into a live, disclosed piece of content that points to the product through the creator's own link, so their audience hears a true message and every sale can be credited to them.

steps.do: For each creator who said yes, set up what was promised: the free account or code the owner issued, and their own link: their affiliate link if a program exists, otherwise this round's tracked link with their label (?v=their-name). Open each link and check it lands on the right page.
steps.evidence: For each creator, the access given and the link, opened and confirmed.

steps.do: Write a one-page brief: who the product is for, the problem it solves in the buyer's words, three benefits from the proven benefits list, the price as shown on the product page, their link and code, the disclosure line, and a 'please do not say' list (no invented results, no guarantees, no fake urgency). Leave the creative choices to them.
steps.evidence: The brief, and a sentence-by-sentence check against the product facts.

steps.do: Show the owner the brief and the delivery message word for word and get a yes, then send each creator their brief once from the approved account.
steps.evidence: The owner's approval and, for each creator, the send time.

steps.do: Answer each creator's product questions from the fact sheet within one business day; anything not on it goes to the owner first.
steps.evidence: The questions asked and the answers given, with the owner's answer where one was needed.

steps.do: When a creator publishes, open the post and check that their link or code is there and the disclosure is shown. If something is missing, ask them politely once to fix it. Never ask them to change their opinion.
steps.evidence: Each live post URL, whether the link and the disclosure are present, and any fix requested.

steps.do: Record each creator's link, terms, post URL and publish date. A commission is owed only on a counted sale and paid only when it has really been paid.
steps.evidence: The creator record with link, terms, post URL, publish date and commission status.

blockers.do: If no creator has published by the end of the window, record that; never publish on their behalf or write their post for them.
If a post has no disclosure, ask the creator once to add it and tell the owner; do not promote that post until it is fixed.
If a creator's link does not open the product, fix it with tracking and send them the corrected link.
If the owner has not issued the free accounts or codes, submit the step as blocked with exactly how many are needed.
If a creator asks for a fee beyond the approved terms, take it to the owner and promise nothing.

C-CR-ENABLE.title_zh: 給答應的創作者免費使用、專屬連結與簡短說明

deliver_help.creators_live: Each creator who agreed, with status: briefed, published, or not published yet.
deliver_help.creator_links: Each creator's own link or code, opened and confirmed.
deliver_help.brief_text: The brief as sent, including the disclosure line and the 'please do not say' list.
deliver_help.post_urls: The public URL of each published post or video, or 'none yet'.

C-BASE-ACCESS.title: Confirm the member list, the channels you may use and the limits
C-BASE-ACCESS.purpose: Find out exactly which list of existing members or customers can be used, through which channels the owner may message them, who agreed to what, and how much there is to sell, so every message goes only to people the brand may contact and no seat is sold that does not exist.

steps.do: Ask the owner where members are recorded: a list uploaded on the hosted owner page, the payment tool (Stripe customers), a booking or ticketing tool, a CRM, a spreadsheet, a LINE Official Account or WhatsApp Business. If nothing is uploaded yet, ask for a CSV export with email or phone, name, status (member, paying, free, past) and last purchase date, uploaded on the owner page or shared as a file. Never ask for a password to their tools.
steps.evidence: The list source, its columns, the row count, and when it was exported.

steps.do: For each channel the owner can message (email, LINE, WhatsApp, Instagram or Facebook messages, SMS), write which account sends, its sending limits and who presses send. Have the owner sign in, or confirm the agent's browser already is.
steps.evidence: Each channel with its sending account, limit and sender.

steps.do: Check consent per channel: who agreed to marketing email or messages, who only bought (some countries allow email to past buyers about similar products if they can opt out; others do not), and who unsubscribed or asked to stop. Write the rule you will apply and ask the owner to confirm it. People with no record of agreeing are left out of marketing messages.
steps.evidence: The consent rule, how many people it allows per channel, and the owner's confirmation.

steps.do: Get the do-not-contact list: unsubscribes, bounces, complaints, people who asked to stop, staff and test accounts. They are removed from every send in this goal.
steps.evidence: The do-not-contact list's size and where it came from.

steps.do: Ask for the capacity: seats, tables, stock or onboarding slots per week and the dates they cover (for example 'Taipei Saturday events: 40 seats a week'). Every offer in this goal stays inside it; if the plan would sell more than exists, the plan changes, not the promise.
steps.evidence: Capacity per week with dates and source, or 'no limit' confirmed by the owner.

steps.do: Read the current offer from the product's own pages: plans, prices, member or season options, existing discounts and referral rewards. Do not create plans, codes or rewards; the owner does that in their own tools if they decide to.
steps.evidence: The offer sheet with each line's URL.

steps.do: Summarise in five lines (list, channels, consent rule, do-not-contact list, capacity) and get the owner's yes.
steps.evidence: The summary and the owner's approval message.

blockers.do: If there is no member list, ask the owner to upload or export one and say exactly where on the owner page to do it; until then this goal sends nothing.
If nobody can say who agreed to messages, use only people who bought or wrote to the brand in the last 90 days and did not opt out, and tell the owner.
If the signed-in sending account is personal or another brand's, stop and ask the owner to switch or to send themselves.
If the owner cannot say how many seats or units exist, offer no dates or stock until they confirm.
Keep the list inside the hosted service or the owner's own files; never paste it into public places or other tools.

C-BASE-ACCESS.title_zh: 確認會員名單、可聯絡的管道與上限

deliver_help.member_list: Where the list lives, its columns, its row count and export date. Example: 'owner page upload, 3,214 rows, exported 2026-11-26'.
deliver_help.channels: Each channel with the sending account, its limit and who presses send.
deliver_help.consent_rule: Who may get marketing messages on which channel, and how many people that is.
deliver_help.suppression: The size and source of the do-not-contact list.
deliver_help.capacity: Seats, stock or slots per week with dates, or 'no limit' confirmed by the owner.

C-BASE-SEGMENT.title: Pick the members this round is for
C-BASE-SEGMENT.purpose: Turn the member list into one clear group for this goal, with a count and a reason, so the message speaks to their situation and the result is read against the right group.

steps.do: Apply the group this goal needs. Win back: paid or attended before, nothing in the last 60 to 180 days (pick the range from how often members normally come back). Referral: paying or recently active members who came at least twice or rated it well. Upgrade: free, trial or one-time buyers who used it at least once in the last 60 days. Write the exact rule with dates.
steps.evidence: The rule in one sentence with its date range.

steps.do: Count the group from the list, then remove the do-not-contact list and anyone outside the consent rule. When the hosted list is used, the counts come from it.
steps.evidence: The count before and after each removal.

steps.do: Split the group by what changes the message: city or location, what they bought, how long ago, how often. Keep at most 3 sub-groups; a sub-group under 30 people merges with another.
steps.evidence: The sub-groups with their counts.

steps.do: For each sub-group, write the one real reason to act now (a new date in their city, a season starting, a feature they asked for), taken from the product facts and the buyer research.
steps.evidence: One reason per sub-group with its source.

steps.do: Choose the channel per sub-group from the confirmed channels: the one they agreed to and use most.
steps.evidence: The channel per sub-group.

steps.do: Check capacity: if everyone in the group said yes, would it fit the seats or stock per week? If not, spread the sends over weeks or make the group smaller.
steps.evidence: The capacity check and the send plan by week.

blockers.do: If the group has fewer than 30 people, widen the date range and say so.
If the list was exported more than 14 days ago, ask the owner for a fresh export before anything is sent.
If you cannot tell who agreed to messages on a channel, leave those people out and tell the owner how many.
If capacity cannot take the whole group, send to part of it now and the rest when seats free up.

C-BASE-SEGMENT.title_zh: 挑出這一輪要聯絡的會員

deliver_help.segment_rule: The exact rule with dates, for example 'paid at least once, nothing since 2026-08-01'.
deliver_help.counts: The count before and after removing the do-not-contact list and people outside the consent rule.
deliver_help.sub_groups: Each sub-group with its count and its reason to act now.
deliver_help.channel_plan: The channel per sub-group and the send plan by week that fits capacity.

C-BASE-METRICS.title: Read this goal's member numbers
C-BASE-METRICS.purpose: Record the number this goal is judged on, counted once per real person and net of refunds and tests, for the window before this round and for this round, so rounds are compared on paying members rather than replies.

steps.do: Call where_are_we (with lane in a month target) and copy this goal's component name and window: reactivated_paying_members, paid_referrals or upgrades.
steps.evidence: The goal id, the component name and the window in hours.

steps.do: Write the counting rule before counting. reactivated_paying_members: a member of this round's win-back group who paid again inside the window. paid_referrals: a new customer who paid inside the window and came through a member's link, label or code. upgrades: a free, trial or one-time user in this round's group who started a paid or season plan inside the window.
steps.evidence: The rule for this goal's component, with dates and time zone.

steps.do: Read the payment records for the window (the payment tool, the booking tool or the owner's export) and tracking's clicks per label. Match each payment to the group by email, member code or label.
steps.evidence: The sources read with times, and the matched payments.

steps.do: Remove the owner's, team's and test payments, refunds inside the window, duplicates, and anyone who was already on that plan or paid before the round started.
steps.evidence: What was removed and why, with counts.

steps.do: For the baseline, count the same thing for the same length of time just before this round, among the same kind of group (members who came back on their own, friends who arrived without an invite, upgrades without an offer). If there is no history, record 0 and say so.
steps.evidence: The baseline count and how it was taken.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with this goal's component and a source naming each report and when it was read. In a month target lane also pass paid_customers (paying customers since the month started, from the payment records), and visits and signups if you have them; they update the month progress and are not judged here. Never estimate; a reply or a booking that is not paid does not count.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call as accepted.

blockers.do: If you cannot open the payment records, ask the owner for an export of the exact window; never estimate.
If payments cannot be matched to the group, count only matched ones and say how many could not be matched.
If there is no earlier window to compare, record 0 and say 'no history'.
If the window has not ended, report the reading as early and read again when it ends.
If the owner's, team's or test payments cannot be separated, ask the owner to mark them before recording.

C-BASE-METRICS.title_zh: 核對會員喚回、推薦與升級的成果

deliver_help.numbers: This goal's component with its value, for example 'reactivated_paying_members: 23'.
deliver_help.where_read: Each source and when it was read, what was removed and why, and payments that could not be matched.
deliver_help.date_range: Start and end of the window with time zone, and whether it is the baseline or the current reading.

C-BASE-WINBACK.title: Send the approved win-back message to inactive members within the daily cap
C-BASE-WINBACK.purpose: Bring inactive members back with one personal, owner-approved message per person about something real and new for them, within the approved daily cap, so lapsed members return as paying members and nobody is spammed.

steps.do: Write one template per sub-group, under 100 words, with placeholders such as {first_name}, {last_thing_they_did} and {next_date_in_their_city}. Lead with what is new or relevant for them, give one next step with the round's tracked link (?v= per sub-group), and an easy way to stop messages. No invented scarcity: 'few seats left' must be true at send time. Each placeholder value is one line of at most 80 characters (40 for a name); where one needs more, write its limit, for example {last_thing_they_did:120} (200 at most). Values carry no links; a link goes in the fixed text or a {link} placeholder.
steps.evidence: Each template with its placeholders and sub-group.

steps.do: Write each template's audience rule and propose a daily cap that fits the channel's limit and the capacity (for example 200 emails a day, or the LINE plan's monthly message allowance spread over the month).
steps.evidence: The audience rule and daily cap for each template.

steps.do: Get the template approved. In a month target, send it with submit_batch as one item of kind 'template' with text, audience_rule and daily_cap, and tell the owner to approve it on their owner page or with the approve command. Outside a month target, show the owner the template, the audience rule and the cap, and get a clear yes. Never approve it yourself.
steps.evidence: The template ids and the owner's approval.

steps.do: Get the next recipients: on the hosted service call next_recipients with the lane, the template's item id and how many you will send today; otherwise take them in order from the owner's export, skipping anyone already contacted this round.
steps.evidence: Today's recipient count and where it came from.

steps.do: Send once per person from the approved account, at most the daily cap per day, filling only the placeholders with true values, each one line, at most 80 characters (40 for a name) unless the template sets its own limit such as {last_thing_they_did:120}, with no link except in a {link} placeholder. A WhatsApp message to someone who has not written in the last 24 hours needs a template Meta has approved. If you are unsure whether a message went, check before resending. When today's messages are out, submit this step with approved_item set to the template's id (in a month target) and the sent texts in output; the engine checks each one against the approved template and the day's cap.
steps.evidence: Per day: how many were sent, on which channel, by whom, and a sample of the sent texts.

steps.do: Answer replies the same day where you can: dates, price and fit from the fact sheet, anything else from the owner. Remove anyone who asks to stop from every later send.
steps.evidence: Replies with the answers given, and the people removed.

steps.do: Send no second message to the same person in this round. Record who came back (booked, renewed or paid) with the date.
steps.evidence: The members who came back, with dates and sources.

blockers.do: If the owner has not approved a template, send nothing with it; show the template, rule and cap and wait.
If the group is used up, say so and stop; never buy, borrow or scrape a list.
If more people are due than the cap allows, send the rest on later days.
If Meta has not approved the WhatsApp template, send on another agreed channel or wait; never send free text to people outside the 24-hour window.
If a spam complaint, block or warning arrives, pause sending on that channel and tell the owner the same day.
If a date fills up, stop offering it at once and update the template only with the owner's yes.

C-BASE-WINBACK.title_zh: 在每日上限內寄出已核准的喚回訊息

deliver_help.templates: Each approved template word for word with its audience rule and daily cap.
deliver_help.owner_approval: The template ids and the owner's approval with dates.
deliver_help.sent_record: Per day: count sent per channel, who sent, and sample texts.
deliver_help.replies: Replies with answers, and the people who asked to stop.
deliver_help.came_back: Members who booked, renewed or paid, with dates and where it was read, or 'none yet'.

C-BASE-REFER.title: Ask happy members to invite a friend with their own invite link
C-BASE-REFER.purpose: Give members who already value the product a simple, honest reason to bring a friend, with an invite link that is theirs, so new paying customers arrive through people they trust and every referral can be counted and rewarded.

steps.do: Settle the referral offer with the owner from existing tools only: what the friend gets (for example a first-visit price or trial that already exists), what the member gets (credit, a free event, a discount), when the reward is given (after the friend pays) and any limit. If there is no reward, ask the owner once whether to add one in their own tools; never promise one yourself.
steps.evidence: The referral terms quoted from the owner, or 'no reward' confirmed.

steps.do: Give each member their own invite link: the product's own referral link if it has one, otherwise this round's tracked link with the member's label (?v=m-{member_code}) using a short code, never their email or name.
steps.evidence: The link format and one example, opened and confirmed to land on the right page.

steps.do: Write one invite template under 100 words with placeholders such as {first_name}, {their_link} and {what_they_liked}, plus a ready-to-forward line the member can paste to a friend. Make it about the friend's benefit, not the reward. Each placeholder value is one line of at most 80 characters (40 for a name); where one needs more, write its limit, for example {what_they_liked:120} (200 at most). Values carry no links; a link goes in the fixed text or a {link} placeholder.
steps.evidence: The template, the forwardable line and the placeholders.

steps.do: Get the template approved. In a month target, send it with submit_batch as one item of kind 'template' with text, audience_rule and daily_cap, and tell the owner to approve it on their owner page or with the approve command. Outside a month target, show the owner the template, the audience rule and the cap, and get a clear yes. Never approve it yourself.
steps.evidence: The template's id and the owner's approval.

steps.do: Send once per member within the daily cap, taking recipients from next_recipients on the hosted service or from the owner's export, from the approved account. When today's messages are out, submit this step with approved_item set to the template's id (in a month target) and the sent texts in output; the engine checks each one against the approved template and the day's cap. Fill each placeholder with a true value: one line, at most 80 characters (40 for a name) unless the template sets its own limit, with no link except in a {link} placeholder.
steps.evidence: Per day: how many were sent, on which channel, and a sample of the sent texts.

steps.do: When a friend pays, check the payment against the member's label or code and record the reward as owed; it is paid only when the owner really gives it. Thank the member.
steps.evidence: Each paid referral with the member label, payment reference and reward status.

blockers.do: If the owner has not decided a reward, send the invite without one and never hint at one.
If the product cannot make per-member links, use the label on the tracked link or a code the owner creates.
If the owner has not approved the template, send nothing; show it and wait.
If more members are due than the cap allows, send the rest on later days.
If a member disputes a reward, pass it to the owner with the payment evidence and promise nothing.

C-BASE-REFER.title_zh: 請滿意的會員用專屬連結邀請朋友

deliver_help.referral_terms: What the friend and the member get and when, quoted from the owner, or 'no reward'.
deliver_help.invite_links: The invite link format and an example, opened and confirmed.
deliver_help.template: The approved template and forwardable line word for word.
deliver_help.sent_record: Per day: count sent per channel and sample texts.
deliver_help.paid_referrals: Each paid referral with member label, payment reference and reward status, or 'none yet'.

C-BASE-UPGRADE.title: Offer free and one-time users the paid or season plan that fits them
C-BASE-UPGRADE.purpose: Show people who already tried the product the existing paid plan that matches how they use it, with the real price and what changes for them, so the ones who would get more from it move up without pressure.

steps.do: From the segment step, write how each sub-group uses the product today and which existing plan fits (for example 'came to two single events in three months: the season pass costs less than three single tickets'). Work out the saving or gain from the real prices; if it is not real for a sub-group, make them no offer.
steps.evidence: Each sub-group with the plan that fits and the calculation from the price page.

steps.do: Write one template per sub-group under 100 words with placeholders such as {first_name}, {times_used} and {what_they_get}. Give the price as shown on the product page, the one main benefit, a link to the plan with the round's tracked link (?v= per sub-group), and how to say no. Mention a deadline only if the offer really ends then. Each placeholder value is one line of at most 80 characters (40 for a name); where one needs more, write its limit, for example {what_they_get:120} (200 at most). Values carry no links; a link goes in the fixed text or a {link} placeholder.
steps.evidence: Each template with its placeholders.

steps.do: Get the template approved. In a month target, send it with submit_batch as one item of kind 'template' with text, audience_rule and daily_cap, and tell the owner to approve it on their owner page or with the approve command. Outside a month target, show the owner the template, the audience rule and the cap, and get a clear yes. Never approve it yourself.
steps.evidence: The template ids and the owner's approval.

steps.do: Check capacity before sending: a season or membership plan needs the seats or slots behind it. Send no more offers in a week than capacity could take if everyone said yes.
steps.evidence: The capacity check for this week's sends.

steps.do: Send once per person within the daily cap, from next_recipients on the hosted service or the owner's export, from the approved account. When today's messages are out, submit this step with approved_item set to the template's id (in a month target) and the sent texts in output; the engine checks each one against the approved template and the day's cap. Fill each placeholder with a true value: one line, at most 80 characters (40 for a name) unless the template sets its own limit, with no link except in a {link} placeholder.
steps.evidence: Per day: how many were sent and on which channel, with a sample of the sent texts.

steps.do: Answer replies from the fact sheet the same day where you can; refunds, billing and exceptions go to the owner. Record each upgrade with its payment reference and date.
steps.evidence: Replies with answers, and each upgrade with its payment reference.

blockers.do: If no existing plan is a real gain for a sub-group, make them no offer and tell the owner what plan they asked for.
If the owner has not approved a template, send nothing with it.
If the plan has no seats or slots left, stop sending offers for it at once.
If upgrading needs something the payment tool cannot do yet, tell the owner; never change billing yourself.
If more people are due than the cap allows, send the rest on later days.

C-BASE-UPGRADE.title_zh: 向免費或單次使用者提供適合的付費或季票方案

deliver_help.plan_fit: Each sub-group, the plan that fits, and the saving or gain worked out from the real prices.
deliver_help.templates: Each approved template word for word with its audience rule and daily cap.
deliver_help.owner_approval: The template ids and the owner's approval with dates.
deliver_help.sent_record: Per day: count sent per channel and sample texts.
deliver_help.upgrades: Each upgrade with payment reference and date, or 'none yet'.

C-B2B-ACCESS.title: Confirm the SaaS offer, the sign-up path and where paid customers are counted
C-B2B-ACCESS.purpose: Pin down what a business buyer can sign up for and pay today, which accounts speak for the company, and where trials and paid customers are read, so every channel in this goal sends people to a working sign-up and every customer is counted once.

steps.do: Use read_page on the pricing, sign-up and docs pages and write the offer: plans, monthly and yearly price, currency, trial length or free plan, whether a card is needed, refund policy, and who the product is for. The owner confirms it.
steps.evidence: The offer sheet with each line's URL and the owner's confirmation.

steps.do: Open the sign-up flow up to the first screen that asks for details and check it loads on a computer and a phone. Create no account unless the owner asks for a test sign-up; if they do, use inbox_address for the email and inbox_latest for the code, and tell the owner to leave it out of the counts.
steps.evidence: The sign-up URL, what its first screen asks for, and any test account created.

steps.do: Ask the owner where trials and paying customers are recorded: Stripe (connected on the hosted owner page, or an export), the product's admin, analytics, or a CRM they already use. Write which number comes from where. Never ask for a password or an API key.
steps.evidence: The source for trials, for paid customers and for visits, and who can read each.

steps.do: Confirm that the sale counter from tracking is on the page shown after the first payment, or name the payment report that replaces it.
steps.evidence: Whether the sale counter is in place, or the report that will be used.

steps.do: Ask which account speaks for the company in each channel this goal uses: the business email or sending domain, the founder's or company's profiles, the marketplace vendor account. Check that the names shown match the brand.
steps.evidence: Each account, who signed in, and the name shown.

steps.do: Write the ideal customer in four lines from the research steps: company type and size, the buyer's role, the problem in their words, and what they use today. Add the 3 to 5 competitors buyers compare with, from the owner and from search.
steps.evidence: The four-line customer profile and the competitor list with URLs.
