steps.do: Agree the limits for this goal: daily caps for messages, the ad budget if ads are used, who presses send, and what may never be promised (roadmap features, custom work, discounts that do not exist). Get the owner's yes.
steps.evidence: The limits and the owner's approval message.

blockers.do: If the sign-up or payment page fails, tell the owner before any channel sends people there.
If paid customers cannot be read anywhere, ask the owner to connect Stripe on the owner page or export the customers list; never estimate.
If a signed-in account is personal or another brand's, stop and ask the owner to switch.
If the pages and the owner disagree on price or plans, use neither until the owner confirms one.
If a verification, terms or identity screen appears, stop and tell the owner which screen and which button.

C-B2B-ACCESS.title_zh: 確認 SaaS 方案、註冊流程與付費客戶的計算來源

deliver_help.offer: Plans, prices, trial and refund terms as shown on the product pages, with URLs, confirmed by the owner.
deliver_help.signup_path: The sign-up URL, what it asks for, and whether it worked on a computer and a phone.
deliver_help.count_sources: Where trials, paid customers and visits are read, for example 'paid: Stripe connected on the owner page; trials: admin export'.
deliver_help.accounts: Each account used in this goal, who signed in and the name shown.
deliver_help.customer_profile: The four-line ideal customer, the competitors, and the limits the owner approved.

C-LTD-ACCESS.title: Choose the deal marketplace and get the deal terms approved by the owner
C-LTD-ACCESS.purpose: Pick the deal marketplace whose buyers match this product and settle deal terms the owner can afford to honour for as long as the deal promises, before anything is listed, because a lifetime deal can sell fast and every buyer must still be served afterwards.

steps.do: List the SaaS deal marketplaces that could fit (for example AppSumo, PitchGround, Dealify or SaaS Mantra) and use read_page on each one's current partner or 'sell with us' page. Note who their buyers are, which categories they accept, and their published requirements and terms (working product, support, refund window, revenue share or fees). Quote what each page says today and write 'unknown' where it does not say.
steps.evidence: Each marketplace with its partner page URL, the quoted requirements and terms, and the date read.

steps.do: Check the product against each marketplace's requirements: it works today without manual setup, it has help pages and a support contact, and it can redeem codes or create accounts for deal buyers the way the marketplace needs. List anything missing as owner work, never as done.
steps.evidence: A pass or missing list per marketplace.

steps.do: Work out with the owner what one deal buyer costs: hosting and AI cost per active account per month, support time per buyer, payment and marketplace fees, and how long service is promised. Compare it with the deal price after the marketplace's share. If a lifetime deal loses money, propose a limited deal instead (a yearly deal, usage caps, or a capped number of codes).
steps.evidence: The cost per buyer, the net per sale after fees, and the recommendation with the numbers behind it.

steps.do: Draft the deal terms: tiers (for example 1, 2 or 3 stacked codes), price per tier, what each includes and its usage limits, what is excluded (future plans, add-ons), the refund window the marketplace sets, the number of codes, and how long service is promised.
steps.evidence: The draft terms as a table.

steps.do: Get the owner's written approval of the exact terms. The owner applies and signs the marketplace's partner agreement themselves; the agent never accepts terms for them. If the form needs a new vendor account, the owner creates it.
steps.evidence: The owner's approval of the terms and the application's status (who submitted it and when).

steps.do: Write the support plan: who answers deal buyers, how fast, where (the deal page's questions, email, help desk), and how many new users a week the team can onboard.
steps.evidence: The support plan with names, response time and weekly capacity.

blockers.do: If the product does not meet a requirement, list the owner work and do not apply until it is done.
If the deal loses money per buyer, do not recommend it; show the owner the numbers and the limited options.
If the owner has not approved the exact terms in writing, list nothing.
If the marketplace declines, record its reason and propose the next marketplace to the owner.
If the marketplace has a waiting list, submit the step as blocked with the expected date.

C-LTD-ACCESS.title_zh: 選擇 SaaS 優惠平台並由負責人核准方案條件

deliver_help.marketplace_choice: The chosen marketplace and why, with the partner page URL and date read.
deliver_help.requirements_check: Each requirement with pass or missing, and the owner work for anything missing.
deliver_help.unit_economics: Cost per deal buyer, net per sale after fees, and how long service is promised.
deliver_help.deal_terms: The tiers, prices, limits, exclusions, refund window and number of codes.
deliver_help.owner_approval: The owner's written approval of the terms and the application status.
deliver_help.support_plan: Who answers, how fast, where, and how many new users a week.

C-B2B-METRICS.title: Read this goal's B2B numbers: trials, meetings, deals and paid customers
C-B2B-METRICS.purpose: Record the number this goal is judged on, counted once per real company and net of tests, refunds and duplicates, for the window before this round and for this round, so channels are compared on buyers rather than activity.

steps.do: Call where_are_we (with lane in a month target) and copy this goal's component names and window.
steps.evidence: The goal id, the component names and the window in hours.

steps.do: Write the counting rule for each component before counting. trial_signups: a new trial or free-plan account from an outside company inside the window, from this goal's links or pages. deals_sold: codes or deals sold on the marketplace inside the window, minus refunds shown inside it. marketplace_signups: installs or sign-ups the marketplace or the tracked link credits to the listing. trial_to_paid_conversions and eligible_trials: trials in this round's group whose pay date fell inside the window, and how many of them paid. confirmed_meetings: a call with a target company that both sides accepted on the calendar. partner_paid_customers: customers who paid inside the window and came through a partner's link, code or introduction.
steps.evidence: The rule for this goal's components, with dates and time zone.

steps.do: Read the sources for the window: tracking (clicks per label and the sale counter), the payment tool or Stripe connection, the product's admin or analytics for sign-ups, the marketplace's vendor dashboard, and the calendar or CRM for meetings. If a source cannot be opened, ask the owner for an export of that exact window.
steps.evidence: Each source with the time it was read or the file received.

steps.do: Keep one row per company: merge duplicates by domain or email, and remove the owner's, team's, test and competitor accounts, free accounts given away, and refunds inside the window.
steps.evidence: What was removed and why, with counts before and after.

steps.do: For the baseline, count the same components for the same length of time just before this round. If there is no history, record 0 and say 'no history'.
steps.evidence: The baseline values and how they were taken.

steps.do: Call record_numbers with each component under its exact name and a source naming each report and when it was read. In a month target lane also pass paid_customers (paying customers since the month started, from the payment records), and visits and signups if you have them; they update the month progress and are not judged here. Never estimate.
steps.evidence: The record_numbers call as accepted.

steps.do: Write one line on where the funnel stalls: too few people reached, reached but not signing up, signing up but not using it, or using it but not paying.
steps.evidence: One line naming the stalled stage with the numbers behind it.

blockers.do: If a source cannot be opened, ask the owner for an export of the exact window; never estimate.
If there is no earlier window to compare, record 0 and say 'no history'; the first round sets the baseline.
If a sign-up or payment cannot be tied to this goal's links, pages or partners, leave it out and say how many.
If the window has not ended, report the reading as early and read again when it ends.
If a rate's denominator is 0, record 0, say so in source, and claim no rate.

C-B2B-METRICS.title_zh: 核對 B2B 試用、會議、成交與付費客戶數字

deliver_help.numbers: Each component under its exact name with its value, for example 'trial_signups: 18'.
deliver_help.where_read: Each source and when it was read, what was removed and why.
deliver_help.date_range: Start and end of the window with time zone, and whether it is the baseline or the current reading.
deliver_help.stalled_stage: The stage where buyers stop, with the numbers behind it.

C-LTD-LISTING.title: Publish the deal listing with true claims and the approved terms
C-LTD-LISTING.purpose: Get the deal live, or in a later round improve it, with a listing that states exactly what buyers get under the approved terms, with real screenshots and a demo, so buyers know what they pay for and refunds stay low.

steps.do: Read the marketplace's listing guide and two or three successful listings in the same category; note their sections, image sizes, video length and the questions buyers ask most.
steps.evidence: The guide URL, the listings read and the sections required.

steps.do: Write the listing from the product facts: a headline with the buyer's outcome, who it is for and not for, what it does today (no roadmap promises), the tiers exactly as approved, limits, and how to redeem. Mark anything that will change after the deal as 'not included'.
steps.evidence: The listing text with a source for each claim.

steps.do: Prepare assets from the real product: screenshots, a short demo of a real task (the demo video step's video can be used), and the founder's short note if the owner wants one.
steps.evidence: The asset list with file names and what each shows.

steps.do: Show the owner the listing and assets word for word and get a clear yes; then the owner, or the agent with its own tools and the owner's yes, submits it in the vendor dashboard.
steps.evidence: The owner's approval and the submission time.

steps.do: Answer the marketplace's review questions and make requested changes; any change to the terms goes back to the owner first.
steps.evidence: Each review question with the answer or change, and the owner's yes for any change to terms.

steps.do: When the deal is live, open the public deal page and check that price, tiers, limits and redemption steps match what was approved. Pass the deal page URL as the first item in links.
steps.evidence: The live deal page URL and the check against the approved terms.

blockers.do: If the listing is still in review, submit the step as blocked with the expected live date.
If the marketplace asks for different terms, take them to the owner; change nothing without their yes.
If a claim cannot be backed by the product facts, remove it.
If a code cannot be redeemed, stop promoting the deal and fix it with the owner first.

C-LTD-LISTING.title_zh: 以真實內容與核准條件上架優惠

deliver_help.listing_url: The public URL of the live deal page.
deliver_help.published_text: The listing text as it appears on the live page.
deliver_help.approved_terms_check: Each approved term and whether the live page matches it.
deliver_help.assets: The screenshots and video used, with what each shows.

C-LTD-SUPPORT.title: Answer deal buyers fast and tell the owner's list about the launch
C-LTD-SUPPORT.purpose: During the window answer every question and review on the deal page from the fact sheet, help buyers redeem, and tell people who already opted in to hear from the brand, because on deal marketplaces quick, honest answers and early real reviews decide how many buy.

steps.do: Check the deal page's questions and reviews at least twice a day during the window. Answer each from the fact sheet in plain words from the brand's vendor account; roadmap, custom work and refunds go to the owner first.
steps.evidence: Each question with the answer posted and its time.

steps.do: Help each buyer who cannot redeem within the support plan's response time; record the problem and the fix.
steps.evidence: Redemption problems with the time each took to fix.

steps.do: Ask buyers who have used it for a few days for an honest review on the deal page. Never offer anything for a good review, never write reviews yourself and never ask the team to.
steps.evidence: Review requests sent (to whom, when) and reviews posted.

steps.do: If the owner has an opted-in list (email, LINE, a community), write one short launch note with the deal link, get the owner's yes on the exact text, and send it once within that list's normal limits.
steps.evidence: The approved note, where it was sent and to how many people.

steps.do: Keep a list of every complaint and refund reason. When the same problem appears three times, tell the owner the same day with a proposed fix.
steps.evidence: The complaint list with counts per reason and what was reported to the owner.

blockers.do: If a question is about the roadmap, custom work or a refund, answer only after the owner decides.
Never offer a reward for reviews, even if a buyer asks for one.
If refunds rise above the usual rate, tell the owner the same day with the reasons.
If nobody on a list agreed to hear from the brand, do not send them the launch note.

C-LTD-SUPPORT.title_zh: 快速回覆優惠買家並通知既有名單

deliver_help.answers_posted: Each question answered on the deal page with time and text.
deliver_help.redemption_issues: Each redemption problem and its fix, or 'none'.
deliver_help.review_requests: Who was asked for a review and when, and reviews posted.
deliver_help.launch_note: The approved launch note, the list it went to and the count, or 'no opted-in list'.
deliver_help.complaints: Complaint and refund reasons with counts, and what was reported to the owner.

C-ALT-RESEARCH.title: Find the competitor searches buyers type and what they dislike about each
C-ALT-RESEARCH.purpose: Find which 'alternative to' and 'versus' searches real buyers type, and what reviewers say they dislike about each competitor, from public sources, so the comparison pages and ads answer an actual buyer question honestly.

steps.do: For each competitor from the access step, list the searches buyers use: '{competitor} alternative', '{competitor} alternatives for {use case}', '{competitor} vs {product}', '{competitor} pricing', 'cheaper than {competitor}'. Check the search engine's suggestions and related questions for each, and the keyword tool's volumes if the owner's ad account is connected.
steps.evidence: The searches per competitor with where each came from and any volume shown.

steps.do: Use read_page on each competitor's pricing and feature pages and write what they charge and include today. Date it; prices change.
steps.evidence: Each competitor's plans and prices with URLs and the date read.

steps.do: Read public reviews of each competitor (G2, Capterra, app marketplace reviews, Reddit threads) and copy 5 to 10 complaints in the reviewers' words with links, above all the ones this product really solves.
steps.evidence: Quoted complaints with URLs, each marked 'we solve this', 'partly' or 'no'.

steps.do: Write a fair comparison table: where this product is better, where the competitor is better, and where they are the same, each with a source. Leave out anything you cannot verify.
steps.evidence: The comparison table with sources, including the competitor's real strengths.

steps.do: Pick 2 to 4 searches for this round, each with real volume or clear buying words and a complaint the product truly solves. Group them as the keyword groups the ad draft step will use.
steps.evidence: The chosen searches grouped for ads, with the reason for each.

steps.do: Note the rules: no competitor trademark in ad text where the ad platform or local law forbids it, no false or unverifiable claim about a competitor, and the date the comparison was checked shown on the page.
steps.evidence: The rules that apply, with a link to the ad platform's trademark policy.

blockers.do: If no competitor is known, search the problem in buyer words and list the tools people mention before going on.
If no search volume can be seen, choose searches with clear buying words and write 'volume unknown'.
If a fact about a competitor cannot be checked on their own pages or a public review, leave it out.
If the ad platform restricts a competitor's trademark, keep it out of the ad text and use it only as a keyword where allowed.

C-ALT-RESEARCH.title_zh: 找出買家搜尋的競品替代關鍵字與對各競品的不滿

deliver_help.searches: The searches per competitor with their source and volume if shown.
deliver_help.competitor_facts: Each competitor's plans and prices with URLs and date read.
deliver_help.complaints: Quoted public complaints with URLs and whether the product solves each.
deliver_help.comparison_table: The fair comparison table with sources.
deliver_help.chosen_searches: The 2 to 4 searches for this round, grouped as keyword groups, with reasons.

C-ALT-PAGES.title: Publish an honest comparison page for each chosen competitor search
C-ALT-PAGES.purpose: Give buyers who search for an alternative a page on the owner's site that answers their question fairly and puts the trial one click away, because a page that is fair to the competitor is the one buyers trust and search engines keep.

steps.do: For each chosen search, write one page: a title that matches the search ('{competitor} alternative for {use case}'), who should switch and who should not, the comparison table with sources and the date checked, the complaints it solves quoted from public reviews with links, how to switch (import, setup time), the price, and one call to the trial with the round's tracked link (?v= per page).
steps.evidence: Each page's full text with sources.

steps.do: Check every claim against the product facts and the competitor's own pages; remove anything not true today. Keep the competitor's strengths in.
steps.evidence: A claim-by-claim check.

steps.do: Show the owner each page word for word and get a clear yes.
steps.evidence: The owner's approval.

steps.do: The owner publishes it on their site, or the agent does with its own tools and the owner's yes. Check it loads, can be indexed (no noindex), has a clear title and description, and is linked from the site's footer or a 'compare' page so search engines find it.
steps.evidence: The live URL, the indexing check, and where it is linked from.

steps.do: Submit the page in the owner's search console if it is connected, or note that it is not. Pass the page URL as the first item in links.
steps.evidence: The submission result or 'not connected'.

blockers.do: If nobody can publish on the site, submit the step as blocked and tell the owner exactly which page to add and where.
If a claim cannot be verified today, remove it before publishing.
If the owner has not approved the page, publish nothing.
If the page cannot be indexed, ask the owner to remove the noindex setting before the round is measured.

C-ALT-PAGES.title_zh: 為選定的競品搜尋發布誠實的比較頁

deliver_help.page_urls: The public URL of each comparison page.
deliver_help.published_text: The text of each page as published.
deliver_help.owner_approval: The owner's approval with its date.
deliver_help.tracked_links: The tracked link with its label on each page.

C-INT-FIND.title: Find public posts and reviews where people ask for this or complain about the problem
C-INT-FIND.purpose: Collect recent public posts where a real buyer asks for a tool like this or complains about the problem or a competitor, in places that allow answers, so every reply goes to someone who already wants a solution.

steps.do: Write 10 to 20 searches in the buyer's words from the research steps: requests ('looking for a tool to {job}', 'recommend {category}'), complaints ('{competitor} too expensive', '{competitor} alternative', 'hate {task}') and switching moments ('moving off {competitor}').
steps.evidence: The searches.

steps.do: Search where buyers ask: Reddit (subreddits for the buyer's role or tools), X, LinkedIn posts, Hacker News, Indie Hackers, product communities and Q&A sites, and competitor reviews on G2, Capterra or app marketplaces. Use read_page on public pages only; never log in to collect pages, and use a private group only if the owner is a member and its rules allow it.
steps.evidence: Each place searched with the searches used and the date.

steps.do: Keep posts from the last 14 days (30 days for reviews) where the author describes the problem this product solves or asks for a tool. Drop vendor posts, posts already solved to the author's satisfaction, and threads that no longer accept replies.
steps.evidence: The kept posts with URL, date, author handle and the sentence that shows the need.

steps.do: Read each place's rules: self-promotion, whether links are allowed, required disclosure, and whether messaging strangers is allowed. Mark each post 'public reply ok', 'reply without link' or 'skip'. Send a private message only where the author asked for one (for example 'DM me recommendations').
steps.evidence: The rule for each place with its URL, and the mark on each post.

steps.do: Score each post by fit (does the product truly solve it), freshness and how the author can be reached under the rules. Keep the top 10 to 30 for this round, no more than the reply cap allows.
steps.evidence: The ranked list with scores.

blockers.do: If fewer than 10 posts qualify, widen the searches or places and tell the owner the list is thin.
If a place forbids replies like these, skip it; never work around its rules.
If a page needs a login to read, ask the owner to paste the text or skip it; never log in to collect pages.
If the author works for a competitor or sells a similar tool, skip the post.

C-INT-FIND.title_zh: 找出公開詢問需求或抱怨問題的貼文與評論

deliver_help.qualified_posts: The ranked posts with URL, date, author handle, the need in their words and the reply mark.
deliver_help.rules_by_place: The rules found for each place, with URLs.
deliver_help.searches_used: The searches and places, with the date.

C-INT-REPLY.title: Reply helpfully to each chosen post with the approved template, within the daily cap
C-INT-REPLY.purpose: Answer each chosen post with a genuinely useful reply that says who you are and offers the product only where it fits, built from one owner-approved template and kept within a daily cap, so buyers get help and the brand never looks like spam.

steps.do: Write one reply template under 90 words with placeholders such as {name_or_handle}, {their_problem} (in their words), {specific_tip:200} (one concrete tip in one sentence that helps even without the product, up to 200 characters) and {fit_line:120} (why the product fits their case, up to 120 characters). Every other value is one line of at most 80 characters (40 for a name), with no link except in a {link} placeholder. The fixed text says the relationship ('I work on {product}') and includes the tracked link only where the place allows links (?v= per place). Make a no-link version for places that forbid links.
steps.evidence: The template with its placeholders, and the no-link version.

steps.do: Write the audience rule ('authors of posts on this round's list marked public reply ok, from the last 14 days') and propose a daily cap: start at 10 replies a day across all places and at most 3 in the same community a day.
steps.evidence: The audience rule and the daily cap.

steps.do: Get the template approved. In a month target, send it with submit_batch as one item of kind 'template' with text, audience_rule and daily_cap, and tell the owner to approve it on their owner page or with the approve command. Outside a month target, show the owner the template, the audience rule and the cap, and get a clear yes. Never approve it yourself.
steps.evidence: The template's id and the owner's approval.

steps.do: Fill the placeholders for each post from what the author wrote, each value true and one line, at most 80 characters (40 for a name) unless the template sets its own limit such as {specific_tip:200}, with no link except in a {link} placeholder. If the product does not fit their case, do not reply with the product; at most give the tip alone.
steps.evidence: Each filled reply with the post it answers.

steps.do: Post each reply from the brand's or founder's own account, at most the daily cap per day; never through new or borrowed accounts. When today's messages are out, submit this step with approved_item set to the template's id (in a month target) and the sent texts in output; the engine checks each one against the approved template and the day's cap. Put each reply's public URL in output. Fill each placeholder with a true value: one line, at most 80 characters (40 for a name) unless the template sets its own limit, with no link except in a {link} placeholder.
steps.evidence: Each reply's public URL, posting time and account.

steps.do: Check back after 24 hours: answer follow-up questions from the fact sheet, and if the author asks how to start, give the trial link. If a reply was removed or the account warned, stop in that community and tell the owner.
steps.evidence: Follow-ups answered, replies removed or warnings received, and authors who started a trial.

blockers.do: If the owner has not approved the template, post nothing.
If a reply is removed or the account is warned, stop posting in that community and tell the owner.
If more posts qualify than the cap allows, keep the best ones for the next day.
If the product does not solve the author's case, do not mention it.
If the account is limited or new accounts cannot reply, tell the owner; never create or borrow other accounts.

C-INT-REPLY.title_zh: 在每日上限內，用核准的模板逐一有用地回覆選定貼文

deliver_help.template: The approved template and its no-link version word for word.
deliver_help.owner_approval: The template's id and the owner's approval with its date.
deliver_help.reply_urls: The public URL of every reply posted.
deliver_help.replied_text: The text of every reply as posted.
deliver_help.conversations: Authors who answered, what they asked, and who started a trial, or 'none yet'.

C-TRIAL-ACCESS.title: Connect the trial list and agree what 'activated' means
C-TRIAL-ACCESS.purpose: Get a current list of trials with sign-up date, activity and pay date from a source the owner controls, and agree with the owner on the one action that shows a trial got value, so every message goes to the right trial at the right stage.

steps.do: Ask the owner where trials are recorded: Stripe trialing subscriptions (connected on the hosted owner page), the product's admin export, or analytics. Get an upload or export of current trials with email, name, company, sign-up date, trial end date, plan and last active date. Never ask for a password or an API key.
steps.evidence: The source, its columns and row count, and the export time.

steps.do: Agree the activation action with the owner: the one thing users who end up paying usually do early (for example 'converted a first song', 'invited a teammate', 'connected their data'). Use the owner's numbers if they have them; otherwise pick the action closest to the product's main promise and mark it 'to check'.
steps.evidence: The activation action and how it shows in the data.

steps.do: Confirm which messages trial users agreed to: product and account emails, in-app messages, marketing emails. Write the rule for each message type and remove anyone who unsubscribed.
steps.evidence: The consent rule per message type and how many were removed.

steps.do: Confirm the tool for trial emails or in-app messages (the product's own email, the owner's email service, or in-app messaging), the sender name and address, and its daily limit, and list the trial emails the product already sends on its own.
steps.evidence: The sending tool, sender, daily limit, and the existing automatic trial emails.

steps.do: Read the trial-to-paid rate for the last 30 to 90 days if the data allows: trials that ended in that period and how many paid.
steps.evidence: The past rate with its period and source, or 'no history'.

blockers.do: If there is no trial list, ask the owner to connect Stripe on the owner page or upload an export; until then send nothing.
If activity cannot be seen, use sign-up and trial end dates only and say so.
If consent for marketing messages is unknown, send only product and account messages about the user's own trial.
If the sending account is not the product's, stop and ask the owner to switch.

C-TRIAL-ACCESS.title_zh: 連接試用名單並定義「已啟用」

deliver_help.trial_list: Where the trial list comes from, its columns, row count and export time.
deliver_help.activation_action: The activation action and how it is seen in the data.
deliver_help.consent_rule: Which message types may go to whom, and how many were removed.
deliver_help.sending_tool: The sending tool, sender, daily limit and the automatic trial emails already sent.
deliver_help.past_rate: The past trial-to-paid rate with period and source, or 'no history'.

C-TRIAL-STAGES.title: Sort trials by where they are stuck
C-TRIAL-STAGES.purpose: Split current trials by stage (signed up but never used it, used it but not activated, activated but not paid) so each gets the one message that moves them a step, instead of the same reminder for everyone.

steps.do: Put each trial in one stage: (a) signed up, never used it; (b) used it but has not done the activation action; (c) activated, with the trial ending in the next 7 days or past the pay date without paying; (d) paid, which is left out.
steps.evidence: Counts per stage with the date of the data.

steps.do: For stages (a) and (b), find where people stop from the data you have: the setup step most people never finish, a common error, or support questions. Use read_page on the help pages for the fix.
steps.evidence: The main stopping point per stage with its evidence.

steps.do: Write the one goal of the message for each stage: (a) finish setup in a few minutes with a direct link; (b) do the activation action with a short how-to; (c) choose a plan, with the real price and what happens to their work if they do not.
steps.evidence: One message goal per stage.

steps.do: Read 5 to 10 replies, support tickets or cancellation reasons if the owner has them, and note the objections in users' words.
steps.evidence: The objections quoted with sources, or 'none available'.

steps.do: Set timing per stage from the sign-up date (for example day 1, day 3, two days before the trial ends) and the most messages one person gets during a trial (at most 4, counting the product's own automatic emails).
steps.evidence: The schedule per stage and the per-person limit.

blockers.do: If there are fewer than 20 trials, keep one stage for all and say so.
If the product already sends automatic trial emails, count them in the per-person limit and ask the owner before adding more.
If there is no help page for the stopping point, write the steps from the product itself and have the owner confirm them.
If no trial is open, record that and wait for new trials.

C-TRIAL-STAGES.title_zh: 依卡關位置分類試用使用者

deliver_help.stages: Counts per stage and the date of the data.
deliver_help.stopping_points: Where people stop in stages (a) and (b), with evidence.
deliver_help.message_goals: The one goal of the message per stage.
deliver_help.objections: Objections in users' words with sources, or 'none available'.
deliver_help.schedule: When each stage gets its message, and the per-person limit.

C-TRIAL-SEND.title: Send the approved stage messages to trials within the daily cap
C-TRIAL-SEND.purpose: Send each trial the one approved message for their stage at the planned time, within the daily cap and the per-person limit, so more of them reach value and choose a plan before their trial ends.

steps.do: Write one template per stage, under 120 words, with placeholders such as {first_name}, {company}, {their_last_action} and {days_left}. One goal per message, one link (the round's tracked link with ?v= per stage, or the in-app link), the real price only in stage (c), and an easy way to stop. Each placeholder value is one line of at most 80 characters (40 for a name); where one needs more, write its limit, for example {their_last_action:120} (200 at most). Values carry no links; a link goes in the fixed text or a {link} placeholder.
steps.evidence: The templates by stage.

steps.do: Write each template's audience rule (the stage definition) and a daily cap within the sending tool's limit.
steps.evidence: The rule and cap per template.

steps.do: Get the template approved. In a month target, send it with submit_batch as one item of kind 'template' with text, audience_rule and daily_cap, and tell the owner to approve it on their owner page or with the approve command. Outside a month target, show the owner the template, the audience rule and the cap, and get a clear yes. Never approve it yourself.
steps.evidence: The template ids and the owner's approval.

steps.do: Each day, take the trials due for a message (next_recipients on the hosted service, or the owner's latest export), remove anyone who paid, unsubscribed or reached the per-person limit, and send within the cap. When today's messages are out, submit this step with approved_item set to the template's id (in a month target) and the sent texts in output; the engine checks each one against the approved template and the day's cap. Fill each placeholder with a true value: one line, at most 80 characters (40 for a name) unless the template sets its own limit, with no link except in a {link} placeholder.
steps.evidence: Per day: how many were sent per stage, who was removed and why, and sample texts.

steps.do: Answer replies within one business day from the fact sheet; billing, discounts and exceptions go to the owner. Offer a short call only if the owner has time for one.
steps.evidence: Replies and the answers given.

steps.do: Record each trial who activated or paid after a message, with dates.
steps.evidence: The list with dates and where it was read.

blockers.do: If the owner has not approved a template, send nothing with it.
If more trials are due than the cap allows, send the most urgent stage first and the rest the next day.
If someone already got the most messages allowed, send them nothing more.
If the trial list is more than 2 days old, ask for a fresh export before sending stage (c) messages.

C-TRIAL-SEND.title_zh: 在每日上限內寄出各階段核准的試用訊息

deliver_help.templates: Each approved template word for word with its stage, audience rule and daily cap.
deliver_help.owner_approval: The template ids and the owner's approval with dates.
deliver_help.sent_record: Per day: count sent per stage, removals and sample texts.
deliver_help.moved_on: Trials who activated or paid after a message, with dates, or 'none yet'.

C-MKT-ACCESS.title: Pick the marketplaces and directories where buyers search, and check what each requires
C-MKT-ACCESS.purpose: List only the integration marketplaces and software directories where this product's buyers look for tools and where it truly qualifies, and confirm the owner's vendor accounts, so every listing is real and nothing is promised that the product cannot do.

steps.do: From the customer profile, list the tools buyers already use and, for each, where people find add-ons: Slack App Directory, HubSpot App Marketplace, Shopify App Store, Zapier's app directory, Chrome Web Store, Atlassian Marketplace, Google Workspace Marketplace; and software directories such as G2, Capterra, SaaSHub, AlternativeTo and Product Hunt.
steps.evidence: The tools buyers use and the matching marketplaces.

steps.do: For each, read the current publishing requirements (for example a working app or integration reviewed by the platform, a security review, privacy policy, support URL, demo account) and note the review time. A directory listing needs only a real product; an app marketplace needs a working integration.
steps.evidence: Requirements and review time per marketplace, with URLs.

steps.do: Check which ones the product qualifies for today: the integration or extension is already built and working, or it is a plain product listing. Building an integration is product work for the owner; list it as an option, never as done.
steps.evidence: 'Qualifies now', 'needs product work' or 'not a fit', per marketplace.

steps.do: Ask the owner which vendor or developer accounts exist and have them sign in. A new account is created by the owner; the agent may use inbox_address and inbox_latest for its verification email if the owner asks. Never accept a developer agreement for the owner.
steps.evidence: The accounts, who signed in, and any agreement the owner accepted.

steps.do: Choose up to 3 marketplaces for this round where the product qualifies now and buyers search, and get the owner's yes.
steps.evidence: The chosen marketplaces with reasons and the owner's approval.

blockers.do: If no app marketplace fits because there is no integration, use directory listings only and tell the owner what integration would open which marketplace.
If a vendor account or identity check is needed, tell the owner which page and which button.
If a developer agreement must be accepted, the owner reads and accepts it; never accept it for them.
If a requirement is unclear, quote the marketplace's text and ask the owner before submitting.

C-MKT-ACCESS.title_zh: 選出買家會搜尋的整合市集與目錄，並確認上架條件

deliver_help.marketplaces: The marketplaces and directories considered, with URLs.
deliver_help.requirements: Each one's requirements and review time.
deliver_help.qualification: 'Qualifies now', 'needs product work' or 'not a fit' per marketplace.
deliver_help.vendor_accounts: The vendor accounts, who signed in, and agreements the owner accepted.
deliver_help.chosen: The up to 3 marketplaces for this round and the owner's yes.

C-MKT-LISTING.title: Publish or improve the marketplace listing with real screenshots and the tracked link
C-MKT-LISTING.purpose: Make each chosen listing answer what a buyer browsing that marketplace wants to know, in their words, with real screenshots and a working install or trial path, so listing visitors become installs and trials.

steps.do: Read the top 5 listings in the same category on that marketplace: their names, first lines, screenshots, categories and the questions in their reviews.
steps.evidence: The listings read, with URLs, and what they have in common.

steps.do: Write the listing in the marketplace's fields: name, short description with the buyer's outcome, long description, categories, pricing as on the product page, setup steps, and support and privacy URLs. Only claims the product facts support.
steps.evidence: The listing text per field with sources.

steps.do: Prepare screenshots and a short video from the real product in the sizes the marketplace asks for.
steps.evidence: The files and what each shows.

steps.do: Set the website or install link to the round's tracked link (?v= per marketplace) where the marketplace allows a redirect; otherwise use the product URL with a utm tag and read installs from the marketplace's own report.
steps.evidence: The link used per marketplace and why.

steps.do: Show the owner the listing and assets word for word and get a yes; the owner, or the agent with its own tools and the owner's yes, submits or updates it. Answer the platform's review questions; any change to claims goes back to the owner.
steps.evidence: The owner's approval, the submission time, and the review questions with answers.

steps.do: When it is live, open the public listing, check it matches what was approved, and pass its URL as the first item in links.
steps.evidence: The live URL and the check.

blockers.do: If a listing is still in review, submit the step as blocked with the expected date.
If a listing is rejected, record the reason and fix it with the owner before submitting again.
If the marketplace forbids redirect links, use the product URL with a utm tag and read numbers from the marketplace's report.
If a claim cannot be backed by the product facts, remove it.

C-MKT-LISTING.title_zh: 以真實截圖與追蹤連結上架或優化市集頁面

deliver_help.listing_urls: The public URL of each live listing.
deliver_help.published_text: The listing text as it appears live.
deliver_help.tracked_links: The link used on each listing.
deliver_help.review_status: Each listing's review status and any changes asked for.

C-OB-ACCESS.title: Set up a warmed-up sending domain, the legal basics and the daily cap
C-OB-ACCESS.purpose: Prepare cold outreach so it reaches inboxes and stays legal: a separate, verified sending domain warmed up slowly, a postal address and unsubscribe in every email, and a daily cap the owner approves, because one burst from a cold domain can hurt the brand's email for months.

steps.do: Ask the owner to use a separate sending domain or subdomain for outreach (for example get{product}.com or mail.{product}.com), never the main domain that sends receipts. The owner buys or sets it up; the agent lists exactly which DNS records to add. On the hosted service, follow the sending-domain checklist on the owner page.
steps.evidence: The sending domain and who set it up.

steps.do: Check that the domain's SPF, DKIM and DMARC records are published and pass (read the DNS or a public checker), and that the mailbox can send and receive. Give the owner any missing record line by line.
steps.evidence: Each record found, pass or missing, with the time checked.

steps.do: Plan the warm-up: for the first two weeks send only to real contacts who expect mail, a few a day per mailbox (for example 5 to 10 a day, adding about 5 a day each week), up to at most 30 to 50 a day per mailbox once replies and bounces look healthy. No outreach volume before warm-up is done.
steps.evidence: The warm-up schedule with dates and the day outreach may start.

steps.do: Write the legal basics for the countries you will email: an honest From name and subject, the company's postal address, a working unsubscribe, and opt-outs honoured promptly (for example the US CAN-SPAM Act). Where the law requires prior consent for business email (for example Canada's CASL and some EU countries), email only contacts the law allows, or leave that country out. Ask the owner to confirm.
steps.evidence: The rules per country targeted, and the owner's confirmation.

steps.do: Agree the daily cap with the owner (all mailboxes together) and the stop rules: pause if bounces pass 3% or any spam complaint arrives in a day.
steps.evidence: The daily cap and stop rules, approved by the owner.

steps.do: Set up the do-not-contact list (opt-outs, bounces, customers, competitors, people who said no) and where replies are read.
steps.evidence: The do-not-contact list and the reply inbox.

blockers.do: If there is no separate sending domain, send no outreach from the main domain; wait for the owner to set one up.
If a record is missing or failing, give the owner the exact record to add and send nothing until it passes.
If warm-up is not finished, send only within the warm-up schedule.
If a country needs prior consent you do not have, leave it out.
If a DNS, billing or verification screen needs the owner, tell them which page and which button.

C-OB-ACCESS.title_zh: 設定已暖機的寄件網域、法規基本要求與每日上限

deliver_help.sending_domain: The outreach domain or subdomain and who set it up.
deliver_help.dns_check: SPF, DKIM and DMARC: found, pass or missing, with the time checked.
deliver_help.warmup_plan: The warm-up schedule and the first day outreach may start.
deliver_help.legal_rules: The rules per country and the owner's confirmation.
deliver_help.daily_cap: The daily cap, the stop rules and the do-not-contact list.

C-OB-LIST.title: Build the target list from published business contacts only
C-OB-LIST.purpose: List companies that match the customer profile and, for each, a person in the buying role with a business contact they or their company published, because guessed or bought addresses bounce, annoy people and break the law in many places.

steps.do: Turn the customer profile into searches: company directories, industry lists, marketplaces where such companies appear, job posts that mention the problem, and companies that publicly reviewed a competitor.
steps.evidence: The searches and sources with dates.

steps.do: Collect 50 to 150 companies that fit (size, type, location, a visible sign of the problem), each with the page that shows the fit.
steps.evidence: The company list with the fit evidence URL for each.

steps.do: For each company, find the person in the buying role on the company's own team page, press page or public profile.
steps.evidence: Name, role and the page that shows it.

steps.do: Find a published business contact for that person or role: an address printed on the company's website, press or contact page, a public profile that lists a business email, or the company's contact form. Never guess an address pattern, never use bought lists or tools that infer addresses, never use personal addresses. If nothing is published, use the contact form or leave the company out.
steps.evidence: The contact and the URL where it is published, for each person.

steps.do: Remove customers, current trials, competitors, the do-not-contact list, and companies in countries the legal rules left out.
steps.evidence: Removed counts by reason.

steps.do: For each kept contact, write one true personal line from their public pages (a recent post, launch, job ad or review) for {why_now}.
steps.evidence: The line and its source URL for each contact.

blockers.do: If no contact is published, use the company's contact form or leave them out; never guess.
If fewer than 50 companies fit, widen the profile one step and tell the owner.
If a site's terms forbid collecting contacts, do not collect from it.
If only a personal address is found, leave the person out.

C-OB-LIST.title_zh: 只用公開發布的商務聯絡方式建立名單

deliver_help.target_list: Company, person, role and fit evidence for each contact.
deliver_help.contact_sources: The published contact and the URL it appears on, for each person.
deliver_help.personal_lines: The personal line and its source URL for each contact.

C-OB-SEQUENCE.title: Send the approved outreach email and up to two follow-ups within the daily cap
C-OB-SEQUENCE.purpose: Reach each target once with a short, personal email built from one owner-approved template, then at most two polite follow-ups, within the warmed-up daily cap, so qualified buyers book a call and nobody is pestered.

steps.do: Write the first email template under 100 words with placeholders such as {first_name}, {company} and {why_now}: one line on why you write to them, the problem in their words, one proof the product facts support, a small ask (a 15-minute call, or 'shall I send a 2-minute video?'), the sender's real name and company, the postal address and an unsubscribe line. Plain text, no images, at most one link. Each placeholder value is one line of at most 80 characters (40 for a name); where one needs more, write its limit, for example {why_now:120} (200 at most). Values carry no links; a link goes in the fixed text or a {link} placeholder.
steps.evidence: The template with its placeholders.

steps.do: Write two follow-up templates (day 3 and day 7, each under 60 words), sent only to people who did not reply, opt out or bounce.
steps.evidence: The two follow-up templates and their rules.

steps.do: Get the template approved. In a month target, send it with submit_batch as one item of kind 'template' with text, audience_rule and daily_cap, and tell the owner to approve it on their owner page or with the approve command. Outside a month target, show the owner the template, the audience rule and the cap, and get a clear yes. Never approve it yourself. The cap counts first emails and follow-ups together and never goes past that day's warm-up schedule.
steps.evidence: The template ids, caps and the owner's approval.

steps.do: Each day, send to the next contacts on the list within the cap, filling placeholders with true values, each one line of at most 80 characters (40 for a name) unless the template sets its own limit such as {why_now:120}, with no link except in a {link} placeholder; one recipient per email, from the warmed-up mailbox. When today's messages are out, submit this step with approved_item set to the template's id (in a month target) and the sent texts in output; the engine checks each one against the approved template and the day's cap.
steps.evidence: Per day: emails, follow-ups, bounces and opt-outs, with sample texts.

steps.do: Read replies twice a day. A yes or a question gets an answer within one business day with the calendar link the owner approved; a no or 'remove me' goes on the do-not-contact list at once and gets no more mail.
steps.evidence: Replies by type and what was done.

steps.do: Check the stop rules every day: bounces over 3% or any spam complaint pause sending, and the owner is told the same day.
steps.evidence: Daily bounce and complaint rates and any pause.

blockers.do: If the owner has not approved a template, send nothing with it.
If the cap is above that day's warm-up limit, send only up to the warm-up limit.
If bounces pass 3% in a day, pause, remove the bad addresses and tell the owner.
If a spam complaint arrives, pause sending and tell the owner the same day.
If more contacts are due than the cap allows, send the rest on later days.

C-OB-SEQUENCE.title_zh: 在每日上限內寄出核准的開發信與最多兩封追蹤信

deliver_help.templates: The approved first email and follow-ups word for word.
deliver_help.owner_approval: The template ids, caps and the owner's approval with dates.
deliver_help.sent_record: Per day: count sent, follow-ups, bounces and opt-outs, with sample texts.
deliver_help.replies: Replies by type (yes, question, no, remove me) and what was done.
deliver_help.meetings_booked: Calls accepted on the calendar, with company and date, or 'none yet'.

C-AGY-FIND.title: Find agencies and consultants who already serve the buyer
C-AGY-FIND.purpose: List agencies, consultants and implementers whose clients are this product's buyers and who publicly work with software partners, because one partner who recommends the product to every client can bring more paying customers than many single sales.

steps.do: Write who the partner is: what service they sell to the buyer (setup, marketing, bookkeeping, development), their clients' size, and why recommending this product helps them (saves their time, adds a service, earns a share).
steps.evidence: The partner profile in four lines.

steps.do: Search partner directories of tools the buyers use (for example the HubSpot Solutions Directory, Shopify Partner directory, Webflow Experts, or accounting software advisor directories), service marketplaces (Clutch, agency pages on Upwork), and searches like '{service} agency for {buyer}'. Collect at least 30 candidates.
steps.evidence: The sources and searches with dates, and at least 30 candidates with URLs.

steps.do: For each candidate, use read_page on their services and case-study pages: who their clients are, which tools they already resell or recommend, and their size.
steps.evidence: For each candidate, the URLs read and one line on client fit.

steps.do: Check that each publishes a partnership or contact route (a partners page, a 'tools we use' page, a contact form or a business email on their site). Never guess addresses.
steps.evidence: The published route and its page for each candidate.

steps.do: Rank by client fit, then by whether they already partner with similar tools, then by size. Keep 10 to 20, mark any that partner with a direct competitor, and show the owner the list to strike anyone.
steps.evidence: The ranked list and the owner's reply.

blockers.do: If fewer than 10 fit, widen to nearby services and tell the owner the list is thin.
If a candidate publishes no contact route, leave them out; never guess.
If a candidate partners with a direct competitor, mark it and let the owner decide.
If the owner has not reviewed the list, submit the step as blocked and say what to check.

C-AGY-FIND.title_zh: 找出已在服務這群買家的代理商與顧問

deliver_help.shortlist: The 10 to 20 ranked partners with URL and the owner's yes or no.
deliver_help.fit_evidence: For each, the pages read and one line on client fit.
deliver_help.contact_routes: For each, the published contact route and its page.
deliver_help.conflicts: Partners who work with a direct competitor, or 'none'.

C-AGY-OUTREACH.title: Invite the chosen partners with the approved partner offer and template
C-AGY-OUTREACH.purpose: Offer each chosen partner a clear, owner-approved reason to recommend the product to their clients, sent once with a personal note within a daily cap, so partner calls get booked with the right firms.

steps.do: Settle the partner offer with the owner from what they will honour: a referral share (percentage and for how long), a reseller discount, a free partner account for their own use, co-marketing (a case study, a place on the owner's partner page), and how referrals are tracked (a partner link with the label ?v=partner-name, or a code). Never promise terms the owner did not approve.
steps.evidence: The approved partner offer quoted from the owner.

steps.do: Write one invitation template under 120 words with placeholders such as {first_name}, {agency}, {their_client_type} and {their_case_study}: why their clients need this, what the partner gets, what you ask (a 20-minute call), and how to say no. Each placeholder value is one line of at most 80 characters (40 for a name); where one needs more, write its limit, for example {their_case_study:120} (200 at most). Values carry no links; a link goes in the fixed text or a {link} placeholder.
steps.evidence: The template with its placeholders.

steps.do: Get the template approved. In a month target, send it with submit_batch as one item of kind 'template' with text, audience_rule and daily_cap, and tell the owner to approve it on their owner page or with the approve command. Outside a month target, show the owner the template, the audience rule and the cap, and get a clear yes. Never approve it yourself. Start at 10 partners a day.
steps.evidence: The template's id and the owner's approval.

steps.do: Send once per partner through their published route within the cap, from the approved account; one follow-up after 5 business days that is part of the approved templates, then stop. When today's messages are out, submit this step with approved_item set to the template's id (in a month target) and the sent texts in output; the engine checks each one against the approved template and the day's cap. Fill each placeholder with a true value: one line, at most 80 characters (40 for a name) unless the template sets its own limit, with no link except in a {link} placeholder.
steps.evidence: Sends, follow-ups and replies with times.

steps.do: Book a call with each interested partner using the owner's calendar link, and send them the partner one-pager before the call.
steps.evidence: Calls booked with dates.

blockers.do: If the owner has not decided the partner offer, contact nobody; show options and wait.
If the owner has not approved the template, send nothing.
If more partners are due than the cap allows, send the rest on later days.
If a partner says no or asks to stop, contact them no more.

C-AGY-OUTREACH.title_zh: 用核准的合作方案與模板邀請選定的合作夥伴

deliver_help.partner_offer: The partner offer exactly as the owner approved it.
deliver_help.template: The approved template word for word.
deliver_help.owner_approval: The template's id and the owner's approval with its date.
deliver_help.sent_record: Each send and follow-up with recipient and time.
deliver_help.calls_booked: Partner calls booked with dates, or 'none yet'.

C-AGY-ENABLE.title: Onboard each partner and help them bring their first client
C-AGY-ENABLE.purpose: Give each partner who says yes what they need to recommend the product with confidence (their own link, a partner account, a short demo and a client-ready one-pager) and help with their first client, because partners who succeed once keep referring.

steps.do: Record each agreed partner's terms in writing (the approved offer, how referrals are tracked, when payouts happen) and have the owner send or approve the agreement; the agent never signs.
steps.evidence: Each partner's written terms and who approved them.

steps.do: Set up the partner's own link (the label ?v=partner-name on the round's tracked link, or the owner's referral tool) and a free partner account if one was offered. Open the link and check it works.
steps.evidence: The link and account for each partner, checked.

steps.do: Give a 20-minute walk-through (the owner live, or a recorded demo) and a one-page client brief: who it is for, the outcome, the price, how to start, and a 'do not promise' list.
steps.evidence: The brief and the date of the walk-through.

steps.do: Ask each partner which one or two clients fit now, and offer to join the first client call or send a short demo the partner can forward.
steps.evidence: The first clients named and the help offered.

steps.do: Check in once a week during the window; record introductions, trials and paid customers per partner. A commission is owed only on a counted payment.
steps.evidence: For each partner: introductions, trials, paid customers and commission owed.

blockers.do: If the owner has not approved the agreement, give the partner no link or account yet.
If a partner's link does not open the product, fix it before sending.
If a partner brings nobody after two check-ins, mark them inactive and stop chasing.
If a partner asks about a payout, answer only with the written terms and pass anything else to the owner.

C-AGY-ENABLE.title_zh: 協助每位合作夥伴上手並帶來第一位客戶

deliver_help.partner_terms: Each partner's written terms and who approved them.
deliver_help.partner_links: Each partner's link, opened and confirmed.
deliver_help.first_clients: Clients each partner named and the help given, or 'none yet'.
deliver_help.partner_record: Per partner: introductions, trials, paid customers and commission owed.
